program_overview.content:
**AI + Statistical Analytics (MSc)** is a **1 year**, **full-time** conversion course starting **28 September 2026**. Conversion courses allow you to study a subject unrelated to your undergraduate degree or current career, and support you with a change of career path.
The MSc AI + Statistical Analytics is a conversion programme designed to provide you with the knowledge, skills, and practical experience needed to thrive in the rapidly expanding fields of artificial intelligence and data analytics. You’ll get an introduction to fundamental concepts in AI, data science, and statistical modelling, with an emphasis on their practical application to real-world problems. You’ll learn the technical expertise, critical awareness, and ethical understanding necessary to apply AI and statistical methods across a wide variety of domains.
You’ll get hands-on experience with programming, data handling, and modelling tools, and engage with the wider opportunities and challenges associated with AI, including issues of governance, communication, and societal impact. You’ll develop a solid foundation in AI models, statistical methods, and computational techniques, and the ability to critically evaluate and apply AI and AI outputs and data-driven approaches to complex problems across business, government, and society. As well as practical skills in programming, machine learning, analytics, and data visualisation, you’ll study the ethical, legal, and social implications of AI, and of applying the outputs of AI.
This conversion course welcomes students from all backgrounds, with no prior coding required. It offers hands-on AI training, practical experience applying AI and data science to real-world problems across sectors, cross-disciplinary expertise from Mathematics and Computer Science within Cardiff’s Data Science Academy, global career readiness, and an ethics and impact focus.
The programme is based in the [School of Mathematics](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/mathematics), Senghennydd Road, Cathays, Cardiff, CF24 4AG. The School states that its intellectually exciting degrees are accredited to meet the educational requirements of the Chartered Mathematician designation.
The MSc AI + Statistical Analytics is a one-year full-time programme (**180 credits**) delivered in two stages. The taught stage consists of six 20-credit modules (**120 credits in total**), followed by a **60-credit independent project**. You will study the 6 compulsory modules to a total of 120 credits, followed by a 60-credit dissertation project undertaken in the summer.
You’ll learn through a blend of lectures, practical workshops, group activities, and independent study, designed to give you both the theoretical understanding and the hands-on experience needed to apply AI and statistical analytics in practice. Each module includes interactive sessions, case studies, and practical exercises using widely used AI and data science tools. You’ll also develop your skills through collaborative project work, presentations, and independent research, culminating in a substantial dissertation project supervised by an expert in the field. Throughout the programme you will be encouraged to apply your learning to real-world data and challenges, ensuring that you graduate with the confidence and ability to use AI responsibly and effectively.
Each module is led by an experienced academic who provides guidance and feedback throughout the course. You will be allocated a personal tutor, a member of the academic staff who will provide pastoral support and academic advice during your course.
As a graduate of the programme you’ll be well-prepared for employment in the AI and data science sectors, with the ability to contribute to solving pressing global challenges and to lead in the responsible and effective application of artificial intelligence. Graduates with AI and statistical analytics expertise are in high demand across industries such as finance, healthcare, security, and manufacturing. This programme equips you with practical skills in programming, machine learning, and statistical modelling, alongside transferable strengths in problem-solving, teamwork, and communication. The emphasis on ethics and governance prepares you to apply AI responsibly in real-world contexts. Your independent research project will showcase your ability to deliver innovative, applied solutions, giving you a competitive edge in the job market or a strong foundation for further study. Typical job titles for graduates include AI Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, Robotics Engineer and Deep Learning Scientist.
Industrial partners are invited to support the delivery of a variety of modules, offering hands-on experience with real-world data and industry projects. An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation, which allows you to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world problem or a more theoretical problem. This might involve working with an external company or organisation.

financial_aid.content:
The 2026 Cardiff University **£6,000 India Scholarships** are open to all eligible India-domiciled students enrolling on a select number of postgraduate programmes commencing in September 2026, including **MSc AI + Statistical Analytics** in the School of Mathematics.
No separate scholarship application is required. You will automatically be awarded the scholarship upon enrolment if you are holding an offer for an eligible programme and meet the criteria as set out in the [India Scholarship terms and conditions](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/documents/3011272-cardiff-university-india-scholarships-september-2026-terms-and-conditions).
- You must submit your eligible course application to the University **by 31 July 2026**.
- Conditional offer holders must meet all offer conditions, including any English Language conditions as stated in the offer, **by 20 August 2026**.
- Applicants who receive their academic offer by 1st July 2026 must accept their offer and pay any deposit by **31 July 2026**. Applicants who receive their academic offer after this date must pay their deposit by their initial deposit deadline and accept their offer within 14 days of it being made. Deposit deadline extensions past **31 July 2026** will not be accepted for scholarship purposes.
- The Scholarship of **£6,000** will be awarded to students defined as being domiciled in India on their course application.
- Scholarship eligibility is separate from admission eligibility. To qualify for the Cardiff University India Scholarship, you must achieve the published minimum academic entry requirements for your chosen programme exactly as stated on the course pages of the website, at the time of your application.
- If you are offered a place at Cardiff University with lower grades or alternative qualifications than those published, you will hold an offer to study, but you will not be eligible for the Cardiff University India Scholarship.
- Any queries regarding scholarship eligibility need to be raised before **30 November 2026** by emailing [InternationalScholarships@cardiff.ac.uk](mailto:InternationalScholarships@cardiff.ac.uk).

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Applicants may be allowed deferred entry to a programme, subject to meeting the entry requirements and places being available. The maximum period of deferral granted will be **no more than 12 months**. Applicants wishing to defer admission for a longer period will be required to reapply. In exceptional circumstances, where an applicant may wish to seek an extension to the deferral period, the School must submit a case for approval to the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Student Experience and Academic Standards). Applicants should use the [online form](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/ask-a-question) to request a deferral.
For postgraduate taught (PGT) programmes, Cardiff University also reserves the right to close programmes and/or to offer a deferred entry place where a programme has reached capacity, and to offer deferred entry to applicants who apply within 12 weeks of the start date of a programme if there is not sufficient time to process all the requirements for an applicant to start their programme by the last date of enrolment.

program_overview.content:
The Master of Accounting Analytics programme offered by the HKU Business School aims to develop accounting professionals equipped with data analytics skills and is specifically designed to foster talents capable of transforming raw and intricate accounting data into actionable intelligence for addressing general accounting-related questions. The primary focus of the programme is to equip students with specialised tools used in the accounting industry to cope with the increasing market demand.
The programme trains accounting professionals with both technical and accounting expertise through the utilisation of data, information technology, statistical analysis, quantitative methods, and mathematical or computer-based models, as well as foundational accounting courses to meet the requirement of professional bodies. Incoming students with diverse undergraduate backgrounds are attracted, and experiences in accounting and/or technology can be highly valuable.
Graduates can anticipate a wide array of analytics-related career opportunities across various levels, from junior to senior positions, in both private and public sectors. These opportunities encompass data-driven decision making, cost control, fraud detection and prevention, performance evaluation, forecasting and budgeting, compliance, and risk management. Graduates will be well-positioned to explore careers in industries that increasingly rely on data analytics.
The programme includes pre-programme boot camp, core courses, elective courses, and a capstone course. The capstone course allows students to integrate and apply knowledge and techniques learned in previous courses in a business project using real-world data, including project planning and management, strategy setting, model building, data analysis and interpretation, and result presentation.
Our Faculty includes [Prof. Anson Yile JIANG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/anson-yile-jiang/), [Prof. Wei LUO](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/wei-luo-2/), [Dr. Kin Hang CHAN](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/kin-hang-chan), [Prof. Michael CHAU](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/michael-c-l-chau/), [Prof. Hailiang CHEN](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/hailiang-chen/), [Prof. Travis CHOW](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/travis-chow/), [Prof. Pingyang GAO](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/pingyang-gao), [Prof. Keri HU](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/keri-peicong-hu/), [Dr. Jasmine KWONG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/jasmine-kwong/), [Prof. David LEE](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/david-s-lee/), [Prof. Xiao LEI](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/xiao-lei/), [Prof. Winnie LEUNG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/winnie-s-c-leung/), [Prof. Peeyush TAORI](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/peeyush-taori/), [Prof. Xin WANG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/xin-wang/), [Prof. Yan XIONG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/yan-xiong/) Ph.D., University of Toronto, MAA Programme Director, Prof. Joseph XU Ph.D, University of Pennsylvania; Chief Technology Officer, Chainproof Digital Asset Insurance Ltd., [Prof. Sammy FUNG](https://www.hkubs.hku.hk/people/sammy-fung/), [Prof. Simon S.K. The programme is accredited by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), CPA Australia, Chartered Global Management Accountants (CGMA), and the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA).

curriculum.content:
The Master of Accounting Analytics curriculum includes mandatory pre-programme boot camp courses, core courses, elective courses, and a capstone course.
- Mandatory boot camp courses cover: Economics; Preparatory Course for Accounting Fundamentals; Introduction to Python and Vibe Coding for Accounting Analytics. Each topic consists of 15 hours of interactive lectures and, for Economics, an examination at the end. Students are required to attend all classes and pass all boot camp courses.
- Refresher course on fundamental accounting concepts, Preparatory Course for Accounting Fundamentals, will also be provided to brush up students' accounting skills.
- Course exemption of up to two required courses, except the capstone course, may be granted normally by examination if candidates can produce evidence that a course is equivalent in content to another course taken elsewhere with a satisfactory grade, or are holding relevant professional qualifications obtained before admission to the curriculum. No credits will be given for the exempted course and candidates shall be required to take an approved alternative course of the same credit value.
Core courses listed include:
- PMAA7005 Integrated Auditing: Bridging the Gap Between IT Audit and Financial Statement Audit
- PMAA7004 Advanced Accounting Analytics
- PMAA7003 Accounting Analytics Foundation
- PMAA7002 Data Modelling and Economic Decisions
- PMAA7001 Accounting and Business Intelligence
Elective courses listed include:
- PMAA7008 Blockchain, Cryptocurrency and Cybersecurity
- PMAA7009 Accounting, Fintech and Innovation
- PMAA7010 Data Mining and Text Analysis
- PMAA7011 Deep Learning and Neural Networks
- PMAA7012 Taxation Framework and Planning
- PMAA7013 Corporate Finance
- PMAA7014 Principles of Management
- PMAA7015 ESG Reporting: Concepts and Practices
- PMAA7016 Accounting Analytics and Managerial Decisions
- PMAA7017 Social Media and Digital Marketing Analytics
- PMAA7018 Database Design and Management
- PMAA7019 Advanced Financial Reporting: A Case-Based Approach
- PMAA7020 Legal and Ethical Environment of Business
- PMAA7021 International Study Field Trip
- PMAA7022 Fundamentals of Banking Institutions
- PMAA7024 Financial Statement Analysis: A Data Analytic Approach
- PMAA7025 AI for Financial Valuation and Investment
Other Masters Programmes electives: Candidates may take up to two elective courses from other taught postgraduate curricula offered by the Faculty of Business and Economics under the advice and approval of the Programme Directors concerned. Students can take up to two electives from the Master of Accounting, Master of Artificial Intelligence in Business, Master of Economics, Master of Finance, Master of Global Management, Master of Science in Business Analytics, Master of Science in Marketing, Master of Sustainable Accounting and Finance or Master of Wealth Management programme at HKU. Enrollment in electives from other programmes is subject to seat availability and approval by the Programme Directors concerned based on the student's profile, capabilities and performance in the MAA programme. Since enrollment in other taught postgraduate electives is not guaranteed, students should always choose two MAA electives during course enrollment.
Capstone Course (Choose One):
- PMAA7007 Artificial Intelligence in Accounting
- PMSC7901 Business Case Analysis Capstone

financial_aid.content:
In 2024, the Faculty of Business and Economics established the Master of Accounting Analytics Scholarship for students of the Master of Accounting Analytics (MAA) programme.
The Scholarship shall be awarded annually either as an Entrance Scholarship to new full-time MAA students or a Merit-based Scholarship to current full-time MAA students.
For the Entrance Scholarship, the number of scholarships to be awarded each year and the value of each scholarship shall be determined by the Faculty Scholarship Committee, upon funding availability and recommendation of the MAA Admissions Committee based on the following criteria:
1. Reputation of candidates’ previous undergraduate or postgraduate institution;
2. Academic performance;
3. Prior international experience; and
4. Relevance of full-time work experience after the first degree.
Financial need may also be taken into consideration. The Scholarship shall not be paid directly to the awardees, but rather be applied to cover their composition fees. In exceptional case, for students who are granted with full scholarship, an additional amount might be granted in the form of subsistence allowance. In any event, the value of each scholarship shall not be less than **HK$10,000**.
For the Merit-based Scholarship, the number of awards shall not exceed **20% of the class size** in the relevant academic year, and the value of each scholarship shall be **10% of the composition fee** of the given intake. The exact number of scholarships shall be determined by the Faculty Scholarship Committee, upon funding availability and recommendation of the MAA Programme Director based on the following criteria:
1. Academic performance in first three modules of the relevant academic year;
2. Participation in extracurricular activities arranged by the programme office and the career and enrichment teams, including, but not limited to, industry seminars, career workshops and student activities, in the first three modules of the relevant academic year;
3. Recommendations from the course instructors of the first three modules in the relevant academic year on the course performance and class participation; and,
4. Level of support provided to the programme office in marketing and admissions efforts, student activities and other programme-related initiatives.

program_overview.content:
MSc Accounting and Data Analytics is a Graduate (Taught) programme in the Department of Accounting. Study mode / programme availability is full-time for Home and Overseas students, with a duration of 10 months. The academic year is 2026/27, the start date is Early September 2026, and the location is Houghton Street, London.
The MSc Accounting and Data Analytics is designed for students who want to understand how roles in accounting, investment banking, and asset management are being reshaped by advances in data science, technology, and digital transformation. Throughout the programme, students develop both theoretical foundations and applied skills across accounting, financial management, data analytics, and computer programming, preparing them for roles that demand a strong understanding of business fundamentals alongside the ability to analyse, model, and interpret complex data.
A defining feature of the programme is its integration of accounting fundamentals with applied data science. Developed in response to growing demand within the investment industry, the programme emphasises the use of analytical tools in key areas such as financial reporting, forecasting, corporate valuation, and performance analysis. It is designed to equip students with financial insight and technical capability valued by data-driven financial and non-financial institutions.
Graduates will be prepared for roles in asset management, private equity, investment banking, corporate finance, ESG analytics, and management consulting. The programme also appeals to students seeking to work in audit and assurance functions that increasingly rely on data-driven approaches. Students benefit from LSE’s location in London, with opportunities to connect with leading financial institutions through employer events, alumni panels, and industry-focused public lectures, complemented by tailored career support throughout the year.
The programme begins with a pre-sessional programme in early September, including preparatory classes in quantitative methods, financial accounting, and management accounting, along with professional development sessions, career, networking, and social events designed to help students connect with faculty and fellow students. Its primary aim is to ensure that all students, regardless of academic background, reach a shared level of knowledge and understanding.
In the first term, students take courses designed to develop advanced skills in both accounting and data analytics. The foundational accounting courses build understanding of how economic activity is captured and communicated through financial statements, while data analytics training combines applied regression, computer programming, and data management and visualisation. In the second term, students take two bespoke core courses exclusive to the degree programme: Advanced Financial Statement Analysis and Forensic Accounting Analytics. The programme also includes electives in both accounting and data analytics, allowing students to tailor the degree to areas such as M&A analysis, ESG disclosure evaluation, management control, machine learning, or natural language processing.
Following the pre-sessional programme, students take examined courses totalling four full units over the academic year. On average, students can expect around 12 hours of contact time per week, including lectures and seminars, alongside independent study. Teaching is informed by the research of LSE faculty active in academic and policy debates in accounting, finance, and data science. Courses are delivered through lectures, classes, and seminars, and faculty use teaching methods including case discussions, programming tasks, group projects, and data-driven problem sets.
Assessment is based on a combination of formal summative evaluations and formative assessments. Summative assessments typically include written examinations, essays, and project work, while formative assessments such as problem sets, class exercises, or group presentations provide feedback without affecting final marks.
Graduates of the MSc in Accounting and Data Analytics will be well equipped for careers at the intersection of finance, accounting, and data science. Typical roles include financial analyst, asset manager, investment banking associate, private equity analyst, forensic accountant, ESG analyst, and management consultant, particularly in firms that prioritise data-driven decision-making. Potential employers span investment banks, hedge funds, consulting firms, asset managers, and audit and advisory firms. The programme also provides a foundation for roles in audit, assurance, financial advisory, ESG strategy, risk analytics, compliance, technology and fintech strategy or product teams, and data science roles requiring domain-specific expertise in finance and accounting. It also serves as preparation for research-focused degrees, including PhD programmes in accounting, finance, or data science.
Top 5 sectors Department of Accounting students work in:
- Financial and Professional Services
- Accounting and Auditing
- FMCG, Manufacturing and Retail
- Consultancy
- Education, Teaching and Research
The Department of Accounting at LSE is recognised worldwide for the excellence of its research and teaching, ranked eighth in the world in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. The department has a long-standing research tradition and has explored the role of accounting in firms, markets, and the economy. It was ranked the top place in the UK to study accounting by the Guardian University Guide in its 2025 and 2026 league tables. Each year, the department admits around 375 students across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes.

cost_of_attendance.content:
[LSE broadly estimates that students should allow £1,550 per month](https://info.lse.ac.uk/current-students/immigration-advice/applying-for-a-Student-visa) for all living expenses, including accommodation, travel, food, laundry, study costs, and other personal expenses.
- Private housing costs can vary considerably depending on location and accommodation type, but start at approximately **£650 per month**.
- Food costs will account for a significant part of your budget. LSE estimates that students will spend **£150-£300 per month** on food, depending on whether they live in catered or self-catered halls, or whether they live in private accommodation.

financial_aid.content:
Applications are considered on a rolling basis, but if you’d like to be considered for any funding opportunities, you must submit your application and all supporting documents by the funding deadline.
- **Fee reduction:** Students who have completed and passed an undergraduate degree at LSE and are beginning taught graduate study at the School are eligible for a **10 per cent tuition fee reduction**. Students who have completed and passed two or more Summer School courses are eligible for a **five per cent reduction**. If you meet the eligibility criteria for both discounts, the higher **10 per cent** discount rate will apply. [Find out more about the LSE alumni discount](https://info.lse.ac.uk/staff/divisions/Finance-Division/Fees-Income-and-Credit-Control/Rewards-and-Discounts).
- **Scholarships and other funding:** LSE provides scholarships to help both home and overseas students. It offers some needs-based awards for this programme, including the [Graduate Support Scheme](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/secure/graduate-support-scheme) and the [LSE Excellence Scholarship](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/LSE-Excellence-Scholarship). Competition for these awards and scholarships is strong.
- To apply for an award, you must have an offer of a place and submit a Graduate Financial Support application before the funding deadline. The funding deadline for needs-based awards from LSE is **23 April 2026**.
- In addition to needs-based awards, LSE offers [scholarships for students from specific regions of the world](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding) and [awards for certain subjects](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/Department-or-programme-specific-funding).
- You can’t apply for a Graduate Support Scheme or LSE scholarship once you’ve joined the School. LSE expects students who register for a programme to have sufficient funds for the duration.
- At LSE, your tuition fees, and eligibility for any financial support, will depend on whether you’re classified as a home or overseas student.

multiple_applications.content:
You may submit an application via the online application system only **ONCE** within the application cycle (**October 2025 to September 2026**).
When completing your initial online application, you may choose up to **two programmes** in order of preference. **If you are applying for two programmes, please submit a separate statement of academic purpose for each programme**. Your choices will be considered in sequence, and it is only possible to hold one offer of a place, so if you are offered a place on your first-choice programme you will not be considered for your second-choice unless you specifically request it.
If you are unsuccessful in your application to both of your initially chosen programmes and you wish to be considered for further, additional choices, you may do this by submitting the **Add/Amend programmes** form via the [Graduate Applicant Portal](https://lseportal.force.com/admissions/s/track-my-graduate-application) and paying an additional administrative fee of **£105**. You should not use this form to add choices 3 and 4 before receiving a decision on each of your original programme choices, unless you wish to withdraw your initial programme choices.
**You may only submit an application using the online application system ONCE in the same admissions cycle. If you submit a second online application within the same admissions cycle, it will not be considered.** **To apply to further programmes after you have submitted your initial online application, you must use the process above.**

deferral_admission_policy.content:
LSE has a no-deferrals policy for offers for graduate programmes. The only exception to this is in cases of unforeseen illness or bereavement.
If a deferral is agreed in exceptional circumstances, you must submit a deferral deposit as requested in your deferral letter, using the student self-funding [payment portal](https://portal.lse.ac.uk/payments/s/fees). The deposit must be received by the **January 31st deadline** to secure your new offer for next year. The deferral deposit is offset against your tuition fees once you register.
If your circumstances match the exceptional circumstances, you may request to defer your offer using the Extenuating Circumstances form on the Graduate Applicant Portal. If your request is agreed, your offer for the current year will be declined automatically, as you do not intend to come to LSE in this cycle.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
Any offer of admission will be subject to proof of your English language score. If you have not taken a test by the time you apply, your application can still be considered without it, but **any offer will be conditional on the required score**.
- If you are set an English language condition, you may be able to take an [English Pre-sessional course at the LSE Language Centre](https://www.lse.ac.uk/language-centre/english-programmes/english-presessional-programme).
- **If you are set an English language condition, we encourage you to book a test at your earliest opportunity**.
- English tests must be **less than two years old on 1 October 2026**.
- If you are unable to take one of LSE’s preferred tests, it may be possible to take an alternative test such as Duolingo or IELTS Indicator and supplement your score by taking the LSE Language Centre Assessment; to request this option, complete the extenuating circumstances form on the GAP, providing any existing test scores and reasons why you are unable to take one of the listed tests.
- On rare occasions, LSE may accept scores below its minimum requirements if there are extenuating circumstances surrounding test scores, but **under NO CIRCUMSTANCES** will it accept scores that do not meet UKVI’s English proficiency requirements for a student visa, because the applicant would not be granted entry to the UK with such a score and LSE will therefore not issue a CAS.

program_overview.content:
MSc in Accounting and Finance Analytics
- Programme Code: 21052; Stream Code: FAM (Full-time), PAM (Part-time).
- Mode of Study: Mixed Mode. Students can pursue their studies with either a full-time study load (taking 9 credits or more in a semester) or a part-time study load (fewer than 9 credits in a semester).
- Normal Duration: 1 year (Full-time), 2 years (Part-time). Students should complete the programme full-time in 1 year and part-time in 2 years within the normal duration. Students will be required to attend more classes in the evening if they choose the full-time option, and the duration will be subject to class quota availability.
- Credits Required for Graduation: 31.
- Programme Director: Prof. Feng TIAN, PhD. Deputy Programme Director: Dr Justin LAW, PhD.
The advancement of information technology has made a great impact on the way of doing business and the practices in the accounting and finance profession. At the same time, the applications of data analytics have become increasingly important and significantly affected almost every business sector and industry. With the widespread application of emerging new digital technology to the accounting and finance profession, there is a need to equip students with the training of technological skills and knowledge to cope with the demands of the business community.
The **Master of Science in Accounting and Finance Analytics** is a conversion programme designed for graduates to develop a broad understanding of the accounting and finance disciplines and the applications of technology to these disciplines. The programme has been accepted into the CFA Institute University Affiliation Programme, positioning students to sit for the CFA examinations.
The programme aims to provide students with a combination of core knowledge in accounting and finance and skills in applying data analytics and technology to related practices. It facilities practitioners in accounting and finance to keep up with the latest data analytics applications and skills. The programme emphasizes:
1. Knowledge and skills in data analytics.
2. Core knowledge in accounting and finance.
3. Applications of data analytics in accounting and finance.
4. Systematic training and development of data analytics skills and capability in solving business problems in accounting and finance.
5. Capitalizing on opportunities offered by big data in solving accounting, finance and business problems.
Alumni describe the programme as helping them learn the latest data analytic skills, including python programming and machine learning, improve quantitative analytic skills in accounting and finance fields, develop combined knowledge in accounting, finance, data analytics and Python programming, and prepare for the job market. One alumnus noted that, with the expertise of world-class faculty and leading practitioners, the programme provided systematic training, knowledge and insights including analysis, programming, valuation, and information system.

Multiple applications are allowed for applicants seeking admission to taught postgraduate programmes. You can make another application under the same account after you have submitted one application.
You are not allowed to change your programme choice after your application has been submitted. However, you may submit another application under the same account after you have submitted one application.
The application fee for admission to taught postgraduate programmes for 2026/27 is **HK$500**, except for Master of Business Administration (MBA) and doctorate programmes of Faculty of Business. The fee is non-refundable and non-transferrable. You must settle the application fee upon submission of your online application, otherwise, your application will not be further processed.
If you want to accept another offer from PolyU after paying the tuition fees for an earlier offer, please [contact us](https://www.polyu.edu.hk/study/pg/enquiry) to transfer the fees already paid for the earlier offer to the other offer. Please remember to provide application number of both offers in your request. This arrangement only applies if both programmes lead to PolyU awards.
Students are not allowed to enrol concurrently on two full-time/sandwich programmes whether or not one of the programmes is offered by another institution. Except for programmes which do not lead to any formal award, students are not allowed to enrol concurrently on a full-time/sandwich programme and a part-time programme, or more than one part-time programmes, including those offered by another institution without any approval from the Head of your academic Department.

gre_gmat_requirements.content:
GMAT/GRE is optional. You are also welcome to submit an application without a GMAT/GRE score. A strong score may enhance your application. Generally, a score of **700 out of 800 for the GMAT**, or the GMAT equivalent in GRE is expected. program_overview.content:
Explore the NUS Master of Science in Accounting and Financial Analytics, tailored to empower graduates in navigating the evolving landscape of the accounting industry and insights to thrive in a data-driven world. With increased adoption of technology, accounting firms now face new demands to recruit employees who possess data analytics skills combined with accounting knowledge. Our programmes integrates cutting-edge technology with traditional accounting principles, providing essential skills.
NUS Business School offers the MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics degree as a trend-setting programme designed to transform you — a graduate with a first degree in any discipline — into an individual who is ready to take on the opportunities and challenges of the new digital world. An MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics graduate, equipped with a blend of accounting and data analytics skills, can either rise as a more finance-savvy executive within the same organisation or branch out into new roles not previously thought possible, such as an auditor, data analyst, equity analyst, M&A advisor, or even an entrepreneur.
**Industries our graduates work in**
Our MACC graduates are hired across a wide range of industries such as:
- Accounting & Audit Services
- Information Communications & Technology
- Banking & Financial Services
- Pharmaceutical, Healthcare, Biomedical Sciences
- Public Sector
- Distribution, Logistics & Supply Chain
- Agriculture & Commodity trade
Our MACC graduates are involved in job functions such as:
- Auditor
- Assistant Accountant
- Financial Analyst
- Fixed Income & Currencies Analyst
- M&A Advisor
- Tax Specialist
- Trust Manager
- Management Associate

curriculum.content:
**12 Months. 40 Units.** The [MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics (MACC)](https://mscacc.nus.edu.sg/) programme is delivered intensively over 12 months in a three-semester structure that includes experiential learning in the final semester. Please [click here](https://www.nus.edu.sg/registrar/calendar) for the NUS Academic Calendar.
| Semester 1 | Semester 2 | Special Term |
|---|---|---|
| Aug - Nov | Jan - Apr | May - Jul/May - Nov |
| 4 Core Courses (16 Units) **OR** 4 Core Courses (16 Units) + 1 Elective Course (4 Units) | 2 Core Courses (8 Units) + 3 Elective Courses (12 Units) **OR** 2 Core Courses (8 Units) + 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units) |
Full Course = 4 units (3 hours/week, 13 weeks duration).
Core courses:
- Semester 1: Applied Data Science & Visualisation; Corporate Valuations Models; Managerial Planning and Control; Preparing Financial Statements.
- Semester 2: Analytics & Data Management; Corporate Accounting and Reporting.
Elective courses:
- Semester 1: Taxes and Business Strategy.
- Semester 2: Bank Compliance and Risk Management; Financial Statement Analysis; Mergers and Acquisitions; Audit Analytics and Business Intelligence.
Special Term:
- Experiential Learning: Through an industry internship or applied project, students engage in experiential learning by analysing and solving problems faced by professionals in the accounting field. These internships and applied projects are primarily self-sourced.
To graduate from the NUS MSc in Accounting and Financial Analytics programme, students must complete the programme requirements and achieve a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least **3.2 out of 5.0**. To stay and complete the programme, students must maintain a GPA of at least **3.2**.

program_overview.content:
MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics at Queen's Business School is a 1 year full-time postgraduate taught programme. The course was previously known as MSc Accounting and Finance. It combines data analytics with accounting and finance, and is designed for a data-driven business environment where accounting and financial decisions are supported by accurate data analysis, predictive models, and strategic insights.
The programme provides:
- Market-leading professional exemptions from the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), Chartered Institute of Management Accounting/American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (CIMA/AICPA), and Chartered Accountants Ireland (CAI).
- Enhanced employability through hands-on engagement with profession-relevant analytics tools and technologies, in a programme developed and delivered with employers.
- A supportive student experience with high quality teaching and active engagement with contemporary research.
The MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics offers substantial exemptions from ACCA professional examinations, including Business and Technology (BT), Management Accounting (MA), Financial Accounting (FA), Corporate and Business Law (LW), Audit and Assurance (AA), Financial Management (FM), Financial Reporting (FR), and Performance Management (PM). It offers full exemption from AICPA/CIMA's Certificate and Operational levels, entering at the Management Level Case Study entry point, with further exemptions available from E2, P2 and F2. It also offers partial exemption from CAI's CAP1 level, providing exemptions from Finance and Management Accounting examinations.
The programme has been developed with employers and includes employer engagement across its modules, including real life simulations in Business Games, assessment, guest lectures and masterclasses. It also includes a Queen's Business School Employability module running throughout the programme.
The programme blends Accounting, Finance, and Analytics. Students gain understanding of financial principles and accounting frameworks while developing advanced data analysis skills. Students learn how to analyse, interpret, and leverage data to make financial forecasts, assess risks, and identify opportunities, using software such as Stata, Excel, PowerBI, Matlab, Python, R and databases such as WRDS, Thomson One Banker, DataStream and Bloomberg.
The programme offers advanced study in accounting, finance and analytics, preparing students for careers in financial institutions, management consulting, industry, the public sector, or PhD study in accounting and finance. In the third semester, students choose either a traditional Dissertation or Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project. The capstone route combines taught classes with additional professional exemptions and a final capstone project requiring data analysis and delivery of a professional-quality report and presentation, including visualisations, to a professional audience of employer representatives.
Students have access to the Queen's Business School building beside Riddel Hall, including a 250-seat tiered lecture space, a 120-seat Harvard-style theatre, a 150-seat computer laboratory, the FinTrU Trading Room, breakout study areas, a cafe, and a Business Engagement and Employability Hub. Students also have access to Bloomberg terminals in the FinTrU Trading Room.
A dedicated team of Queen's Business School Postgraduate Student Advisers offers support including English language assistance, study skills classes, academic skills development, time and project management, and guidance on referencing and citation.
People teaching on the programme include Dr Bibek Bhatta, Senior Lecturer and Programme Director, whose research spans energy policy, finance, and climate with a focus on Big Data; Dr Enayet Karim, Lecturer in Accounting, whose research focuses on textual analysis of corporate reports, auditing, risk disclosure, sustainability, and behavioural accounting; Dr Mohamed Elsayed, Senior Lecturer in Accounting, whose research interests include market-based accounting research, corporate governance, corporate disclosures, corporate failure, textual analysis, and external auditing/internal controls; Dr Xinwu He, Lecturer in Accounting, whose research interests include Sustainability Reporting, Integrated Reporting and Corporate Social Responsibility; Ms Brenda Clerkin, Senior Lecturer of Practice (Accounting), who teaches auditing, ethics, data analytics and modern technologies; Professor Danielle McConville, Professor in Accounting and Head of Department for Accounting at QBS, whose teaching specialisms include accounting information systems, contemporary technologies and management accounting; and Professor Martin Quinn, Professor in Accounting, whose teaching area is management accounting and whose research focuses on organisational and accounting change.
This Masters programme provides the basis for both profession- and research-orientated careers, as well as skills and knowledge required to progress into management careers in accounting and financial services. It opens career opportunities in banking, accounting and auditing, government, corporate finance, investment analysis and academia. Queen's is ranked third in the UK for Graduate Prospects in Accounting and Finance (Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2024). Graduates from the programme's predecessor, MSc Accounting and Finance, have secured roles with employers such as Bank of China, Deloitte, EY, KPMG, PwC, Allstate, and many others. Typical graduate roles include chartered and certified accountants, consultants, auditors and finance professionals.
Course location: Queen's Business School.

curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)**.
Course Structure: The programme offers the opportunity to pursue appropriately advanced studies in accounting, finance and analytics. In the first semester, students take four modules; in the second semester, students take an additional four modules; in the third semester, students choose either a traditional Dissertation or Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project.
- **Semester 1 (60 CATS):** International Financial Accounting and Reporting; Contemporary Research Methods and Analysis; Corporate Finance; Business Technologies and Analytics.
- **Semester 2 (60 CATS):** Management Accounting for Decision Makers; Accounting for Sustainability; Advanced Business Technologies and Analytics; Money and Banking OR International Finance (Choose one).
- **Semester 3 (60 CATS):** Route 1 – Dissertation OR Route 2 – Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project.
Core Modules:
- Dissertation – MSc Accounting Finance & Analytics (**60 credits**)
- International Financial Accounting and Reporting (**15 credits**)
- Contemporary Research Methods and Analysis (**15 credits**)
- Management Accounting for Decision Makers (**15 credits**)
- Corporate Finance (**15 credits**)
- Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project (**60 credits**)
- Business Technologies and Analytics (**15 credits**)
- Accounting for Sustainability (**15 credits**)
- Advanced Business Technologies and Analytics (**15 credits**)
Optional Modules:
- International Finance (**15 credits**)
- Money and Banking (**15 credits**)
Route 1 – Dissertation: The aim of the dissertation is to provide students with the skills needed for conducting theoretical and/or empirical research in accounting and finance.
Route 2 – Audit, Ethics and Capstone Project: This route combines taught classes with additional professional exemptions and a final capstone project. Auditing and Accountability is 25%, Ethics and Governance is 25%, and Capstone Project is 50%. The Capstone Project requires data analysis plus delivery of a professional-quality report and presentation, including visualisations, to a professional audience comprised of employer representatives.

financial_aid.content:
Four Vice Chancellor’s International Attainment Scholarships - Postgraduate Taught offer a **50% reduction on full tuition fees** to exceptionally talented international students paying international tuition fee rates who will be starting full-time postgraduate taught studies in 2026/27 on an eligible programme, including **MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics**. The 50% tuition fee reduction is paid for all years of the programme, up to a **maximum of two years**.
Applicants can only apply and be considered after they have been offered a place on their chosen eligible programme and have **FIRMLY** accepted their offer. The offer **must be confirmed** as the applicant’s FIRM choice by the scholarship deadline. Applications close **Thursday 7 May 2026 15:00 BST**.
To apply, applicants must submit a short video and complete the online application form. The video topic is: **Why you want to come and study at Queen's University Belfast and how you believe your programme of choice will benefit you in your future career aspirations.** Videos that exceed **2 minutes** will not be considered, and videos received after **15:00 BST Thursday 7 May 2026** will not be opened.
Eligibility and conditions include:
- Students must hold an offer of a full-time place at Queen’s University Belfast campus for 2026/27 on one of the specified postgraduate taught programmes, including **MSc Accounting, Finance and Analytics**.
- Students must be classified as international fee-paying students paying the full international tuition fee rate. Students paying NI ROI, EU or GB fees are not eligible.
- Students must be self-funded, i.e. paying the tuition fees for the course themselves at the international rate.
- If a student is in receipt of funding, either tuition fees or tuition fees and living costs, from an external sponsorship body such as Government, a charity or a private organisation, they will not be eligible. This excludes students in receipt of educational loans.
- Applicants may apply and/or be considered for more than one tuition fee award administered by Queen’s University Belfast, but if successful would receive **only** the highest value award.
- The Vice Chancellor’s International Attainment Scholarship - Postgraduate Taught may be combined with the Early Confirmation Award or ISC Scholarship where eligible.
- The University is unable to consider requests for increased and/or further funding; the amount of scholarship offered is non-negotiable.

program_overview.content:
The role of a traditional actuary is changing. Organisations require actuarial professionals with the analytical and statistical skills needed to analyse the large sets of data that they are being presented in today’s data-driven world. You should study this programme if you are seeking to pursue or further your actuarial professional qualification, while at the same time future-proofing your skills.
If you have prior training in actuarial science, to obtain an Associate level qualification from the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (IFoA), you will need to pass the Core Practices (CP1, CP2, CP3) examination subjects after completing the Core Principles. If you have already passed or achieved exemption from the Core Principles, you can jump straight into studying modules consistent with the Core Practices, which are at the heart of this programme. If you have not studied actuarial science before, there is also the option to include selected Core Principles in the MSc programme.
- You will be taught by faculty members who are Fellows and Independent Examiners with the IFoA.
- The actuarial training has a mixture of theory and professional practice.
- You will be taught the skills needed to become highly employable across a wide range of industries.
After successful completion of the course, students should have the skills necessary to obtain employment in a wide variety of roles in the field of general or life insurance, pension funds, healthcare, banking, regulatory bodies, or broadly in consultancy and other corporations or public organisations.
The compulsory component of the programme includes actuarial risk management, machine learning, time series for business, and a dissertation project consistent with Modelling Practice, CP2 and Communication Practice, CP3 of the IFoA syllabus. In addition, students choose from a range of modules covering both Data Science and Actuarial Science, depending on their interests and previous background.

curriculum.content:
The Actuarial Science and Data Analytics MSc is offered on campus at Queen Mary London Campuses, with a full-time September offering lasting 12 months and a part-time September offering lasting 24 months.
The programme consists of **180 credits**: **120 credits** of core, compulsory and guided elective taught modules, plus a **60-credit dissertation/project**. It consists of four compulsory taught modules, four elective modules, and a summer dissertation project. Full-time students are expected to complete eight taught modules and the project dissertation in one academic year.
- Semester A compulsory modules: MTH7013P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 1 (CP1); MTH786P [7] Machine Learning with Python.
- Semester A electives: MTH7025P [7] Survival Models (CS2); MTH7026P [7] Foundations of Mathematics and Statistics for Actuaries (CS2); MTH765P [7] Storing, Manipulating and Visualising Data; MTH739P [7] Topics in Scientific Computing.
- Semester B compulsory modules: MTH7014P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 2 (CP1); MTH783P [7] Time Series for Business (CS2).
- Semester B electives: MTH7027P [7] Financial Engineering (CM2); MTH7028P [7] Mathematical Tools for Asset and Liability Management (CM2); MTH793P [7] Advanced Machine Learning; MTH792P [7] Financial Data Analytics; MTH767P [7] Neural Networks and Deep Learning; MTH791P [7] Computational Statistics with R.
- Semester C core: Actuarial Science and Data Analytics Dissertation (CP2 and CP3), **60 credits**.
Part-time diet:
- Semester A, Year 1 compulsory: MTH7013P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 1 (CP1); MTH786P [7] Machine Learning with Python.
- Semester B, Year 1 compulsory: MTH7014P [7] Actuarial Risk Management 2 (CP1); MTH783P [7] Time Series for Business (CS2).
- Semester A, Year 2 electives, choose 2: MTH7025P [7] Survival Models (CS2); MTH7026P [7] Foundations of Mathematics and Statistics (CS2); MTH765P [7] Storing, Manipulating and Visualising Data; MTH739P [7] Topics in Scientific Computing.
- Semester B, Year 2 electives, choose 2: MTH7027P [7] Financial Engineering (CM2); MTH7028P [7] Mathematical Tools for Asset and Liability Management (CM2); MTH793P [7] Advanced Machine Learning; MTH792P [7] Financial Data Analytics; MTH767P [7] Neural Networks and Deep Learning; MTH791P [7] Computational Statistics with R.
- Semester C, Year 2 core: MTH7029P [7] Actuarial Science and Data Analytics Dissertation (CP2 and CP3), **60 credits**.
Students choose elective modules according to their academic background and interests, in consultation with the Programme Director and other staff as needed. Students with no prior accreditation and QM students with an undergraduate degree from SMS without the modules that cover CS2 and CM2 can choose the elective modules covering CS2 and CM2. If a student already has accreditations for either CS2 or CM2, or graduated from QM SMS with an undergraduate degree with modules covering CS2 or CM2, their choice of electives on this MSc will exclude CM2 or CS2 modules.
The MSc dissertation project is a summer dissertation project and a significant component of assessment. Students conduct independent research, design and execute a research study, analyze data, and present findings in a formal written dissertation. The project consists of two parts: modelling and communication, focusing on critical analysis and modelling of common actuarial data using analytical and statistical methods, and effective written communication of research and actuarial/financial solutions to actuarial and non-actuarial audiences.

program_overview.content:
The MSc in Actuarial Science and Insurance Analytics (ASI) is a full-time master’s programme designed to nurture high-calibre actuaries to meet Asia’s growing demand. Built on the highly successful [BBA in Insurance, Financial and Actuarial Analysis (IFAA)](https://ifaa.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/) and augmented by the academic and career support of the CUHK Business School, the programme helps students develop adaptable skills for actuarial or analytical roles in insurance companies, banks, financial institutions, or InsurTech start-ups. Students are also primed for associate-level professional examinations administered by the Society of Actuaries (US), enabling them to practise across the world.
The MSc in ASI is Hong Kong’s only actuarial science master’s programme. Students study under a syllabus approved by the International Actuarial Association and gain regional insights into the insurance markets of Hong Kong and mainland China. They learn from locally and internationally qualified teachers and have opportunities to partake in fellowships in Hong Kong (with the Hong Kong Actuarial Society), Singapore, the US and the UK. The programme trains students to standards stipulated by leading actuarial bodies and can lead to globally recognised professional qualifications upon graduation.
MSc in ASI is a **Center of Actuarial Excellence (CAE)** designated by the **Society of Actuaries (SOA), USA**. The programme offers rigorous academic training for students aspiring to enter the actuarial profession and is specifically designed to prepare graduates for early actuarial professional examinations. The curriculum is fully aligned with SOA standards and covers associate level examination content. The programme has been awarded **University Earned Credit (UEC)** status by the SOA for **five preliminary examinations—FM, FAM, SRM, ALTAM, and ASTAM**—enabling students to earn internationally recognised credits and enter the profession well prepared upon graduation.
As Asia transforms into the world’s fastest-growing insurance market, ASI graduates will find prospects in diverse industries. In Hong Kong, actuaries have been identified by the government as a category of professionals urgently needed by the city, with the profession appearing on the Talent List of Hong Kong. In the Greater Bay Area (GBA), actuaries versed in international insurance practices and actuarial leadership roles are also highly sought after.
**Duration:** Full-time: 1 year
**Programme commencement:** September

curriculum.content:
The MSc in Actuarial Science and Insurance Analytics (MScASI) is a **full-time** Master’s programme. Duration: **Full-time: 1 year**. The medium of instruction is **English**.
The MScASI curriculum is tailored for fresh graduates and junior professionals who want to obtain a solid foundation in insurance knowledge, actuarial science, mathematics and statistics skills. The curriculum is aligned to standards of professional bodies and covers the associate-level exam materials administered by the Society of Actuaries (SOA). The programme has received University-Earned Credit status from the SOA for five preliminary exams – FM, FAM, SRM, ALTAM and ASTAM.
To graduate from the programme, students need to complete **36 units of coursework**, including **10 core courses and 2 elective courses**. Core and elective courses are subject to change.
Full-time Programme (1 Year):
- Term 1 Sep-Dec: 4 core courses; 1 elective course
- Term 2 Dec-Mar: 3 core courses; 1-2 elective course(s)
- Term 3 Mar-Jun: 3 core courses; 1-2 elective course(s)
Core Courses (Total 10 Courses / 30 Units):
- [FINA6601 Economics for Actuaries](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-0)
- [FINA6602 Accounting and Corporate Finance](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-1)
- [FINA6603 Probability with Applications in Finance and Insurance](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-2)
- [FINA6604 Financial Mathematics for Actuaries](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-3)
- [FINA6605 Statistics for Risk Modelling](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-4)
- [FINA6606 Actuarial Mathematics for Long-Term Insurance](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-5)
- [FINA6607 Actuarial Mathematics for Short-Term Insurance](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-6)
- [FINA6608 Derivatives for Actuaries](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-7)
- [FINA6609 Data Science for Insurance Analytics](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-8)
- [FINA6610 Statistical Modelling for Insurance Analytics](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-9)
Elective Courses (Total 6 Units):
- [FINA6611 Insurance and Risk Management](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-2-0)
- [FINA6612 Life Insurance](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-2-1)
- [FINA6613 Commercial Property and Liability Insurance](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-2-2)
- [FINA6616 Advanced Life Contingencies](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-2-3)
- [FINA6617 Loss and Survival Models](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscasi/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-2-4)
Students may take up to **3 credits’ worth of courses** offered by the MAcc, MBA and other MSc programmes within CUHK Business School, subject to the approval of the programme directors.
Course Exemption: Exemptions may be granted for up to **2 core courses**. If a student is exempted from any of the selected core courses, they will be required to replace the units with other elective courses. An exemption may be granted if a student has completed an equivalent undergraduate-level course and obtained a grade of “B” or above, or if they have passed relevant professional exams from the SOA or IFoA.
Graduation Requirements: To graduate, students must complete the prescribed coursework and achieve a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least **2.50**. Students who receive a grade of D+ or below in a course must repeat it or take an approved substitute course.
Corresponding ASI courses for ASA requirements:
| ASA requirement | Corresponding ASI course(s) |
| --- | --- |
| VEE Micro + Macro Economics | FINA6601 |
| VEE Accounting and Finance | FINA6602 |
| VEE Mathematical Statistics | FINA6605 |
| Exam FM: Financial Mathematics | FINA6604 |
| Exam FAM-L: Fundamentals of Actuarial Math (Long-term) | FINA6606 |
| Exam FAM-S: Fundamentals of Actuarial Math (Short-term) | FINA6607 |
| Exam SRM: Statistics for Risk Modelling | FINA6609 FINA6610 |
| Exam ALTAM: Advanced Long-term Actuarial Math | FINA6608 FINA6616 |
| Exam ASTAM: Advanced Short-term Actuarial Math | FINA6617 |
| Exam P: Probability | FINA6603 |
| Exam PA: Predictive Analytics | FINA6609 FINA6610 |
University-Earned Credit (UEC) Program: The MSc in ASI programme is part of the UEC program approved by the SoA. Students can use university exemptions to earn credits for the following exams:
| SoA exam | ASI course(s) |
| --- | --- |
| Exam FM | FINA6604 |
| Exam FAM | FINA6606 + FINA6607 |
| Exam SRM | FINA6609 + FINA6610 |
| Exam ALTAM | FINA6616 + FINA6608 |
| Exam ASTAM | FINA6617 |
This is contingent upon achieving a score of **60 or above** in the corresponding course(s). Exam P and Exam PA cannot be exempted using university courses. For the three areas covered by Validation by Educational Experience, students can earn VEE credits by completing FINA 6601, 6602, and 6605, provided they achieve a grade of **B- or higher** in these courses.

program_overview.content:
Build a career at the intersection of finance, risk, and sustainability with the MSc Actuarial and Risk Analytics programme. Blending actuarial science, risk management, and sustainability insights, this interdisciplinary programme equips you to succeed in a world defined by rapid change and complex challenges. You will gain the analytical expertise and strategic mindset needed to manage emerging risks, respond to environmental shifts, and drive responsible decision-making across industries. The programme’s practical, hands-on approach ensures you apply what you learn to real business scenarios, giving you the skills and experience to launch a career in actuarial science, risk consulting, insurance, finance, and beyond.
MARA is offered as a full-time, one-year programme. The programme is delivered entirely in English on the vibrant main campus at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore.
The demand for actuarial and risk analytics professionals continues to grow, as organisations seek experts who can assess uncertainty, manage financial risks, and support data-driven decision-making. Employers value graduates who are proficient in statistical modelling, risk assessment, and the application of quantitative insights across sectors such as insurance, finance, consulting and beyond.
The programme also offers an optional six-month internship, which can be undertaken as part of the curriculum. This provides participants with valuable, hands-on exposure to real-world risk challenges, strengthening their career prospects as actuaries, risk analysts, and consultants, while preparing them for professional actuarial accreditation.

curriculum.content:
MARA is offered as a full-time, one-year programme. The programme is delivered entirely in English on the vibrant main campus at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore.
#### Core Modules
- [**Database and Programming for Actuarial and Risk Analyst**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C021_Col00): This module aims to equip students with a comprehensive understanding of database management and programming concepts relevant to actuarial science and risk management.
- [**Enterprise Risk Management**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C015_Col00): This module offers a comprehensive introduction to enterprise risk management, harmonizing quantitative and qualitative approaches.
- [**Financial Markets and Products**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C019_Col00): This module introduces the financial markets as well as basic financial products with a focus on derivatives.
- [**Foundation of Quantitative Risk Management**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C022_Col00): This module introduces necessary analytical tools for risk management.
- [**Modern Risk and Actuarial Theory**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C023_Col00): This module introduces fundamental principles of risk management and actuarial theory.
- [**Principles of Climate Risk and Carbon Markets**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C020_Col00): This module brings a general introduction to Climate Risk and Carbon markets.
#### Elective Modules
- [**Advanced Quantitative Risk Management**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C014_Col00): This module introduces diverse quantitative disciplines essential for market, credit, and operational risk modeling.
- [**Credit Risk Analytics**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C016_Col00): This module provides introduction to credit risk, the reasons it arises, and describes quantitative measurements and factors of credit risk.
- [**Financial Mathematics**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C018_Col00): This module covers the basics of financial valuation, including the most important financial concept, the time value of money.
- [**Portfolio Risk Analytics**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C013_Col00): This module covers topics of different analytical methods for portfolio management.
- [**Quantitative Climate Risk Analytics**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C017_Col00): This module will introduce state-of-the-art analytical tools for measuring and modelling climate-related risks.
- [**Sustainable Finance and Risk Management**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-actuarial-risk-analytics/programme-overview#Content_C012_Col00): This module introduces how to incorporate general risk management techniques into sustainable risk management.
The programme also offers an optional six-month internship, which can be undertaken as part of the curriculum.

financial_aid.content:
No separate application for scholarships is required – simply tick on the box relating to the scholarship you are applying for in the online application form and complete the essay for scholarship consideration.
#### **MSc Actuarial And Risk Analytics Merit Scholarship**
NBS offers partial scholarships to stellar candidates, on a competitive basis. Only applicants who have been offered a place in MSc in Actuarial and Risk Analytics programme are eligible for the scholarships. The partial scholarship will go towards off-setting the fees of the programme, and does not cover the living expenses in Singapore, travel, and accommodation.​
#### ​Eligibility Criteria
- Possess excellent academic credentials
- Performed well in the admission interview
- Granted admission to the MSc in Actuarial and Risk Analytics programme
#### How to Apply
- Please complete the scholarship part of the online application, including the scholarship essay.
- Applicants who wish to be considered for the scholarship should ensure that their scholarship applications are completed (including submission of all supporting documents) by [round 1 deadline](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/index).
- Scholarship application will only be considered when it is submitted together with the application.
#### **ASEAN Development Scholarship**
This partial scholarship is awarded to nationals of ASEAN member countries (excluding Singapore) as part of NBS’s effort to accelerate economic and social progress in the Member States of ASEAN. Recipients may receive up to 90% funding towards their tuition fees.
#### Eligibility Criteria
Scholarship applicants must possess strong academic records, demonstrated leadership qualities and potential, and for working professionals, a strong career progression.
#### How to Apply
A complete online application including the scholarship section, and required supporting documents must be submitted by the [first round](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/index) application deadline to be eligible for the ASEAN Development Scholarship.
#### Diversity Scholarship
The Diversity Scholarship aims to cultivate a vibrant community by supporting individuals who bring unique perspectives and experiences to the programme and the NBS community. Diversity encompasses a broad range of dimensions, including but not limited to ethnicity, gender, and cultural heritage. Scholarship applicants are encouraged to define diversity in a way that reflects their personal journeys and experiences. Each scholarship awarded covers 40% of the tuition fees.
#### Eligibility Criteria
Applicants must showcase a distinctive background, demonstrate how it enhances the broader understanding of diversity, and possess a track record of success in initiatives or activities that promote diversity within their communities or workplaces.
#### How to Apply
A complete online application including the scholarship section, and required supporting documents must be submitted by the [first round of application deadline](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/index) to be eligible for the Diversity Scholarship.
#### **NTU Alumni Grant**
NTU alumni who have completed a bachelor’s or post-graduate degree at NTU are eligible for an alumni grant of 10% of the tuition fees. The subsidy can only be used to offset the tuition fee and cannot be used to offset other costs such as student service fees or miscellaneous fees.​
#### **Singapore Citizen & Singapore PR Grant**
Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents are eligible for a grant of S$5,000, with those awarded financial aid getting up to S$10,000. The subsidy can only be used to offset the tuition fee and cannot be used to offset other costs such as student service fees or miscellaneous fees. To be eligible for financial aid, applicants must have a monthly PCI of less than S$2,500 or a gross household income of less than S$10,000. Financial aid is subject to a successful application.

This condition will be clearly outlined in the offer letter, stating: 'The offer of admission is on condition that you obtain your Bachelor's degree with a ________ from ___________ , ___________ "
- **International Student with International Qualification**: Official degree certificate and final transcript; Digital copy of Student Pass (Full-time students) / Valid immigration pass (For Part-time students only); Degree verification report (English) from NTU approved credential verification agency **within one month of your term start date**; Latest Passport (If not yet submitted).
- **International Student with Local (Singapore) Qualification**: Official degree certificate and final transcript; Digital copy of Student Pass (Full-time students) / Valid immigration pass (For Part-time students only); Degree verification screen capture from respective local university online degree verification portal; Latest Passport (If not yet submitted).

- **Singapore Citizen / Singapore Permanent Resident with Local (Singapore) Qualification**: Official degree certificate and final transcript; Degree verification screen capture from respective local university online degree verification portal.
For **Conditional Offer** (i.e. subject to attaining a Bachelor/ Masters’ degree), you are required to upload your **Bachelor/ Masters’ degree scrolls and Official Transcript** (Original and English Language translated). If you are unable to upload your Bachelor/ Masters’ degree scroll during verification period, you are to upload **a letter of completion** from your university stating that you have completed and attained Bachelor/ Masters’ degree. **Do not complete e-verification if you do not meet the condition stated on the offer letter.** Kindly contact your school for assistance.

application_materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together. Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal.
Your application must include:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume: include an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa, for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
- If you entered your current degree programme later than year 1, include separate details of the qualification used to gain entry into that later year of your degree, including any transcripts and certificates for that qualification.
If you have them, include:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard, but could strengthen your application in circumstances such as explaining a gap in your education or showing relevance if your education/degree subject is not directly relevant to the programme. The personal statement should be **no more than one side of A4** and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
Documents which are not required:
- References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases a reference may be required to help make a decision.
Country-specific documentation:
- Applicants with Chinese degrees: provide evidence of your current/final overall weighted percentage (%).
- Applicants with Indian degrees: include a copy of your bachelor’s degree certificate; a copy of your consolidated mark sheet; a copy of your semester mark sheets; a copy of your University marking scheme; and official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%). If you have not completed your degree, provide the bottom three items.
- Applicants with Canadian degrees: provide details of the grading system used on your transcript, including the percentage pass mark for your degree. If your degree was taught in English, include official evidence of this.
