program_overview.content:
Start date September 2026. Delivery type On campus. Duration 12 Months (Full time).
From science to marketing, engineering to medicine, big data has become crucial to a wide range of industries. Many organisations are keen to employ qualified experts in computing who have a particular focus in data. The Advanced Computer Science (Data Analytics) MSc will equip you with specialist knowledge in this field and allow you to explore a range of advanced topics in computer science. You’ll gain a foundation in topics like data science, as well as the basics of machine learning and knowledge representation, and can broaden your approach with topics like cloud computing.
Studying in the [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing) gives you access to specialist facilities, whilst being taught by academics who are experts in their fields. The School has internationally excellent research and long-established links in industry and with the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) (LIDA), which is at the forefront of big data research. The University is also partnered with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence.
In the first half of the year, you’ll study core modules which lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of key topics of data science, cloud computing and machine learning. From there you’ll tailor your studies through optional modules on diverse topics such as deep learning, knowledge representation, blockchain technologies, data mining and text analytics. In the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll work on a research project as an integral part of one of the School’s active research groups, focusing on a specialist topic in computer science and selecting appropriate research methods. A proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.
The course gives you the chance to build industry experience by conducting an individual project focused on a real-world topic of your choice, developing professional skills in research and critical thinking. You’ll access industry-standard specialist facilities including a state-of-the-art cloud computing lab, a large High Performance Computing (HPC) resource, robotics labs, a state-of-the-art computing cluster with access to Azure services and GPU computing, high-performance graphics workstations, dedicated Linux laboratories with a combined capacity of an average of 150 machines, and facilities and teaching spaces in the Sir William Henry Bragg building.
The programme team includes expert academics, from lecturers through to professors, specialising in a wide range of computing topics. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers. The School’s research feeds directly into teaching, and you’ll have regular contact with staff through lectures, seminars, tutorials, small group work and project meetings. Independent study is also important to the programme, as you develop your problem-solving and research skills as well as your subject knowledge.
You’ll be assessed using a range of techniques which may include case studies, technical reports, group work, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessment methods.
Computing is an essential component of nearly every daily activity, from the collection and processing of information in business, through to smart systems embedded in devices, image processing in medical diagnosis and the middleware that underpins distributed technologies like cloud computing and the semantic web. This programme will give you the practical skills to enter many areas of applied computing, working as application developers, system designers and evaluators. Links between the taught modules and research provide students with added strengths in artificial intelligence, intelligent systems, distributed systems, and the analysis of complex data. Graduates will be well-prepared for a range of careers, as well as further research at PhD level.
The University of Leeds is in the top 5 most targeted universities in the UK by graduate recruiters, according to [High Fliers’ The Graduate Market in 2024 report](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/). Job positions and organisations previous advanced computer science graduates have secured include Engineer at Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory, Senior Software Engineer at Funding Circle, Technical Developer at Reading Room, Head of Audience Development at Al Jazeera Media Network, Systems Engineer at Systematic, Software Engineer at THG, Programmer at Alibaba, and PhD candidate at Monash University.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. The work experience is formally integrated into your degree, enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
In the first half of the year, you'll study core modules which will lay the foundations of the programme by giving you an understanding of the key topics of data science, cloud computing and machine learning. From there you’ll have the chance to tailor your studies to suit your own preferences. You’ll choose from a wide range of optional modules on diverse topics such as deep learning, knowledge representation, blockchain technologies, data mining and text analytics. In the second half of the year, over the summer months, you’ll also work on your research project.
The list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time.
Compulsory modules:
- **Data Science – 15 credits**: The aim of the module is for you to understand methods of analysis that allow people to gain insights from complex data.
- **Cloud Computing Systems – 15 credits**: The module aims to develop a practical understanding of methods, techniques and architectures needed to build big data systems, so that knowledge can be extracted from large, diverse data sets.
- **Machine learning - 15 credits**: This module covers topics selected from: Decision trees, Bayesian networks, instance-based learning, kernel machines, clustering, reinforcement learning inductive logic programming, artificial neural networks, deep learning.
- **MSc Project – 60 credits**: You’ll undertake a research project during the summer months. The professional project allows you to apply what you’ve learned to a piece of research focusing on a real-world problem. Recent projects include Text mining of e-health patient records; Java-based visualisation on ultra-high resolution displays; Data mining of sports performance data. A proportion of projects are formally linked to industry and can include spending time at the collaborator’s site over the summer.
Optional modules listed are indicative of typical options:
- **Blockchain Technologies – 15 credits**
- **Knowledge Representation and Reasoning – 15 credits**
- **Deep Learning – 15 credits**
- **Algorithms – 15 credits**
- **Programming for Data Science – 15 credits**
- **Data Mining and Text Analytics – 15 credits**
- **Advanced Software Engineering – 15 credits**
- **Scientific Computation – 15 credits**
- **Graph Theory: Structure and Algorithms – 15 credits**
As part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0). [For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Advanced Computer Science (Data Analytics) MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-ACS%2FD-FT).
You’ll be assessed using a range of techniques which may include case studies, technical reports, group work, presentations, in-class tests, assignments and exams. Optional modules may also use alternative assessment methods.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. This work experience is formally integrated into your degree, enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

program_overview.content:
[**The Master of Science (MSc) in Analytics**](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/spms/about-us/mathematics/grad/msc-in-analytics) programme is an interdisciplinary post-graduate programme suitable for professionals seeking to leverage business analytics in their respective fields, as well as recent college graduates pursuing a career in the data science industry. Analytics is the science of finding patterns in data to aid decision making. It is an interdisciplinary field rooted in applied mathematics, with a wide range of applications in business, finance, and industry. The MSc in Analytics programme provides the skills and knowledge for applying cutting-edge data science techniques to business challenges in the modern economy. [MSc in Analytics Brochure](https://wcms-prod-admin.ntu.edu.sg/docs/librariesprovider123/graduate/msc-programmes/ntu-spms-brochure_msa_2026.pdf?sfvrsn=32df954e_3/%20NTU-SPMS-Brochure_MSA_2026)
The MSc in Analytics programme is an intensive **one-year full-time or two-year part-time** programme by coursework taught in three trimesters. Upon completion of the study, students are awarded a Master of Science (MSc) in Analytics degree. The programme consists of a total of **30 Academic Units (AU)**, with **18 AU** stemming from core courses and **12 AU** from elective courses. The curriculum includes core courses, elective courses, **1 Analytics Practicum Course (self-sourced internship)**, ad-hoc seminars on analytics software tools, and ad-hoc seminars from industry professionals.
The curriculum strongly emphasises the application of analytics on real-world data and includes one practicum, elective course of 6 AU. Full-time students had internships in organisations for the practicum course, including APL, BreadTalk, Charles & Keith, DHL, Experian, Grab, UPS, Shopee, Lazada, DBS, UOB, Johnson & Johnson, JR Group, Lenovo, MSD, PSA, and PwC.
On average, full-time students take **4-5** classes a week, and part-time students take **2-3** classes a week. For academic enquiries, email the Programme Director, Dr Lim Kay Jin ([limkj@ntu.edu.sg](mailto:limkj@ntu.edu.sg)).

program_overview.content:
Newly introduced in 2026, the Master of Science in Applied Materials Analytics expands NTU MSE’s postgraduate coursework offerings in response to **growing industry demand for expertise in materials characterisation, diagnostics, and failure analysis**. The programme focuses specifically on the **analytical techniques and investigative approaches** used to understand how materials behave under real operating conditions, including applications across semiconductor devices, aerospace systems, sustainable infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing.
The MSc in Applied Materials Analytics is designed for those who wish to develop advanced capabilities in materials characterisation, diagnostics, and failure investigation. The programme is suitable for materials, mechanical, civil, chemical, aerospace, and electrical engineers; professionals in semiconductor manufacturing, aerospace, marine engineering, construction, and advanced manufacturing; engineers and researchers in analytical laboratories or R&D environments; and graduates with a background in materials science, engineering, physics, or related disciplines.
By combining advanced analytical techniques with case-based learning in failure analysis, the programme equips students with practical skills directly relevant to industrial and research environments. Graduates are prepared for roles requiring expertise in materials diagnostics, reliability, and analytical investigation, including Materials Analyst / Materials Scientist, Failure Analysis Engineer, Characterisation Scientist / Engineer, Quality Assurance / Quality Control Engineer, Process Engineer, Laboratory / Analytical Scientist, Research and Development (R&D) Engineer, and Technical Specialist / Applications Engineer. These roles are in demand across semiconductors, aerospace, energy, marine engineering, infrastructure, biomedical technology, and advanced manufacturing. Graduates may also pursue research careers in industrial laboratories, government agencies, or doctoral programmes.
Students learn from a Materials Science and Engineering faculty whose expertise and research provide insights and mentorship for careers in the field. The programme offers a mixed-learning approach that combines asynchronous online learning with conventional face-to-face teaching.
Programme structure: MSc students are enrolled on the coursework study option by default, requiring 30 AUs, made up of 10 AUs of core courses and 20 AUs of elective courses. Students may opt in to a coursework and dissertation route requiring 24 AUs of coursework, made up of 10 AUs core courses and 14 AUs elective courses, plus a 6 AU dissertation. Total graduation requirement is 30 AUs and a minimum CGPA of 2.5.

| Full Time Study | 1 year (2 semesters) | 3 years (6 semesters) |
| Part Time Study | 2 years (4 semesters) | 4 years (8 semesters) |

program_overview.content:
With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) and big data techniques in recent years, there have been a huge number of innovative applications in various domains. AI and business analytics are an inter-disciplinary sub-field that integrates knowledge and skills from both with critical and out-of-the-box thinking to process business datasets through the use of AI techniques. The MScAIBA Programme emphasizes a balanced coverage of subjects in AI and business analytics, as well as focuses on business data analytics by using AI techniques to solve practical business problems.
- It provides students with knowledge that spans the core disciplines of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and business analytics, and integrates various disciplines to allow students to better understand all aspects of AI and business analytics and how they are used in the real world.
- It takes into consideration more practical business applications and frontier technologies by combining AI and business analytics with blockchain, marketing, healthcare, geographical information systems, and optimisation. Thereby enhancing the competitiveness of graduates in the job market.
- It serves a wide range of professionals, decision and policy makers who need to process and analyse big data. It is also ideal for healthcare and public utility sector practitioners who understand the importance of AI and business analytics in enhancing the quality of society and effectiveness of operations.
- It develops students’ analytical and critical thinking, as well as their problem-solving skills, which enables graduates to pursue careers as business analysts, data analysts, data scientists, and AI consultants/experts across various industries.

academic_requirements.content:
Entrance to the MSc Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics programme is highly competitive. Applicants can increase their chances of a successful application by exceeding the minimum eligibility criteria through academic grades above standard requirements and/or relevant work experience.
- Applicants need a **UK first-class** or **2:1 honours degree** in one of the following subjects, or an equivalent overseas qualification:
- An undergraduate degree in management science, operational research, statistics, econometrics, mathematics, physics, computer science, or engineering.
- A degree in business, management, finance, or economics that has covered quantitative content.
- Candidates with a very good Honours degree in other areas of study or with relevant work experience will be considered on an individual basis.
- Relevant work experience is not required but may increase chances of acceptance.
- Preference will be given to those with grades above the minimum requirements due to strong competition for places on this programme.
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as their studies will be completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date.
- For overseas students, the minimum academic requirement is a **UK 2:1 honours degree in a related subject** or an **equivalent international qualification**.
- China-specific requirement: **85%+; Band A from the [Priority list of Chinese universities](https://www.ed.ac.uk/sites/default/files/atoms/files/priority_list_of_chinese_universities.pdf)**.
- China-specific requirement from International Qualifications: a **minimum of 85%** awarded by a Chinese university on the Priority List. This degree programme is **Band A**.
- Edinburgh China postgraduate entry guidance for Band A: **a minimum of 85% awarded by a university on the Priority List**.
- The ranking of the university at which applicants studied is considered when determining whether or not a degree is equivalent to a first or upper second-class honours degree in the UK.
- If a degree is not of the required standard and the applicant does not have highly relevant work or other experience, the application will normally be rejected.
- Meeting the degree requirement does not ensure acceptance; a higher standard may be needed for an application to be competitive for admission or funding.
- A conditional offer can be made if an applicant is waiting for a final degree result.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
Regardless of your nationality or country of residence, you must demonstrate a level of English language competency which will enable you to succeed in your studies.
English language qualifications accepted at the grades specified:
- [IELTS Academic](https://www.ielts.org/): **total 7.0 with at least 6.0 in each component**. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted to meet English language requirements.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) before 21 January 2026: **total 100 with at least 20 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) from 21 January 2026: **total 5.0 with at least 4.0 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [C1 Advanced](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/advanced/) (formerly CAE) / [C2 Proficiency](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/proficiency/) (formerly CPE): **total 185 with at least 169 in each component**.
- [Trinity ISE](https://www.trinitycollege.com/site/?id=3287): **ISE III with passes in all four components**.
- [Oxford ELLT](https://oxfordellt.com/) (Global and Digital): **8 overall with at least 6 in each component**.
Unless you are a national of a majority English speaking country, your English language qualification must be no more than **three and a half years old** from the start of the month in which the programme begins. If using IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, Trinity ISE, or Oxford ELLT, it must be no more than **two years old** on the first of the month in which the programme begins, regardless of nationality.
Degrees taught and assessed in English are also accepted if the undergraduate or postgraduate degree was taught and assessed in a majority English speaking country, as defined by UK Visas and Immigration: [UKVI list of majority English speaking countries](https://www.gov.uk/tier-4-general-visa/knowledge-of-english). A degree taught and assessed in English from a university on the list of approved universities in non-majority English speaking countries is also accepted: [Approved universities in non-majority English speaking countries](https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/postgraduate/applying/your-application/entry-requirements/english-requirements/approved-universities). If you are not a national of a majority English speaking country, then your degree must be no more than **five years old** at the start of the month in which your programme begins.
If you already have an English language certificate then you can include this with your application. If you have not yet taken a test, the application will still be processed and you will be able to upload your results when you receive them. A conditional offer may be given if you do not yet meet the minimum English requirement, but you must provide evidence that you have reached the minimum English requirement before an unconditional offer can be provided.
Optional pre-sessional English courses are available. English for Business Masters is for students accepted by the School who have already met the English requirement and want to improve English skills. General English for Academic Purposes is for international students who need to improve their English language level before commencing study; at the end of the course, students undertake an assessment which can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September. [English for Academic Purposes summer courses](https://www.ed.ac.uk/english-language-teaching/pre-sessional-english/summer-eap-courses)

program_overview.content:
The financial industry is experiencing rapid innovation. From digital banking, it has progressed towards biometric security, the rise of fintech platforms, and the streamlining of banking processes with the use of AI, to name a few. Advancements in the field of analytics are enhancing the ability of banks to predict and manage various kinds of financial risks.
The MSc Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics programme provides an understanding of the role of banking in the economy, the risk factors, and how to manage these. By meeting the demands of specialist departments within financial firms, this programmes differs from others in the fields of finance or analytics.
- Programme structure: Find an overview of the typical structure of the MSc Banking Innovation and Risk Analytics programme, including information on compulsory and option courses. [View programme structure](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/banking-risk/overview/programme-structure)
- Learning outcomes: You will gain practical skills in understanding financial statements, predicting risks associated with potential borrowers, and estimating predictive risks using software. [View the learning outcomes](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/banking-risk/overview/learning-outcomes)
- Industry opportunities: Participate in industry treks, group consultancy, client sourced dissertations, and benefit from speaking to a variety of industry professionals. [Engagement with industry](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/banking-risk/overview/industry-opportunities)

#### Do not submit more than five applications
We recommend that you submit only one or two applications in order to have the best possible chance of receiving a positive outcome. deferral_admission_policy.content:
Each year we have limited capacity for deferred offers. All deferral requests will be considered on an individual basis.
- The deadline for submitting a deferral request is **31 August**.
- If your deferral request is unsuccessful, you are encouraged to take up your place for entry this year, or to withdraw and submit a new application for entry next year when applications open. There is no guarantee that a new application will be successful.
- If you defer your place, you may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date. The new SELT will be required by **31 October** of your original entry year.
- The deposit must be paid before a deferral is agreed. This should be done within **28 days** of receiving the original offer. The deposit is non-refundable.
- We defer unconditional offers only. It is possible to defer an offer only once.

application_materials.content:
Write your application, including references, CV, transcripts, and personal statement.
- **References:** You must supply **one academic or professional reference**; your referee can know you on either an academic or professional level. Once you have paid your application fee, Warwick will email your referee inviting them to submit a reference online. It is your responsibility to ensure that your reference has been submitted. References submitted by email will not be acceptable.
- **CV:** You are required to submit a CV as part of the application process. Your CV should contain your educational background, employment history, any volunteering experience, and any extra-curricular activities, hobbies and interests.
- **Transcripts:** You must upload a final or interim transcript for your undergraduate bachelor’s degree. Your transcripts must show the modules you have taken for each year, including the first year, and the marks you have gained to date. Please also upload a list of your final year modules as a **PDF or Word document**. If your transcript is not printed in English, please also include a translation.
- **Personal Statement:** Key areas to cover include: why you have selected this course and your motivating factors; how you see the course benefitting your career plans; and what you will contribute to your cohort. Warwick says this is your opportunity to share achievements and ambitions and advises avoiding repeating information from your CV.
- **Supporting documents:** Following submission of your application and payment of your application fee, the Postgraduate Admissions team will send an email with a link to access the upload facility. Documents cannot be submitted via email and applicants should not post hard copy documents at this time. If made an offer, applicants will then be asked to supply original documents.
- **Translations:** All transcripts from higher learning must be officially translated. A valid translation must have an original stamp from an official translation company and be attached to the original document.
- You only need to upload one set of supplementary documents with each application, but Warwick recommends tailoring each Personal Statement specifically for every course applied to.

interview_requirements.content: At WBS, there are **no interviews for MSc courses**. Instead, all decisions are made based on the application you submit. Your undergraduate transcript will be reviewed in depth along with your CV and personal statement.

academic_requirements.content:
- You must have, or be expecting to obtain, **at least a 2.1 degree at Undergraduate level from a UK university or overseas equivalent**.
- The course requires **strong numeracy and IT statistical ability**.
- Applications are considered from a wide range of degrees such as **economics, business, engineering, psychology, geography, sociology, and politics**.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
If English is not your first language, you must meet a minimum overall standard in a recognised test of English. You must show a good balance across all sections of the test and it must have been taken within **two years of starting the course**. Certificates are required as evidence.
- **IELTS (Academic, UKVI or Online): 7.0 overall**, with a maximum of two language components at lowest level 6.0/6.5 and the rest at 7.0 or above. One skill retakes are not accepted; the test must be taken in one sitting.
- **CPE: 190 overall**; 2 x 170, 2 x 190.
- **CAE: 190 overall**; 2 x 170, 2 x 190.
- **TOEFL: 5**; minimum language components L4.5, R4.5, W4.5, S4.5.
- **Trinity ISE III:** Merit, Merit, Pass, Pass in four components.
- **Trinity ISE IV:** Pass, Pass, Pass, Pass in four components.
- **Duolingo: Band B: 130**, with at least 110 in two components and 130 in two components.
If you are a non-native speaker of English but have been educated entirely in English for your degree, and completed this within the last two years, this may satisfy the University of your language skills. [See more details on English Language Requirements on the University's website](http://www2.warwick.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/apply/english/).

program_overview.content:
**MSc Business Analytics & Artificial Intelligence** teaches students how to gain insights from large data sets using Artificial Intelligence (AI), statistical methods, optimisation and machine learning, and apply them to business challenges. The course covers cutting-edge and industry-standard analytical techniques, including visualisation in Tableau, machine learning, statistics and optimisation, and provides cross-disciplinary training in business models, quantitative methods and data science.
- Ranked 3rd in the UK and 17th in the world in the QS University Rankings 2025.
- MSc Business Analytics, now MSc Business Analytics & Artificial Intelligence, is ranked 3rd in the UK and 13th in the world in the QS Business Masters Rankings 2026.
- Students learn how to translate a variety of data into business value through cutting-edge techniques, cover analytics modules from data engineering to applied statistics aligned with industry trends, and continue developing programming skills in SQL, R, and Python, as well as the use of AI tools.
- Students can conduct an [external consultancy project](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/business-analytics-artificial-intelligence/structure/?tab=dissertation-or-business-in-practice) with a real client, undertake [individual academic research](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/business-analytics-artificial-intelligence/structure/?tab=dissertation-or-business-in-practice), or put their learnings into practice with the applied [Business in Practice](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/business-analytics-artificial-intelligence/structure/?tab=dissertation-or-business-in-practice) module.
- Duration: 1 year; Location: Warwick Campus; Format: Full-time; Start Date: September 2026.
- Formerly MSc Business Analytics, this course has been reviewed and relaunched for 2026 entry.
- The dedicated [MSc CareersPlus & Employer Relations](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/careers/) team provides personalised support throughout the journey. Graduates have recently secured roles including AI Analyst, Data Consultant and Market Strategy Lead at employers such as Accenture, EY and KPMG.
- The graduating Class of 2025 averaged a salary of $71,541 (converted for PPP) within six months of completion. This data reflects those that participated in the [MSc Employment Report](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/763598704/) survey, which averaged a 72% response rate overall; this cohort studied the 'MSc Business Analytics' version of this course, which has since been reviewed and relaunched for 2026 entry.

curriculum.content:
Over three terms you will complete four core modules, alongside four modules from one of the new specialisms: Artificial Intelligence; Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics; Management Analytics; and Marketing Analytics & Technology. Assessment will vary between group presentations, peer assessments, individual assignments and examinations.
Your studies will be completed by one of the following routes:
- One elective + Research Paper
- Two electives + Self-sourced Internship
- Two electives + Business in Practice
- Two electives + Analytics Portfolio.
You will develop your programming skills in Python, SQL and R, and gain guidance in obtaining optional certifications such as Associate Certified Analytics Professional. You will be given access to a wide-range of additional analytics and data science online courses, and gain exposure to industry-standard software such as Tableau, PyTorch and Large Language Models.
Core modules include:
- Analytics Engineering, AI and Visualisation: theoretical and practical exposure to modern data workflows in business analytics and AI, covering data extraction through to product deployment in the form of business dashboards.
- Analytics in Practice: how to structure and conduct an end-to-end analytics/data science project including data engineering, modelling using machine learning methods, visualisation and communicating results to the end-user.
- Applied Analytics Projects: an opportunity to apply the techniques and methodologies taught on the course to real-world settings, including project management for analytical interventions, ethics and risks in analytics projects, and structuring analytics in the business model of the organisation.
- Business Statistics: a foundation in the analysis and presentation of quantitative data and the basic elements of statistics that are the foundation of analytics and business analysis.
Specialisms:
- Artificial Intelligence: Advanced Data Analysis; Algorithms and Optimisation in Software Applications; Deep Learning and AI Engineering; Generative AI and AI Applications.
- Management Analytics: Developing an Analytics Capability; Financial Analytics; Prescriptive Analytics and Optimisation; Supply Chain Analytics.
- Marketing Analytics and Technology: Algorithms and Optimisation in Software Applications; Developing an Analytics Capability; Generative AI and AI Applications; Marketing and Digital Analytics.
- Predictive and Prescriptive Analytics: Advanced Analytics: Models and Applications; Advanced Data Analysis; Deep Learning and AI Engineering; Prescriptive Analytics and Optimisation.
Indicative optional modules may vary year-on-year and include: AI and Moral Decision-Making in Business; Business, International Finance & Economics; Case Studies in Data Science & Economics; Consumer Behaviour; Digital Business Services; Digital Marketing Technology and Management; Digital Strategy and Agile Transformation; Entrepreneurship and Business Venturing; FinTech for Consumer Financial Services; Forecasting; International Business; Leading for Innovation; Pricing Analytics; Strategic Human Resource Management. Key: * Analytics Portfolio, Business in Practice and Internship routes only.
Pathways:
- Analytics Portfolio: structure analytics projects, perform hands-on analysis of data, interpret results in the context of the business domain, and develop a visual portfolio of your work.
- Business in Practice: an alternative to the traditional route, simulating real-life business challenges; after the simulation you will complete an Individual Reflection and a Business Analysis.
- Self-sourced Internship: opportunity to self-source a summer internship to apply theoretical learnings to a real-world industry setting.
- Research Paper: conduct academic research on a topic critical to effective decision-making in organisations, under the guidance and supervision of academics.
Your course will be taught through a mix of face-to-face and online learning, utilising the format most suitable to the content. Your learning will be assessed by a mix of exams, individual assessments, group work, project work, and tests. The online learning platform my.wbs will host teaching materials, key information, and the online classroom wbsLive.
Duration: **1 year**. Location: **Warwick Campus**. Format: **Full-time**.

financial_aid.content:
We have £1.5 million+ of [WBS scholarships](https://www.wbs.ac.uk/courses/masters/scholarships/) available for students applying to study on our MSc postgraduate courses. Scholarships awards range from 10% of your tuition fee to a maximum of 50% for exceptional candidates. They are highly competitive and awarded on an ongoing basis, so applicants are strongly encouraged to apply early.
- **The OR Society Scholarships**: Each year The OR Society offers two master's degree scholarships of up to £10,000 towards tuition fees for UK students who demonstrate academic ability but require funding to continue their studies and fulfil their potential in making a future contribution to Operational Research. [Discover more on The OR Society website.](https://www.theorsociety.com/what-we-do/awards-medals-and-scholarships/masters-scholarship/)
- **High Potential Scholarship**: For those who stand out academically, challenge the norm, and have gone beyond their course to delve deeper into extra-curricular activities, volunteering work, or student societies.
- **Warwick Undergraduate Scholarship**: Warwick students will be awarded with an automatic 30% scholarship (with 10% of this scholarship coming from the Warwick Alumni Discount Scheme). You will also be considered for our other scholarships, which could discount up to a further 20%.
- **Alumni Scholarship**: All alumni from the University of Warwick who are accepted onto a postgraduate Master's receive a minimum 25% scholarship, and up to an additional 25% for exceptional academic and/or extra-curricular achievements.
- **UK and Commonwealth Scholarship**: For outstanding individuals across the UK and Commonwealth to encourage geographical diversity.
- **International/EU Scholarship**: Available on a competitive basis for exceptional talent living outside of the UK or the Commonwealth.
- [Country-specific partnerships & scholarships](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/finance/scholarships "COUNTRY-SPECIFIC PARTNERSHIPS & SCHOLARSHIPS")
- [Warwick and External Scholarships](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/scholarships-and-bursaries/ "Warwick and External Scholarships")
- [More about fees and funding](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/funding/funding-routes "More about fees and funding")
If you have a disability, including a mental-health condition or specific learning difficulty, such as dyslexia or dyspraxia, you might be able to get Disabled Students’ Allowance (DSAs). DSAs don’t have to be paid back. Postgraduate students can apply for DSAs even if they aren’t eligible for a Postgraduate Loan.

multiple_applications.content: You may apply for as many courses as you wish, however you will need to complete a new application form for each course and an application assessment fee is payable for each taught application. You can apply to each course only once during an admissions cycle. If a duplicate application is made it will be deleted.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Some departments do allow applicants to defer their offer (not application) to a later date or by **one academic year**.
- If your request to defer your offer is approved by your department, the Admissions Service may ask you to meet some conditions again, for example if your English language certificate is no longer valid.
- Departments usually only allow applicants to defer once.
- If a request to change a start date or defer your studies is approved, **the central admissions team will review your record and may be required to add conditions back into your offer**.
- **Changing your start date or deferring will in many cases, result is fee increases**. Details regarding fees will be included on your new offer letter.
- **In some cases, in order for the admissions team to amend your record and change your start dates, we will have to request that the enrolment team withdraw your record initially**.
- **If you have began the CAS process before completing this form, please note that you may incur extra costs if you choose to proceed with changing your start date or deferring**. By completing this form, you are confirming that you wish for Warwick to withdraw your CAS.
- [Please complete the form to request to defer your offer.](https://warwick.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/apply/pgadmissions/offerholders/respond/defer/request_deferral)

conditional_admission_policy.content:
If your application is approved, the University will make an official offer of a place on the course. There is normally a time limit to accept this. **Offers may be conditional on you meeting academic, language, or other requirements.** Once you have met your conditions, the offer will automatically be made unconditional.
You can apply before you have completed your degree. You will need to supply interim transcripts of your marks and modules to date with your application. You can also apply before you have received your language score. You should put the date of your English test on your application form and you can send in your score later. In both cases, **if an offer is made it will most likely be conditional and dependent on you achieving the required grade/score for admission.**

application_materials.content:
- We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained. Please send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** the originals.
- If you are not a national of a [majority English-speaking country](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/) you will need to submit evidence of your proficiency in English to the UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) and University's required standards.
- One completed reference: Please check whether one or two references are required for the programme for which you are applying. You should supply at least one reference from an academic referee who is in a position to comment on the standard of your academic work and suitability for postgraduate level study. Where this is not possible, references from other sources that provide evidence of your ability to undertake postgraduate study and suitability for your chosen programme will be accepted; references from family members, partners or spouses cannot be accepted.
- References for Postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If your reference is coming direct from your referee, it must come direct from their institutional or company email address and can be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk), along with your student reference number, name and programme of study.
- Not all programmes require a personal statement; however, if provided, it should be tailored to the particular course. Admissions tutors will be looking for an explanation of how the course links your past and future, an insight into your abilities and fit with the course, evidence of your skills, commitment and enthusiasm, reasons why you want to study this course at the University of Exeter, and your particular interest in the subject.
- Personal statement guidance: **Stick to under 500 words in length**; keep sentences short and clear; consider using headings such as 'Why the University of Exeter?' 'Why this course?' 'Career plans’; proofread; check grammar, punctuation and spelling; and use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
- As a **minimum** to enable an initial decision on taught programme applications, applicants need to complete the Module Information section of the application form giving details of any outstanding modules and expected date of completion, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application.
- We recommend uploading all supporting documents with your application. You can apply before completing all academic qualifications, but you will need to provide any interim transcripts that you have to support your application.
- International students: original copies are not required at the application stage and the University would not recommend sending these during the application process.

interview_requirements.content: We may require you to attend an interview before we issue you with your CAS. If you are required to attend an interview, we will send you an email with details of the time and date and joining instructions. The meeting will take place via Microsoft Teams. The purpose of the Pre-CAS interview is to assess that an applicant has a genuine intent to study at the University of Exeter, it is not to assess academic abilities. Attendance at an interview is mandatory and we will be unable to issue a CAS until the interview has taken place. Applicants required to attend a Pre-CAS interview will be sent further details once they have an unconditional place and where applicable a deposit has been paid.

application_deadlines.content: **January start date:** applications to apply for programmes that start in January 2027 will open on **Monday 2 March 2026** and close at **23:59 Monday 4 January 2027**. View a list of [programmes with a January 2027 start](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/january-start/).

academic_requirements.content:
- **A 2:2 or equivalent** from a recognised university, including **at least one mathematical / quantitative module at 2:2 or equivalent**.
- The University considers applications where there is evidence of exceptional performance in modules relevant to the programme of study, **significant relevant work experience or professional qualifications**.
- For students from China: applicants to postgraduate taught Masters courses need a bachelor’s degree certificate and graduation certificate from a domestic university recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education, with grades equivalent to the UK **2:1 or 2:2** requirement depending on the course.

Some courses may have additional undergraduate subject background requirements.

program_overview.content:
MSc Business Analytics is a **1 year full-time** programme offered at **Streatham Campus**, with a January start option. The programme runs from September to September or **January to January** depending on your chosen start month.
The programme is for students interested in a career related to business analytics or who wish to study a related PhD. Students learn how to support managers to make data driven decisions using techniques including analysis of social media and marketing data, optimisation and forecasting. The course provides foundations in business analytics, basic programming and mathematical skills, alongside techniques to present and communicate data to managers.
The programme is inspired by global challenges and draws on the University of Exeter’s environmental research, including business challenges around climate exposure in supply chains and investment portfolios, climate change and natural hazards risk, and wider environmental impacts. Optional study areas allow students to flex the programme to suit their interests and career or research aspirations, including areas such as Marketing Analytics, Strategic & HR Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Environmental Analytics.
Students complete a research project / Business Project supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department, based around a sizeable business problem that draws on their business analytics skills. The programme is delivered over three terms and is University-based throughout; taught components are delivered in the first two terms, with the third term used to complete the Business Project.
Teaching and learning include lectures, workshops, practical sessions, practitioner insight seminars, private study, case study development, group work, individual projects, and collaboration with industry partners. Assessment includes practical exercises, project work, written assignments, presentations, multiple-choice tests, and examinations.
The University has invested £50 million in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence capabilities through the Accelerating Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (ADA) project, which has invested in teaching, research and infrastructure that benefits this programme. Students are taught by internationally respected academics, and the programme is embedded within the [Operations and Analytics group](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/management/about/operations-analytics/) in the Department of Management. The [Centre for Simulation and Analytics Management](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/centres/csam/) supports research and teaching within the programme, focusing on analytical modelling and computer simulation to address real-world problems.
The programme has links with professional organisations such as the Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM) and the Chartered Institute of Personnel Development (CIPD), enriching the programme with industry insights and aligning the curriculum with professional standards and real-world needs.
The QS Business Master’s Ranking 2025: Business Analytics ranks Exeter’s MSc Business Analytics **26th globally** within the Diversity Indicator Group and **top 90 globally** for Employability. Graduates can pursue roles including Business Consultant, Data Consultant, Business Analyst, Supply Chain Analyst, Marketing Analyst, HR Analyst, and Business Manager, with opportunities in consulting, tech, finance, procurement, HR, marketing, public sector and third sector organisations, as well as Graduate Management schemes.
High achieving students may apply for the [QTEM Programme](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroad/pgstudyabroad/qtem/). If accepted, students spend an additional semester studying at one of QTEM’s academic partners, followed by a quantitatively focused internship and participation in the [QTEM Data Challenge](https://www.qtem.org/en/students/data-challenge/1), which includes online data science and leadership courses and real data analysis.

application_materials.content:
For MSc Business Analytics & AI, supporting documents include:
- Current CV (view [CV template](https://ib-programmes.imperial.ac.uk/hubfs/Website-pdfs/CV-Templates/CV-template-for-FTMBA-and-MSc-applicants.docx) for guidance).
- Personal Statement Questions ([see blog for tips on how to write a personal statement](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/blogs/admissions/top-tips-writing-your-personal-statement/)).
- Complete degree transcripts with English translation if necessary ([view international entry requirements](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/apply/postgraduate-taught/entry-requirements/accepted-qualifications/)).
- Contact details of two academic referees or one academic and one professional referee including their company/business email address. We recommend that one should be your current line manager.
- Career planning question, a quantitative experience statement and programming/computer software experience (if applicable).
- GMAT/GRE is not mandatory requirement for any programme, however, it can enhance the strength of your application.
- English language scores (if required i.e. TOEFL, IELTS. [View English language requirements](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/english-language-requirements/https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/english-language-requirements/)).
References: You will need to share the contact details of two academic referees or one academic and one professional referee. Please note we cannot accept references sent from personal or free email addresses, such as Gmail, Hotmail, Yahoo etc. Referees will receive a notification upon application submission to provide a reference for the candidate. Each reference letter submitted must be sent from an academic or professional email address; references sent from personal email addresses, such as Gmail, Hotmail, 126, 163, Sina, QQ, and Yahoo, cannot be accepted.
Essays are a vital part of your application. The questions for the MSc Business Analytics & AI programme are:
1. Please discuss your career plans after graduation. (350 words)
2. Why do you want to study at Imperial Business School and how will you contribute to our community? (500 words)
3. Imperial’s values are Respect, Collaboration, Integrity, Innovation, and Excellence. Describe a time where you embodied one, or more, of these values and explain the impact it had. (500 words)
Quantitative experience statement: You should use the quantitative experience statement on the application form to list the most advanced quantitative courses that you have taken in your academic career to date and to provide brief examples of the relevant topics covered by the programme. Alternatively, if you have gained quantitative experience through work experience, please describe this in the quantitative experience statement. In the quantitative experience statement, you need to list up to five of the most quantitative modules or elements of your studies to date. You should detail the main topics of study (eg: algebra, probability etc) and the level of study (eg: high school, undergraduate degree, short course etc).

interview_requirements.content:
- Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete an online interview, through Imperial's online interview platform. This is the best opportunity to demonstrate your passion and drive, and why you want to study a Master's at Imperial.
- Interviews are conducted through the video interview platform; candidates can access it online to record and submit their answers. The interview process typically takes about **20 minutes** and does not require extensive preparation.
- The interview aims to supplement the written application and help candidates convey their suitability for their chosen Master's by answering questions about previous experience and future aspirations.
- AI/Chat GPT guidance: The purpose of the interview is to get to know more about you. Imperial wants to see how you approach problems, your motivations and wider interests. If malpractice or answers provided are not genuine are identified, this may factor negatively into the admissions committee decision.
- Application decisions will be communicated by the corresponding decision date for the round in which you applied; applicants should refer to the [key dates and deadlines](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics/admissions/#dates-deadlines) for timeframes.

academic_requirements.content:
- You should have a **First or Upper Second Class Honours undergraduate degree** from a recognised university or the [international equivalent](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/international-entry-requirements) in a quantitative discipline such as Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, or a quantitative economics degree.
- Your quantitative experience should typically include topics such as **advanced calculus, probability, statistics and linear algebra**. Complete the [online Maths test](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics-maths-test) to determine if you are suitable to apply for the programme.
- MSc Business Analytics & AI includes modules using programming languages such as **SQL, R, and Python**, so previous experience of using these or an interest in coding and programming will add weight to your application.
- Work experience is **not a requirement**, although undertaking relevant internships and work placements will add weight to your application. The programme typically looks for candidates with **no more than three years of work experience**; those with more than three years will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
- Most MSc programmes require at least an **Upper Second Class Honours degree or international equivalent** to be admitted. Work experience can add weight to an application, but would not replace the academic requirement.
- China applicants: Imperial requires a **Bachelor’s degree awarded with a final overall weighted average mark of at least 85% from a Project 211 university**.

gre_gmat_requirements.content:
GMAT is not required for MSc Business Analytics & AI, but will add weight to your application. For the [GMAT 10th edition Exam](https://www.gmac.com/gmat-other-assessments/about-the-gmat-exam), you will need scores in the **90th percentile**. Similarly, if you are taking the GRE, you will need scores in the **90th percentile**. Scores are valid for **five years from your appointment date**. GMAT or GRE is highly recommended for candidates with less quantitative degree backgrounds to strengthen their application for this highly competitive programme.
GMAT/GRE is not mandatory requirement for any programme, however, it can enhance the strength of your application.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
All home, EU, and overseas applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency. Students who were not awarded their degree in a qualifying English-speaking country must demonstrate their proficiency by completing an approved English language qualification at the required level. Minimum test requirements for the most popular tests are:
- **IELTS (academic): A minimum score of 7.0 with minimum scores of 6.5 in all elements**
- **TOEFL iBT:** Tests taken before 21 January 2026: **A minimum score of 100 overall with minimum scores of 22 in all elements.** Tests taken after 21 January 2026: **We accept an overall score of 5.0 with minimum scores of 5.0 in all elements.** We will accept both scores for a period of two years.
- **Duolingo English Test: 125 Overall with no less than 115 in any band score**
More detailed information can be found on the [English language requirements page](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/english-language-requirements).
English language scores should be submitted if required, i.e. TOEFL, IELTS. It is not compulsory to submit the results of an approved English language test with your application, but it is strongly encouraged and will add weight to your application if you are able to show that you have met the language requirement prior to applying.
The Business School does not offer pre-sessional English courses and does not accept attendance of a pre-sessional English course as a means of meeting the English language requirement.

program_overview.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics & AI equips students with advanced computational, machine learning, and AI capabilities for an increasingly data-driven world. Students develop expertise in predictive, prescriptive and AI-powered decision models while applying these tools to real-world business challenges through workshops, placement opportunities and an optional extended term. The programme builds coding skills in languages such as Python and R and prepares graduates for roles such as business analyst, data scientist or consultant.
The programme is taught within Imperial College London, a world-leading university with STEM roots, and students learn across the South Kensington and White City [campuses](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/programmes/imperial-advantage/london/#campus) in London. It is ranked 4th in Europe and 8th in the world in the QS Business Master’s Rankings 2026 for Business Analytics, and offers 10 elective options.
Programme preparation and core modules provide foundation skills in statistics, machine learning, data visualisation and genAI. Electives allow students to tailor the programme to their interests, with options focused on industries such as finance, energy and healthcare and technical topics such as LLMs and reinforcement learning. In the summer, students apply their knowledge through a practical project, gaining consulting experience, completing a work placement, or conducting a research report. An [optional extended term](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/extended-term/) allows students to extend the programme duration to 16 months for a longer Work Placement and additional credits.
The programme includes online pre-study modules from July to September and a compulsory on-campus induction week in early September at the South Kensington campus. Over the summer term, students complete the Analytics in Business Capstone, choosing either a Consulting Project or Work Placement; students interested in pursuing a PhD may complete an Individual Research Report with a faculty supervisor instead. The Work Placement gives students the opportunity to apply programme material in a challenging business situation, and the Extended Work Placement provides access to additional and longer summer internship opportunities in the UK and worldwide.
The Class of 2026 includes 107 students, 44% female students, and 34 nationalities.
Career support is tailored to individual aspirations and includes career planning, CV advice and mock interviews before the programme, during study, and after graduation. Graduates work across technology, finance, consulting, healthcare, advertising and luxury, with employers including Amazon, Bloomberg, Mastercard, J.P. Morgan, Google, HSBC and Mastercard. Employment outcomes for the Class of 2024: 95% employed within six months, 56% employed in the UK, and 38% employed in finance. [Find out more about career outcomes](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics/career-impact/).
The programme is taught by business-focussed academics and data science specialists researching how analytics, data and AI will transform business and society. Faculty use state-of-the-art technology such as the Data Observatory and combine research with practical insights from industry and government networks. Faculty listed for the programme include Gah-Yi Ban, Associate Professor of Analytics and Operations and Academic Director of MSc Business Analytics & AI; Jiahua Wu; Michael Yeomans; Gokhan Yildirim; Fanyin Zheng; Edward Anderson; Martin Haugh; Esma Koca; Zhe Liu; Fintan Nagle; Laure de Preux; Ragvir Sabharwal; Reza Skandari; Kalyan Talluri; and Wolfram Wiesemann.

curriculum.content:
MSc Business Analytics & AI programme content includes pre-study and Core modules that prepare students with foundation skills in statistics, machine learning, data visualisation and genAI, elective modules focused on industries and technical topics, and a summer practical project to apply knowledge in a real-world setting through consulting experience, a work placement, or a research report.
- The programme has **10 elective options** and includes elective options such as Advanced Machine Learning, Causal Modelling, and Generative AI and Large Language Models.
- Online pre-study modules: **Online | July-September**. Before the start of the programme, students are expected to complete online pre-study modules delivered via Canvas; some are compulsory and others are strongly recommended.
- Induction week: **On campus | Early September, compulsory**. MSc Business Analytics & AI induction is spent at the South Kensington campus in London.
- Core modules: Data Structures and Algorithms; Data Wrangling and Visualisation; Deep Learning and Generative AI; Fundamentals of Database Technologies; Machine Learning; Maths & Statistics Foundations for Analytics; Optimisation and Decision Models; Statistics and Econometrics.
- Electives: Advanced Machine Learning; Causal Modelling for Business Analytics; Data Management and Ethics; Energy Analytics; Financial Analytics; Generative AI and Large Language Models; Healthcare and Medical Analytics; Leadership in analytics; Logistics and Supply-Chain Analytics; Network Analytics; Retail and Marketing Analytics; Text Analysis for Business.
- Over the summer term, students complete the **Analytics in Business Capstone**, choosing either a **Consulting Project** or **Work Placement**.
- Analytics in Business Capstone applies methodological and domain-specific knowledge gathered throughout the Imperial MSc Business Analytics & AI to business case studies.
- Consulting Project: a substantial group-based consulting project undertaken for a real client.
- Work Placement: an opportunity to apply programme material to a challenging business situation in a real-world setting; students must secure their own work placements and submit details to the Programme Team.
- Individual Research Report: offered to students interested in pursuing a PhD; it constitutes a small piece of research over the summer period, supervised by a faculty member, and can be done in place of the Analytics in Business Capstone module.
- Optional extended term: students may extend the programme duration to **16 months** through an [optional extended term](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/extended-term/), allowing a longer Work Placement, additional professional and global experience, and additional credits; it is subject to an additional tuition fee.
- Extended Work Placement: provides additional work placement opportunities, including longer summer internships in the UK and worldwide.
- Global modules are electives with an application process and additional costs. Options listed include Global Business Challenge (Entrepreneurship), Global Business Challenge (Social Impact), and Global Immersion.
- Global Immersion is an optional, one-week trip with visits to companies across industry sectors, plus social and cultural activities.
- The Business School FAQ states that almost all MSc programmes are **12 month, full-time programmes**; the only exception is MSc Strategic Marketing (online, part-time).

financial_aid.content:
Imperial Business School offers significant scholarship funding to talented Master's applicants, including scholarships and bursaries for MSc Business Analytics & AI. Applicants should apply early and submit their application by one of the [two scholarship submission deadlines](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/business-school/masters/business-analytics/admissions/#dates-deadlines) for the 2026 Master's intake; scholarships are awarded from the first deadline onwards. Some scholarships require an additional video interview, with details provided in the offer email.
- African Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Applicants must be residents in one of the 54 African countries as defined by the United Nations and demonstrate an outstanding track record of leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- Black Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Applicants must self-identify as being from a Black or mixed Black background and demonstrate leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply; the offer email includes video assessment details.
- Bright Network Scholarship: up to £10,000. Applicants need to be members of the Bright Network. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- Dean's Impact Scholarship: £25,000. Applicants must provide clear evidence of tangible impact in entrepreneurship, technology and innovation, sustainability, social impact, or leadership. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply; scholarships are limited and earlier application is recommended.
- Female Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Female applicants must demonstrate leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply.
- Imperial Excellence Bursary: up to £25,000. Applicants must be self-funded students who demonstrate exceptional academic merit and/or potential, and financial need showing inability to otherwise enrol on an MSc programme. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply.
- Imperial Excellence Scholarship: up to £15,000. Applicants should have a strong all-round application with an excellent academic background, career potential and personal statement. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- Imperial Loyalty Bursary: 10% off tuition. Imperial College London students or alumni who submit their application for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two and receive an offer will automatically receive this award, subject to availability. Alumni must have achieved an undergraduate degree from Imperial College London awarded at a minimum of Upper Second Class Honours or a Master's degree awarded with a minimum of Merit.
- LATAM Future Leader Award: up to £20,000. Applicants must be residents in one of the 21 Latin American countries as defined by the United Nations and demonstrate leadership and/or leadership potential. Candidates who receive an offer for an MSc programme in admission rounds one or two will automatically be considered.
- LGBTQ+ Scholarship: up to £20,000. Applicants should demonstrate a strong track record of promoting diversity and inclusion and a desire to encourage LGBTQ+ participation in business education and champion equality. Candidates receiving an offer in admission rounds one or two can apply.
Other merit or needs-based scholarships may be available: [Imperial College London](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/) offers postgraduate scholarships, [The British Council](https://study-uk.britishcouncil.org/) offers scholarships for international students, and details of [non-Imperial scholarships](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/students/fees-and-funding/postgraduate-funding/scholarships/further-funding-opportunities-/external-awards/) are available online. Further funding options may also be found in The Grants Register, Awards for postgraduate study at Commonwealth Universities, Study Abroad, and on the [Imperial College London website](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/).
If offered an Imperial Business School scholarship and subsequently offered a larger award by Imperial, the larger award supersedes the first and is not additional. Scholarships awarded by Imperial Business School are in the form of a reduction of the tuition fee; if another scholarship pays the full tuition fee directly to Imperial, the student cannot also receive a Business School scholarship.

multiple_applications.content:
- You can apply for **up to two courses** in an academic year, only one of which can be for Imperial Business School.
- If you are applying for two courses you should submit only one application, listing your course preferences, rather than submitting two separate applications.
- You should list your preferred course as your first choice and your reserve course as your second choice as applications are considered in the order they are submitted; the second choice will only be considered if the first-choice application is unsuccessful.
- You can only apply for **one Master's course** per admissions cycle in Imperial Business School. To be considered, this course must be submitted as your first choice in your application.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Under exceptional circumstances, you may apply to defer your admission to the next academic year. Deferral requests are based on a change of circumstance that is outside your control and could not have been foreseen, and that will prevent you from taking up your place on the original course start date. Deferral requests are granted or denied at the discretion of academic departments.
To request a deferral, contact the relevant [admissions team](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/study/apply/contact/) outlining your circumstances and reasons for your request.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
After receiving your offer, you will need to submit documents to satisfy your offer conditions. As part of this process, you must verify your degree award through the online Qualification Check service, using a unique link provided in your offer conditions. You will then be required to pay a **£6,500 deposit** for the programme. The application portal can be used to respond to your offer and review the full details of your conditions.
You will be able to see full details of your offer conditions once your official offer has been confirmed. For visa applicants, CAS numbers will start to be issued from April, but the CAS will appear on My Imperial only after you have met all the conditions of your offer. Imperial notes: “we cannot provide you with a CAS if you have outstanding conditions on your offer.”
The Business School does **not** offer pre-sessional English courses and does **not** accept attendance of a pre-sessional English course as a means of meeting the English language requirement.

application_materials.content:
- Submit all supporting documents with your application; upload **each supporting document separately** (do not combine files into one document) and give each file a relevant title that clearly states what it contains. If you have already submitted an application, email outstanding documents to [pgadmissions.ambs@manchester.ac.uk](mailto:pgadmissions.ambs@manchester.ac.uk) and include your ID number.
- **Statement of purpose:** tell why you are interested in the course, how it will impact your future, and what makes you stand out as an exceptional candidate. Your statement should be **no more than one page**.
- **Academic transcript and degree certificate:** submit a copy of your official transcript, including modules and grades obtained to date. If you have already graduated, submit your degree certificate and final degree transcript confirming the title of your award, final grade and date of completion. If these documents are not in English, attach an official certified translation. Original copies are not required during the application process.
- **Academic references:** you are **not required to submit an academic reference** when you complete your online application, but after an initial assessment you may be contacted and asked to provide one.
- **CV:** if you have **more than two years' postgraduate work experience** you need to submit your CV.
- **University grading scale:** if you are studying outside the UK, you need to provide the grading scale from your university.
- **Proof of English language ability:** if English is not your first language, you must submit evidence of your English language ability before a decision will be made on your application. If you have studied in a majority English-speaking country, upload a copy of either your visa, CAS, BRP card, or an official letter from your undergraduate institution confirming where your studies were conducted; this can be uploaded within the same file as your CV. Find out more about [language requirements >>](https://www.alliancembs.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/masters-entry-requirements/).
- **Copy of passport:** if you are an international student who needs a Tier 4 visa to study in the UK, you will need to submit a copy of your passport with your application.
