academic_requirements.content:
- We require a **First or Upper Second class honours degree (2:1, with 60% average)** from a UK university or the overseas equivalent.
- Your degree background must be in a **quantitative subject** such as mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, computing, management science or economics, and we require you to demonstrate study of **quantitative modules** (e.g. maths, statistics, calculus) consistently throughout each year of your studies and achieve good grades.
- Study of programming is desirable, but **mathematical-related modules are essential**.
- When assessing your academic record we take into account your grade average, position in class and the standing of the institution where you studied your qualification. We particularly welcome applicants from institutions of high ranking and repute.
- For applicants from **China (Mainland)**: taught master's applicants with a bachelor's degree from a recognised good-quality Chinese university, with a **minimum overall average grade of 80%** or a **minimum GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0)** will be considered for admission on to taught master's programmes; please refer to the entrance requirements of individual programmes for further guidance.

gre_gmat_requirements.content: For the one-year pre-experience business master's courses, the most important element of your application is your current GPA. **GMAT and/or GRE are not required for entry.** Unlike the USA there is no history of testing for these courses in England; academic skills evidenced by your GPA are what we will look at.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
- For Alliance MBS master's courses, the most recent English language test submitted with the application is the only one accepted. English test scores must be **no more than two years old at the start of the course**.
- Accepted tests and minimum scores:
- [IELTS](http://www.ielts.org/): **7.0 overall and no other element below 6.5**.
- [TOEFL](http://www.ets.org/toefl): **100 overall with a minimum score of 22 in other elements**.
- [Cambridge Proficiency Examination (CPE)](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/proficiency/): **minimum grade B**.
- [Cambridge Advanced Examination (CAE)](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/advanced/): **minimum grade B**.
- English for Academic Purposes (EAP): **overall grade A with minimum grade B in all components**.
- Indian Standard XII English (CBSE and ISC): **minimum 85%**.
- [PTE Academic](https://pearsonpte.com/): **overall score of 76, with a minimum 70 in other elements**.
- For a pre-sessional English language course, the minimum is **IELTS 6.5 overall with no element below 6.0**. See [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.ucae.manchester.ac.uk/study/).
- The following are **not accepted**: TOEFL Home Edition, IELTS Indicator, Duolingo English Test, GMAT, and GRE. A combination of two test scores or TOEFL "MyBest" Scores is also not accepted; applicants must meet the minimum requirements **in one sitting**.
- If an applicant has completed **between one and two years of study in the UK**, an English language test score must be submitted.
- If an applicant has completed a **minimum of three years of undergraduate study within a majority English-speaking country** and has **graduated within the last two years**, an English language test is not required. Applicants who graduated more than two years ago and have remained in an English-speaking country to work or study may also be exempt, **at the discretion of the Admissions Team**. The list of majority English-speaking countries is [here](http://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/international/admissions/language-requirements/).
- If an applicant has completed **one to two years of study within a majority English-speaking country**, they must submit an English language test score. If they studied in a majority English-speaking country, they should upload a copy of their visa, CAS, BRP card, or an official letter from their undergraduate institution confirming where the studies were conducted.
- If an application is submitted without an English language test score, it can be processed, but **no offer can be made until there is evidence of English language ability**. If a test date is already arranged, it should be noted on the application.
- If the score is slightly below the minimum requirements, the minimum IELTS score to consider the application is **6.5 overall with no element below 6.0**. On receiving an offer, applicants may either re-take IELTS to achieve **7.0 overall with no other element below 6.5** or may be eligible for a pre-sessional English course at The University of Manchester.
- To submit scores, scanned copies of score reports are accepted and verified by the Admissions team. Applicants should include their scores and test date on the application form. Results do not need to be sent electronically through the examination centre because the Admissions team can verify them directly using the IELTS TRF Number, TOEFL Appointment Number, or Pearson Score Report Code. If the application has already been submitted without an English language test, results should be emailed directly to the Admissions team.

program_overview.content:
Master of Science (**MSc**), **1 year**, **full-time**.
With MSc Business Analytics and Artificial Intelligence, you will learn the fundamental theories, approaches and analytical toolkit of data analytics, decision sciences, applied operational research and statistics. You will apply this knowledge to real-life scenarios to enhance your learning.
This MSc prepares you to lead data-driven decision-making in organisations using advanced analytics and AI.
- Tackle real business challenges using applied AI methods and industry-standard analytical tools, building practical capability alongside strong theoretical foundations.
- Develop advanced expertise in machine learning, data analytics and strategic optimisation, equipping you to improve performance and manage risk in complex environments.
- Learn from research-active experts connected to the Centre for AI and Decision Sciences, ensuring your studies reflect current industry and technological developments.
- Apply your skills through substantial project work, strengthening your ability to translate analytical insight into strategic action.
- Benefit from the programme’s relaunch for September 2026 with an enhanced focus on AI for Business, and tailor your studies through optional units aligned to your career ambitions.
**Formerly MSc Business Analytics, Operational Research and Risk Analysis, this course has been reviewed and relaunched from September 2026, with an increased emphasis on AI for Business.**

conditional_admission_policy.content:
- AMBS is unable to make aspirational offers. If you submit your application before you've completed your undergraduate degree, your current average grade must meet our minimum entry requirements for your application to be considered.
- If your score is slightly below the minimum English requirements, then on receiving an offer for an AMBS master's course, you will be given the option to re-take IELTS to achieve **7.0 overall with no other element below 6.5** or you may be eligible to attend a [pre-sessional English course](https://www.ucae.manchester.ac.uk/study/). This formal recommendation is an alternative option to retaking an English Language test and only comes as a condition in your official offer letter.
- If your English language ability is slightly below our requirements, you may be eligible for a pre-sessional English language course in order to progress to the Masters degree. You must achieve a minimum IELTS score of **6.5 overall with no element below 6.0** for entry to a pre-sessional course.
- If you have already met our academic requirements and English language requirements, a single visa may be issued covering both the pre-sessional course and the Masters degree. If, however, you obtain a conditional offer for the Master degree and your academic results are pending you may still enrol in a pre-sessional course on a separate visa.
- If you haven’t completed your current academic study and are interested in studying a Pre-sessional English course prior to a Masters degree, AMBS strongly recommends that you take the UKVI IELTS test to ensure you are eligible for a separate visa for the language course.

program_overview.content:
Qualification type: MSc. Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months or 24 months.
The Business Analytics and Big Data MSc equips you with the technical and analytical skills to turn data into strategic insight. Designed in collaboration with industry, the programme blends data science, business acumen, and practical applications. You'll graduate ready to solve complex business challenges in a data-driven world.
Competitive advantage and innovation in the digital world involve the accurate analysis and insights offered by big data - huge data sets that are constantly being generated - in order to improve effectiveness and efficiencies across several business areas, such as operations management and marketing. In order to exploit the insights provided by big data, business analytics and the effective use and understanding of data is crucial. This is a rapidly developing field, which is exhibiting massive demand from industry for qualified individuals in this area to take up roles in management globally. You will develop your knowledge of the organisation, administration and governance of this data, as well as hone your analytical, organisational and leadership skills. The programme is designed for students who wish to pursue a career in this dynamic field or continue their studies to PhD level. Developed in collaboration with industry contributors and partners including PepsiCo and AstraZeneca, the programme is also underpinned by multidisciplinary research.
This course is ideal for students who want to use data to drive business decisions and solve real-world problems. It suits those with a strong interest in analytics, technology, and business strategy, and who are looking to build a career in data-driven roles across industries.
What you'll learn:
- How to collect, manage, and analyse big data for business insights
- Data mining and machine learning techniques
- Use of analytics and simulation tools such as Witness, R, Qlik, and SAP
- How to develop and implement digital business strategies
- Data visualisation and communication of analytical findings
- Applying big data solutions to real business challenges.
The University of Liverpool Management School (ULMS) is one of an elite group of institutions worldwide to hold the gold standard 'triple-crown' accreditation from AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS.
The 12-month programme consists of four compulsory modules and two optional modules followed by the Main Project over the summer period on completion of Semester two. Modules are taught using active learning techniques including business simulations, real-world case studies, coding in higher-level programming languages such as RStudio and Python, business analytics software such as Tableau, Qlik, and SAP, interactive participation software, lecture capture, tutorials and project work. Following semester two you will complete either the Business Simulation and Analysis or MSc Project with the support of an academic supervisor. Teaching time will account for an average of 10 hours per week and you should anticipate an additional 20 hours of self-directed study and group work. Students are required to complete 180 credits to achieve a full MSc.
This programme is delivered by the triple-accredited [University of Liverpool Management School](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/management/). The School has a thriving international master's community with a comprehensive, interdisciplinary programme of social and extra-curricular events and dedicated careers and employability support.
The Management School's master's programmes have been designed from the ground up to prepare you for success in your chosen career. We have close ties with local, national and international organisations and constantly review the content of our programmes to meet the demands of top graduate employers. From the moment you start your master's programme, you'll have access to a specialist, in-house [careers team](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/management/study/postgraduate-taught/careers/) and one-to-one careers guidance, workshops, seminars and employability initiatives.
Through exposure to strategic initiatives in the management of Big Data, as well as case-based workshops and practical application developments for data mining, analysis and visualisation using industry-leading software, graduates of the programme shall find themselves well-equipped to meet the many challenges associated with strategic, operational and technological adaptation in the digital enterprise.
Alumni have secured jobs with the following companies:
- Hampshire Bank Trust
- Ericcson UK
- Amazon
- Liverpool Association for Space Engineering Research
- Future
In roles such as:
- PCB engineer
- Reward Analyst
- Lead Commercial Analyst
- Business solution architect

cost_of_attendance.content:
UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) requires that you have **£10,539 per academic year**, equivalent to **£1,171 per month for nine months**, to cover daily living expenses including accommodation, food and local travel. The £10,539 figure is based on a nine-month stay in the UK. If you're staying for 12 months, you're likely to need at least **£14,052** to cover your living costs, based on the UKVI's minimum monthly amount.

program_overview.content:
Start date: 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
Business Analytics and Decision Sciences MSc is designed to develop expertise in data analysis and the psychology of how people make decisions, so students can transform data into meaningful business action. The course combines theoretical concepts with practical application, developing decision-oriented analytical skills that managers need. Students learn how to translate data, such as customer reviews, sales figures and cost-over-time, into actionable insights that have a positive impact on organisational effectiveness.
The course builds knowledge and understanding of how business analytics can provide evidence to support management decision making. Using different evidence-based approaches to make effective decisions, students develop quantitative analysis skills and learn advanced analytical techniques such as forecasting, predictive modelling, clustering and optimisation, while applying decision-making skills to real-life business and management scenarios. Students also gain an understanding of research methods and consultancy. A range of optional modules allows students to gain specialist knowledge that suits their interests or career plans. The course culminates in a dissertation or project, enabling students to apply their learning to a topic of their choice with support from an academic supervisor.
- Taught by globally recognised experts: academics and business practitioners who teach the course are from the [Centre for Decision Research](https://cdr.leeds.ac.uk/about/) and are actively engaged in advising businesses, governments and international bodies.
- The curriculum is based on real business applications shaped by industry links, with opportunities to work with and learn from major names in business.
- Students can apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-study-tour-2), with company visits, guest lectures and networking events. Previous study tours have included Berlin, Frankfurt, Milan and Zurich.
- Students have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme.
Leeds University Business School has triple accreditation from the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations), [Association of MBAs (AMBA)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations), and [European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS)](http://business.leeds.ac.uk/about-us/doc/accreditations).
Students are taught through lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops, with independent learning supported by the Virtual Learning Environment. Teaching is delivered by expert academics, from lecturers through to professors, and may also include industry professionals with years of experience and trained postgraduate researchers. Assessment may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs.
Career paths for graduates include Business Analysts, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Data Hunters, Business Consultants, Analytics Consultants and Commercial Managers. Graduates have found employment as Credit Risk Manager at Lloyds Banking Group, Business Analyst at Transport for London, Business QA Manager at HSBC, Associate at PwC, Analyst at Deloitte, Data Hunter at Allianz Insurance, Consultant at EY, Senior Advisor Data Science at Dell Technologies, Accountant at Beijing Capital Airlines and Operational Researcher at the Home Office.
Key skills developed include business analytics using industry-standard tools such as R, Python and SQL; processes such as CRISP-DM and Agile; time-series forecasting and machine learning, including the application of artificial intelligence; decision making, including human bias and heuristics, risk communication and risk assessment; and business acumen for managing complex business situations.
Students engage with senior business leaders through the [Leaders in Residence](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/divisions-management/doc/leaders-residence) initiative. Past students have worked on industry-led projects with partners such as the Met Office, Britest, OPSS and Universal Music Group, and have been taught by experts in analytics and decision science from companies including Oakland, Amazon and PlayStation.
As a Masters student at Leeds, students can gain real-world industry experience through the Global Industry Programme, solving a real business problem from a live company brief. The programme is fully online and designed to fit around studies, with opportunities to build professional networks, consultancy experience, teamwork across disciplines and employability prospects.
The programme is ranked [Top 60 in the world for Business Analytics, QS Business Masters Rankings 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/business-masters-rankings/business-analytics).

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics and Finance (MSc) is a **Master of Science** course starting **September 2026** for **1 year**. It is a **full-time** course based at **Highfield** and awarded by the **University of Southampton**.
Data analysis has become a dominant force in the modern global business landscape, and industries are looking for data-literate professionals with strong decision making and analytics skills, as well as financial acumen. This course will equip you with technical data science skills and non-technical management skills, along with a deep understanding of the application of analytics within the context of financial management. You will develop an interdisciplinary understanding of the applications of analytics in a financial context through data collection, data visualization, statistical/pattern analysis, and data mining.
The degree is ideal for those who have previously been exposed to other disciplines and fields which incorporated data analytics skills or a quantitative subject, such as economics, mathematics, physics, engineering or computer science. It will also suit applicants with relevant professional experience who are contemplating either furthering their career or making a career change.
Modules are designed to meet the latest industry demands and course contents are reviewed by the [Business Advisory Board](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/about/businessadvisory.page), which includes industry experts from organisations such as Rolls Royce, BT Openreach, Ford and Shell. Students also benefit from the expertise of the [Centre of Operational Research, Management Sciences and Information Systems (CORMSIS)](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/), one of the country’s strongest analytics research groups. Learning is informed by specialist research, and students can personalise their studies with optional modules focusing on areas such as financial risk management, advanced analytics, simulation and revenue management.
A dissertation component is integrated as part of the programme. Students either choose a dissertation topic with the help and guidance of a supervisor, or apply to work on an industry project; if selected, the industry project becomes the dissertation topic. The course structure runs for a full 12 months: the first 9 months cover taught modules, with exams in January and May, followed by dissertation work from June to September.
Learning includes lectures and seminars, individual and group exercises, computer classes, private study and workshops. Students explore topics through exercises using real-world data, case studies and numerical problem solving, and can gain specialist experience using analytics, modelling, coding and programming software such as Excel, Python and Anylogic. Assessment methods vary between modules and may include examinations, individual coursework, group work and dissertation. Students are assigned a personal tutor and have access to a senior tutor.
[Dr Steffen Bayer](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xhjf7/doctor-steffen-bayer) is the lead for this course. He is an Associate Professor at the University of Southampton Business School and Programme Leader for the MSc Business Analytics and Finance and MSc Business Analytics and Management Science. His research focuses on health service planning, including stroke and renal care, human resource planning and technology-supported healthcare delivery.
The course is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](https://www.aacsb.edu/). Facilities include [Business study spaces](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/facilities/business-study-spaces) and a [Financial laboratory](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/study/facilities/financial-laboratory), which provides experience using Bloomberg terminals to access real-world financial market data.
Graduates commonly work in sectors including consultancy, technology, business, public sector and finance. Careers directly related to this course include operational researcher, market researcher, management consultant, financial analyst, business analyst, data scientist, quantitative analyst, data analyst, risk manager and supply chain manager. Example job titles of Southampton MSc Business Analytics and Finance graduates include data analyst, investment analyst, business analyst, management trainee, business and credit analyst, business intelligence analyst, credit risk analyst, financial analyst, management consultant and market research assistant.
Job prospects for MSc Business Analytics and Finance graduates: **£33k Average professional salary**, **81% In a skilled profession or further study**, and **95% Graduate employment rate**. Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics are taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about the activities and perspectives of graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

- Victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK.
- Personal accident or injury of a significant nature.
- Child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities.
- Relevant work experience/placements/internships.
- Military service.
- Change of employment circumstances.
- Unforeseen ATAS delays.
- Unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include:
- Unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship) except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship.
- To undertake employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics and Management Science (MSc) is a Master of Science course starting September 2026, lasting 1 year, taught full-time at Highfield Campus. With this master's, students develop skills in business analysis and learn how to gain insights from data. The degree equips students for a career in data analysis and is ideal for graduates with analytical skills who can use data to improve business performance and solve problems for organisations. It is also suited to students with a background in quantitative study or work experience in this area, and can help students specialise in further study, advance in a current professional role or change career.
The MSc teaches theory and practical application, with course content based on the latest industry practice. It is taught in partnership with the [Centre of Operational Research, Management Sciences and Information Systems (CORMSIS)](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/), described as one of the country’s best analytics research groups. As part of CORMSIS, learning is informed by specialist research and students have a wider module choice in business and maths topics, giving them a chance to customise their postgraduate experience.
Students can either complete a dissertation or compete for a 3-month analytics summer project with an organisation, such as British Telecommunications, Deloitte or Ford. This competitive industry placement is designed to boost career prospects through a real-world challenge and a business connection. The course is taught by supportive lecturers through case studies, active discussions and practical exercises.
The course structure is full-time over 12 months, from September to the following September. In the first 9 months, semesters 1 and 2 cover the taught part of the course, made up of modules everyone takes and optional modules chosen from a list. Optional areas include advanced analytics methods such as machine learning, strategic analytics, behavioural operations, and applications of analytics in management such as finance, logistics, project and risk management, and revenue management. During semester 2 students prepare for the dissertation, then spend the final 3 months over the summer working independently to research and write it. Students also have an opportunity to compete for a 3-month summer placement in an external organisation; around 50 spaces per year are usually offered for all CORMSIS MSc students, across projects and organisations including overseas organisations such as those from China and India.
Learning develops practical skills through lectures, seminars, discussions, case studies, group work, individual reading and coursework. Students gain knowledge and understanding of IT skills through lectures, computer workshops and coursework. Speakers from different organisations visit to provide insight into how business analytics and management science are used in business, and workshops led by companies cover career-relevant topics such as report writing and skills required for summer project placements.
The dissertation gives students the opportunity to apply skills developed during the programme to a challenging problem. Students may apply for a dissertation topic set by a company or organisation, based on a real challenge they are facing, or develop their own topic. Throughout the dissertation, students work closely with an academic supervisor; if the project is with an external organisation, they also work with a representative from that organisation.
Students have access to learning and welfare services offered by the Business School and the University. A personal academic tutor offers ongoing support throughout the course, and a team of industry liaison officers can answer questions about the summer project.
Course lead: [Dr Steffen Bayer](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xhjf7/doctor-steffen-bayer), Lecturer in Business Analytics. The course is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](https://www.aacsb.edu/).
Graduates commonly work in consultancy, technology, business, the public sector and finance. Careers directly related to this course include operational researcher, market researcher, management consultant, financial analyst, business analyst, data scientist, quantitative analyst, data analyst, risk manager and supply chain manager. Example job titles of Southampton MSc Business Analytics and Management Science graduates include data analyst, investment analyst, business analyst, management trainee, business and credit analyst, business intelligence analyst, credit risk analyst, financial analyst, management consultant and market research assistant.
Job prospects for MSc Business Analytics and Management Science graduates: £33k average professional salary; 81% in a skilled profession or further study; 95% graduate employment rate. These example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics are taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
Reasons typically accepted for deferral include: bereavement due to the loss of a close family member; serious illness and health problems; victim of a natural disaster; victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK; personal accident or injury of a significant nature; child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities; relevant work experience/placements/internships; military service; change of employment circumstances; unforeseen ATAS delays; unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include: unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship) except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship; to undertake employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.

program_overview.content:
The NUS Master of Science in Business Analytics (MSBA) programme at the National University of Singapore is co-designed by NUS Business School and NUS Computing and offered through the Business Analytics Centre (BAC). BAC was established in 2013 as a collaborative effort between NUS and IBM and serves as the operational hub for the NUS MSBA programme, blending academic rigor with industrial prowess.
The programme prepares future leaders proficient in data science and business analytics to navigate digital transformation across sectors. It offers both full-time and part-time options: full-time students can complete the programme in approximately 14 months, with a maximum duration of 2 academic years; part-time students can complete it in approximately 26 months, with a maximum duration of 4 academic years.
The curriculum blends rigorous academic theory with practical, hands-on learning, preparing graduates to tackle real-world challenges in industries such as finance, information technology, retail, manufacturing, healthcare, and more. NUS MSBA is supported by NUS Business School and NUS School of Computing, works closely with industry partners in developing new and relevant course content, and has a unique curriculum to nurture data-savvy business leaders and practitioners of data science.
BAC has a robust industry network with over 100 partners, including Accenture, Alibaba, Amazon, AXA, DBS, Ernst & Young, Google, Huawei, IBM, Johnson & Johnson, Morgan Stanley, SAP, State Street, Swiss Re, Ant Financial, Grab, Shopee, TigerGraph, and TikTok. These collaborations extend into educational initiatives and translational research. More than 1000 real-world industrial analytics and operations research (OR) projects have been completed by NUS MSBA students with partner corporations in the past 10 years. NUS MSBA partners with more than 100 companies in student education and career development, offers a unique industry-oriented learning experience, and provides 100% internship placements with partner companies for NUS MSBA students.
The programme was ranked Asia No. 1 and Top 10 worldwide in the 2024 QS Business Masters Rankings in Business Analytics. Since its inception, NUS MSBA has graduated about 900 alumni, forming a community of more than 900 alumni from 30 different nationalities/regions. Graduates emerge as skilled practitioners capable of employing data-driven strategies to solve complex business challenges in local and international markets.
The NUS BAC Advisory Board helps shape NUS MSBA’s strategic direction and ensures that its curriculum remains at the forefront of the business analytics field. Advisory Board members include Mr Ian Wilson, Chairman, NUS BAC Advisory Board; Mr Abraham Thomas, ASEAN Managing Partner, IBM Consulting; Dean Andrew K. Rose, Dean, NUS Business School; Dean Tulika Mitra, Dean, NUS Computing; Mr David Xie, Chief Executive Officer, Lark/Feishu; Mr Joe Chiu, Vice President, Changi Airport Group; Dr Matthew Wang, President, Cybernaut Investment Group; Mr Manik Saha, Managing Director, SAP Labs Singapore & Vietnam; Mr Sameer Gupta, Chief Analytics Officer, DBS; and Mr Shah Bhavesh, ConvaTec Group Global Vice President, Finance and Operational Excellence.
[Download NUS MSBA Brochure](https://msba.nus.edu.sg/brochure-download/)

curriculum.content:
Students must complete:
- Units: **44**
- Courses: **8**
- Capstone Project: **1**
- Consist of **5 Essentials** and **3 Electives**
The Professional Consulting Capstone Course will be a year-long course in the form of capstone classes, industry analytics seminars, and a **3 – 6 month full-time^ capstone project**. ^Part-time students are recommended to do their capstone project with the company they are working for.
Essential Courses: Students will complete **5 essential courses** to build a cross-disciplinary foundation for Business Analytics and engage in rigorous study beyond the assumed disciplinary borders. This covers the interface between computer science, statistics, and other professional disciplines in the NUS Education framework.
- Analytics in Managerial Economics
- Data Management and Warehousing
- Operations Research and Analytics
- Foundations of Business Analytics
- Advanced Analytics and Machine Learning
Elective Courses (From 5 Verticals): In addition to essential courses, students are required to take **three elective courses from at most two** of the following vertical sectors. Students who aspire to be a Business Analytics expert in other vertical sectors beyond the five below may take relevant advanced courses from the respective participating faculties, subject to approval by the Academic Committee.
- Big Data Analytics Techniques: Big Data Analytics Technology; Cloud Computing; Neural Networks and Deep Learning
- Consumer Data Analytics: Hands-on with Business Analytics (Consumer); Introduction to Network Science & Analytics
- Financial & Risk Analytics: Fintech, Enabling Technologies and Analytics; Quantitative Risk Management
- Healthcare Analytics: Economic Methods in Healthcare Technology Assessment; Analytics For Better Health; Information Technology in Healthcare
- Statistical Modelling: Applied Regression Analysis; Survival Analysis; Deep Learning in Data Analytics
*This list is not exhaustive and subject to change.*

program_overview.content:
Develop your understanding of business analytics. You’ll graduate with the skills you need to start a career specialising in data and decision analysis. This course is for graduates who want to pursue a career in business analytics. The course teaches how companies can use ‘big data’ to gain business insight and how to convert data into knowledge. Students get hands-on practical experience using the latest business intelligence software and interpreting real data.
This course includes guest lectures from industry experts, and a unit co-delivered by a specialist from IBM. It is in partnership with IBM, Qlik, WinPure and [the Women in OR & Analytics Network](https://www.theorsociety.com/get-involved/society-groups/special-interest-groups-and-networks/women-in-or-analytics-network/).
- An MSc in Business Analytics gives you a range of career opportunities across different sectors.
- Students get practical experience in computer programming and the latest business analytics software.
- Small, carefully-selected class sizes allow for plenty of individual interaction with academics, career advisors and industry experts.
- Graduates are equipped with the skills global employers want; big data's importance to businesses is growing, and graduates are in high demand.
- A dissertation based on real data might allow you to work with a partner company. [Watch Business Analytics students share their experience of doing an industrial dissertation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LYcI9L6r07w).
- Meetings with graduates, business challenges and careers fairs give experience of the global job market.
The MSc in Business Analytics is ranked top 100 in the world and UK top 10 in the [QS Business Masters rankings 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/business-masters-rankings/business-analytics).
The School combines the latest research with opportunities to apply it. Students develop key professional skills and work with partner organisations on optional projects from day one. Graduates have a great employment record; most go on to careers in a range of areas, start their own business or begin a PhD. 81% of 2022 and 2023 graduates had accepted a job offer within three months of completing their degree.
[The School of Management building opened in June 2022](https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/the-school-of-managements-home/). The latest technology provides a flexible and modern learning environment, with an open layout to enable teamwork and a dedicated Employability Hub for meeting and networking with industry partners.
Students learn from staff with backgrounds and expertise in relevant areas of business analytics. The course has been designed so the available units complement each other to meet its overall aims. Timetabled contact hours, made up of lectures, seminars, tutorials and laboratory classes, are typically between 10 and 16 hours a week during the taught semesters. Additional briefing sessions support preparation for the dissertation period and live projects. Students receive direct guidance from an allocated member of academic staff for dissertation activity. Independent learning and assessment is typically around 25 - 30 hours per week.
Assessment includes individual and group assignments, examinations, written submissions, live presentations and recorded videos. Assessment is designed to support professional development in important business skills. The final degree grade is determined by a weighted average of the taught semesters (two thirds) and the dissertation/practice activity (one third).

curriculum.content:
- Course title: Business Analytics
- Final award: MSc
- Mode of study: Full-time
- Location: University of Bath, Claverton Down, Bath BA2 7AY
Units include:
- Business statistics and forecasting: 10 credits
- Databases and business intelligence: 10 credits
- Optimisation and spreadsheet modelling: 10 credits
- Analytics in practice: 5 credits
- Data mining and machine learning: 10 credits
- Heuristics and simulation: 10 credits
Optional units:
- Advanced business forecasting: 5 credits
- Advanced data visualisation: 5 credits
- Operations strategy: 5 credits
- Project management: 5 credits
- Dissertation in business analytics: 30 credits
Dissertation in business analytics: **30 credits**. Complete a written research project. You'll find a business analytics problem in an area that interests you, investigate the problem using an existing technique or by developing your own method, come up with a way to solve the problem, interpret your results, derive insights from them and suggest courses of action, and have the chance to work on a real analytics challenge set by one of our industrial partners.
Timetabled contact hours, which can be made up of lectures, seminars, tutorials and laboratory classes, vary throughout your course and between courses but are typically between 10 and 16 hours a week during the taught semesters. Additional briefing sessions will be provided to help you prepare for the dissertation period and as part of the co-curricular offering of live projects. You will receive direct guidance from an allocated member of academic staff for your dissertation activity.
As well as timetabled contact hours, you're expected to undertake independent learning and assessment. Typically, this might be around 25 - 30 hours per week, and include individual research, reading journal articles and books, working on individual and group projects, preparing coursework, presentations, or revising for exams.
Assessment includes individual and group assignments, as well as examinations. The work required may include written submissions, live presentations and recorded videos. The final degree grade is determined by a weighted average of the taught semesters (two thirds) and the dissertation/practice activity (one third).

application_materials.content:
Throughout your application you will be given the opportunity to upload scanned documents in support of your application. **A decision on your application may be delayed if the relevant supporting documents are not received.** The following information will usually be needed before a decision can be made on your application:
- Academic reference(s)
- Degree transcripts (interim transcripts)
- English language test certificate (if appropriate)
- Research proposal (if appropriate)
Scanned transcripts and certificates need to be uploaded in the Education section. This page is also where you can upload English language requirement documents. In the Professional/Work experience section, you can upload your CV and detail any relevant work experience that may be beneficial to your application, with space for professional or other qualifications.
Personal statement: approximately **5,000 characters**, explaining why you are interested in studying on your chosen programme. This can be uploaded to the personal statement section in **PDF or Microsoft Word format**, or typed within the application portal. The statement should show interest and commitment to the subject and address: passion for your subject; why you; preparation and evidence of relevant skills; and why Birmingham / why this particular course.
References: you may either upload references if you already have them, or input referee details so the University can contact them after submission. The referee’s contact email address must be an official email address, not a personal one. The University recommends the reference is sent in **PDF format** and, preferably, that it:
- Is on official headed paper with the organisation or university’s logo and address
- Includes the date, your details and the referee’s details
- Summarises how the referee knows you and confirms your suitability for studying on the course
- Is signed by the referee with their official contact details
If you already have a written reference and upload it on behalf of your referee, it must be a scanned copy of the original and on official headed paper. A referee can also email the reference directly to [pgadmissions@contacts.bham.ac.uk](mailto:pgadmissions@contacts.bham.ac.uk) from their official email address, including their full name and role. For the vast majority of programmes, references are not required for a decision to be made; if an offer is made and references are outstanding, they will form part of the offer conditions.
Academic certificate and transcript(s) for all prior degrees: if you have graduated, upload a scan of your original or certified copies of your degree certificate(s) and transcript(s). If you are currently a student, upload an interim transcript from your latest exams. Otherwise your application cannot be considered. You may be asked to send original or certified copies for verification.
Proof of English Language skills: you can scan and upload a copy of your results to the Postgraduate Application Portal. Test results must be no more than two years old from the start date of your course.

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc is delivered in person at Birmingham (Edgbaston), starts in September 2026, lasts 1 year full-time, and awards a Master of Science. The programme is Triple Crown Accredited and ranked Top 70 globally in Business Analytics in the QS Business Masters Rankings 2026.
The MSc Business Analytics programme allows students to gain an understanding of the theory and practice behind business analytics, developing the business understanding, data analytic skills, and ability to communicate insights needed to support informed business decisions. It is suited to those from a variety of backgrounds who are interested in conducting detailed data analysis and translating these insights to resolve practical business issues for organisations from start-ups to global companies.
Programme highlights include:
- Through the Business Analytics Capstone Project, students have the opportunity to gain relevant work experience by analysing a set of data and delivering their findings.
- Students can tailor the programme towards their interests with the Business Analytics micro-courses.
- Students develop the ability to analyse data sets and communicate insights, a skill highly in demand by companies across the globe.
- Birmingham has the largest city economy outside of London with key links to global companies, giving students the opportunity to network with a variety of organisations.
Students have the opportunity to take part in the award-winning Future Leaders Certificate, an extra-curricular programme involving an exciting virtual live project set by a multi-national company. The Future Leaders Certificate helps students understand the impact technology is having on the business world and the implications for their own career.
Birmingham Business School is one of a small number of schools worldwide to hold triple-crown accreditation from the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA) and the European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS).
Course delivery includes a wide variety of learning and teaching: taught modules including lectures, seminars, tutorials, project and case analysis; assessments including essays and reports, group assessments, presentations and case analysis; and a Capstone Project in which students work in a team to develop a working solution to a live analytics problem. The course comprises 180 credits, taught through a series of 20 credit modules and a 60 credit Capstone Project. As a research-intensive University, teaching is informed by the latest academic thinking and expertise of staff.
Programme Director: [**Robert Fleming**](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/staff/profiles/business/fleming-robert.aspx), Programme Director, MSc Business Analytics. Robert is an experienced programme director with over twenty years' experience.
Career opportunities: This programme allows students to tackle real-world challenges, using data analysis to evaluate the success of previous business projects and forecast future decisions. This skillset is highly in demand by businesses looking to become more efficient and increase growth. The MSc Business Analytics programme is also useful for those who run their own organisations, allowing them to gain an overview of the datasets available and what this means for their business.
Business School students access specialist careers guidance tailored to the global business landscape, including dedicated Business School careers consultants, targeted career coaching, exclusive employer networking events, business-focused careers fairs, direct connections to top graduate recruiters, tailored workshops, one-to-one consultations, and an extensive alumni network. The University is one of the most consistently targeted UK universities by top graduate employers according to the High Fliers report, The Graduate Market 2026.
Student stories include Business Analytics MSc students Gesare Ombati, Hazel, Jawad Zaarif, and Shafkat Rahman, and Business Analytics alumni Poojan Pavagadhi.

academic_requirements.content:
- You will typically need **an upper second-class honours degree or an international equivalent in a quantitative subject** (whether as a single, joint or combined honours degree) such as Accounting and Finance, Actuarial Sciences, Computer Science, Data Science, Economics, Engineering, Finance, International Economics and Trade, Mathematics, Physics, Commerce (with specialism in Accounting/Finance/Economics).
- If your degree is not listed above, you need **a 2:1 or equivalent in two different quantitative units** from the [Maths qualification requirements](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/taught/msc-business-analytics/#accordion-163258) list.
- Alternatively, you need **A-level Mathematics with grade A** if there are no mathematics or quantitative units in your degree.
- If your degree subject is not listed in the main entry requirements, you must have evidence of **an upper second class honours degree which includes two units of mathematics with 60% or above (or international equivalent) in each unit**. Examples of acceptable units include Advanced Maths, Algebra/Linear Algebra, Calculus, Financial Maths, Maths, Pure Maths, Business Mathematics, Business Statistics, Computer Science (including programming/algorithms), Data Mining/Data Science/Data Analytics, Derivatives, Econometrics, Financial Modelling, Financial Statement Analysis, Investment Analysis, Probability, Quantitative Methods, Quantitative Research Methods, and Statistics/Statistical Methods/Statistical Analysis.
- We will consider your application if your interim grades are currently slightly lower than the programme's entry requirements and may make you an aspirational offer; you would need to achieve the standard entry requirements by the end of your degree, and specific module requirements would still apply.
- If your achieved grade is lower than the entry requirements, your application may be more likely to receive an offer if you have additional relevant work experience or qualifications, including **relevant work experience (5 years minimum)** in Digital Marketing, Data/Business Analytics, Data Science, Data Engineering, Banking and Finance, or other sectors requiring expertise in business/data analytics/analysis and/or statistics, or **a relevant postgraduate qualification**.
- China-specific: To be considered for admission to a master's degree programme at the University of Bristol, the minimum requirement is typically an undergraduate degree from an acceptable institution equivalent to a UK upper second-class degree (2:1). Applicants who hold **a four-year bachelor's (honours) degree from an accepted Chinese university with a minimum of 78% - 87%** will be considered; the required percentage depends on the undergraduate university and the programme applied for. Qualifications from selected institutions may require accreditation.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
For Profile B, postgraduate programmes require the listed English language level. Accepted tests are valid when taken **no more than two years before the start date** of the programme; component scores must be met fully through **one sitting** of the test and scores cannot be combined from multiple certificates.
- IELTS Academic / IELTS Academic for UKVI: **PG: 7.0 overall with 6.5 in all skills**.
- TOEFL iBT and TOEFL at Home: for tests taken up to **20 January 2026**, **PG: 95 overall with R22, L21, S23, W22**; for tests taken from **21 January 2026 onwards**, **PG: 5 overall with 4.5 in all skills**.
- Pearson PTE Academic / Pearson PTE Academic UKVI: **PG: 71 overall with no lower than 67 in all skills**.
- C1 Advanced (CAE): **PG: Grade C, or Level B2 with 176 in all skills**.
- C2 Proficiency (CPE): **Grade C, or Level C1 with 184 in writing and 176 in all other skills**.
- Trinity Integrated Skills in English (ISE): **PG: Level III or IV test with 105 overall and 96 in all skills**.
- LanguageCert Academic / LanguageCert Academic SELT: **PG: C1 level with 75 overall and 70 in all skills**.
- Skills for English: **C1 Pass or C2 Pass**.
- Other accepted English Language Proficiency Tests include NCUK EAP; University of Portsmouth Pre-Sessional English; Heriot-Watt Pre-Sessional English; Strathclyde ELT; Kaplan EAP; Oxford International ELLT; University of Warwick EAP; and AEMG Direct Entry Programme EAP, with the listed Profile B grades.
Applicants who are nationals of listed English-speaking countries will generally be exempt from providing additional evidence of English language ability. Applicants who have studied one of the listed qualifications in an English-speaking country may meet the University's English language requirements: final four years of high school education; two years of a full-time Bachelor's degree; one year of a Master's degree; or two years of a TNE/international partnership degree. In all cases, **the qualification must have been awarded no more than seven years prior to the start of the degree programme**.
Applicants with a university-level qualification listed above, when fully taught and examined in English, may also meet the University's English language requirements with an official Medium of Instruction (MOI) letter confirming that English is the medium of teaching and examination, or an ECCTIS English Language Proficiency Statement confirming the degree is comparable to an English language level of C1 or above.
Applicants can demonstrate ongoing engagement with English post-study through work experience in a listed English-speaking country if they have worked for **a minimum of two years** where the main language for the role was English, the role involved daily professional use of English, and the role ended **no more than two years before** the course start date. The University reserves the right to refuse an English language exemption if it has concerns about an applicant's abilities.

program_overview.content:
The MSc Business Analytics is a professionally accredited, one-year specialist programme for students aiming to master the latest techniques in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. Students develop skills to integrate advanced data analytics with business decision-making, bridge the gap between technical expertise and business leadership, and collaborate effectively with decision-makers in diverse organisational contexts.
Accredited by the [Institute of Analytics (IoA)](https://ioaglobal.org/), MSc Business Analytics emphasises professional and ethical standards while enhancing employability. Designed with industry insights from leading organisations such as IBM, NHS, Amazon, and Barilla Group, and enriched by alumni feedback, it delivers a cutting-edge education.
The programme offers opportunities to work with the Professional Liaison Network (PLN) on consulting projects, providing hands-on experience with organisations. Students work on real-world challenges with partners like Barilla, Yeo Valley, Financial Times, IBM, and Bristol Airport, covering topics such as resource allocation, people analytics, customer segmentation, performance measurement, healthcare workforce analysis, and renewable energy systems automation.
Students gain experience with decision-support tools such as:
- Python
- R
- MS Excel
- Tableau for data visualisation
- Lingo for ad-hoc analytics
Alumni and industry panel discussions, guest lectures by business analytics experts from a variety of sectors, career development workshops, technology sessions on industry tools such as PowerBI, SQL, and @RISK, and mentorship programmes connecting students with alumni and industry experts are integral elements.
The programme covers:
- Mastering data identification, extraction, and cleaning techniques to ensure high-quality datasets.
- Applying statistical and machine learning methods for data mining and predictive analytics.
- Formulating and executing statistical and mathematical models to drive optimal business decisions.
- Visualising, interpreting, and communicating the results of statistical analyses to inform decision-making.
The programme is taught at the Temple Quarter Enterprise Campus, with enhanced links with businesses providing real-world knowledge, networks and skills, and students also benefit from access to student services and facilities at the Clifton Campus.
Key information: Programme duration is one year full-time; delivery method is on-campus; location is [Temple Quarter](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/temple-quarter-enterprise-campus/) as the main location and [Clifton campus](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/clifton-campus/); award available is MSc.
Successful completion of four core units, two optional units, and a final business analytics dissertation project lead to an MSc Business Analytics award. In the first term, core units provide a foundation in descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. In the second term, students can choose electives to deepen expertise. Students attend the mandatory Business Analytics Consulting Project unit, applying knowledge to real-life business problems for an external client. In the summer term, students undertake the Business Analytics Dissertation Project, applying acquired knowledge to research a topic of interest, enhancing critical analysis skills, exploring real-world business problems, providing practical solutions, and communicating findings to relevant stakeholders.
The MSc Business Analytics programme addresses the growing demand for business analytics expertise in the UK and globally. Graduates have secured roles at leading organizations including PwC China, Capgemini, Deloitte South Asia, Reckitt, Volkswagen, EDF Trading, Jaguar Land Rover UK, 3Vision, Low Carbon Contracts Company, Play Sports Network, and MTC - Manufacturing Technology Centre. Graduates pursue careers across industries such as technology, consulting, finance, automotive, manufacturing, and analytical roles. Common career paths include Business Analytics Specialist/Professional, Management Consultant, Product Manager, Market Research Analyst/Digital Marketing Specialist, Operations/Data Analyst, Modelling/Data Scientist, Business Operations Analytics Specialist, HR/People/Insurance Analytics Specialist, and Financial Analyst.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
Offers made may be conditional or unconditional. An unconditional offer will be made to applicants who have already met the conditions and provided evidence that conditions have been met. Where academic or language requirements have not yet been fulfilled, applicants will receive a conditional offer outlining the requirements that must be met.
Applicants who receive a conditional offer will be required to submit all final results to meet their offer conditions by the date noted in their offer letter. Offer holders who are unable to provide their final results by this date should email choosebristol-pg@bristol.ac.uk to notify the team as soon as possible.

application_materials.content:
Applicants must submit the following documents by the specified deadline:
- Academic/professional certificates: for all applicants, both graduation and professional qualification certificates. For degrees obtained from Chinese Mainland: both degree (學位證書) and graduation (畢業證書) certificates printed in Chinese, plus valid Online Verification Reports of Higher Education Qualification Certificates (教育部學歷證書電子註冊備案表) and Degree Certificates (中國高等教育學位在線驗證報告) issued from CHESICC for Mainland China degrees.
- Official transcripts and grading schemes: all copies of official transcripts and grading schemes with explanatory notes for all tertiary education. E-transcripts must be sent directly by the issuing university; paper transcripts must be in a sealed envelope issued by the university. Transcripts must bear official seal; unofficial or improper letterhead documents will not be accepted. Non-English/Chinese transcripts require certified English translation. CUHK graduates can submit photocopies of transcripts, excluding CUHK (Shenzhen); the University reserves the right to require an original copy.
- English language proficiency documents: submit one of the listed documents, such as a copy of graduation certificate issued by a university in Hong Kong; a certifying letter from the Registry confirming the medium of instruction was English; an official score report of TOEFL, IELTS (Academic), or GMAT (Verbal); specified Hong Kong examination results; certified true copy of GCE A-level or AS-level/CUHK Matriculation Examination English results; or certified true copy of a recognised professional qualification where the examination was in English.
- Confidential recommendations: for other programmes, **two referee reports are required**. Submit referee information via the [Online Application System](https://www.gradsch.cuhk.edu.hk/OnlineApp/login_email.aspx).
- Identification documents: Hong Kong Identity Card or other identity document.
- Qualification assessment: degrees awarded by overseas universities by distance learning or by completing a curriculum of short duration may be required to provide [HKCAAVQ](https://www.hkcaavq.edu.hk/en/) assessment on the level of qualification obtained.
- **Applicants will be required to complete an Authorisation Form for the University to verify their academic qualifications.** The programme staff may further contact applicants to proceed with applying for academic verification from a third-party organization, e.g. Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE), as needed.
Submitted documents are non-returnable; materials from unsuccessful applications will be destroyed after the completion of the admission exercise.

program_overview.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics is an advanced one-year programme designed to train professionals to analyse data with quantitative tools and convert it into useful information. Students are equipped to guide strategic decision making for organisations all over the world.
Students are trained in statistical tools and quantitative methods to explore and investigate mass data. Under the guidance of professionals, they learn to make extensive use of data, identify key insights about performance, predict market changes and improve strategic decisions.
**Duration:** Full-time: 1 year. **Programme commencement:** September.
Students study in Hong Kong, a global centre of finance and logistics, with geographical proximity to China. CUHK Business School was the first to offer an MSc in Business Analytics in Hong Kong, giving students access to experienced professionals with in-depth knowledge of the market and state-of-the-art facilities.
The advanced curriculum is highly flexible, with a wide range of electives so students can tailor their studies to their interests. By the end of the programme, graduates are prepared for careers in business consulting, finance, marketing, retail, logistics and supply chain management, and other service industries.
The programme was set up in response to the growing demand for data-driven decision making, with the aim of filling a significant skills gap in the industry. It is designed for those with a keen mind for numbers and statistics.
**1st** MSc in Business Analytics programme in Greater China.
An alumna describes the programme as taught by “internationally renowned professors” using teaching methods such as group projects, case studies, simulations, guest speakers and real-life examples, providing in-depth market insights, critical thinking development, and exposure to Asian business culture.

curriculum.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics is a full-time, **1-year** programme commencing in September. To complete the programme, students need to attain **30 credits of coursework**, comprising **5 core courses and 5 elective courses worth 3 credits each**.
Programme schedule notes: Core and elective courses are subject to change. Courses are taught in English, except when Chinese is preferable. Elective courses may be offered in the form of an intensive course every alternate year or in the summer term.
Full-time Programme (1 Year):
- Term 1 Sep-Nov: 3 core courses; 1-2 elective courses
- Term 2 Dec-Mar: 1 core course; 1-2 elective courses
- Term 3 Mar-Jun: 1 core course; 1-2 elective courses
Core courses:
- [Statistical Analysis](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-0)
- [Decision Models and Applications](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-1)
- [Data Mining for Managers](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-2)
- [Machine Learning for Business I](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-3)
- [Advanced Business Analytics Practicum](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-curriculum-1-4): requires students to complete a real-world information systems project, in collaboration with a company or an organisation, in a project team under the joint supervision of a teacher and an executive of the sponsoring company.
Elective courses include:
- Managing Service Operations
- Economic Analytics
- Web Analytics and Intelligence
- Business Process Analysis and Simulation
- Database and Big Data Management
- Supply Chain and Logistics Management
- Technology Field Study
- Machine Learning for Business II
- Fintech and Its Applications
- Business Field Study
- Risk and Operations Analytics
- Generative Artificial Intelligence for Business
- Selected Topics of Information and Technology Management: Building AI for Business
- Selected Topics in Business Analytics: Marketing Intelligence
Other elective courses: Students may take up to **6-credits-worth** of courses from other programmes within CUHK Business School or from the Faculty of Engineering, subject to approval by Programme Directors. Courses may include Customer Relationship Management, Mergers and Acquisitions, Financial Analysis and Security Trading, and Organisational Marketing.
Course exemption: Students may be exempt from taking a course if they have completed an equivalent course in postgraduate studies and achieved a grade B or above. Students may be exempt from a maximum of **6 credits**, subject to approval, and need to substitute these exempt credits with other elective courses.
Graduation requirements: To graduate, students must complete the prescribed coursework and achieve a cumulative grade-point average (GPA) of at least **2.50**. Students who receive a grade D+ or below in a course must repeat the course or take an approved substitute course.
Overseas field trip elective courses include:
- [Technology Field Study (Elective Course)](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-eal-6a517ba0813a6): preparatory assignments in readings and a written study plan, followed by a five-day residential programme to Silicon Valley, California or similar Science Parks in Asia, concluded with a written report and an oral presentation.
- [Business Field Study (Elective Course)](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/mscba/?tab=curriculum#collapse-eal-6a517ba08140c): preparatory assignments in readings and a written study plan, followed by a five to seven-day residential programme in a selected country or economy outside of Hong Kong, concluded with a written report and oral presentation.
Non-local students, subject to endorsement from the Programme Director, may take curriculum-related internships for up to **one-third of the duration of the programme**.
The programme offers highly flexible personalised pathways for specialisations in fintech, digital marketing, business intelligence and supply chain analytics.

Eligible candidate could reimburse up to **HK$20,000** once successfully completed the course. For details, please check with programme office.
- A wide range of scholarships is offered by CUHK Business School and specific Master’s programmes to outstanding candidates. These scholarships encompass both admission-based and merit-based awards.

The Programmes will identify qualified students and inform the selected students of the scholarship offers.
- **BOC-CUHK International Scholarship** is designed to support outstanding students from ASEAN countries who wish to further pursue their postgraduate studies at CUHK Business School. To be eligible, applicants must be admitted into one of the listed CUHK Business School Master’s Programmes, including **MSc in Business Analytics**. Scholars will be entitled to 60% coverage of tuition fees, work on a practicum project sponsored by BOCHK during the study period, and fast-track interview opportunities to work for BOC offices in HK or SEA upon graduation.
- **BTS Group Scholarship** aims to support students from Thailand to pursue their graduate degree in business at CUHK Business School. Scholars will be awarded **HK$120,000 in tuition**, in addition to a living expenses of **HK$30,000**.
- **Scholarship for Malaysian students**: Support outstanding students who are Malaysian citizen to pursue Master’s studies at CUHK Business School. Scholars will be awarded up to **HK$320,000 in tuition**.
- Different scholarship schemes will be awarded to exceptional candidates based on the decision of each Master’s programme below: **MSc in Business Analytics**.
- [Merit-based Scholarships](https://masters.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/tuitionfee-financialaid-scholarships/#collapse-3510f69a-2): Students who consistently excel in academic performance and professional development are eligible to receive the award for their outstanding achievements. There is no need to submit a separate application for the majority of our merit-based scholarships; some scholarships schemes may require application.
- **Additional Opportunities**: MSc in Business Analytics also provide different varieties of merit-based scholarship scheme to outstanding student during Master’s study. Respective programme will evaluate eligible students and communicate scholarship offers directly to the selected individuals.

multiple_applications.content: You can apply for multiple programmes, but you must submit separate applications and pay the application fees for each programme. The paid application fee is non-refundable and non-transferable. If admitted to multiple programmes, you can only enrol in one. All fees paid to the previous programmes will not be refunded or transferred.

deferral_admission_policy.content:

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics (MSc) is a **1-year full-time** programme starting 28 September 2026. The programme allows you to develop practical in-demand skills for extracting and handling ‘big data’, with a specific focus on applying data analytics for decision-making in real-life business contexts.
You’ll learn from experts in Cardiff Business School and the School of Mathematics who specialise in applications of data science, operational research and analytics across manufacturing and service industries, discovering and communicating meaningful patterns from data and applying analytical tools to help private and public sector businesses make better strategic and operational decisions.
The programme combines advanced software with core business and mathematical theory and practice, preparing students for employment in an interconnected, diverse and rapidly evolving global business arena. It provides grounding for careers in analytics, data management and consultancy roles.
Key areas include operations analytics, time series and forecasting, strategic operations management, enterprise research planning, risk management, research skills, data analysis and machine learning. Students use real-world advanced simulation systems and games to manage a virtual company in a competitive market, supporting learning through a dynamic business environment.
The programme runs from September to September. During the **Taught Stage** (September-June), students study 120 credits of taught modules. During the **Dissertation Stage** (July-September), students undertake a dissertation project. Optional modules allow students to tailor learning to their interests and career aspirations. On successful completion of the taught stage, students undertake an independent research project focused on applications of data analytics in the real business world and may have the opportunity to conduct a live project, subject to academic performance.
The course is based in [Cardiff Business School](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/business-school), an AACSB International and AMBA-accredited Business School located at Colum Road, Cathays, Cardiff, CF10 3EU.
An employability focus is embedded throughout the programme, including case studies and assessments that mirror workplace challenges. Although the programme does not include a formal placement, students benefit from experiential and work-based learning opportunities such as guest lectures and site visits. Strong links with research groups and industrial partners offer networking and exposure to potential employers. Within the dissertation phase, students may be offered the opportunity, subject to academic performance, to undertake a project with an industrial partner through a competitive process.
