program_overview.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics equips you with cutting-edge skills in AI, data science, and decision-making, empowering you to turn big data into strategic business insights and drive innovation, efficiency, and competitive advantage in today’s data-driven world.
Course details: Degree type: MSc; Course code: G5K709; Course length: 1 year full-time; Start date: [September 2026](https://www.durham.ac.uk/business/courses/business-analytics-g5k709/september-2026/).
Our MSc in Business Analytics will equip you with the skills and knowledge to harness AI-driven analytics for gaining competitive business insights from big data. With businesses increasingly relying on Artificial Intelligence and advanced analytics to understand and predict customer behaviour, optimise internal processes, and manage suppliers effectively, this programme prepares you to navigate and lead in this data-driven world.
In a supportive, research-led learning environment, you will explore the complexities of big data, machine learning, and natural language processing, applying cutting-edge AI techniques to extract key insights and drive strategic decision-making. You will benefit from the programme’s strong international connections and gain hands-on experience with AI-powered analytics on the [**International Field Trip**](https://www.durham.ac.uk/business/programmes/masters/business-analytics-international-field-trip/). A key part of your studies, where you can turn your learning into action, is the [**Business Analytics Project**](https://www.durham.ac.uk/business/programmes/masters/business-analytics-projects/) - a unique opportunity to tackle real-world business challenges using data-driven insights. Additionally, you will have the opportunity to engage with industry leaders and renowned scholars through Business School presentations, featuring major global multinationals and leading academic experts.
Delivered full-time over one year, the programme is led by the **Department of Computer Science** and co-delivered and co-managed with the **Business School**, combining expertise from both departments to provide a well-rounded education in AI-driven business analytics. The Business School is one of the longest established in the UK, with a reputation for academic excellence and state-of-the-art learning facilities. It is also one of an elite group of institutions in the UK to be accredited by all three major business education accreditation bodies: the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB), the Association of MBAs (AMBA) and the European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS). The Department of Computer Science is ranked 11th out of 117 universities in the Complete University Guide 2026.
World class Business Education: **50th in the World** - QS Global Business Masters Rankings 2026: Business Analytics.
Your MSc Business Analytics programme consists of a set of core modules beginning with an in-depth understanding and introduction to Business Analytics, through to modules that will provide you with an appreciation of, and the ability to apply, a range of predictive and prescriptive business analytics techniques. A highlight of the programme is the International Field Trip, with the programme culminating in the Business Analytics Project.
As part of the programme, you will be encouraged to attend presentations by leading academics and professionals who are specialists in your particular area of interest. Past speakers have included representatives of major global multinationals and leading scholars, combining critical and progressive thinking with practical insights.
The course is taught through a mixture of lectures, seminars and practicals as well as the requirement to complete a major dissertation. There is also a major International Field trip, which takes place in the third term. Practicals are medium sized group sessions, where you will practice computer software, applying topics from lectures and seminars.
The Business Analytics Project makes up one-third of your marks and is assessed through a 15,000-word document that tests your acquisition of relevant subject-specific knowledge and skills and your ability to apply these, and appropriate key skills, in the context of a Masters-level research project.
You will be taught at our Business School, Waterside. This additional building will complement our current Mill Hill Lane site, and both sites will deliver a world-class business teaching and learning experience. Waterside is nestled in the heart of Durham City Centre, just a few minutes walk from the railway station, along the scenic banks of the River Wear.
The Department of Computer Science’s academic fusion of technology and independent thinking places it firmly at the cutting edge of computer learning. Learning from academics who lead cutting-edge research provides valuable insight into high quality projects, and gives our postgraduate community the opportunity to play a role in shaping a future in which crucial developments in society are supported by technological innovation. Researchers in the Department offer a range of expertise across the computer science spectrum in areas such as artificial intelligence, data science, bioinformatics, high-performance computing, graphics and fundamental algorithms. The Department keeps close links with local high-technology industries as well as national and international employers.
Our postgraduate programmes with a focus on employability fully equip you with the skills and industry insight to embark on a successful and rewarding business career. You gain a combination of analytical and practical skills that employers value, such as independent thinking and problem-solving, and are able to enhance your people skills that are essential in business and much sought after by employers.

curriculum.content:
Course length: **1 year full-time**.
Delivered full-time over one year, the MSc Business Analytics programme is led by the **Department of Computer Science** and co-delivered and co-managed with the **Business School**.
The programme consists of a set of core modules beginning with an in-depth understanding and introduction to Business Analytics, through to modules that provide an appreciation of, and the ability to apply, a range of predictive and prescriptive business analytics techniques. A highlight of the programme is the International Field Trip, with the programme culminating in the Business Analytics Project.
Core modules:
- Introduction to Business Analytics
- Data Analytics in Action
- Learning from Data
- Managing Data Driven Innovation
- Natural Language Analysis
- Retail Analytics
- Data Analytics for Strategic Decision-Making
- Data Analytics in Action - International Field Trip
- Business Analytics Project
The International Field Trip aims to provide experiential learning needed to acquire an inside perspective of operating globally. Students visit a series of data-intensive participating organisations, analyse each organisation using a structured learning approach, and present their analysis to representatives of the participating organisations.
The Business Analytics Project requires an in-depth investigation into an issue applicable and relevant to business analytics, underpinned by business analytics approaches, methods and techniques covered in the other modules. Students choose a project either by working with a host organisation or by producing an issue-led investigation, and the project is supervised by a faculty member.
The course is taught through a mixture of lectures, seminars and practicals as well as the requirement to complete a major dissertation. There is also a major International Field Trip, which takes place in the third term.
Assessment includes written assignments and combinations of written assignments and individual and group presentations. The Business Analytics Project makes up **one-third of your marks** and is assessed through a **15,000-word document**.

academic_requirements.content:
Entrance to the **MSc in Business Analytics** is strongly competitive; applicants can increase their chances by exceeding the minimum programme requirements.
- You will need a **UK first-class or 2:1 honours degree** in a related subject, or an **equivalent overseas qualification**.
- An undergraduate degree in any disciplinary area related to **management science, operational research, statistics, econometrics, mathematics, physics, computer science, engineering, or business and management** which incorporates a distinct quantitative element is required.
- Candidates with a first-class or 2:1 honours degree in an unrelated subject area but who have relevant work experience will be considered on an individual basis.
- Candidates' background should ideally include courses and/or experience in topics such as **linear algebra, calculus, probability, statistics, and computer programming**.
- Relevant work experience is not required but may increase your chances of acceptance.
- Relevant professional qualifications will be considered.
- Preference will be given to those with grades above the minimum requirements due to strong competition for places on this programme.
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as their studies will be completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date.
- If your degree is not of the required standard and you do not have highly relevant work or other experience, the application will normally be rejected.
- Meeting the degree requirement does not ensure acceptance; a higher standard may be needed for admission or funding.
- A conditional offer can be made if you are waiting for a final degree result.
International qualification examples for the minimum academic requirement include:
- Canada: **B+; 3.25+ (4 point scale); 7+ (9 point scale)**
- China: **85%+; Band A from the [Priority list of Chinese universities](https://www.ed.ac.uk/sites/default/files/atoms/files/priority_list_of_chinese_universities.pdf)**
- Germany: **2.2+ (reverse 5 point scale); Sehr Gut/Gut**
- India: **1st Class degree (60%+); 3.2 on a 4 point scale; 8.0 on a 10 point scale**
- Nigeria: **2:1**
- South Africa: **2:1/1st**
- USA: **GPA 3.25+ (4 point scale)**
For applicants from China: this degree programme is **Band A**, requiring a **minimum of 85% awarded by a Chinese university on the Priority List**. General Edinburgh China guidance states that postgraduate taught applicants should have a first degree from a university on the Priority List of Chinese universities or a recognised university, with minimum grades between **80-85%**; for **Band A**, the requirement is **a minimum of 85% awarded by a university on the Priority List**.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
Regardless of nationality or country of residence, applicants must demonstrate a level of English language competency which will enable them to succeed in their studies.
Accepted English language qualifications at the specified grades:
- [IELTS Academic](https://www.ielts.org/): **total 7.0 with at least 6.0 in each component**. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) before 21 January 2026: **total 100 with at least 20 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [TOEFL iBT](http://www.ets.org/toefl) (including Home Edition) from 21 January 2026: **total 5.0 with at least 4.0 in each component**. TOEFL MyBest Score is not accepted.
- [C1 Advanced](https://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/advanced/) (formerly CAE) / [C2 Proficiency](http://www.cambridgeenglish.org/exams-and-tests/proficiency/) (formerly CPE): **total 185 with at least 169 in each component**.
- [Trinity ISE](https://www.trinitycollege.com/site/?id=3287): **ISE III with passes in all four components**.
- [Oxford ELLT](https://oxfordellt.com/) (Global and Digital): **8 overall with at least 6 in each component**.
Unless the applicant is a national of a majority English speaking country, the English language qualification must be no more than **three and a half years old** from the start of the month in which the programme begins. IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, Trinity ISE, or Oxford ELLT tests must be no more than **two years old** on the first of the month in which the programme begins, regardless of nationality.
The University also accepts an undergraduate or postgraduate degree taught and assessed in a majority English speaking country, as defined by UK Visas and Immigration: [UKVI list of majority English speaking countries](https://www.gov.uk/tier-4-general-visa/knowledge-of-english). It also accepts a degree taught and assessed in English from a university on the approved list: [Approved universities in non-majority English speaking countries](https://www.ed.ac.uk/studying/postgraduate/applying/your-application/entry-requirements/english-requirements/approved-universities). If the applicant is not a national of a majority English speaking country, the degree must be no more than **five years old** at the start of the month in which the programme begins.
Applicants may include an existing English language certificate with the application. If they have not yet taken a test, the application will still be processed and results can be uploaded later. A conditional offer may be given if the applicant does not yet meet the minimum English requirement, but evidence of meeting the minimum English requirement must be provided before an unconditional offer can be issued.
Optional pre-sessional English courses are available through English Language Education. General English for Academic Purposes is intended for international students who need to improve their English before starting a programme; the end-of-course assessment can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September. [English for Academic Purposes summer courses](https://www.ed.ac.uk/english-language-teaching/pre-sessional-english/summer-eap-courses)

program_overview.content:
Our MSc Business Analytics programme equips students with the computational and analytical skills demanded by employers. In an increasingly data-driven age, organisations are looking for innovative ways to use business intelligence data to gain a competitive edge. Through a curriculum that combines theoretical knowledge with practical application, this master's degree will empower you with the ability to transform raw data into impactful insights.
- **Programme structure:** The MSc Business Analytics programme offers the opportunity to develop advanced knowledge in specific areas of analytics before specialising through a choice of option courses. [View programme structure](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/business-analytics/overview/programme-structure)
- **Learning outcomes:** The programme enables students to recognise, understand, and apply the language, theory, and models of business analytics and improve problem-solving abilities. [View the learning outcomes](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/business-analytics/overview/learning-outcomes)
- **Industry opportunities:** Students can participate in industry treks, group consultancy, client sourced dissertations, and benefit from speaking to a variety of industry professionals. [Engagement with industry](https://www.business-school.ed.ac.uk/msc/business-analytics/overview/industry-opportunities)

multiple_applications.content: We recommend that you submit only one or two applications in order to have the best possible chance of receiving a positive outcome. We understand that you may find it difficult to choose between one or two related degree programmes, and we are prepared to consider more than one application in those circumstances. However, **we cannot consider more than five applications from the same applicant**, and this number may be lower in high demand areas.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Each year we have limited capacity for deferred offers. All deferral requests will be considered on an individual basis.
- The deadline for submitting a deferral request is **31 August**.
- If your deferral request is unsuccessful, you are encouraged to take up your place for entry this year, or to withdraw and submit a new application for entry next year when applications open. Because competition for places varies each year, there is no guarantee that a new application will be successful.
- If you defer your place you may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date. The new SELT will be required by **31 October** of your original entry year.
- The deposit must be paid before a deferral is agreed. This should be done within **28 days** of receiving the original offer. The deposit is non-refundable.
- We defer unconditional offers only. It is possible to defer an offer only once.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
- Final year undergraduate students are welcome to apply, so long as your studies will be **completed prior to the MSc programme commencement date**.
- A conditional offer can be made if you are waiting for a **final degree result** or a **language test result**.
- A conditional offer may be given if you do not yet meet the minimum English requirement, but you must provide evidence that you have reached the **minimum English requirement** before an unconditional offer can be provided.
- If you require a visa, you must have achieved your English qualification and have met any other conditions to qualify for an unconditional offer, which is a requirement for the CAS. The University will commence issuing CAS from **June onwards**.
- Optional pre-sessional English courses are available. General English for Academic Purposes is intended for international students who need to improve their English language level before commencing study; at the end of the course, students undertake an assessment which can be used to meet the English requirements of their Masters programme beginning in September.

application_materials.content:
- Transcript: “We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained.” Send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** the originals.
- One completed reference: Applicants should check whether one or two references are required for the programme. “You should supply at least one reference from an academic referee who is in a position to comment on the standard of your academic work and suitability for postgraduate level study.” References from other sources, such as an employer or colleague, may be accepted where an academic reference is not possible; references from family members, partners or spouses are not accepted.
- Reference submission/format: References can be uploaded via the online application system, via the Gateway after submission, posted, sent via the [enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/), or emailed by the referee from a university or company email address. References for postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If sent direct by the referee, it should come from their institutional or company email address and can be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk), along with the student reference number, name and programme of study.
- Personal statement: “not all programmes require one,” but applicants may provide one. It should be tailored to the course and include how the course links past and future, insight into abilities and fit with the course, evidence of skills/commitment/enthusiasm, reasons for wanting to study at the University of Exeter, and particular interest in the subject. Keep it **under 500 words**, use short and clear sentences, consider headings, proofread, and use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
- Essential documentation for an initial decision on taught programme applications: applicants should send as many required supporting documents as possible with the application; as a **minimum**, complete the Module Information section with details of outstanding modules and expected completion date, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application.
- International students: original copies are not required at the application stage and are not recommended during the application process. If academic or English language qualifications are not yet completed, an offer may normally be made conditional on completing these and supplying any required references; documentary evidence must be provided before the offer can be considered unconditional.

interview_requirements.content: Pre-CAS Interview: We may require you to attend an interview before we issue you with your CAS. If you are required to attend an interview, we will send you an email with details of the time and date and joining instructions. The meeting will take place via Microsoft Teams. The purpose of the Pre-CAS interview is to assess that an applicant has a genuine intent to study at the University of Exeter, it is not to assess academic abilities. Attendance at an interview is mandatory and we will be unable to issue a CAS until the interview has taken place. Applicants required to attend a Pre-CAS interview will be sent further details once they have an unconditional place and where applicable a deposit has been paid.

application_deadlines.content:
Teaching starts for most programmes in **late September**.
For **international applicants** wishing to join in 2026/2027, the application deadline is **23:59 Friday 11 September 2026** UK time.
International applicants are advised to submit a complete application by **mid-July** for September start.

academic_requirements.content:
- **A 2:2 or equivalent** from a recognised university, including **at least one mathematical / quantitative module at 2:2 or equivalent**.
- The University will consider applications where there is evidence of exceptional performance in modules relevant to the programme of study, **significant relevant work experience or professional qualifications**.

Some courses may have additional undergraduate subject-background requirements.

program_overview.content:
MSc Business Analytics is a **1 year full time** programme at **Streatham Campus**, with September-to-September or January-to-January start options depending on the chosen start month. The programme is for students interested in a career related to business analytics or wishing to study a related PhD, and teaches students how to support managers to make data driven decisions using techniques including optimisation and forecasting, analysis of data from social media and marketing, and approaches connected to environmental and global business challenges.
The programme provides foundations in business analytics, basic programming and mathematical skills, plus techniques to present and communicate data to managers. Students can flex the programme through optional areas such as Marketing Analytics, Strategic & HR Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Environmental Analytics. The programme is delivered over three terms and is University-based throughout; taught components are delivered in the first two terms, with the third term used to complete a Business Project based around a sizeable business problem and supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department.
The University of Exeter Business School is triple accredited by **AMBA, AACSB, EQUIS**. In the QS Business Master’s Rankings 2025 for Business Analytics, the programme is ranked **26th globally** for diversity and **top 90 globally** for employability. High achieving students may apply for the Quantitative Techniques for Economics and Management (QTEM) programme, which includes an additional semester at one of QTEM’s academic partners, a quantitatively focused internship, and participation in the QTEM Data Challenge.
Teaching is delivered through lectures, workshops, practical sessions, practitioner insight seminars, private study, case study development, group work, individual projects, and collaboration with industry partners. Students benefit from the University of Exeter Business School teaching environment and support resources, including the [Centre for Innovation in Business Education](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/centres/teaching/). The University has invested **£50 million** in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence capabilities through the Accelerating Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (ADA) project, which benefits the programme.
Students are taught by internationally respected academics active in the University of Exeter Business School’s research culture. The programme is embedded within the [Operations and Analytics group](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/management/about/operations-analytics/) in the Department of Management, and the [Centre for Simulation and Analytics Management](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/centres/csam/) supports research and teaching in the programme, focusing on analytical modelling and computer simulation to address real-world problems including circular economy modelling, resilience to climate change, and urgent medical and emergency care.
Graduates develop the ability to use data and analytics confidently and creatively to resolve operational and strategic problems across sectors. After graduation, students join more than 26,000 Business School alumni in over 150 countries. Graduate roles include Business Consultant, Data Consultant, Business Analyst, Supply Chain Analyst, Marketing Analyst, HR Analyst, and Business Manager, with opportunities in consulting, tech, finance, procurement, HR, marketing, public and third sector organisations, and Graduate Management schemes.

curriculum.content:
Duration: **1 year full time**. Entry year: **2026 + January 2027 start**. Campus: **Streatham Campus**.
The programme is delivered over **three terms** and is **University-based throughout this time**. The taught components are delivered in the first two terms, leaving the third term to complete the Business Project. The programme runs from **September to September** or **January to January** depending on chosen start month.
During the programme students study modules totalling **180 credits**: **120 credits of compulsory modules** and **60 credits of optional modules**. Students complete a research project / Business Project supervised by an academic from the Business and Management department, based around a sizeable business problem that draws upon business analytics skills.
Compulsory modules:

Optional modules allow students to flex the programme to suit interests and career or research aspirations, including areas such as Marketing Analytics, Strategic & HR Analytics, Operations Analytics, and Environmental Analytics.
Teaching is delivered through lectures, workshops, practical sessions, practitioner insight seminars, private study, case study development, group work, individual projects, and collaboration with industry partners. conditional_admission_policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet satisfied academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of offer conditions and how to satisfy these requirements, including [paying your deposit](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/fees/tuition-fee-deposit/), will be given in the offer letter.
- For a **full-time taught postgraduate programme**, applicants need to pay the deposit to secure their place and should pay by the deadline even if they have not yet met all the conditions of the offer.
- The deadline for meeting all conditions of the offer is normally **31 August** for September entry. Applicants must supply required documentation showing they have met outstanding academic requirements, English language and/or references, or inform the University by **31 August** what conditions are still to be met and when they expect to meet them.
- If the University does not hear from the applicant by **31 August** and outstanding conditions remain, it reserves the right to either withdraw or defer the application to the following year.
- To receive a formal unconditional offer letter and, where needed, a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies to apply for a Student Visa, applicants must meet academic conditions by providing copies of degree certificates, transcripts and references as explained in the conditional offer letter; non-academic conditions such as a [DBS](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/dbs/) check; and the required standard of English language competence by providing an English language test certificate meeting the University’s [requirements](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/).
- Offer holders who successfully complete a [Pre-Sessional English course at the University of Exeter International Study Centre](https://www.exeterisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english) and meet the requirements for progression to their chosen degree are not required to undertake an additional IELTS or TOEFL test. The University does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other INTO centres or organisations.

application_materials.content:

You have **42 days** to submit your application once you begin the process. You may save and return to your application as many times as you wish to update information, complete sections or upload supporting documents such as your final transcript or your language test. For more information about submitting documents or other topics related to applying to a postgraduate taught programme, see [how to apply for a postgraduate taught degree](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/how-to-apply-for-a-postgraduate-taught-degree/).
**Reference**: Please provide one reference. This should typically be an academic reference but in cases where this is not possible then a reference from a current employer may be accepted instead. Certain programmes, such as the MBA programme, may also accept an employer reference. If you already have a copy of a reference on letter headed paper then please upload this to your application. If you do not already have a reference to upload then please enter your referee’s name and contact details on the online application and we will contact your referee directly.
Employment and Experience: Please complete this section as fully as possible with all employments relevant to your course. Additional details may be attached in your personal statement/proposal where appropriate.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
For applicants from non-English speaking countries, as defined by the [UK Government](https://www.gov.uk/student-visa/knowledge-of-english), the University sets a minimum English Language proficiency level.
- **IELTS Academic and Academic Online (not General Training): 6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. IELTS One Skill Retake Accepted. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **TOEFL (ibt, mybest or athome)**, tests taken up to 20 January 2026: **90 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 20; Listening 19; Speaking 19; Writing 21. Tests taken from 21 January 2026: **92 Overall**, no subtest lower than Reading 22; Listening 20; Speaking 23; Writing 21. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test, this includes TOEFL mybest.
- **Pearsons PTE Academic: 65 overall** with no subtest less than Reading 60; Listening 60; Speaking 65; Writing 60. Online PTE not accepted for entry. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Cambridge Proficiency in English (CPE) and Cambridge Advanced English (CAE): 176 overall with no subtest less than 169**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Oxford English Test: 7 overall with no subtest less than 6**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **LanguageCert Academic/ Academic Online: 70 overall with no subtest less than 65**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Password Skills Plus: 6.5 overall with no subtest less than 6.0**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Trinity College Integrated Skills in English II:** two subtests at **96 or higher**, and two subtests at **80 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **Kaplan Test of English:** any two subtests at **480 or higher**, and any two subtests at **450 or higher**. Tests must have been taken within **2 years 5 months** of programme start date. Applicants must meet the overall and subtest requirements using a single test.
- **University of Glasgow Pre-sessional courses:** tests are accepted for **2 years** following date of successful completion.
Alternatives to English Language qualification:
- Degree from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have studied for a minimum of their final year at Undergraduate level, or **9 months at Master's level**, and must have completed their degree in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
- Undergraduate 2+2 and 3+1 degrees from majority-English speaking country (as defined by the UKVI including Canada if taught in English): students must have completed their final year of study in that majority-English speaking country within the last **6 years**.
For international students, the Home Office has confirmed that the University can choose to use these tests to make its own assessment of English language ability for visa applications to degree level programmes. The University is also able to accept UKVI approved Secure English Language Tests (SELT) but does not require a specific UKVI SELT for degree level programmes; it still accepts any of the English tests listed for admission to this programme.
The University of Glasgow accepts evidence of the required language level from the English for Academic Study Unit Pre-sessional courses. Pre-sessional courses give successful students direct entry to the University programme with no need to take IELTS. More information: [Pre-sessional courses](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/mlc/eas/pre-sessionalcourses/). The University can also consider pre-sessional courses accredited by BALEAP approved institutions to meet the language requirements for admission to postgraduate taught degrees: Heriot Watt, Kingston Upon Thames, Middlesex University, Manchester University, Reading University, Edinburgh University, ST Andrews University, UCL, Durham.
As part of the online application, applicants need to submit evidence of English language ability if their first language is not English. In the online application guidance, under **English Language Proficiency**, applicants should state the date of any English language test taken (or to be taken) and the award date (or expected award date if known).

program_overview.content:
The Masters in Business Analytics is designed to help you stay competitive in a data-driven world. You will learn how to turn data into valuable insights that drive business success, and gain practical skills to enhance decision-making, optimise business performance and drive innovation. This programme gives you the tools you need to excel in today’s business environment to make a real impact. It provides flexibility to suit your interests and career goals, allowing you to customise your learning path with optional courses.
- **Teaching start:** September
- [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/)
- **MSc:** 12 months full-time
- Build practical skills to solve real-world business challenges in a dynamic and blended learning environment.
- Develop critical thinking, problem-solving, and communication skills that are highly valued by employers, giving you a competitive edge.
- Explore key topics like statistical analysis, data mining, predictive modelling, and machine learning with a focus on practical business use.
- Benefit from career development tools, mentoring, and industry connections to help you succeed in business analytics and related fields.
- Get hands-on experience with tools like Python, Tableau, SQL, and R. Learn to analyse real-world data, optimise processes, and uncover insights with expert support.
- Gain valuable experience by working with live clients on [industry projects](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/business-analytics/?card=industryprojects). Bridge classroom theory with practical, real-world applications. *Industry Projects are not guaranteed. All applications are subject to availability and review processes. We will support candidates with their applications before the deadline but if unsuccessful, they can opt for a research proposal for their dissertation. Students can also secure their own projects with approval from academic and/or professional services.*
[Adam Smith Business School is **triple accredited**](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/aboutus/accreditationsandrankings/accreditations/ "Home » Schools » Adam Smith Business School » About us » Accreditations and rankings » Accreditations").
You will take four core and a selection of optional courses, delivered across two semesters. Optional courses are tailored to deepen your knowledge in key areas, while offering the opportunity to specialise. During the summer term, you will undertake a significant piece of work through the Applied Project in Business Analytics. This project enables you to apply the skills and knowledge gained during the year to real-world business challenges, preparing you for a successful career in the field of business analytics.
Graduates are well-prepared for careers as Business Analysts, Data Analysts, Data Scientists, Operations Analysts, Market Research Analysts, and Quantitative Consultants. These roles are available across various sectors, including finance, healthcare, technology, retail, and manufacturing, making graduates highly adaptable and in demand.
This is a conversion course for students who have no previous studies in the area of Business Analytics.

program_overview.content:
The Master of Science in Business Analytics programme at HKU Business School offers a comprehensive curriculum that aims to help students develop both hard and soft skills related to business analytics throughout the programme. Students learn the knowledge and skills of understanding data, transforming data into information and converting information into executable actions. The school offers an extensive range of elective options to allow students to proceed in many specific focus areas.
The programme boasts a real world business analytics project - The Capstone Project - with reputable corporations in the region, in which students apply newly-learned analytics knowledge and skills to a real-life business problem facing project sponsors. Students form a team and apply analytics knowledge and skills learnt in previous courses to solve a real-life business problem facing project sponsors. The programme has collaborated with over 30 companies or government agencies in the past three years’ capstone projects.
The curriculum is structured as follows:
- Information analytics to understand the basis of data
- General analytics to transform data into information
- Operations analytics to convert information into executable actions
- Capstone Course to tie the above three areas together through real world business projects
Students gain an in-depth knowledge of tools such as R and Python for applying data science and analytics to a business context. The Programme offers two streams: 1) Artificial Intelligence (AI), 2) Management Consulting (MC). Students may choose to concentrate in one of the two streams according to their interests and career aspirations. Students may also choose to graduate without concentration provided that they complete the four fundamental core courses, the capstone course and five electives.
With the help of close ties to the industry, the MSc(BA) programme launched the Business Analytics Industry Seminar Series, which aims to make the programme more industry and career oriented.
Class profile: the programme recruits students from diverse backgrounds each year to enrich students’ learning experience. The class profile shows 63% female and 37% male students, average age 22, and 97% with prior internship experience, with 3 months average internship duration. Previous employers include Agricultural Bank of China, American International Group, Bank of China, Bank of East Asia, Boston Consulting Group, ByteDance, CITIC Securities, Hang Seng Bank Limited, Huawei, Ipsos China, and State Power Investment Corporation Group.
Programme faculty include Prof. Liao Wang, MSc(BA) Programme Director, along with faculty such as Prof. Boris BABIC, Prof. Zhanrui CAI, Prof. Michael C.L. CHAU, Prof. Hailiang CHEN, Prof. Xing HU, Prof. Shan HUANG, Prof. Zhenhui Jack JIANG, Prof. Xiao LEI, Prof. Xin TONG, Prof. Lionel Zhepeng LI, Prof. Haipeng SHEN, Prof. Tuan Quang PHAN, Prof. Benjamin YEN, Prof. Wei ZHANG, Prof. Yulin FANG, and Prof. Yifan YU.

curriculum.content:
Students are required to complete a total of **10 courses**. The curriculum is structured as follows:
- Information analytics to understand the basis of data
- General analytics to transform data into information
- Operations analytics to convert information into executable actions
- Capstone Course to tie the above three areas together through real world business projects
The Programme offers two streams: **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Management Consulting (MC)**. Students may choose to concentrate in one of the two streams according to their interests and career aspirations. Students may also choose to graduate without concentration provided that they complete the four fundamental core courses, the capstone course and five electives.
The Boot Camp covers basic knowledge in mathematical techniques, programming, databases and statistics that are related to business analytics. The Boot Camp consists **36 hours** of teaching and will be held prior to the commencement of the 1st module:
- Consulting Fundamentals 1 & 2 (6 hours)
- Database – 3 hours
- Mathematics – 6 hours
- Programming – 15 hours
- Statistics – 6 hours
Core Courses:
- MSBA7001 Phthon for Data Analytics
- MSBA7002 Business Statistics
- MSBA7003 Decision Analytics
- MSBA7004 Operations Analytics
Course exemption of up to two required courses may be granted, except for the capstone course. No credits will be given for the exempted course and candidates shall be required to take an approved alternative course of the same credit value.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stream: Students who choose to graduate with the Artificial Intelligence (AI) stream are required to take a minimum of 1 course from AI Methods electives and a minimum of 1 course from AI Applications electives.
AI Methods Electives (Minimum 1):
- MSBA7028 Deep Learning
- MSBA7013 Forecasting and Predictive Analytics
- MSBA7027 Machine Learning
- MSBA7021 Optimization and Reinforcement Learning
AI Applications Electives (Minimum 1):
- MSBA7035 Applied Large Language Models
- MSBA7026 Big Data Analytics on the Cloud
- MSBA7036 Ethics in Artificial Intelligence
- MSBA7033 Generative Artificial Intelligence
- MSBA7032 Quantitative Trading
Management Consulting (MC) Stream: Students who choose to graduate with the Management Consulting (MC) stream are required to take a minimum of 1 course from Analytical Methods electives and a minimum of 1 course from Domain Expertise electives.
Analytical Methods Electives (Minimum 1):
- MSBA7037 A/B Testing in Product Management
- MSBA7014 Business Simulation
- MSBA7024 Database Design and Management
- MSBA7025 Digital Experimentation Methods
- MSBA7023 Geospatial and Business Analytics
- MSBA7027 Machine Learning
- MSBA7015 Service Operations Management
- MSBA7029 Storytelling with Data
Domain Expertise Electives (Minimum 1):
- MSBA7030 Digital Innovation
- MSBA7017 Financial Engineering
- MSBA7012 Social Media and Digital Marketing Analytics
- MSBA7016 Supply Chain and Logistics Management
Other Electives from MSc(BA) Programme:
- MSBA7020 Accounting Analytics for Managerial Decisions
- MSBA7041 Artificial Intelligence Generated Content in Business
- MSBA7034 International Study Field Trip
- MSBA7040 Sports Analytics
Other Masters Programmes: You can take up to two electives from the Master of Accounting, Master of Accounting Analytics, Master of Artificial Intelligence in Business, Master of Economics, Master of Finance, Master of Finance in Financial Technology, Master of Global Management, Master of Science in Marketing, Master of Sustainable Accounting and Finance or Master of Wealth Management programme at HKU. Enrollment in electives from other programmes is subject to seat availability and approval by the Programme Directors concerned based on your profile, capabilities and performance in the MSc(BA) programme. It is your responsibility to make sure you obtain **60 credits** to fulfill the graduation requirements and there is no overlapping of classes and exams in courses from different programmes. Up to two electives may be chosen from other taught postgraduate curricula offered by HKU Business School under the advice and approval of the Programme Directors concerned.
Capstone Course (Choose One):
- MSBA7005 Business Analytics Capstone
- PMSC7901 Business Case Analysis Capstone
Remark: Not all the courses listed will necessarily be offered each academic year and the listed courses are subject to further adjustments.

financial_aid.content:
**HKU Business School Dean's Master Fellowship**: The Fellowship shall be awarded to new full-time students admitted to any one of the taught postgraduate programmes offered by the HKU Business School based on academic performance, relevance of work experience, if applicable, and interview performance, if applicable. The value of the Fellowship ranges from **HK$250,000 to the full prevailing composition fee**. All eligible candidates are automatically considered; no separate application is required except for the Master of Family Wealth Management (MFWM) programme. Outstanding students will only be awarded either the Entrance Scholarship or the Dean's Master Fellowship; the scholarship and fellowship will not be issued to the same candidate.
**Entrance Scholarship**: Scholarships are offered to qualified students, who may receive a scholarship ranging from **5% to 50%** in most cases, on the basis of student's academic merit at the time of admission. A full tuition fee waiver may be offered to outstanding cases. All eligible candidates are automatically considered; no separate application is required except for the Master of Family Wealth Management (MFWM) programme.
**Merit-based Scholarship**: Merit-based scholarships are offered to qualified students, who shall receive a scholarship of **10%**, on the basis of student's performance, including but not limited to, academic performance of the first three modules, participation in the extra-curricular activities, recommendation from course instructors, and level of support provided to the programme office. All eligible candidates are automatically considered; no separate application is required.
**Fargo Wealth Excellence Scholarship**: Up to fourteen scholarships shall be awarded each year to full-time Year One students of Master of Science in Business Analytics, among other listed programmes, on the basis of academic performance in the respective programme and contributions to the community of the respective masters programme. The Scholarship shall be of the value of **HK$10,000** each.
**Hong Kong Future Talents Scholarship Scheme for Advanced Studies**: Starting from the 2025-26 academic year, the Government is introducing the Hong Kong Future Talents Scholarship Scheme for Advanced Studies (HKFTSS). Master of Science in Business Analytics is eligible for FTSS in the 2026 intake. Applications are open to local students admitted to the programmes listed above in the 2026 intake; scholarship awards will be based on merit taking into account students' academic achievements, professional qualifications, relevant work experience and achievements in other areas as well as the proposals submitted by the students; applications from students who are receiving other forms of government scholarship (except student financial assistance) for pursuing the same programme will not be considered. All awardees must sign a written undertaking that upon graduation they will contribute to relevant industries/sectors through full-time employment or entrepreneurial activities either in Hong Kong or within the Greater Bay Area. HKFTSS scholarship is capped at **HK$100,000** for each student for the whole TPg programme, regardless of the actual study period and mode of study. Awardees are required to pay a minimum tuition fee being the prevailing rate of UGC-funded full-time degree programmes, i.e. **HK$47,000 for 2026-2027 academic year**.
**Continuing Education Fund (CEF)**: There are currently 3 courses in HKU MSc(BA) that are listed as a reimbursement course under the Continuing Education Fund (CEF) scheme, which provides a maximum of **HK$25,000** in reimbursement to those who fulfil the criteria. Eligible MSc(BA) courses: 1. Financial Engineering 2. Service Operations Management 3. Social Media and Digital Marketing Analytics. Please visit the CEF website for further details: http://www.wfsfaa.gov.hk/cef/en/index.htm

program_overview.content:
The HKUST MSBA program places a primary focus on delivering business value while also fostering the development of advanced data analysis skills and continuous learning and adaptation. Moreover, the program emphasizes the development of skills required to effectively interface with stakeholders from both the business side and technical teams. This inclusive approach, utilizing the strengths of our world-class business school, ensures that students from diverse backgrounds, including those with extensive technical skills such as engineering backgrounds, as well as those with more traditional business backgrounds, can benefit from the program. Our aim is to bridge the gap between academic education and the professional world while producing exceptionally employable graduates.
The program's distinctive curriculum is designed to be intensive, optimizing outcomes for one year of full-time study for recent graduates and two years of part-time study for upskilling and enhanced competitiveness. The program accomplishes this through a blended curriculum that combines an innovative academic program taught by our world-class faculty with mandatory professional workshops in design thinking for business analytics, data management, and the latest data analytics tools, including Auto ML platforms taught from a business perspective. Importantly, there are opportunities for extensive practical experience working with major companies in our elective corporate consulting track sequence. The program experience for students is further enhanced by our active Corporate Advisory Board.
The HKUST MSBA program is offered in both in one-year full-time and two-year part-time study modes. Students are required to attend all classes in HKUST campus. Distance learning or online learning mode is NOT offered.
To support deeper career exploration, MSc full-time students may choose to remain at HKUST for an additional half year during their second year. This option allows students to balance academic learning with practical and international experiences, while maintaining full student status.
How it works
- Students complete up to 28 credits in Year 1
- A minimum of 2 credits must be reserved for the Fall term of Year 2
- These credits can be fulfilled through approved experiential learning activities such as practicum, study tours, or other designated coursework
Why it matters
- Provides greater flexibility for career planning
- Enables participation in internships, industry exposure, and global learning opportunities
- Supports a smoother transition from study to employment

curriculum.content:
The HKUST MScBA program offers a **one-year full-time or two-year part-time** option. It offers a consultancy and project management track collaborating with global industry leaders. Students have mandatory corporate style workshops in design thinking for business analytics, data base management in business and exposure to the latest data analytics tools to be generally completed in the Fall semester.
To graduate, complete **30 credits**, including **16 credits of Required Courses** and **14 credits of Elective Courses** (which may include the Corporate Consulting Track electives), along with other mandatory requirements. Students can also take up to **34 credits** at no extra cost, subject to approval. The list of Elective Course options is different for each intake and will be announced to students prior to the start of the course registration period.

application_materials.content:
When you have completed and submitted the application form, Lancaster will determine the documents needed to assess your application based on your provided information; these will appear in the supporting document section of your application. To be considered, you must upload the required documents marked with a \*. If documents are not in English, you must provide an official English translation and your untranslated copy.
Information usually required:
- **Academic transcript and degree certificate:** upload an official copy of your degree transcript showing the subjects studied, marks, and confirmation of degree award. If studies are not complete, provide an interim transcript. If studying outside the UK and the university’s grading scale is not detailed on the transcript, provide this too.
- **Personal statement:** explain why you are applying for the course, what you hope to gain from your studies, and how it fits with your plans. Recommended maximum: **500 words**.
- **References:** for Postgraduate Taught applications, provide **one reference**, ideally from someone who can comment on suitability for academic study, such as a tutor from previous studies. A professional reference may be accepted if an academic reference cannot be provided.

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc, entry year 2026, is offered full time over 1 year. Lancaster is ranked 12th for Master's in Business Analytics in the UK and 30th in Europe in the QS Business Master's Rankings (2026), and 8th for Thought Leadership in the UK.
The MSc Business Analytics is designed for students seeking a career in data or business analytics, decision support, industrial engineering or management science. The programme trains students in analytical decision-making, combining the theory of business analytics with practical application through data-driven methodologies and tools. It teaches the entire business analytics life cycle, covering descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analytics.
The programme develops technical, critical thinking and soft skills, including programming in R and Python, statistics, data analytics and visualisation, problem structuring and problem solving, presentation, negotiation and leadership skills. It has partnerships with business analytics practitioners in industry and is continually updated to reflect the changing landscape of business analytics. Students can complete an analytics project that solves a real-life problem as part of the programme.
Lancaster University established the first Operational Research department in the world in 1964, now developed into the Department of Management Science. Academics are leaders in forecasting, optimisation, simulation and stochastic modelling, with expertise in logistics and supply chain analytics, healthcare analytics, sports analytics, network analytics, marketing analytics and pricing analytics.
Key features include practical case-study learning, an industry-based dissertation where students may act as consultants for a company and solve a real-life problem, and the chance to work with companies such as Jaguar Land Rover, Belmond, Costa, Aldi and Unilever. Students take four core modules, one Dissertation module (Research or Industry) and two optional modules.
Lancaster is the only university in the UK that awards IIF (International Institute of Forecasters) certificates after successful completion of the programme. Successful MSc Business Analytics graduates supervised by members of the Centre for Marketing Analytics and Forecasting for their dissertations may be awarded the IIF Certificate in Forecasting Practice, entitling them to use the credential "IIF Certified Forecaster".
A Business Analytics degree can be widely applied across the business world. Recent graduate destinations include Virgin Atlantic, Avanti West Coast, EY, Amazon, NielsenIQ, NHS, Asda, Perch Group, Ascertia, ITV, Sainsbury’s and Serco. Graduate roles include Data Scientist, Business Analyst, Insights Analyst, Account Executive, Financial Analyst, eCommerce Data Analyst, Customer Analyst, Strategy Analyst, Product Analyst, Fraud Specialist, Business Intelligence Developer, Business Consultant and Credit Analyst. Students benefit from the LUMS Careers Team, employer networking events and a strong alumni network.

curriculum.content:
Duration: **Full time 1 year**.
You will take **four core modules**, **one Dissertation module (Research or Industry)** and **two further optional modules**.
Core modules:
- **Decision Analytics**: focuses on translating real-world business problems into quantitative models and applying quantitative methods and software tools. It introduces optimisation, decision analysis and simulation, with implementation in MS Excel and Python.
- **Forecasting and Time-Series Analytics**: covers forecasting model building in regression and extensions, extrapolative forecasting methods including Exponential Smoothing, and Machine Learning or Artificial Intelligence methods including Neural Networks.
- **Python Programming**: covers sorting and searching algorithms, data manipulation, visualisation, and package extensions such as pandas and numpty, with applications in Business Analytics such as simulation and optimisation.
- **Statistics for Business**: covers probability, sampling, hypothesis testing, regression analysis, model building and model selection, using R and real-world business problems.
Dissertation options:
- **Dissertation: Industry**: an in-depth research project linked to the MSc programme, applying knowledge to a real business problem and delivering a professional research project in a real organisation.
- **Dissertation: Research**: an independent investigation of a scholarly question linked to real business problems, normally involving literature review, research question design, methodology selection and a dissertation defending the findings.
Optional modules include:
- **Machine Learning and Data Mining**: covers the data analysis process, including formulating a project objective, understanding data and resources, statistical modelling and performance assessment, focusing on classification using R.
- **Marketing Analytics**: covers applied quantitative models including customer segmentation, text mining, image analytics and marketing mix modelling.
- **Operations and Supply Chain Excellence**: covers lean principles, Six Sigma, the theory of constraints and statistical process control, plus supplier development and sustainability performance in supply chains.
- **Optimisation and Heuristics**: introduces problem formulations and algorithmic methods for applying optimisation techniques to business problems.
- **Simulation and Reinforcement Learning**: introduces methods for modelling and optimising systems under uncertainty, including simulation and reinforcement learning, with applications such as healthcare services, manufacturing, inventory management and dynamic pricing.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet met Lancaster University's academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of the offer conditions and how you can meet these requirements will be in the offer letter.
- You can accept your offer before you have met the conditions; you do not need to wait until your offer is unconditional. The offer letter will include a deadline date for making a decision, and if a deposit is required for your course you will need to pay this by the deadline date in the offer letter. If Lancaster has not heard from you by your deadline, they may withdraw your application.
- The deadline for meeting the conditions is in the offer letter. You may have an offer that is conditional on more than one qualification, for example, you may need to complete your university studies and take an English language test. You do not have to meet all the conditions at the same time.
- **Academic conditions:** your transcript and certificate needs to be an official copy and, if it is not in English, you will also need to provide an official translation. Your transcript needs to state your name, the course studied, your marks for each subject, the dates you studied and confirmation that you have completed your studies.
- **English language conditions:** if you need to sit an English Language test to meet the conditions of your offer, you should do this as soon as possible and upload your score to the [postgraduate application portal](https://www.e-res.lancaster.ac.uk/postgraduate-applications/Account/Login). If your English score does not meet the conditions of the offer, Lancaster will automatically consider your eligibility for one of its [pre-sessional English language courses](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/study/entry-requirements/pre-sessional-english/) and will contact you by email if this is an option for you. Lancaster cannot consider you for a pre-sessional course without seeing a valid English language score and does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other organisations or institutions.
- Pre-sessional English language programmes are specifically designed to help international students prepare for their studies at Lancaster. Lancaster cannot consider you for a pre-sessional course if you do not have an offer to study at Lancaster University, and needs to see a valid English language score that meets its pre-sessional requirements before considering you for a place.
- For international students who need a student visa, the process for issuing a CAS cannot start until your offer is unconditional and Lancaster has received your passport details.

application_materials.content:

- **Educational Documents**: Degree scroll/certificate(s) and academic transcripts of each university attended; official English translation is required for non-English certificates and transcripts.
- **Passport Photo**: Coloured photo taken within the last **3 months** in hi-resolution jpeg format.
- **Passport or NRIC**: International applicants must have a valid passport on hand and complete a video identification within the application. Singapore Citizens and SPR should use NRIC. Applicants are also required to upload a scanned copy of passport or NRIC.
- **GMAT/GMAT Focus or GRE Score Report**: Applicants may upload an unofficial or test taker copy if official test scores are not on hand. Official test scores should be sent to Nanyang Business School; GMAT institution code **V24-ZV-70** and GRE ID code **3123**. Applicants who have yet to take the GMAT/GMAT Focus or GRE and TOEFL/IELTS may still submit their application and indicate the test dates in the online application form.

- **Referee Reports**: Applicants are required to nominate **two referees** in the online application form. Upon nomination, an online referee report form will be sent to them for completion. All referee reports must be submitted from an official institution or organisational email address; submissions from personal email addresses will not be accepted.
- **Professional Membership Certificates, if any**.
The essay questions are compulsory and applicants should articulate their thoughts clearly, using good judgement with respect to the word limit. No separate application for scholarships is required; applicants should tick the box relating to the scholarship in the online application form and complete the essay for scholarship consideration.
For scholarship consideration, applicants should complete the scholarship part of the online application, including the scholarship essay. Scholarship application will only be considered when it is submitted together with the application.

program_overview.content:
The MSc Business Analytics at Nanyang Business School equips students to excel in business analytics. The curriculum imparts a strong commercial sense through business strategy and tools to gain insights from data analysis, with a hands-on approach that allows students to apply classroom knowledge to real-world business situations. Graduates will be able to lead analytics projects as the head of a business unit and analytics business lead, or as professional consultants with business domain expertise.
MSBA is offered as a **full-time, one-year programme**. The programme is delivered entirely in English on the main campus at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore.
The Data Analytics Practicum taps on industry and business environments as teaching platforms for students to acquire real-life working experience in data analytics applications and apply theory and skills from classroom settings to actual project environments. Students work full-time for at least **12 weeks** on relevant data analytics/AI projects through either a Work Track with Singapore-registered companies, organisations, or agencies, or a Project Track supervised by faculty on data-analytics-related projects.
Organisations are looking for graduates who are adept at working with large data sets, applying insights and business intelligence to solve business needs and drive transformation. Through the programme’s strong industry partnerships, students can take advantage of internship opportunities with industry leaders such as DBS, KPMG, and GE Digital, providing hands-on experience and preparation for a career in business analytics.

financial_aid.content:

Only applicants who have been offered a place in MSc Business Analytics programme are eligible for the scholarships. The partial scholarship will go towards off-setting the fees of the programme, and does not cover the living expenses in Singapore, travel and accommodation.

- **How to Apply:** Please complete the scholarship part of the online application, including the scholarship essay. Applicants who wish to be considered for the scholarship should ensure that their scholarship applications are completed, including submission of all supporting documents, by [30 November 2025 deadline](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-business-analytics/admissions#round-1). Scholarship application will only be considered when it is submitted together with the application.
- **ASEAN Development Scholarship:** This partial scholarship is awarded to nationals of ASEAN member countries, excluding Singapore. Recipients may receive up to **90% funding towards their tuition fee**. Scholarship applicants must possess strong academic records, demonstrated leadership qualities and potential, and for working professionals, a strong career progression. A complete online application including the scholarship section, and required supporting documents must be submitted by the [first round application deadline](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-business-analytics/admissions#round-1) to be eligible.

Applicants must showcase a distinctive background, demonstrate how it enhances the broader understanding of diversity, and possess a track record of success in initiatives or activities that promote diversity within their communities or workplaces. A complete online application including the scholarship section, and required supporting documents must be submitted by the [first round of application deadline](https://www.ntu.edu.sg/business/admissions/graduate-studies/msc-business-analytics/admissions#round-1) to be eligible.

- **NTU Alumni Grant:** NTU alumni who have completed a bachelor’s or post-graduate degree at NTU are eligible for an alumni grant of **10% of the tuition fees**. The subsidy can only be used to offset the tuition fee and cannot be used to offset other costs such as student service fees or miscellaneous fees.
- **Singapore Citizen & Singapore PR Grant:** Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents are eligible for a grant of **$5000**. The subsidy can only be used to offset the tuition fee and cannot be used to offset other costs such as student service fees or miscellaneous fees.
- **SkillsFuture Credit:** SkillsFuture Credit aims to encourage individual ownership of skills development and lifelong learning. All Singaporeans aged 25 and above will receive an opening credit of **S$500** from January 2016. The MSBA programme is a certified course under this programme. Please click [here](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/credit) for more information on the disbursement of the credit.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
A conditional offer is extended to an applicant who is in the process of completing the final term, semester, or trimester of their current course of study, and has outstanding educational documents. This condition will be clearly outlined in the offer letter, stating: "The offer of admission is on condition that you obtain your Bachelor's degree with a ________ from ___________ , ___________ "
For **Conditional Offer** (i.e. subject to attaining a Bachelor/ Masters’ degree), you are required to upload your **Bachelor/ Masters’ degree scrolls and Official Transcript** (Original and English Language translated). If you are unable to upload your Bachelor/ Masters’ degree scroll during verification period, you are to upload **a letter of completion** from your university stating that you have completed and attained Bachelor/ Masters’ degree. Do not complete e-verification if you do not meet the condition stated on the offer letter. Kindly contact your school for assistance.
**International Student with International Qualification**:
- Official degree certificate and final transcript
- Digital copy of Student Pass (Full-time students) / Valid immigration pass (For Part-time students only)
- Degree verification report (English) from NTU approved credential verification agency within **one month of your term start date**
- Latest Passport (If not yet submitted)

application_materials.content:
For PGT courses, and some PGR courses, you'll provide a personal statement. It should share your motivation and enthusiasm for your chosen course, show your suitability for postgraduate study, include examples of relevant work, voluntary or study experiences, and incorporate skills such as time management, project management, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. You should also cover successes and achievements relevant to the course and outline why you have chosen the course, chosen Newcastle University, and how you will apply your current skills, knowledge and experience. You may also consider showing how the course fits into your career plans and ambitions.
You'll need to include contact details for **two referees**. At least one referee should be able to comment on your academic ability. Newcastle will contact referees to request references, usually at the same time as sending the conditional offer. If you already have a reference from your referee(s), you can attach it in the application portal; the reference must be signed by your referee, dated and on official letterhead. Where you have attached the reference, Newcastle may also contact your referees for confirmation.
Check the 'How to Apply' tab on your course page to see what documents to include. The main documents the University requires for postgraduate programmes are:
- a transcript of your degree studies. This is an academic record of the subjects you’ve studied and the grades/marks achieved. If you are still studying you should provide a current transcript of your degree studies to date.
- certificates to confirm your degree or highest qualification, if your degree is complete
- evidence of your English language ability
- a copy of your passport
- a curriculum vitae
- a research proposal for research programmes, if your course requires one
- a Personal Statement
- a portfolio. This is only for some creative courses; check the 'How to Apply' tab on the course page to find out if you need to include one.
- any transcripts of marks or certified documents should be translated into English
Newcastle does not need you to send any pre-university qualification documentation or any non-academic certificates of achievement.
To attach document(s) to your application, select ‘Supporting Documentation’ from the left-hand menu. There will be a list of required documents. Complete the following steps:
- Click 'Upload Documents' to find and select your document
- Select the document type from the dropdown list
- Click 'Choose files' to upload your document
- Click 'Submit'
Before you can submit your application, you must attach a copy of any mandatory documents including your degree transcript. If you are still studying you should provide a current transcript of your degree studies to date. When you upload these documents you must select the document type, such as 'transcript' or 'translated transcript'.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
