program_overview.content:
Unlock the future with Newcastle University's MSc in Business Analytics. The MSc in Business Analytics gives you the skills and knowledge to thrive as a business analyst, operations analyst, consultant, or data analyst, capable of operating across a wide range of functions and industries.
Key features include:
- Comprehensive skill development: you will gain a versatile set of business analytics skills that you can apply across diverse sectors.
- Tool proficiency and critical insight: you will develop expertise in analytical tools and cultivate a critical mindset for data-driven decision-making.
- Practical project experience: you will work on real-world business analytics projects, bridging theory and practice.
- Experiential learning: you will engage with real industry challenges through hands-on learning and gain valuable exposure to current business practices.
The programme does not just teach technical skills. It also emphasises critical thinking. You will learn how to approach business analytics projects strategically and understand how to extract maximum value from data, a crucial skill in modern decision-making.
The programme is structured around three interconnected pillars:
- Semester 1 - Foundations of Data Science: you will develop core competencies in statistics and programming, specifically tailored to business analytics applications.
- Semester 2 - Managerial Perspectives: you will gain insights into the strategic and operational management of business analytics projects, focusing on effective implementation and impact.
- Semester 3 - Real-World Application: you will apply your skills in practical contexts and critically evaluate analytics solutions across different business environments.
The programme culminates in a substantial individual research project. This allows you to apply your learning to a real-world business problem and demonstrate your analytical capabilities in depth.
Our Business Analytics MSc provides you with a rigorous and comprehensive foundation in data-driven decision-making. It covers both the theoretical and practical aspects in depth. You will develop core expertise in data analytics for business insights, statistical foundations of data science, statistical learning, and research methods for business analytics. You will also acquire practical, industry-relevant skills in project management, web and social media analytics, operations analytics, artificial intelligence in business, marketing analytics, teamwork, presenting, and report writing.
You will explore how to leverage data analytics for strategic business insights. You'll apply your knowledge through a collaborative group project designed to simulate real-world challenges. By the end of the programme, you'll be able to extract actionable insights from complex datasets and make informed, data-driven decisions.
Depending on your modules, you'll be assessed through a combination of design or creative project, dissertation, essay, oral presentation, problem-solving exercises, report, reflective log, and research proposal.
Throughout your studies, you'll have access to support from academic staff, academic advisers and research supervisors, the University Student Services Team, student representatives, and peers. You'll also be assigned an academic member of staff, who will be your academic adviser throughout your time with us.
Our staff include [Nick Howey](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/nickhowey.html) (Degree Programme Director), [Dr Josephine Go Jefferies](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/josephinego-jefferies.html), [Dr James Bentham](https://search.ncl.ac.uk/s/redirect?collection=neu-meta&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.ncl.ac.uk%2Fmaths-physics%2Fpeople%2Fprofile%2Fjamesbentham.html&auth=p4yf1AazPqczflFNi%2FlgFg&profile=_default&rank=1&query=james+bentham), Dr Ajinkya Tanksale, [Dr Davit Marikyan](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/davitmarikyan.html), [Dr Haiyan Liu](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/haiyanlu.html), [Dr Paul Liu](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/people/profile/paulliu2.html), and [Dr Aamir Khan](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/maths-physics/people/profile/aamirkhan.html).
Skills development is a central focus of the Business Analytics MSc. The programme will help you build a robust and versatile skill set valued across industries. You will enhance your ability to analyse complex business scenarios, make informed data-driven decisions, and communicate insights effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experiential learning allows you to apply advanced analytical tools and techniques to real-world problems, bridging the gap between academic theory and industry practice.
The Postgraduate Semester Abroad is an opportunity to study a complementary subject for one semester at a European partner university on an exchange basis. The experience takes place at the end of your studies, once you have submitted your dissertation/final project. Studies undertaken at a partner university will not count towards a double/dual degree award, but you'll receive a transcript from your host university evidencing your achievements. Students who complete this scheme will not be eligible for the UK graduate work visa.
Upon completing the programme, you will be well-prepared to lead data-driven innovations across various industries. The MSc in Business Analytics could lead to analytics-related roles such as business analyst, data analyst, consultant, market analyst, or quantitative analyst. These roles could cover sectors including retail enterprises, professional services firms, marketing and media-based businesses, pharmaceutical-based businesses, telecommunications companies, information technology-based organisations, consultancy firms, government and public services, and educational institutions.
Career development and employability are woven throughout teaching, learning and student experience. Business School students get access to both the wider University careers service and exclusive Business School events and resources, including one-to-one career support, industry-specific career events, online career learning tools, career planning and information sessions, an annual careers week, networking opportunities, specialist careers and business start-up support, and the chance to apply for work experience opportunities while studying.
Newcastle University Business School is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](http://www.aacsb.edu/), [European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS)](https://efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/), and [Association of MBAs (AMBA)](https://www.associationofmbas.com/about-us/). Only **1% of business schools worldwide** hold this triple crown. The Business School is also one of 140 business schools worldwide to be accredited by the EQUIS scheme for managerial and entrepreneurial skills development.
Newcastle University Business School is one of the largest Schools in the University, with over 4,000 students from over 85 countries. The Business School is the gateway to [Newcastle Helix](https://newcastlehelix.com/home), a landmark 24 acre hybrid city quarter that brings together researchers, business and communities. Facilities include computer clusters, lecture theatres, seminar and teaching spaces, a dedicated Student Hub and Quiet Space, study pods and bookable rooms, employability support and event hubs, a Bloomberg lab with over 20 terminals, and an Experimental and Behavioural Economics Lab.

cost_of_attendance.content:
Living costs cover expenses other than tuition fees, such as accommodation, food, drink, travel and study materials. The average cost of living for a student studying in the UK is just over **£1,100 per month**.
Estimated monthly costs while studying at Newcastle:
- Rent in University-owned or managed partnership accommodation, including bills such as electricity, water, gas and wifi: **Postgraduate: £392 – £940**.
- Groceries: **£144**.
- Socialising: **£99**.
- Mobile phone: **£16** (SIM only).
- Course costs, including books, stationery, photocopying, field trips, specialist materials or equipment: around **£11 - £59 per month**.
For international students, as part of the visa application, you’ll have to prove you have sufficient funds to support yourself while at university in the UK. International students will also have further costs associated with studying in the UK, such as a student visa and a health surcharge to access the NHS.

multiple_applications.content: You may have received multiple programme offers, but please note that you can only accept one. Once you confirm your acceptance, all other offers—including applications still awaiting decisions—will be automatically declined. However, if you change your mind, you can request to reinstate a previously declined offer, subject to availability.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Once you've received your offer, you have three choices: accept, decline or defer.
If you decide to defer your offer, log in to the application portal you applied through to let us know. For most courses, you can defer your offer to the next academic year. If we’re able to defer your offer and you have a deposit condition outstanding, we’ll apply a January deposit condition for the following year. We’ll decline your current offer and send you a new offer for the next academic year. If we are unable to defer your offer, we’ll ask you to apply again the following year. You can only defer your offer once. To defer for a further year, you’ll need to submit a new application the following year.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
There are two types of offer you can receive: unconditional and conditional.
- You’ll receive a conditional offer if there are conditions that you need to meet before you can start your course. The conditions of your offer are in the ‘Terms and Conditions of your Offer’ section of your offer document, and can also be seen in the application portal you applied through.
- To provide evidence that you’ve met the conditions of your offer, upload your supporting documents to the application portal you applied through. If you’re still studying, upload the documents as soon as they’re available. If your supporting documents aren’t in English, you must provide certified English language translations.
- When your documents demonstrate that you’ve met your offer conditions, your offer will become unconditional. If you have just missed the conditions of your offer, Newcastle encourages you to upload your results anyway; they will review your application and may still be able to give you a place on your chosen course.
- Academic conditions include a transcript of your degree studies and your degree certificate or a certified copy.
- English language conditions can be met by taking an [international language test](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/international/language/#overview) such as IELTS, TOEFL, or Pearsons, or by completing one of Newcastle’s six- or ten-week English language courses at the [International Study Centre](https://nclisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english).
- When you’ve accepted your offer and met any conditions, Newcastle will send a Confirmation of a Place (COP) document. This is formal confirmation of acceptance of the unconditional offer.

application_materials.content:
Make sure that you upload clear scanned copies of your degree certificate (if completed) and final or current transcript, as well as any other supporting documents. We will not be able to assess your application without them. Please do not send us the original copies in the post, as we will be unable to return these.
Depending on the course you are applying for, you may also need to provide two references, including at least one who can comment on your academic ability. These must be dated within two years of the date of your application and, if not submitted directly by your referee, signed and on letter-headed paper.
We may also require a personal statement. If you aren't sure what to include or need more help, please refer to our [guidance](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/careers/students/furtherstudy/applying.aspx "Writing a personal statement for further study") or [contact us](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/help-and-support/home/contact-us.html).
Your application provides an opportunity for you to articulate the skills and experiences you have that make you suitable for a place on our courses. AI tools may help structure things such as personal statements, or check for readability, but generating all, or a large part of your application submissions and communications regarding your application, using an AI tool and presenting this as your own work or words could affect the outcome of your application.
Admissions may, at their discretion, ask applicants to provide further information in order to assess their application fairly and accurately. This can include CVs, references (academic and professional) and clarifications regarding their previous and current education.

academic_requirements.content:
- Entry requirement: **2:1 (or international equivalent) in any discipline**; applicants should not have previously studied a significant amount of business analytics, but must have a **strong 2:1 (65%) in quantitative modules at degree level with a significant amount of mathematical/statistical content**.
- Alternative qualifications: applicants are treated on an individual basis, and relevant work experience may also be considered.
- China applicants: applicants should hold a bachelors degree of a good standard from a recognised university, usually in a relevant subject area. Entry requirements for degrees from Chinese universities vary depending on the university studied at and the course applied for.
- China applicants: depending on the tiers of institutions applicants graduated from, Chinese grade equivalence varies. For a **2:1**, the stated range is **72% - 80%**.
- China applicants: HND/SQA AD (**BB/BBB/60%/Merit**) + final year/top-ups to a UK Bachelor degree studied in the UK only, and 3 years Chinese Junior Diploma (Dazhuan) + 1/2 years final years/top-ups to a Bachelor degree may be accepted as long as applicants meet the grade requirement, e.g. **2.1**, in both parts of the programme.
- China applicants: Bachelor degrees obtained via **2-year China Diploma plus 1-year top-up in the UK cannot be accepted** by any Departments/Schools at UoN.
- China applicants: for a **3+1 joint programme**, the university would expect an offer to be made on the second part, but applicants must also have achieved the requirement, e.g. **2:1**, in part 1 of the programme. For a **2+2 joint programme**, the decision will be made only based on overseas transcripts.

- For China (mainland) applicants: if you successfully completed a UK Degree **within two years of the University of Nottingham course start date**, where at least one full academic year was physically taught in the UK, this would usually satisfy the English language requirements of your course.

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc is a **full-time, 12-month** programme starting in **September 2027**; part-time study is not available.
The MSc in Business Analytics is designed with input from top multinational companies to build technical and business skills for data-driven decision-making. The programme is delivered by the [Neo-demographic Laboratory for Analytics in Business (N/LAB)](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/business/businesscentres/n-lab/index.aspx), an advanced research and teaching facility within the Business School. Students benefit from N/LAB’s strong industry ties, accessing real-world datasets and insights from global partners.
The course develops specialist technical skills and strategic thinking, preparing students as data scientists equipped with:
- skills to implement advanced data science methods using big data tools
- practical experience of delivering business analytics projects using real-world case studies
- managerial and communication skills to lead data-driven decision-making
Students get access to advanced facilities including secure computer environments, 3D visualisation technology and an immersive video wall for advanced research and analytics projects.
The Business School is triple accredited, part of an elite group of business schools worldwide with ‘triple crown’ accreditation: [EQUIS](https://www.efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/), [AMBA](https://www.associationofmbas.com/) and [AACSB](https://www.aacsb.edu/). The course is delivered by N/LAB, which provides state-of-the-art research, data visualisation and teaching facilities. Business School students also have the opportunity to gain digital skills with industry-recognised [Microsoft and SAP certifications](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/business/study-with-us/digital-professional-skills/index.aspx).
Across the autumn and spring semesters, students take **120 credits** of taught modules. They complete a **60-credit dissertation** over the summer and are allocated an appropriate dissertation supervisor. The summer project represents the culmination of the programme, requiring students to design, execute and report a research project based on the analysis of real-world or simulated data. There is also an option of a Business Project, subject to availability and a student selection process.
Teaching takes place through lectures, seminars, tutorials and workshops. Assessment is by dissertation, examinations and coursework. Students have at least a weekly average of **8 timetabled hours** through lectures, seminars and workshops, tutorials or supervision.
The programme is based at [Jubilee Campus](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/about/campuses/jubileecampus.aspx), home to the university’s business, education and computer science schools.
With tailored [careers support](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/business/careers-and-employability/careers-support-for-masters-students.aspx), many master’s students go on to secure roles with world-leading employers. Recent graduates have been hired by companies such as Allianz, Amazon, Boots, KPMG and Unilever. The Business School Postgraduate Careers team provides advice, guidance and coaching, and the Accelerated Career Leader Programme is integrated within the MSc. Graduate destinations for postgraduates include business analysts, data analysts, management consultants, finance and investment analysts and advisers, business development managers, financial managers, marketing associate professionals, human resources managers and accountants. Some MSc graduates have gone on to doctoral studies, while others have become entrepreneurs. The average starting salary for postgraduates in Nottingham University Business School was **£38,931**.

curriculum.content:
Business Analytics MSc is offered **full-time: 12 months**; **part-time: Not available**.
Across the autumn and spring semesters, students take **120 credits of taught modules**. Students complete a **60-credit dissertation** over the summer and are allocated an appropriate dissertation supervisor.
Semester one core modules:
- Foundational Business Analytics
- Data at Scale: Management, Processing and Visualisation
Semester one optional modules: one from:
- Entrepreneurship in Context
- Management Science for Decision Support
- Supply Chain Planning and Management
Semester two core modules:
- Analytics Specialisations and Applications
- Leading Big Data Business Projects
- Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics
Semester two optional modules: one from:
- Advanced Operations Analysis
- Digital Marketing
Summer:
- Data Driven Dissertation Project in Business Analytics: students design, execute and report a research project based on the analysis of real-world or simulated data, including an **8,000-word dissertation**, exhibits and data visualisations.
- Business Project: requires students, working as groups, to undertake research in a topic relevant to business, management, marketing, finance, accounting, or information system; the topic must be relevant to the named degree programme and is subject to formal approval. Option of a Business Project is subject to availability and a student selection process.
Modules are assessed by a combination of exams and coursework at the end of the relevant semester. Students have at least a weekly average of **8 timetabled hours** through lectures, seminars and workshops, tutorials or supervision. As a guide, a **20 credit module is approximately 200 hours of work** combined teaching and self-study.
Learning methods include lectures, seminars, tutorials and workshops. Assessment methods include dissertation, examinations and coursework.
The course is taught at **Jubilee Campus**.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
You can request a deferral of your postgraduate offer to the next academic year, providing that:
- the course accepts deferred entry
- you have accepted your offer
- you have met any academic and reference conditions on the offer within the [deadline](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/pgstudy/already-applied/offer.aspx#deadlines "I have an offer") to do so
- you have paid any [tuition fee deposits](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/fabs/finance/frequentlyaskedquestions/casfaq.aspx "Tuition fee deposits - Frequently Asked Questions") if it's required - most postgraduate taught courses require international students to pay a deposit for visa purposes
Postgraduate Taught (PGT) and Postgraduate Research (PGR) change of start dates can be requested through [our enquiry form](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studywithus/enquiry.aspx "Make an enquiry"). Please include your full name and University of Nottingham ID number. The deadline to request this is **one day after the latest date to register**.
Deferral requests will be considered by the university and are not guaranteed. We may need to refer to the individual school or the academic supervisor (for postgraduate research courses) before confirming. Offers are usually confirmed once all necessary deposits have been paid and offer details for the following year are available.
Ordinarily, you can only defer the same offer **once**. If you still cannot attend in the following year and want to study the course another year later, you would need to make a new application.
If you are considering or have requested a deferral, you should not complete registration processes for your course in the current year as deferrals cannot be processed once you have registered as a student.
[Complete the Deferral Request Form](https://app.geckoform.com/public/#/modern/21FO00hzsr9ok800es8ni3yxsc)
The university does not usually defer scholarship offers to the following year. If we've offered you a scholarship, this will be withdrawn and you would need to reapply for scholarships in the following year.
International students who will be sponsored by an external organisation will usually have their [student visa CAS deposit](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/fabs/finance/frequentlyaskedquestions/cas-deposits.aspx#sponsor "Student visa CAS deposits - Frequently Asked Questions") waived after providing evidence of sponsorship for the relevant course and academic year. If you need to defer your studies, you must provide a new letter or written confirmation from your sponsor, confirming that your sponsorship will be still be valid in the next academic year. If you cannot provide this confirmation, you must pay the deposit to defer your offer.
We are unable to support deposit waivers for Chevening or Commonwealth Scholarship applicants deferring an offer. If you intend to fund your deferred study via an application to one of these bodies and have not had confirmation of an award, you must pay the appropriate deposit in order to defer your offer.

program_overview.content:
MSc in Business Analytics (MAF/MAP), Programme Code 23090, has Stream Code MAF (Full-time) and MAP (Part-time). The mode of study is Mixed Mode. Normal duration is 1.5 years (Full-time) and 2.5 years (Part-time), with 31 credits required for graduation. Programme Leader(s): **Programme Director** Prof. Xin Xu, BEcon, MPhil, PhD; **Deputy Programme Director** Dr Vincent Cho, BSc, MEngSc, PhD.
Programme Aims: This programme starts with the fundamentals of applying analytical techniques on big data for decision supports of an organisation, and progresses to in-depth studies of various application domains.
Characteristics:
1. Emphasises essential skills and knowledge of business analytics
2. Applies domains of business analytics
3. Covers theoretical knowledge and research findings of decision making using big data
4. Offers opportunities to apply theories to investigating and solving business problems
5. Focuses on the systematic training and development of skills and competence in business analytics
6. Enhances the ability to solve big data problems
7. Empowers students to achieve career potential via professional coaching and career services
Alumni describe the MSc in Business Analytics programme as a well-structured platform whose curriculum blends domain-specific business knowledge with cutting-edge data analytics tools. Students learn from faculty who bring expertise from business, academia, and technology, and who regularly share developments in AI and machine learning beyond textbook theory. The programme provides an accessible introduction to analytical techniques and a forward-looking perspective on technological evolution for those transitioning from traditional industries.
The curriculum strikes a balance between theory and practice, equipping students with skills for data-driven roles. Training in industry-standard tools such as Python, SQL, SPSS, SmartPLS, and Excel strengthens technical skills. The programme emphasises essential business analytics and problem-solving skills for translating data into meaningful insights and making informed decisions. It also focuses on experiential learning through case studies, group projects, and hands-on assignments, with faculty support and networking events connecting students with industry leaders and alumni.

curriculum.content:
For MSc, students complete **31 credits**:
- Non-Dissertation Option: 4 Compulsory Subjects (3 credits each), 1 AIE Subject (1 credit), and 6 Elective Subjects (3 credits each).
- Dissertation Option: 4 Compulsory Subjects (3 credits each), 1 AIE Subject (1 credit), 2 Elective Subjects (3 credits each), the subject Research Methods (3 credits), and a Dissertation (9 credits).
- Students may, on completion of 4 Compulsory Subjects, 1 credit of AIE Subject and 3 Elective Subjects (**22 credits in total**), opt for the Postgraduate Diploma.
From 2025/26 Cohort onwards:
- Compulsory Subjects (4 subjects - 12 credits) (Non-Dissertation Option / Dissertation Option): MM5112 Organization and Management; MM5412 Business Intelligence and Decisions; MM5424 Management Information Systems; MM5425 Business Analytics.
- AIE Subject (1 credit) (Non-Dissertation Option / Dissertation Option): MM5T21 Academic Integrity and Business Ethics (non-chargeable).
- Non-Dissertation Option Elective Subjects (any 6 subjects - 18 credits): MM501 Research Methods; MM5203 Decision Making for Leadership; MM531 Strategic Management; MM534 Entrepreneurship; MM5413 Business Forecasting; MM5426 Business Applications of Blockchain; MM5427 Textual Analysis in Business; MM5433 Decision Analytics by Machine Learning; MM544 E-Commerce; MM5451 Technology Innovation and Management; MM5452 Seminars in Emerging Technology; MM576 Marketing Management; MM5831 Social Media Marketing; LGT5102 Models for Decision Making; LGT5105 Managing Operations Systems; LGT5113 Enterprise Resource Planning; LGT5122 Applications of Decision Making Models; MM5913 Field Study for Business Management; MM5995 MM MSc Career Workshop (0 credit).
- Dissertation Option Dissertation Subjects (total 12 credits): MM501 Research Methods (3 credits); MM594 Business Analytics Dissertation (9 credits).
- Dissertation Option Elective Subjects (any 2 subject - 6 credits): MM5203 Decision Making for Leadership; MM531 Strategic Management; MM534 Entrepreneurship; MM5413 Business Forecasting; MM5426 Business Applications of Blockchain; MM5427 Textual Analysis in Business; MM5433 Decision Analytics by Machine Learning; MM544 E-Commerce; MM5451 Technology Innovation and Management; MM5452 Seminars in Emerging Technology; MM576 Marketing Management; MM5831 Social Media Marketing; LGT5102 Models for Decision Making; LGT5105 Managing Operations Systems; LGT5113 Enterprise Resource Planning; LGT5122 Applications of Decision Making Models; MM5913 Field Study for Business Management; MM5995 MM MSc Career Workshop (0 credit).
The offering of subjects is subject to class quota availability. Students may also choose from a list of [Common Pool Electives](https://www.polyu.edu.hk/fb/study/tpg-landing/common-pool-electives/), subject to the prescriptions of programme curriculum. Programme structure, course names and content are subject to continuous review and change.
Mode of study: **Mixed-mode**. Students can pursue their studies with either a full-time study load (**9 credits or more in a semester**) or a part-time study load (**less than 9 credits in a semester**). Students normally complete the programme full-time in **1.5 years** or part-time in **2.5 years**. The programme offers a structured progression pattern. Students are encouraged to follow the pattern to benefit from the cohort-based structure. Classes are normally scheduled on weekday evenings, with some daytime classes for full-time students. Each 3-credit subject requires **39 contact hours** over a teaching semester, with one 3-hour class per week.

program_overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc is part of Business and Management, AI, Computer and Data Science, and Mathematical Sciences. With the increasing use of data in business decision making, there is a need for graduates with a strong understanding of the tools and methodologies used for business analysis. Students learn to interpret data and use the results to inform business direction, build management and leadership skills, and learn to use the principal software tools for business analysis, graduating with certifications that demonstrate practical skills.
Study options include full-time study starting September 2026 or September 2027, each lasting 1 year. The location is Mile End.
The programme is jointly run by the [School of Business and Management](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/) and [School of Mathematical Sciences](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/). Students develop mathematical and statistical knowledge and gain practical experience using leading software tools. The course material aims to equip students with the skills to manage IT and analytics specialists, and to understand the leadership and organisational challenges associated with the digitisation of business processes. It examines how robust findings can be obtained from analytics and applied to the direction of businesses. The programme is taught using real-world cases from different markets and countries, and draws on the experience of an advisory group of current managers from real digital businesses. Summer placement opportunities with these industry partners may be available.
Programme structure:
- Six compulsory modules.
- Three optional modules.
- Compulsory group research project.
The Group Project in Business Analytics is the capstone module for the MSc in Business Analytics. Students work in groups to analyse a problem or question using complex data from a business context, with each group assigned a Mentor to guide the analytical problem, data organisation, analysis and presentation of results. The research project uses complex data from a business context, usually supplied by a partner company.
Teaching uses an interdisciplinary approach, including lectures led by experienced academics, Queen Mary’s Virtual Learning Environment QMplus, guest speakers, hands-on experience using industry-leading software, interactive seminars, presentations and group discussions. Students are assigned an Academic Advisor for academic and pastoral support throughout the course.
Industry and facilities features include:
- Learn from industry figures through connections with Citigroup, Nomura, Morgan Stanley, IBM and HP.
- ThinkPod interactive collaboration space with presentation, recording and video conferencing facilities.
- Free subscriptions to publications such as Bloomberg and Financial Times.
- Additional self-study content through DataCamp.
- Access to a wide range of software packages, including SAS and SPSS.
- 24-hour library on campus.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital. The Graduate Centre at Mile End provides 7,700 square metres of learning and teaching space.
The School of Business and Management is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business](https://www.aacsb.edu/about-us) (AACSB). In REF 2021, among 108 UK business schools, the School ranked 22nd for overall research quality, 28th for research outputs, 12th for research impact, and 21st for research environment.
Faculty associated with the programme include:
- [Dr Guven Demirel](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/demirelg.html), Reader in Supply Chain Management, whose research focuses on complex systems, including the resilience of supply networks, international business networks, and ecological networks.
- Dr Evangelos Markopoulos, Teaching Fellow (Lecturer) in Operations and Project Management, who bridges industry and academia with experience in practical research and industrial projects and initiatives.
- [Dr Sebastian del Bano Rollin](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/profiles/rollinsdelbano.html), Reader in Mathematics, who previously held senior positions in investment banking focused on mathematical finance and technology for trading and risk management.
- [Dr Georg von Graevenitz](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/vongraevenitzg.html), Reader in Quantitative Methods and Programme Director for MSc Business Analytics, who is involved in empirical research involving trade mark data and has advised competition and regulatory authorities and international organisations.
- Dr Zeynep Gürgüç, Lecturer in Digital Economy, whose research interests include experimental and behavioural economics, applied microeconomics, game theory, digital economy, innovative technologies in energy sustainability, climate change mitigation and adaptation, and blockchain-enabled market mechanisms.
Career paths: The university’s close connections with businesses in the United Kingdom and France provide opportunities to network with practitioners during guest lectures and project work done for businesses as clients. The course provides graduates with a foundation to pursue roles in data analysis and consulting across different industries. Alumni from the course are now working in roles such as Data Science Specialist, Data Analyst, Digital Strategy Analyst, Product Specialist and Senior Business Intelligence Developer.

curriculum.content:
The MSc in Business Analytics is available as a **full-time** course. It is taught at the University of London, within the Schools of Business and Management and the School of Mathematical Sciences on the London Campus.
Offerings:
- Business Analytics-Full Time-January (SEM2): Delivery mode **On Campus**; Duration **12 Months**.
- Business Analytics-Full Time-September (SEM1): Delivery mode **On Campus**; Duration **12 Months**.
The programme consists of **180 credits in total**: five compulsory modules each of 15 credits at level 7, three elective modules each of 15 credits at level 7, a Masterclass of 30 credits, and a Group Project of 30 credits.
Compulsory/core modules:
- MTH785P Programming for Business Analytics (term 1)
- MTH781P Data Analytics (term 1)
- BUS7061P Strategic Analysis (term 1)
- BUS7057P Leadership Skills for Business Analytics (term 1)
- BUS7064P Experiments for Business Analytics (term 2)
- BUS7052P The Masterclass in Business Analytics, core module worth **30 credits** (Semesters 1 & 2)
- BUS7051P Group Project worth **30 credits** (term 3) (core)
- BUS7140P Introduction to Mathematics and Statistics for Business (term 1), **0 credits**
Level 7 structure:
| Category | Credits | Modules |
|---|---:|---|
| Core, compulsory and guided elective | 150 | |
| Compulsory | 105 | BUS7052P - Masterclass in Business Analytics; BUS7057P - Leadership Skills for Business Analytics; BUS7061P - Strategic Analysis; MTH781P - Data Analytics; MTH785P - Programming for Business Analytics; BUS7064P - Experiments for Business and Analytics; BUS7140P - Introduction to Mathematics and Statistics for Business |
| Guided elective | 45 | MTH782P - SAS for Business Intelligence; BUS7005P - Project Management; MTH783P - Time Series Analysis for Business; MTH792P - Financial Data Analytics; MTH784P - Optimisation for Business Processes; BUS7053P - Complex Networks and Innovation; BUS7093P - Entrepreneurship for Digital Technologies; BUS7088P - Digital Business, Innovation and Transparency |
| Dissertation / project | 30 | BUS7051P - Group Project in Business Analytics |
In project based course units (Masterclass and Group Project) students work together to acquire team working skills and knowledge. Work in the Masterclass and the Group Project is examined on the basis of a written report, a formal oral presentation, and a demonstration of the insights from analysis carried by the students.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
This policy applies to admission to all undergraduate, postgraduate (taught and research) programmes at Queen Mary University of London where the Queen Mary central Admissions team is responsible for administration of the admissions process, except for listed Medicine and Dentistry exclusions.
- **Conditional offer** – the offer includes conditions which the applicant must achieve before their place on the programme is confirmed. Conditions may include achievement of minimum grades, academic qualifications, English language qualifications and scores, and non-academic requirements, such as confirmation of scholarship funding.
- **Alternative offer (change of course offer)** – an alternative offer may be made where the applicant is not qualified for the programme for which they applied, but a different course, which may be at a lower level (e.g. Pre-Masters, Foundation) or may have lower entry requirements, is available. This is not offered automatically in all circumstances and offered based on agreed criteria of the programme or at the discretion of the admissions office in consultation with the Director of Admissions or Academic School.
- Applicants holding conditional offers will be informed of the procedure for submitting evidence that they have met their offer conditions, in the form of qualification documents or other evidence. Queen Mary matches the qualifications and grades achieved to the conditions specified in the offer. Where all offer conditions are met, the applicant’s place is confirmed. Where the applicant has fallen short of the offer conditions, Queen Mary may exercise discretion and confirm the place in line with agreed minimum thresholds for admission, subject to the availability of places.
- Deferred entry offers for postgraduate programmes may include English language conditions.

program_overview.content:
The MSc Business Analytics is a **1 year full-time** postgraduate taught programme at **Queen's Business School**. The increase in the volume, variety, and velocity of data creates opportunities for businesses to improve decision making and develop new data driven products and services. The MSc Business Analytics has been developed to meet the demand for qualified professionals who possess the necessary expertise to realise end-to-end business analytics solutions and are equipped to utilise data for business decision-making purposes.
The programme is built around the three core areas needed to succeed in analytics: **business knowledge, statistics, and computing**. It includes modules focusing on the application of analytics in core business functions such as marketing and human resources, as well as developing and applying technical skills such as advanced analytics and machine learning, text mining, data management, and data driven decision making. In total, students will study **eight modules** in addition to pre-course training and a final dissertation project. The programme includes an induction, where pre-course training in key statistics and computer skills will ensure students from a range of backgrounds have the necessary skills to undertake the course.
The dissertation is a key highlight of the programme, providing students with the opportunity to undertake an independent project where they will create a technical business analytics solution incorporating all elements of the programme. The dissertation requires students to draw from across the course, incorporating knowledge from the three core business analytics domains: statistics, computing, and business.
**Industry Links:** Developed by staff with industry and academic backgrounds, the course is tailored towards the key skills required to succeed in a business analytics role. Some students on the programme may engage in Data Duo Mentoring with businesses, providing advice on how to utilise business data and gaining valuable career and professional mentoring; places are dependent on business demand, usually approximately **15 places**. In partnership with the QBS Analytics Lab, students also have the opportunity to participate in the annual Data for Good hackathon, working with industry mentors to develop data driven solutions aimed at solving important societal problems.
**Career Development:** Industry reports show a global shortage for data scientists. Students will learn to use cutting edge and industry standard tools and techniques to enable career development. Students on the course can benefit from the QBS Postgraduate Employability Programme, which aims to enhance core employability skills through interactive workshops, informational sessions, and employer presentations.
Students will learn how to use state-of-the-art, industry standard software over the duration of the programme, including Python, R, SQL, KNIME, Power BI and Tableau. Queen’s University Belfast has also benefitted from an in-kind donation from US-based Alteryx Software, valued at approximately **$15 million**, including licenses that provide students with free access to software, training, and accreditation in data analytics.
Teaching methods include a mix of computer lab based sessions and lectures. Tools and techniques learned in the classroom context will be used to address business problems, with teaching methods including computer/software practical demonstrations and training, lectures, tutorials, seminars, problem-centred techniques such as national and international case studies, non-book media, individual research, oral presentations, group projects, online discussion forums, industry visits and practitioner workshops.
The programme will appeal to students who intend to pursue a career in a business analytics related field, such as data science, business intelligence, consultancy, informatics, or decision intelligence. Graduates from this programme have secured roles with employers such as KPMG, PwC, EY, Tata Consulting, Citi, FD Technologies, Alibaba Group, and Severn Trent. Typical roles include data analyst, data scientist, business analyst, and consultant.
[Dr. Byron Graham](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/portal/en/persons/byron-graham(20096cb7-57e8-4fb9-a5b7-8a0411f67154).html) is Programme Director in Queen's Business School. With a background in industry and academia, Dr Graham specialises in helping businesses gain benefits from the effective use of data for decision making and new products and processes. His current research focuses on the application of machine learning and other data science approaches to solve business problems.

curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)**.
The programme is built around three core areas: business knowledge, statistics, and computing. In total, students will study **eight modules** in addition to **pre-course training** and a **final dissertation project**. The programme will include an induction, where pre-course training in key statistics and computer skills will ensure students from a range of backgrounds have the necessary skills to undertake the course.
Course Structure: MSc Business Analytics students can expect to study the following modules:
- Semester 1: Statistics for Business; Data Management; HR Analytics; Artificial Intelligence in Business and Society.
- Semester 2: Advanced Analytics and Machine Learning; Data Mining; Data Driven Decision Making; Marketing Analytics.
- Semester 3: Dissertation.
Core Modules:
| Module | Credits | Teaching Period | Duration | Core/Optional |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Statistics for Business | 15 | Autumn | 15 weeks | Core |
| Data Management | 15 | Autumn | 15 weeks | Core |
| Advanced Analytics & Machine Learning | 15 | Spring | 15 weeks | Core |
| Data Driven Decision Making | 15 | Spring | 15 weeks | Core |
| Artificial Intelligence in Business and Society | 15 | Autumn | 15 weeks | Core |
| Dissertation MSc Business Analytics | 60 | Summer | 15 weeks | Core |
| Marketing Analytics | 15 | Spring | 15 weeks | Core |
| Data Mining | 15 | Spring | 15 weeks | Core |
| MSc Business Analytics Dissertation Portfolio | 60 | Summer | 15 weeks | Core |
| Human Resources Analytics BA | 15 | Autumn | 15 weeks | Core |
The dissertation provides students with the opportunity to undertake an independent project. This will involve the development of a technical business analytics solution incorporating elements from the course. The suggested technologies for the solution will be those covered in the course. The solution should typically include a combination of a database, machine learning, and a visualisation component. In addition to the technical solution, students will be required to produce an initial feasibility study, a technical report, and a written report including a review of the literature, methodology for solving the problem, and results, discussion and conclusions.
Learning and teaching methods include a mix of computer lab based sessions and lectures. Teaching methods include computer/software practical demonstrations and training, lectures, tutorials, seminars, problem-centred techniques such as national and international case studies, non-book media, individual research, oral presentations, group projects, online discussion forums, industry visits and practitioner workshops. Assessments will focus on both theory and practical application of business analytics, including the use of data to gain business insights, the development of analytics solutions, essays and group work. Students will have approximately **30 hours direct academic contact time** per module and normally approximately **120 hours** on individual study time plus assessment completion per module.

application_materials.content:
Typically, postgraduate applicants should supply relevant supporting documents, but should consult school webpages for any specific or additional requirements.
- **Proof of previous degree(s):** usually an academic transcript and certificate. If you have not yet graduated, upload your most recent transcript showing results to date. If studying qualifications from outside the UK, also include documents indicating the marking scheme used.
- **Official English translations:** if certificates or transcripts are in a language other than English, include official, authenticated English translations with the original documents. The translation should state it is accurate and include the translator/translation company contact details, credentials or qualifications, date of translation, and full name and signature.
- **Academic references:** for postgraduate taught courses, most applications will not require references. Sometimes one or two references are requested in the application or assessment process. If requested, references should normally be from academic staff at university-level institutions; one employer reference may be used if you have been out of education for the last two years. References should normally be dated no more than two years before the course start date, at least one should be from your most recent institution if you studied at more than one, and referees should not be family members. Uploaded references **must be signed, dated and on official letterheaded paper**.
- **English language certificates (International applicants):** the certificate from the test provider/awarding body confirming you have been awarded the qualification.
- **Supporting statement:** for most postgraduate taught courses, a supporting statement is not required, although you may be asked about your motivation for studying the course. Where a personal statement is required, supply a statement of **at least 300 words** giving your reasons for applying and any other information in support of your application, such as how your previous education and experience relates to the course and how the course fits your long-term academic or career plans.
- **Curriculum vitae (CV)/resume:** you may wish to supply a CV or resume, particularly if you have professional experience relevant to the area you want to study.
- **Examples of work:** some courses may ask for samples of written work or a portfolio of artwork; where required, information will be included on the course webpages.
Supporting documents can be attached to the online application when applying or later by [logging back into the application](https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/postgradapplication). Upload high quality scanned colour copies or colour photographs showing the full document, including all text, images and security features. Clear, colour photographs or scans of original qualification documents must confirm the qualification has been awarded, show the date of award, and show the final awarded grade.

program_overview.content:
The MSc Business Analytics is offered by the Management School, Faculty of Social Sciences. The course starts in September 2026, lasts **1 year**, and is **full-time**.
The complex business challenges of today need managers with the analytical and technical skills to tackle them. Students gain skills including the use of Python and data visualisation, and explore how to apply them to decision-making within a business.
Making effective decisions is crucial in today’s business world. This course will develop the skills needed to analyse complex business challenges and make decisions that have a positive impact. Students do not need to have studied data or analytics before; the course starts with fundamentals and progresses to complex analytical models, decision-making and independent research.
The course uses links with industry to bring guest lecturers to the course, and students work with real-world data sets to put skills into practice. Working with industry experts helps students develop knowledge of working with stakeholders to understand their needs. For the project dissertation, students can choose to work with an organisation to gain more industry experience and apply course theory to a real-world challenge.
The Management School is Triple Crown accredited by [AMBA](https://www.associationofmbas.com/), [EQUIS](https://www.efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/) and [AACSB](https://www.aacsb.edu/).
Teaching methods include lectures, seminars, tutorials and computer-based laboratories. Assessment methods include exams, essays, projects, portfolios, lab sessions and tests, presentations, and a dissertation project.
The course includes an industry-focused capstone project, desirably conducted in collaboration with business partners, where students apply analytical skills to solve practical business problems and gain real-world experience.
Students graduate with knowledge and experience for a career in business analytics, gaining hands-on skills such as Python programming for data analysis and automation, data wrangling, statistical modelling and basic predictive analytics, mathematical programming and optimisation for business decision-making, data visualisation using tools like Power BI, Tableau or Python libraries, database management and data governance principles, business problem-solving using analytics tools, decision support systems and scenario analysis, communication of data insights, and project-based learning through the Capstone Project.
Possible career pathways include Business/Data Analyst, Analytics Consultant, Data Scientist, Operations/Supply Chain Analyst, Marketing/Customer Insights Analyst, Risk/Financial Analyst, Business Intelligence, Product/Strategy Analyst, and Supply Chain/Data Coordinator. These roles could be based in industries such as consulting, finance, retail, logistics, tech, healthcare and government.
Dr Emilia Vann Yaroson, Lecturer in Operations and Supply Chain Management in the Management School, is listed as an academic involved in the programme.

- The scholarship is for full-time and part-time students only. Students studying online or via distance learning are not eligible.
- Part-time students will receive the full-time equivalent of the scholarship split pro rata over the duration of the Masters course, subject to all eligibility and award criteria.
- If you are studying a 2-year masters programme the scholarship will be available in the second year of your studies subject to successful completion of year 1.
- This scholarship cannot be deferred to a future year of entry.

multiple_applications.content:
Part 2 is where you select the course or courses you want to apply for. **You can apply for a total of three different postgraduate courses.**
If you want to apply for more than one course, you don't need to submit them all at the same time. Each course choice has its own 'Submit Application' button.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
If we've offered you a study place and you will be unable to attend at the start of your course, you may be able to defer your entry to the next admission point. Most postgraduate taught courses have one admission per year, at the start of the autumn semester in September/October.
For most courses, you can request a deferral through [your original online application](https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/postgradapplication) by clicking on the 'Request Deferral' link in the 'Your Applications' section. Requesting a deferral will deactivate your current offer, so you should only request one when you're sure that you can't start on the original start date. If you aren't sure, the University advises submitting a new application for the next admission point, when applications open for that year.
If the academic selectors approve your request, the University will send you an amended offer letter with a deferred start date. You should submit your deferral request by the deadline published on the [key dates](https://sheffield.ac.uk/postgraduate/deadlines "Key dates and deadlines for postgraduate courses") webpage.
You can ask to defer your application for a **maximum of two academic years from your original start date**. If you want to defer beyond that, the University will ask you to re-apply. Deferral requests are reviewed by admissions selectors, then the University will let you know the decision. The University can't always review deferral requests when they receive them, and can't issue deferred offers until after the new admissions year has begun, usually in September. Receipt of the request will be acknowledged within two weeks.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
#### Pathway programme for international students
If you're an international student who does not meet the entry requirements for this course, you have the opportunity to apply for a pre-masters programme in [Science and Engineering](https://usic.sheffield.ac.uk/programmes/pre-masters/science-and-engineering) or [Business, Social Sciences and Humanities](https://usic.sheffield.ac.uk/programmes/pre-masters/business-social-sciences-and-humanities) at the [University of Sheffield International College](https://usic.sheffield.ac.uk/). This course is designed to develop your English language and academic skills. Upon successful completion, you can progress to degree level study at the University of Sheffield.

application_materials.content:
Required application materials include:
- **A degree transcript** in one of the suggested disciplines.
- **One reference**.
- **A personal statement**.
- Overseas applicants should also supply evidence of their English language ability, usually via an IELTS test. Other acceptable tests by UCL can be found on [UCL’s English Language requirements webpage](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements).
For the personal statement, UCL asks applicants to address:
- Why do you want to study Business Analytics at a postgraduate level;
- What particularly attracts you to this programme and to the UCL School of Management;
- How does your academic and professional background meet the demands of this challenging programme;
- What your post-degree aspirations are and how does your success on this programme support them?
The personal statement is an opportunity to illustrate whether your reasons for applying to this programme match what the programme will deliver and is a right fit for you. Applicants should use this part of the application to show uniqueness, critical thinking, personality, academic prowess, and passion for business, technology, and data.

interview_requirements.content: If you meet the entry requirements and are suitable for the MSc Business Analytics programme, you may be invited for an online interview. Those invited to interview will have a window of **7 calendar days** from receipt of the email to complete the interview. Failure to complete the interview within this window will lead to an unsuccessful application.

academic_requirements.content:
- **Entry:** Minimum of **2:1 honours or equivalent in a relevant discipline**.
- **Academic Profile:** The minimum entrance requirements are an **upper second-class (2:1) Bachelor’s degree from a UK university or an overseas equivalent** and a **strong aptitude for quantitative analysis**. Applicants are likely to have studied a range of degrees including **business, engineering, computer science, economics, and psychology**. International students may ascertain qualification equivalents from the [UCL international students website](http://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/international-students).
- **Contextual offers:** UCL normally requires an upper second-class Bachelor’s degree from a UK university or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard. Applicants with **lower second-class degrees (UK 2:2 or the overseas equivalent)** may be considered if their application is supported strongly by relevant experience.
- Technical skills: UCL recommends applicants have experience of using a programming language, as this will be required throughout the programme.
- Mathematical/statistical skills: A good mathematical understanding is needed for the programme.
- If degree results are just under a 2:1, applicants who fall short of the academic requirements by a small margin but have **significant work experience (over 2 years) in relevant fields** may be considered on an exceptional case basis; this is not guaranteed to secure a place.
- **China-specific equivalency:** A **four-year bachelor’s degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered. The required grade varies depending on the awarding university.
- **China-specific 2:1 equivalent:** Applicants from UCL’s list of Chinese universities, which includes a selection of Project 211, Project 985, and Double First-Class universities, need a Bachelor’s degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 85%** for upper second-class (2:1). Not all universities from these projects are included.
- **China-specific 2:1 equivalent for all other recognised Chinese universities:** Applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education need a Bachelor’s degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 90%** for upper second-class (2:1).

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
Business Analytics MSc requires UCL English language **Level 2**. Applicants whose first language is not English must provide evidence that their spoken and written English is adequate. UCL’s preferred English language qualification is IELTS.
- **IELTS Academic:** **overall 7.0**, with **minimum 6.5 in each component/subtest**. IELTS Academic Online is accepted. IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- **TOEFL iBT, tests taken from 21 January 2026:** **overall 4.5**, with **4.5 in reading, writing, speaking and listening**.
- **TOEFL iBT, tests taken before 21 January 2026:** **overall 96**, with **24/30 in reading and writing** and **22/30 in speaking and listening**. Tests must be within the two-year timeframe. TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted; TOEFL iBT MyBestScore is not acceptable. UCL’s institution code for TOEFL is **9163**.
- **Cambridge English C2 Proficiency (CPE):** **overall 180**, with **172 in all subtests**.
- **Cambridge English C1 Advanced (CAE):** **overall 180**, with **172 in all subtests**.
- **Pearson Test of English (Academic) / PTE Academic:** **overall 76**, with **minimum 75 in each Communicative Skill**.
Any student who is not a national of a UK Home Office majority English-speaking country is required to provide recent evidence of English language proficiency. Those who have studied in English or completed at least **12 months** of academic education leading to an awarded qualification in a country UCL considers to be “majority English-speaking” may not be required to provide further English Language qualification/test results. More information is available on UCL’s [English Language Requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements) page.

program_overview.content:
**Start date:** September 2026
**Duration:** 12 months full-time
**Location:** This programme is delivered in person at UCL School of Management’s Canary Wharf campus. The majority of classes are taught at [Levels 38, 49, and 50 of One Canada Square, Canary Wharf](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/about/canary-wharf), UCL’s home within London’s global business district. Some optional modules will take place at the Bloomsbury campus, which will also be open to students. The course lasts for a full calendar year from mid-September 2026 to mid-September 2027 and is not offered part-time.
Join this one-year MSc in Business Analytics at the UCL School of Management to prepare for data analytics and leadership roles by developing the skills needed to unlock the value of data and understand how it is revolutionising areas such as strategy, marketing, and operations. The programme develops understanding of the nuances, potential, and limitations of data, as well as statistical and computational skills to make effective use of the latest analytics tools and methods, frame complex data-driven business problems, analyse data with appropriate statistical techniques, and communicate analytics results to senior leadership, business partners, and customers.
The UCL Business Analytics programme provides a rigorous, practical foundation and a platform for careers with global companies and high-growth businesses tackling world-scale problems, with opportunities to tap into partnerships to grow networks and skills further.
On UCL’s Business Analytics MSc programme, students develop a rigorous understanding of how companies use data to make decisions and improve business performance. The programme combines modules exploring how data and analytics are transforming key areas of business, such as decision-making, strategy, marketing, and operations, with modules providing the statistical and computational foundations needed to use the latest business analytics tools and platforms. During the year, students undertake six core modules, two optional modules, and complete a Consulting Project/Dissertation. Students gain experience in data analysis techniques including computational thinking, validation and testing models, manipulating datasets, regression models, and statistical modelling, with many modules requiring leading business analytics tools such as Python.
The programme is delivered through lectures, optional workshops, and project work. Assessment methods include in-person examinations, tests, quizzes, individual coursework, group coursework, presentations, and a dissertation project. Students typically study four modules in Term One and four modules in Term Two, of which two are selected from the optional module list. In Term Three, students undertake the supervised dissertation project.
In Term Three, students may undertake either a practical consulting project with organisations that have provided a challenging analytical project, or an independent consulting/research project. Projects require the application of skills learned in Terms One and Two and have historically required students to work with leading-edge tools and techniques, resulting in a dissertation report of 12,000 words and a 15-minute presentation. Dissertation project types include research projects, technical projects, and consultative projects.
The teaching team brings together people with experience of how companies are evolving their management practices in a complex, interconnected and data-driven world and how they are employing the latest business analytics platforms and tools to make decisions and improve business performance. Dimitris Giraleas is Programme Director. The core teaching team includes [Alastair Moore](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/alastairmoore), Assistant Professor; [Anil Doshi](http://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/anildoshi), Assistant Professor; [Zhenyu Zhang](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/mengzhenyuzhang), Assistant Professor; [Tjun Hoh](http://management.ucl.ac.uk/people/tjunyeehoh), Assistant Professor; and [Wei Miao](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/people/miaowei), Assistant Professor.
UCL School of Management is AACSB accredited, a global mark of excellence recognising its commitment to innovative, research-led teaching, rigorous academic standards, and preparing students for impactful global careers in business and management. Students also benefit from extensive industry networks and close links with many global companies and high-growth businesses.
The Careers service offered to MSc Business Analytics students is designed to help build a strong foundation for early career success through tailored support, employer engagement, and alumni connections. MSc Business Analytics students receive bespoke careers support from a specialist careers team, including one-to-one career coaching with professionally-certified, industry-focused Careers Consultants, access to a global alumni network, online resources, and a Careers and Professional Development Programme for postgraduate taught students.
Graduates pursue global careers across a wide range of roles, sectors, and geographies. Popular sectors include consulting, banking and finance, marketing, technology, and data and analytics. Top job titles among recent graduates include Data analysts, Programmers and software development professionals, Actuaries, economists and statisticians, Information technology professionals, IT business analysts, architects and systems designers. Top companies graduates have secured roles in include Bloomberg LP, 173 Tech, Burberry Ltd, CenterPoint, Cloud IQ and EY.

curriculum.content:
- **Start date:** September 2026. **Duration:** 12 months full-time. **Location:** This programme is delivered in person at UCL’s Canary Wharf campus. Full-time course dates: Mid-September 2026 - Mid-September 2027. The programme is not offered as part-time study.
- During the year, students undertake six core modules, two optional modules, and complete a Consulting Project/Dissertation. Students typically study four modules in Term One and four modules in Term Two, of which two are selected from the optional module list. In Term Three, students undertake the supervised dissertation project.
- The programme is delivered through a combination of lectures, optional workshops and project work. Assessment methods include in-person examinations, tests, quizzes, individual coursework, group coursework, presentations and a dissertation project. Each taught module is delivered over 10 weeks, with three contact hours per week comprising lecture content and interactive components; some modules may have additional workshop sessions. Students should spend approximately 7-12 hours a week for each module on assessment and independent study.
- Term One core modules: [**MSIN0093 Business Strategy and Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/business-strategy-and-analytics/MSIN0093); [**MSIN0094 Marketing Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/marketing-analytics/MSIN0094); [**MSIN0096 Statistical Foundations for Business Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/mathematical-foundations-of-business-analytics/MSIN0096); [**MSIN0143 Programming for Business Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/programming-for-business-analytics/MSIN0143).
- Term Two core modules: [**MSIN0097 Predictive Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/predictive-analytics/MSIN0097); [**MSIN0095 Operations Analytics**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/operations-analytics/MSIN0095).
- Term Two optional modules are chosen from an indicative list including [**MSIN0166 Data Engineering**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/data-engineering-MSIN0166), [**MSIN0167 Data Visualisation**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/data-visualisation-MSIN0167), [**MSIN0221 Natural Language Processing**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/natural-language-processing-MSIN0221), [**MSIN0088 Leading High-Performance Teams**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/leading-high-performance-teams-MSIN0088), [**MSIN0098 Technology Entrepreneurship**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/technology-entrepreneurship-MSIN0098), [**MSIN0148 Influence and Negotiations**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/influence-and-negotiations-MSIN0148), [**MSIN0159 Decision and Risk Analysis**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/decision-and-risk-analysis-MSIN0159), [**MSIN0226 Fintech**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/fintech-MSIN0226), [**MSIN0236 Managing Diversity**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/managing-diversity-MSIN0236), [**MSIN0261 Building Sustainable Ventures**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/building-sustainable-ventures-MSIN0261), and [**COMP0142 Machine Learning for Domain Specialists**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/machine-learning-for-domain-specialists-COMP0142). Optional modules are subject to change each year.
- Term Three: students undertake a [**Consulting/Dissertation Project**](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/business-analytics-consulting-projectdissertation/MSIN0114). Students may undertake either a practical consulting project with organisations that have provided a challenging analytical project or an independent consulting/research project. Projects require application of skills learned in terms one and two and have historically resulted in a dissertation report of 12,000 words and a 15-minute presentation.
- Dissertation project types include Type One: Research Projects, Type Two: Technical Projects, and Type Three: Consultative Projects. The programme notes a more detailed overview of the [three types of dissertation projects](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/blog/exploring-innovation-three-types-dissertation-projects-our-business-analytics-programme).
- The majority of classes are taught at [Levels 38, 49, and 50 of One Canada Square, Canary Wharf](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/about/canary-wharf). Some optional modules will take place at the Bloomsbury campus.
