financial_aid.content:
- **MSc Business Analytics Scholarships:** A total of **£40,000** of scholarships are are available for outstanding candidates on the MSc Business Analytics programme. All applicants who apply to study MSc Business Analytics at UCL and who meet the scholarship criteria will be considered for scholarship funding.
- University College London offers a range of scholarships across all programmes. Postgraduate scholarships are typically awarded to the most talented students across a range of categories, and applicants wishing to obtain scholarships are strongly encouraged to apply early.
- **UCL East Scholarships:** This scholarship supports east Londoners by funding tuition fees and living costs of all UCL East Master’s programmes and select School of Management programmes. [Learn more about the UCL East Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/ucl-east-london-scholarship)
- **UCL Global Master’s Scholarship:** The UCL Global Masters Scholarship aims to enable and encourage international students from lower income backgrounds to pursue full-time Master’s degree studies at UCL. There are **85 scholarships available each year worth up to £15,000 each**. The scholarship is awarded on the basis of financial need and upon the recommendation of the Student Funding Office. [Learn more about the UCL Global Master’s Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/ucl-global-masters-scholarship)
- **UCL Musubi Global Master’s Scholarship (Japan):** There is **one scholarship of £20,250** available to a Japanese student applying to study during the **2026/2027 academic year**. [Learn more about the Musubi Global Master’s Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/musubi-global-masters-scholarship)
- **UCL Fee Partnerships:** UCL has partnerships with external funding providers in which the university offers a contribution towards tuition fees. Applications for the awards listed should be made directly to the external funding body; applicants must also apply directly to UCL for a place on a programme of study at the same time. Applicants selected for the relevant external awards, who are also offered a place at UCL, will then automatically qualify for the fee contribution. [View the complete list of fee partnerships](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/fee-partnerships)
- **Fulbright Commission Award:** The Fulbright Commission Award is available for a US graduate student or those with equivalent experience in a relevant field to study any MSc programme at the UCL School of Management. Please note this is only available to citizens of the United States of America. [Learn more about the Fullbright Commission Award](https://fulbright.org.uk/our-programmes/fulbright-scholarships-to-the-uk/us-postgraduates/)
- UCL recommends using UCL’s [Scholarship Finder](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/scholarships-finder) to find all of the scholarships that are available. [Learn more about scholarships at UCL](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships)

multiple_applications.content:
You may submit applications for a maximum of **two** taught graduate courses for entry to the 2026/27 academic year. The applications must be for different courses. Please note that if an application fee is charged, it will be charged per application. UCL does not accept multiple applications for the same course in the same academic year.
If you apply for more than one course the fee is payable for each application that requires an application fee.
Once you have submitted an application you cannot change the course that you have applied for. If you would like to apply for a different course, you will need to submit a new application for the course you wish to be considered for.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer, but will consider requests in exceptional circumstances outside the offer holder's control. Deferral requests are considered only for: serious illness of the offer holder or serious illness/death of a parent, guardian, partner or child; parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months; being directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster; being awarded a UCL scholarship or full scholarship from a recognised funding body for study in the following academic year; or holding an offer to study the UCL International Pre-Masters.
To be eligible for a deferral, the offer holder must hold **an unconditional offer which has been accepted** and must have **paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt** if a deposit is required for the programme. If the request is approved, tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment.
Deferral requests must be made on the offer page of the application portal. Requests due to illness or parental/adoption leave require a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. Scholarship-based requests require an official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information before making a final decision.
An application **cannot be deferred twice**. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants. The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If the request is unsuccessful, applicants who cannot join that year may apply for the next academic year once applications open, but applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake. If a deferral is approved, a new offer letter will be issued and the applicant may need to take a new English test if the current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
You must meet all your conditions and hold an unconditional offer before you can enrol.
- Your offer letter will contain information on any deadlines that apply to your offer. If circumstances mean that you will not be able to meet your offer conditions by these dates, contact the [Graduate Admissions Team](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/stay-touch/ask-admissions-postgraduate-and-teacher-training-enquiries).
- Your offer letter will outline exactly which degree documents you need to provide. UCL cannot accept anything other than final official documents to meet the conditions of your offer.
- If you need to take an English language test to meet your offer conditions, UCL recommends booking a test as early as possible. If providing English language test scores, you must provide official results; UCL will not accept screenshots of your results portal.
- You can take a UCL Pre-sessional English course to settle the English language condition in your offer. See the [Pre-sessional English website](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses/pre-sessional-english-courses/pg) for entry requirements, availability and applications.
- To clear offer conditions, upload copies to the applicant portal if you have an academic condition and have received your degree documents and transcripts from your university. Proof of English language proficiency must also be uploaded to the applicant portal.
- If you have not met your academic offer condition, you should still upload your documents; the Admissions team will still consider whether your offer can be confirmed.
- If you have not met your English language test condition but have received scores that meet the UCL level 1 requirement, you can still supply your test scores to UCL for review. UCL will not ordinarily accept a lower score than stipulated in the offer and cannot consider test scores that do not meet the UCL level 1 requirement.

application_materials.content:
- Mandatory for all applicants: **Academic transcripts**.
- Course-specific requirements may include samples of written work or professional portfolio work, personal statement, curriculum vitae (CV) or resume, and academic reference ([Guidance for references (PDF, 54kb)](https://www.york.ac.uk/media/study-new/postgraduate/postgraduatetaught/applying/guidance-for-references.pdf)).
- International applicants: Evidence of your English language ability.
- A transcript must be provided with your application before it's submitted. If you've completed your studies, provide copies of your degree certificates and formal transcripts of your academic record, including full details of degrees, classifications, grades obtained and modules/units taken. If the qualification was taken in a non-English-speaking country, provide documents in the original language with a formally certified English translation. If you have not yet finished your studies, provide an interim transcript of results to date.
- Written work: some courses require a sample of written work; details of what is required will be in the application form. [Find out more about course-specific written work requirements](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/apply/documents/written-work/).
- Personal statement: a personal statement can be included as part of your application; for some courses it forms part of the assessment process. Details of what to include will be provided during the application process. [Find out more about course-specific requirements for personal statements](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/apply/documents/personal-statements/).
- Curriculum vitae/resume: your CV or resume can be uploaded as part of your application to provide further information on prior experience and qualifications.
- Academic referee: you will need to supply the details of **one referee** when you submit your application. The referee may be contacted by email and asked to provide a reference if needed. You should provide an academic referee if you have graduated within the last five years.
- If English is not your first language, you may be asked to provide evidence of your English language ability to the required level. If you've taken an [approved English language test](https://www.york.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-taught/apply/international/english/), upload a copy of your certificate.
- File formats: Word (.doc or .docx), Acrobat (.pdf), text (.txt); scanned documents should be JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg), Acrobat (.pdf) or GIF (.gif). **Each document must be less than 1MB**.
- Multiple page documents, such as a transcript, should be scanned as **one file**, eg a single PDF, and should not fill more than one document slot.
- Additional documents can be provided after submitting your application via your You@York account. Do not email documents because this will cause delays in assessing your application.

Applications to study a postgraduate taught course at York in 2026/27 close on **28 August 2026** for international applications (excluding online courses). Some courses may have earlier closing dates.

program_overview.content:
MSc Business Analytics starts in September 2026 and is a **1 year full-time** course in the [School for Business and Society](https://www.york.ac.uk/business-society/). It is designed to develop competent analytics professionals using artificial intelligence, statistics and operational research to tackle complex business and societal challenges.
The MSc provides an in-depth understanding of data science principles and analytics techniques. Taught by leading analytics researchers and practitioners, it equips students with essential skills in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, operational research, computer programming, and their applications within business and society. The programme emphasises social responsibility and environmental sustainability, preparing students to address real-world challenges effectively and ethically.
Python is used as the main programming language for essential data science and analytics modules, including computer programming, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, operational research, and data communication. The course covers the business analytics life cycle, including descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. Alongside the core curriculum, students choose option modules across business and management, social science, science, and engineering disciplines, allowing them to customise their studies around advanced data science and analytics methods and business or societal applications. The course also develops independent research skills leading to an applied-focus dissertation project.
The course is taught through a combination of lectures and practical workshops, with most modules featuring more workshops than lectures. Teaching focuses heavily on practical data science and business analytics skills using Python for real-world application. Each module consists of 20 credits, with the final research task totalling 60 credits. Assessment includes computer programmes, written reports, oral presentations and a poster.
Students are based in the [School for Business and Society](https://www.york.ac.uk/map/#locid271) on Campus West. Most teaching takes place in the Church Lane Building, with additional contact hours elsewhere on Campus East and Campus West. The Church Lane Building features modern teaching rooms, a café, and spaces for group work and socialising. The programme also uses well-equipped computer classrooms with software available on Windows, Mac and Linux-based operating systems.
The School for Business and Society is a UK top 30 research department for management according to the Times Higher Education ranking of the latest REF results (2021). The programme is taught by world-leading academics in data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, statistics, business analytics, and operational research, and the faculty includes authors of world-leading textbooks taught on the programme.
Career preparation includes opportunities to apply knowledge through complex real-world problems, case studies, group projects, and an applied dissertation. Career opportunities listed for graduates include business analyst, market research analyst, quantitative analyst, policy analyst, data scientist, analytics engineer, and management consultant. Transferable skills include data science and analytics techniques, artificial intelligence and machine learning knowledge, statistical analysis, operational research and data visualisation, critical thinking and problem solving, data communication and presentation skills, project management and leadership skills, and research capabilities.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
There are two types of offer that you might receive.
- **Conditional offers**: York makes conditional offers when there are criteria you need to meet before you can start your course. If your offer is conditional, the conditions of entry will be included in your offer letter.
- Offer conditions typically fall into three categories: **academic**, **language** (if you're a non-native English-speaking applicant you must provide evidence of your English language proficiency), and **reference conditions**.
- Supporting documents needed to meet the conditions of your offer should be uploaded via You@York. If you do not meet the original conditions of your offer, you should upload your documentation anyway, as York may be able to reconsider you.
- Once you have met all the conditions of your offer, York will email you confirming this, and an unconditional offer letter will be available online to download and print.
- If you require a Student Visa, York can issue your CAS once your offer becomes unconditional, and not longer than six months before your course starts.

program_overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
**Understand the people behind the data as you unlock crucial insights businesses need to grow.** Brands are constantly looking to make smarter, more meaningful connections with consumers, so customer data has never been more important. With a strong focus on understanding the numbers behind human behaviour, this course gives you both advanced analytical skills and strategic marketing know-how. Learn skills spanning big data, predictive analytics and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and stand out with this unique Masters. From retail, location planning, logistics and marketing, your options are open to forge the path you want to take next. Plus, you'll be based in Leeds, a city that’s right at the heart of global marketing action.
Why study at Leeds:
- **Give yourself the edge in a competitive job market:** Gain sought-after skills in analytical expertise and psychological insight.
- **A course with dual focus:** With input from Leeds University Business School and the School of Geography, this means you’ll be connecting complex analytics directly to market outcomes.
- **Affiliation with the UK’s [Consumer Data Research Centre](https://www.cdrc.ac.uk/):** Make the most of our connections as well as the expertise of the School of Geography’s [Centre for Spatial Analysis and Policy](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research-centre-spatial-analysis-policy).
- **Close industry connections:** Connect you to emerging trends in topics including consumer behaviour, decision science and digital and interactive marketing.
- **Access a wealth of data and resources:** When it comes to data sciences, our campus-based [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) is the place to be.
- **State-of-the-art computing facilities:** You can immerse yourself in coding, programming and modelling software.
- **Join Leeds Data Society:** You can join societies that link in with your studies which regularly hosts guest speakers from other organisations.
- **International Study Tour:** Apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/masters/doc/international-study-tour-2) which includes company visits, guest lectures and networking events.
Leeds University Business School has triple accreditation from the three leading bodies, AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS.
Core modules will introduce you to a range of analytical methods, ensuring you develop a solid foundation in the essential skills for consumer analytics and marketing strategy. You’ll learn how to analyse geographic data using GIS software, developing your knowledge of retail modelling to evaluate new markets and locations. You’ll study consumer and business analytics, while learning how to deploy data to inform decisions about marketing strategy. You’ll also be involved in collaborative work to analyse data and make marketing predictions. The choice of one optional module allows you to develop your marketing or geography interests, explore new ideas and concepts, or develop skills and knowledge relevant to your career path. The course culminates in a final dissertation, allowing you to demonstrate the knowledge and skills you’ve gained through detailed analysis of a specific topic. Two options are available – you can complete a standard research dissertation, with either a Marketing or Geography academic focus, or choose to complete a practice-based dissertation, allowing you to work on a real-world marketing problem.
You’ll be taught using a range of methods including lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops. On this course, you’ll be taught by expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers.
Where this degree could take you:
- Job roles some consumer analytics and marketing strategy graduates have obtained include Marketing Data Analyst, Junior CRM Manager, Retail Store Manager on leadership programmes, and Graduate Marketing Executive.
- Typical organisations graduates work with include retail and FMCG, marketing and advertising agencies, e-commerce and digital platforms, consultancy and market research, hospitality, tourism and leisure, and technology and data services.
- Graduates who aspire to a research or academic career will also be prepared for a [research degree](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-degrees) in marketing.
The Global Industry Programme gives Masters students a great opportunity to gain real-world experience through live industry projects. This course offers you the chance to spend time abroad, usually as an extra academic year, which will extend your studies by 12 months; once completed, you'll be awarded the ‘international’ variant in your degree title. A work placement can be undertaken as an industrial placement year as part of your course; if you decide to undertake a placement year, your period of study will be extended by 12 months, and on successful completion, you'll be awarded the ‘industrial’ variant in your degree title.

Core modules introduce analytical methods and a foundation in consumer analytics and marketing strategy, including GIS software, retail modelling, consumer and business analytics, and using data to inform marketing strategy. Modules include marketing strategy, marketing analytics and consumer behaviour. Students also complete collaborative work to analyse data and make marketing predictions. One optional module allows students to develop marketing or geography interests. The course culminates in a final dissertation; students can complete a standard research dissertation, with either a Marketing or Geography academic focus, or a practice-based dissertation working on a real-world marketing problem.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
A conditional offer from the University of Leeds means you need to achieve the grades or points outlined in your offer letter. Your offer letter will also explain any English language requirements, if applicable. If you have an academic offer condition, the University may need to see your degree certificate and transcripts as evidence. If you have an English language condition, you may be able to meet the requirements by taking a [pre-sessional course at the Language Centre](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english). You can upload evidence that you have met your conditions and accept your offer in the [application portal](https://myleedsportal.leeds.ac.uk/signin-landing/). You may have to accept your offer again if it becomes unconditional.
If your offer has an academic condition, you will need to include official translations alongside your final academic documents if they were not originally produced in English.
If you take a [pre-sessional English course](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english) with the Language Centre to meet your language condition, you may be eligible for a combined offer. This means that when you pass your pre-sessional, and have met any conditions in your offer letter, you are automatically enrolled on your degree course.

References from family members, partners or spouses are not accepted. References for postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If sent directly by the referee, it must come from their institutional or company email address and may be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk) with the student reference number, name and programme of study.

Guidance says to tailor it to the course, explain how the course links past and future, show abilities and fit with the course, provide evidence of skills, commitment and enthusiasm, explain reasons for studying the course at the University of Exeter, and include particular interest in the subject. program_overview.content:
The MSc Cyber Security Analytics is a **1 year full-time** programme at **Streatham Campus**. It is for applicants with a degree in a strongly numerate subject and an interest in a career in cyber security, data analytics, or the intersection of both; a computing background is not required.
- The programme is taught in a multi-disciplinary partnership of Computer Science, the University of Exeter Business School and the Law School, with input from leading industry experts.
- Exeter works closely with the local cyber security community, including the [South West Cyber Security Cluster](https://southwestcsc.org/) and [BSides Exeter](https://bsidesexeter.co.uk/community/).
- Students learn how to recognise and manage risks to a network or system’s security with data analytics, and how to build and defend secure systems with cyber security.
- The course investigates wider security elements including mathematical, human and societal factors, with the option to study cyber security law and the future of virtual currency.
The MSc Cyber Security Analytics allows students to study two highly sought after skills: cyber security and data science. This combination enables students to study challenges in modern life from two complementary viewpoints. The course has a strong focus on ensuring that safety, security and data privacy are inherent in the design of software systems. Compulsory modules provide a foundation in cyber security and data science, while optional module choices allow students to create a degree that matches their interests.
MSc Cyber Security Analytics consists of core compulsory Cyber Security and Data Analytics focused modules worth 60 credits, a 60-credit MSc Research project, and 60 credits of optional modules: two chosen from Cyber modules and two from Data Science / Analytics. The research project typically applies knowledge of both cyber security and data analytics and is supervised by a research expert in the student’s chosen area. The full-time programme starts in September, taught elements are concluded by May, and research continues until September. A part-time two-year route is also available starting in September.
As academic partners of the Chartered Institute of Information Security, MSc students are eligible for free student membership, enabling them to develop their network, make contacts within the cyber security community, attend CIISec events and contribute articles to their magazine. Exeter’s long-established partnership with the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/institutes/idsai/turinginstitute/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence, provides strong connections to the UK data science and AI research community. The University currently hosts 11 Turing Fellows and one Turing AI Fellow; lectures, conferences and seminars organised by Turing and the Turing University Network are usually open to students in person or online.
Computer science students use world-class spacious teaching labs designed for comfortable, collaborative working in a sensory-friendly environment. The University has invested £50 million in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence capabilities through the [Accelerating Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (ADA) project](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/projectada/), which has invested in teaching, research and infrastructure that this programme benefits from.
Teaching is mainly delivered by lectures, workshops and online materials. Industry connections and local, national and international cyber security networks inform the curriculum, which is regularly reviewed to support the employability of MSc students. Students are taught by experts active in research and practice; academic staff are active in internationally recognised research across a wide range of topics. Exeter’s Security and Trust of Advanced Systems group focuses on building secure, safe, privacy-preserving, reliable and trustworthy systems, and students can also engage with data science research through the [Institute for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/research/institutes/idsai/).
Cyber security and data science affect almost every aspect of society, and companies worldwide need cyber security experts. The programme provides foundations for careers in data analytics, cyber security, or the intersection of both. Graduate opportunities span sectors including software engineering, health communications, education, life sciences, finance, civil service, intelligence and manufacturing. The programme is particularly suited to professionals and graduates looking to develop career options or pursue academia. Students receive support from the dedicated Career Zone team, including one-on-one guidance, business and industry contacts, training events, workshops and lectures.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet satisfied academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of offer conditions and how to satisfy these requirements, including [paying your deposit](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/fees/tuition-fee-deposit/), will be given in the offer letter.
- For a **full-time taught postgraduate programme**, applicants need to pay the deposit to secure their place and should pay by the deadline even if they have not yet met all the conditions of the offer.
- The deadline for meeting all conditions is normally **31 August** for September entry. Applicants must supply required documentation showing they have met outstanding academic requirements, English language and/or references, or inform Exeter by **31 August** what conditions remain and when they expect to meet them.
- If Exeter does not hear from the applicant by **31 August** and outstanding conditions remain, the University reserves the right to **withdraw or defer the application to the following year**.
- To receive a formal unconditional offer letter and, where needed, a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies for a Student Visa, applicants must meet: academic conditions by providing degree certificates, transcripts and references as explained in the Conditional offer letter; non-academic conditions such as a [DBS](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/dbs/) check; and the required English language standard by providing an English language test certificate meeting [Exeter’s requirements](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/).
- Offer holders who successfully complete a [Pre-Sessional English course at the University of Exeter International Study Centre](https://www.exeterisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english) and meet the requirements for progression to their chosen degree are not required to undertake an additional IELTS or TOEFL test. Exeter does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other INTO centres or organisations.

program_overview.content:
Data Analytics and AI MSc is a full-time, 12-month interdisciplinary programme starting in September 2026; part-time study is not available. It provides a solid foundation in data analytics and artificial intelligence and is taught principally by the School of Mathematical Sciences, with the option to choose modules from the Business School. The curriculum teaches how approaches in data analytics and AI can be applied to decision making in modern, data-rich environments.
In addition to the core data analytics component, the programme includes options to specialise in:
- Modelling and AI for health sciences and pharmacology
- Data-driven techniques for business analytics
- Statistical machine learning and AI
The flexible structure gives students an opportunity to specialise or keep their options open, aligning their education with career goals and interests. Students develop a strong mathematical foundation along with practical and interdisciplinary skills, learn the theory behind data analytics and AI, and practise tackling real-world challenges.
This course is ideal for:
- **Aspiring data professionals** looking to work in data analysis, data science, machine learning and AI
- **STEM graduates and professionals** wanting to improve their data skills and solve real-world problems
- **Industry professionals** aiming to learn modern data analytics, statistics and AI techniques
- **Non-STEM professionals** wishing to switch to data-driven careers
The course follows a modular structure, with students completing **180 credits** over a **12-month** period: **20 credits** of core modules and **40 credits** of optional modules in the autumn semester, **60 credits** of optional modules in the spring semester, and a **60-credit** dissertation project in the summer semester. Dissertation projects may be completed in collaboration with industry or as funded placements, co-supervised by industrial partners. Students also have opportunities for summer placements, co-supervised projects with leading industry partners, guest lectures from experts in finance, pharmaceuticals and health technology, and industry-relevant dissertation projects.
Teaching is delivered through lectures, workshops, computer labs, problem-solving classes and hands-on sessions, with practical application through individual reports, posters and projects, plus collaborative learning through group projects. Assessment includes coursework, examinations, dissertation and project work, including programming. During June, July and August, students work on the dissertation, supported by a minimum of three one-to-one supervision meetings with a supervisor.
The programme is based at University Park Campus. Students have access to libraries, shops, cafes, the Students’ Union, the sports village and a health centre; free hopper buses connect to other campuses, and Nottingham city centre is 15 minutes away by public bus or tram.
Graduates of this programme are industry-ready and can pursue careers in technology, finance, healthcare and more. With strong maths and computational skills, graduates can understand and use complex data analytics and AI methods, making them highly desirable in the job market. Graduates from the School of Mathematical Sciences go on to work for top employers such as Capital One, Kubrick Group, BAE Systems, Amazon, BP and China Zheshang Bank. **92.6%** of postgraduates from the School of Mathematical Sciences secured graduate level employment or further study within 15 months of graduation, with an average starting salary of **£30,476** (HESA Graduate Outcomes 2017/18-2022/23).
The School of Mathematical Sciences is ranked Top 100 in the world for Statistics and Operational Research in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2025, Top 3 in the UK for quality of research environment in Mathematical Sciences in the Research Excellence Framework 2021, and **98%** of its research is classed as **‘world-leading’ or ‘internationally excellent’**.

Students will be awarded the Master of Science degree provided they have successfully completed the taught stage by achieving a weighted average mark of at least **50%**, with no more than **40 credits below 50%** and at most **20 credits below 40%**. program_overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time). Accredited: Yes.
Developed alongside world-leading experts in data analytics and HR professionals, this innovative course provides you with an in-depth, critical understanding of strategic human resource management, alongside principles and concepts underpinning data science and statistics. In addition to mastering cutting-edge data analytics methods, you’ll gain a practical understanding of how these principles and concepts can be applied in the fields of HR and people management. The course will develop your skills in ‘data translation’. You'll learn how to identify people-related business problems, understand how analytics can provide solutions for these problems and identify and explain actionable insights. You’ll learn alongside inspirational academics, highly qualified teaching staff with extensive research expertise and consultancy experience in the field of HR analytics. You’ll gain knowledge and understanding of advanced HRM concepts.
**Course Highlights**
- This course is shaped by the latest knowledge and critical thinking. Your learning will be informed by cutting edge research into the use of data and analytics in HR, developed at the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) (LIDA), as well as specialist research from the [Centre for Employment Relations, Innovation and Change](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-ceric) (CERIC).
- Gain valuable, real-world insight from high profile industrial guest speakers. Recent speakers have included the former Head of HR for NHS England.
- Graduate with the skills to tackle complex HR and organisational problems through a combination of knowledge of the theory and practice of strategic HRM, and applied statistics and data analysis skills.
- On all Masters courses at Leeds University Business School you’ll have an opportunity to apply for a place on a week-long [international study tour](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fbusiness.leeds.ac.uk%2Fmasters%2Fdoc%2Finternational-study-tour-2&data=05%7C02%7CJ.H.Neary%40leeds.ac.uk%7Ca556d137a1aa4b17380108dca5ad3ca4%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638567410667728266%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=A2qg6C57v7IxUXudS6PCv35kZTyb%2Bl0KrxQSlvJtaRU%3D&reserved=0) which will include company visits, guest lectures and networking events, as well as an opportunity to visit local places of interest. Previous study tours have included visits to Berlin, Frankfurt, Milan and Zurich.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme. As well as giving you the opportunity to build key industry connections, you’ll also develop invaluable professional and practical skills that are highly valued by employers.
Our MSc Data Analytics and HRM is fully accredited by the [Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development](https://www.cipd.org/uk) (CIPD), the only HR institution in the world to recognise HR professionals through chartered membership. This course will allow you to satisfy the entry requirements for associate CIPD membership and chartered CIPD membership (if you have relevant work experience).
There are three core pillars to the taught part of the course: the theory and practice of strategic HRM, the principles of statistics and data analytics and the application of data analytics to HR problems. You'll study these three core areas, as well as being able to choose from several optional modules to suit your interests. In strategic HRM, you'll consider how organisational strategy and context shape ‘good HR’ in functional areas such as workforce planning, recruitment and selection, training and development, and pay and performance management. In data analytics for human resources, you'll study how these principles can be applied in HR. The teaching approach is practical, focusing on helping you to understand how to apply data science and statistics to solve problems in an organisational context.
During your time at Leeds, you'll also attend professional skill workshops as part of your regular timetable. These practical sessions are taught by business professionals and allow you to gain skills and insight to help you cope effectively with the challenges of the world of work upon graduation. You can choose to enhance your studies by opting to gain [Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cipd.co.uk%2F%23gref&data=05%7C01%7CK.Barclay%40leeds.ac.uk%7C60c324f402214dd2a78208daa1f5cb8a%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C1%7C0%7C638000374287231493%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIiLCJBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C3000%7C%7C%7C&sdata=gBmsNuQj5Oiwf7vswsjz%2FACXiR7p8eovyGf3KqW5WAo%3D&reserved=0) (CIPD) membership alongside your degree.
You’ll be taught using a range of methods including lectures, tutorials, seminars and workshops. The rest of your time will be spent in independent learning, allowing you to develop your skills in research and analysis. On this course, you’ll be taught by our expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers, connecting you to some of the brightest minds on campus. Assessment methods emphasise both knowledge and essential skills development. This may include formal exams, group projects, reports, computer simulation exercises, essays and written assignments, group and individual presentations and reflective logs.
This course will provide you with the academic knowledge and professional skills needed for a career in global human resource management. It will also provide you with the opportunity to specialise in the rapidly developing area of HR analytics. You’ll develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills and become a reflective HR professional. If you're considering further study, the course also provides a solid foundation for a [research degree](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/research-degrees).
As part of this course, dedicated academic and professional development tutors will provide tailored academic and careers support to help you achieve your career ambitions. You can expect expert advice and guidance on your career choices, help in identifying and applying for jobs and support to boost your employability. You’ll also receive coaching to develop the professional skills you'll need to start a successful career and how to evidence these to prospective employers.
As a Masters student at Leeds, you’ll have the unique opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with the Global Industry Programme. You’ll develop key professional skills and gain invaluable insight into working in your chosen field, helping to solve a real business problem from a live company brief. Benefits include fully online delivery designed to fit around your studies, opportunities to make professional networks, consultancy experience with a UK or international organisation, teamwork across disciplines, putting course teachings into practice, and improving your employability prospects.

program_overview.content:
The Masters in Data Analytics for Economics & Finance is a multi-disciplinary programme that prepares you for data-driven careers in economics and finance. It combines insights from economics, finance, statistics, and computing science. With a focus on rigorous data methods, graduates gain essential skills to inform complex decision-making. Jointly delivered by the Adam Smith Business School and the School of Computing Science, the programme provides future-proof, in-demand expertise for today’s fast-changing industries.
- **Teaching start:** September
- **Location:** [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/)
- **MSc:** 12 months full-time
The programme offers a distinctive and innovative multi-disciplinary approach to data analytics as applied to economics and finance, comprising core and elective courses from the Departments of Economics, Accounting & Finance, and Computing Science. It provides advanced training to develop data analytic skills for successful careers in business or industry and also provides a solid foundation for PhD study. Students have the opportunity to participate in summer project internships with prestigious partners and can gain recognition for extra-curricular activities through the Adam Smith Business School’s Graduate Award Scheme. The programme is ranked in the top 70 of the [QS World University Business Masters Ranking 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/business-masters-rankings/business-analytics), and students can experience practical learning with real business challenges through competitive, merit-based [industry projects](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/?card=industryprojects). Industry Projects are not guaranteed; applications are subject to availability and review processes, and unsuccessful candidates can opt for a research proposal for their dissertation. Students can also secure their own projects with approval from academic and/or professional services.
[Adam Smith Business School is **triple accredited**](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/business/aboutus/accreditationsandrankings/accreditations/).
The programme provides advanced training in time series analysis, panel data econometrics and Bayesian inference, based on internationally-recognised research, to equip students to apply their knowledge and skills to conduct state-of-the-art research and lead and deliver projects. Pre-sessional courses ensure that students from different backgrounds can catch up to the required level of pre-requisite knowledge. Students take four core courses and a selection of optional courses. Over the summer months, students complete a dissertation, either under the standard research pathway or as part of an internship with one of the programme’s industry partners.
The Data Analytics for Economics & Finance MSc is suitable for those who have developed a strong interest in obtaining data analytic skills combined with economic insights and aspire to follow a career in finance, banking, consulting, government and other major international institutions. The programme delivers a multi-disciplinary curriculum that prepares graduates for work in all fields of data-rigorous professions related to economics and finance, as well as marketing and business. It is also advantageous for direct admission to a PhD programme. [See our alumni success stories](https://www.gla.ac.uk/postgraduate/taught/dataanalyticsforeconomicsfinance/ouralumnisuccessstories/).

program_overview.content:
Data Analytics MSc is offered at the University of Glasgow's Gilmorehill campus, with teaching starting in September. The MSc is **12 months full-time**; the University also offers a part-time online MSc in Data Analytics.
Data is becoming an ever increasing part of modern life, yet the talent to extract information and value from complex data is scarce. This Masters provides a thorough grounding in state-of-the art methods for learning from data, both in terms of statistical modelling and computation, and gives practical hands-on experience in carrying out various data-driven analytical projects. Previous study of Statistics or Computing Science is not required.
The Statistics Group at Glasgow is a large group, internationally renowned for its research excellence. Its expertise spans topics including biostatistics and statistical genetics; environmental statistics; statistical methodology; statistical modelling; and the scholarship of learning and teaching in statistics.
The programme works closely with [The Data Lab](http://www.thedatalab.com/), an internationally leading research and innovation centre in data science. Students benefit from learning and networking events that connect leading organisations seeking business analytics skills with students looking for opportunities in this field. The Masters in Data Analytics is accredited by the [Royal Statistical Society](https://www.rss.org.uk/).
Students are required to take 10 compulsory taught courses and select 1 taught course from the optional courses in semester 2. In the summer, students complete one project route: Statistics Project and Dissertation, or Statistics Project and Dissertation (with Placement).
Graduates have an excellent track record of gaining employment in many sectors including medical research, the pharmaceutical industry, finance and government statistical services, while others have continued to a PhD.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
It may be possible to defer your offer to the next available intake. Deferral requests will be considered individually and are not guaranteed.
Deferral requests for the 2027 intake are open. To be considered for a deferral, you must have accepted a conditional or unconditional offer for the 2027 intake and have paid any relevant deposits to secure your place on the course. The deadline for requesting a deferral to the 2027 intake is **30 September 2026**. If you do not meet these criteria, your request will declined.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
- You can apply for a postgraduate taught programme if you have not yet finished your first degree. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you finishing your degree at the required grade. If you are made a conditional offer, then you should upload your final results (transcript and degree certificate) when you receive them.
- You can normally apply for a programme if you have not yet met the English language requirements. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you meeting the English language requirements by the date stated on your offer letter. A few exceptions exist where an English test is required at time of application; applicants should check the programme page for details.
- If you cannot provide all required documents when you apply, it is still possible to apply, but you must include a full current transcript (and an English translation if required). The University may then be able to make you a conditional offer, and you can upload the remaining documents at a later date. Some programmes require all listed documents before a decision can be made.

application_materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload to your application clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents (not copies or certified copies). These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. References sent by email must be sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as 'Yahoo' or 'Hotmail' are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof. See the [English Language Requirements](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/international-students/englishlanguagerequirements/) section for more details.
- You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. You will receive a conditional offer stating what qualifications and grades you will need to achieve; once you have evidence of obtaining your qualifications you can upload them to the MySIS Applicant portal.
- Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.

program_overview.content:
Data Analytics MSc is part of Mathematical Sciences and AI, Computer and Data Science at Queen Mary University of London. In today's data-driven economy, organisations need data experts to extract clear insights and inform decision making. This masters teaches the core mathematical principles of data analysis and AI, and how to apply these to real-world scenarios, while developing programming, machine learning and visualisation skills. Students build a foundation in mathematics and statistics, work with Python and R, apply learning to real-world datasets from a wide variety of sectors, learn from experienced educators including industry practitioners and Fellows of the Alan Turing Institute for Data Science and AI, and choose their own specialism.
Study options include full-time study starting September 2026 for 1 year, part-time study starting September 2026 for 2 years, and full-time study starting September 2027 for 1 year. The location is Mile End.
In the first semester, students complete compulsory modules that provide a foundation in data analytics, machine learning, and the statistics of data analysis, building on this knowledge with industry-standard tools and software. In the second semester, students decide on a specialism, also known as a stream, designed to prepare them for specific career paths. Streams include Applied Machine Learning, Pattern Recognition and Deep Learning, and Statistical Inference. Over the summer in the third semester, students work alongside one of the programme's researchers on an independent research project to consolidate learning and develop applied data science skills. Students do not need to be programming experts and will explore data analysis tools such as R and Python.
Assessment is 67% modules and 33% research project. Students are assessed by a mixture of formal examinations and coursework in taught modules and undertake more self-directed work in completing the final Data Analytics Project.
Teaching is primarily through lectures and tutorials, alongside independent study and research. Students are assigned an Academic Adviser who will guide them throughout their time at Queen Mary.
Programme-related teaching and faculty include Dr Alexander Shestopaloff, Senior Lecturer in Statistics, whose interests include efficient Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods, high-dimensional time series analysis, network science, online Bayesian learning and empirical market microstructure; Professor Mark Jerrum, Professor of Mathematics, whose research interests include combinatorics, computational complexity, stochastic processes and randomised algorithms; Professor Vito Latora, Professor of Applied Mathematics and Chair of Complex Systems, with expertise in complex systems and complex networks; Dr Melania Nica, Reader in Actuarial Science and Programme Director for MSc Actuarial Science and Data Analytics, whose research interests include finance and insurance based on application of economic theory; and Dr Nicola Perra, Reader in Applied Mathematics and Programme Director for MSc Data Analytics, whose research focuses on human dynamics, data analytics, network science, mathematical and digital epidemiology.
Facilities include the recently refurbished, £18m Mathematical Sciences building with high-quality teaching rooms, private and group study areas and a social hub; a shared office and dedicated computer lab with Bloomberg terminals for MSc students; library access to 8,000 mathematical books and subscriptions to mathematical journals; and on-campus accommodation for all new full-time postgraduate students from outside London. Teaching is based at Queen Mary's main [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital, 15 minutes by tube from Central London.
Students who have graduated from this programme have gone into data analysis, data science and software development roles including Data Science Consultant, AI Scientist, Pricing Analyst, Customer Insights Analyst, Senior Product Data Analyst, APP Development Specialist, Quantitative Risk Analyst and Market Risk Analyst. Recent employers include British Airways, Ocado, Accenture, PwC, KPMG, UBS, BlackRock, London Stock Exchange Group, Canary Wharf Group, Tata Consultancy Services and Bloomberg.

curriculum.content:
Programme Structure: the MSc Data Analytics programme is structured across three semesters. In the first semester, students complete compulsory modules that provide a foundation in data analytics, machine learning, and the statistics of data analysis, working with industry-standard tools and software. In the second semester, students decide on a specialism/stream. In the third semester, over the summer, students work alongside one of the School’s researchers on an independent research project.
Semester A compulsory modules:
- Machine Learning with Python
- Probability and Statistics for Data Analysis
- Storing, Manipulating and Visualising Data
- Programming in Python
Semester B streams:
- Applied Machine Learning: two compulsory modules, Computational Statistics with R and Forecasting with AI; choose two elective modules from Bayesian Statistics, SAS for Business Intelligence, Optimisation for Business Processes, Financial Data Analytics, and Digital and Real Asset Analytics.
- Pattern Recognition and Deep Learning: two compulsory modules, Neural Networks and Deep Learning and Advanced Machine Learning; choose two elective modules from Graphs and Networks, Forecasting with AI, Bayesian Statistics, and Computational Statistics with R.
- Statistical Inference: two compulsory modules, Bayesian Statistics and Computational Statistics with R; choose two elective modules from Graphs and Networks, Neural Networks and Deep Learning, Forecasting with AI, and Advanced Machine Learning.
Data Analytics Project and Dissertation: Each Data Analytics MSc student is required to complete a **60 credit project dissertation**. A typical MSc project dissertation consists of about 30 word-processed pages, covering a specific research-level topic in data analytics, usually requiring the student to understand, explain and elaborate on results from one or more journal articles and/or performing computation, simulations, or analysis. Possible areas include time series analysis, exploratory data analysis on a dataset, performance and comparative analysis of state of the art techniques, theoretical models of data, complex systems, dynamical systems, topological data analysis, experimental design with data, and statistical aspects of data analytics techniques.

Due to the popularity of this programme, applicants are advised to apply as early as possible, and ideally no later than **30th June** for courses which commence in **mid/late September**.
Please note the closing date for MSc Data Analytics for **September 2026 entry is 30 June**. Applications received after this date and time will be regarded as LATE and will be considered only if vacancies exist when all applications received by this date and time have been processed.
In the event that any programme receives a high number of applications, the University reserves the right to close the application portal prior to the deadline stated on course finder.

academic_requirements.content:
- Normally a **2.1 Honours degree** in **Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Computer Applications, or a closely related discipline**, or equivalent qualification acceptable to the University.
- Applicants with a **minimum 2.2 Honours degree in a cognate discipline**, a **2.1 Honours degree in a non-cognate discipline**, or who have not yet completed their degree, will be considered on a case-by-case basis.
- All applicants will be expected to have **significant mathematical ability** for this course. Although there will be no requirement to take an aptitude test, the level of mathematical ability required is indicated at: https://www.admissionstesting.org/for-test-takers/test-of-mathematics-for-university-admission/preparation/
- Applications may be considered from those who do not meet the above requirements but can provide evidence of recent relevant technical experience in industry, for example, in **programming, data analytics, or AI development**. The University's Recognition of Prior Learning Policy provides guidance on the assessment of experiential learning (RPEL).
- For applicants from China Mainland: applicants should hold a good **four-year bachelor degree** from a recognised, well ranked university with an average grade of at least **70-85%**.

program_overview.content:
Data Analytics MSc is offered as a postgraduate taught programme with **1 year full-time** or **2 years part-time** attendance. Places available are **58 full-time** and **10 part-time**.
Data Analytics is described as a field of rapid developments, with growing demand for qualified experts able to extract benefit from data. The role of a data scientist overlaps computer science, mathematics, statistics, modelling and analytics, while also requiring problem-solving and communication skills. The diversity of data analytics opens job opportunities in software companies, healthcare, banking, insurance, policing, tech companies, intelligent buildings and customer behaviour analytics.
The programme provides a balanced route to learning through a blend of academic study and lab sessions, with a heavy focus on practical engagement with industry. In the first and second semesters, students study six modules full-time, including opportunities for blended and collaborative learning. In the third semester, students undertake a significant industry based project.
Special features include the Analytics in Action module and industry commitment to provide real data for “Analytathons” and projects. The module offers real-world examples of data analytics presented by industry experts working alongside academics who provide the theory, with provision across many academic disciplines in the University. The Frontiers in Analytics module includes state-of-the-art techniques in analytics, particularly Visual Analytics and Behavioural Analytics.
The course is unique in having been developed from engagement with industry rather than traditional academic subject areas. The key core skills that a data scientist needs have been clearly defined and form the basis for the course. There are no optional modules or choice, as all skills are packaged into each individual to produce the “all rounded” data scientist.
The course comprises six taught modules worth **120 CATS** plus a Summer Industry Based Placement project module worth **60 CATS**. Full-time study consists of the six core taught modules and an Industry Based Project module. Part-time students are normally enrolled for two years, with three taught modules in the first year and the remaining taught modules plus the Industry Based Project module in the second year during the Summer session. Each module consists of lectures/labs, helpdesk sessions and assessments, with background reading and preparation work.
The aim of the programme is to offer a multi-disciplinary education in data analytics that prepares graduates with key knowledge, skills and competencies necessary for employment in analytics and data science positions. It aims to provide comprehensive knowledge of the fundamental principles of statistics and computer science underpinning analytics; advanced knowledge and practical skills in analytics theory and practice; tools and techniques for careers in data analytics and data science; skills in practices, processes, tools and methods applicable to commercial and research analytics contexts; exposure to current software packages and emerging analytics applications; and opportunities to develop practical skills in a commercial context.
People teaching the course include [Dr David Wilkins](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/david-wilkins), [Dr Emanuele Fino](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/emanuele-fino), [Dr Felicity Lamrock](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/felicity-lamrock) as Course Director, [Dr Laura Boyle](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/laura-boyle), [Dr Matt Nicholl](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/matt-nicholl), [Dr Matthew Streeter](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/matthew-streeter), [Dr Salissou Moutari](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/salissou-moutari), and [Prof Adele Marshall](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/adele-marshall).
Assessment includes coursework, written/practical examinations, project dissertation, and presentations. Canvas is used as the University’s Virtual Learning Environment, with module sites containing recorded lectures, readings, video links, useful web links, discussion forums and activities.
Industry forecasts indicate that Data Analytics is a growing field internationally, with job opportunities predicted to grow by **160% between 2013 and 2020** according to the eSkills report, Big Data Analytics 2013-2020. The course is designed to meet industry needs by giving graduates skills and expertise in computer science, mathematics and statistics, plus experience from an individual industry based project. Queen’s postgraduates also benefit from leadership and executive programmes and integration with business experts. The Energia Data Analytics Prize is awarded to the MSc Data Analytics student with the best overall performance.
Course location: [Mathematics and Physics](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/SchoolofMathematicsandPhysics/).

curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)** or **2 years (Part-time)**. The programme provides a blend of academic study and lab sessions, with practical engagement with industry. In the first and second semesters, full-time students study 6 modules; in the third semester they undertake a significant industry-based project.
The course comprises **six taught modules (120 CATS)** plus a **Summer Industry Based Placement project module (60 CATS)**:
- Data Analytics Fundamentals
- Database & Programming Fundamentals
- Data Mining
- Machine Learning
- Frontiers in Analytics
- Analytics in Action
- PLUS Individual Industry Based Project (Summer)
Full-Time/Part-Time Study Options:
- **Full-time (1 year):** consists of the six core taught modules (**120 CATS points**) and an Industry Based Project module (**60 CATS**).
- **Part-time (2+ years):** part-time students are normally enrolled for two years. The first year will normally comprise three taught modules (**60 CATS**) - Data Analytics Fundamentals, Data Mining and Frontiers in Analytics. The second year normally comprises the remaining three taught modules (**60 CATS**) - Database & Programming Fundamentals, Machine Learning, Analytics in Action PLUS the Industry Based Project module (**60 units**) which will take place during the Summer session (June-September).
Each module will consist of lectures/labs, helpdesk sessions and assessments and will include some background reading and preparation work. Indicative number of modules per semester: 3.

application_materials.content:

- You may need **two references**; referees will be contacted and asked to submit a reference directly via the referee portal.

The translation should be on official letter-headed paper, state that it is an accurate translation of the original, and include: the translator or translation company's name and contact details; credentials or qualifications; the date of translation; and the translator's full name and signature, or the full name and signature of an authorised official from the translation company.

program_overview.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**. **Degree awarded:** **MSc**. **Study mode:** **Full-time: In person**.
- This MSc Data Science (Earth and Environmental Analytics) prepares students for a career in data science, with a focus on data techniques and uses most relevant to environmental management. It applies data-driven insights to current environmental challenges such as Climate Change, Biodiversity and Conservation, Natural Hazards, and Environment and Health.
- The course develops skills in data analysis, project design, computational methods, and data stewardship. It is intended for graduates from a broad range of disciplines, and welcomes applicants from STEM, business and humanities backgrounds to create a diverse cohort.
- The course aims to help students understand and respond to the complex interactions between the environment, climate, natural ecosystems, human social and economic systems, and health; ask important research questions; evaluate evidence; select appropriate methods; visualise, interpret and provide strategic advice and insight; and develop into agile data scientists able to work in interdisciplinary settings.
- Special features include an **interdisciplinary approach** and **hands-on** experience analysing real-world data using software such as **R, Python, and Excel**. The course is taught by an interdisciplinary team through lectures, computer based practicals, e-learning, meetings with industry partners, workshops, group work, and individual research.
- A master’s degree is formed of **180 credits**. **120 credits** are made up of a mix of mandatory and optional course units, and the remaining **60 credits** are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation**. Dissertation research is supported by weekly research methodology lectures designed to improve academic, research and writing skills.
- Graduates develop a highly valued skillset that enhances employability across sectors such as policy, business, research and more. Previous students have gone on to roles such as **data scientists, civil servants, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, and in AI**. The University states that this MSc provides data skills for careers in banking and financial services, the Civil Service, the IT and tech sector, high performance sports analysis, large retail chains, and the pharmaceutical industry. Students also have access to the University’s dedicated [Careers Service](https://www.careers.manchester.ac.uk/) during the course and for two years after graduation.
- The course is offered at a university ranked top 10 in the UK for maths, statistics and computer science (Times Higher Education World University Rankings by Subject, 2025), and the University of Manchester is described as one of the UK’s most targeted universities by top employers (High Fliers, The Graduate Market Report 2024).

curriculum.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**.
- **Delivery format:** **Full-time: In person**.
- A master’s degree is formed of **180 credits**. **120** of these credits are made up by a mix of mandatory and optional course units, worth **15 credits each**. You will need to select **eight** of these course units, with **60 credits taken each semester**.
- The core units are:
- Statistics and Machine Learning 1: Statistical Foundations (**DATA70121**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Statistics & Machine Learning 2: AI, Complex Data, Computationally Intensive Statistics (**DATA70132**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Understanding Databases (**DATA70141**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Applying Data Science (**DATA70202**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- Understanding Data and their Environment (**DATA71011**, 15 credits, Mandatory)
- The remaining **60 credits** are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation**. Your dissertation must be within the area of one of the course units you have chosen.
- Optional course units range from statistical foundations to environmental based data analysis and GIS. Examples shown on the page include:
- Privacy, Confidentiality and Disclosure Control (**DATA70402**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Measuring and Predicting 2 (**EART60071**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Computational Subsurface Geoscience (**EART60152**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Key Interpretation Skills (**EART60381**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Earth and Environmental Data Science (**EART60702**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Environmental Monitoring and Modelling (**EART62012**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Pollutant Mobility and Transformation (**EART62022**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Pollution Management in Practice 2 (**EART63012**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Environmental Remote Sensing (**GEOG60941**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Understanding GIS (**GEOG71551**, 15 credits, Optional)
- Neighbourhood Planning Project (**PLAN60812**, 15 credits, Optional)
- The page notes: "Displaying 10 of 17 course units" and provides [Display all course units](https://www.manchester.ac.uk/study/masters/courses/list/18096/msc-data-science-earth-and-environmental-analytics/#).

academic_requirements.content:

program_overview.content:
The Master of Data Science (Social Analytics) at Durham University equips you with the tools to analyse complex social data, uncover patterns in human behaviour, and inform evidence-based decision-making. Whether you're aiming for a career in government, policy, market research, or social impact organisations, this programme prepares you to lead with insight in a data-driven world.
- Start date: September 2026
- Degree type: MDS
- Course code: G5P423
- Course length: 1 year full-time
Use data to understand and improve society. This conversion course equips you with the skills to analyse social data, uncover patterns in human behaviour, and inform policy and business decisions. Learn to apply advanced data science techniques to real-world social challenges across sectors.
The Master of Data Science (Social Analytics) is a conversion course that opens up a future in data science, even if your first degree is in a non-quantitative subject (including the social sciences, the arts and humanities). The course equips you with the skills to process and analyse data, communicate your findings to a wide audience, whilst applying this knowledge to practical situations.
The MDS provides training in contemporary data science, learning from practising researchers who are making a difference across a range of industries. Shared core modules across the suite of MDS courses build wider skills in statistical and machine learning, while subject-specific modules integrate data science with social science, equipping you with the skills to design and carry out social data science research and communicate it to optimise impact across a variety of settings.
The MDS culminates in the research project, an in-depth investigation into an area of specific interest in which you apply the skills learned during the course to a research problem in a social science domain of your choice. The Durham Research Methods Centre can help with the allocation of project topics through local authorities, NHS Trusts and the wider health and social care sector.
The course begins with a range of introductory modules before progressing to more advanced contemporary techniques such as statistical modelling (in R), computer programming (in Python), machine learning, AI and neural networks. Social analytics modules provide insight into the specialised methods needed for social data as well as the theoretical foundations to understand how to use them effectively.
This interdisciplinary course is made up of modules that span across the University. It incorporates a wide range of learning and teaching methods, including lectures, seminars, workshops and computer/practical classes. The taught elements are further reinforced through independent study, research and analysis, case studies and structured reading. All modules are underpinned by research and embed elements of research training in both delivery and assessment.
The Master of Data Science is assessed via a combination of essays, online assessments, reports and presentations – both individual and in small groups. The course culminates with a major research project, which is conducted and written up as a self-directed piece of work with support from your appointed supervisor.
Data Science is a conversion course that incorporates content from many Departments across the University. This provides access to a selection of related modern facilities from across the University, in particular Computer Science and Mathematics. Facilities will depend on the subject specialism but include laboratories, libraries, project spaces, lecture theatres, study and networking spaces as well as shared social spaces. Most departments are close to the historic centre of Durham which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
In today’s data-driven world, the ability to capture, analyse, and communicate insights from complex information is one of the most sought-after skills by employers globally. Graduates are equipped for exciting and meaningful careers across a wide range of sectors, from science, health, and the environment to the humanities and social policy, where data is driving innovation and transforming how we live and work.

Core modules:
- The Data Science Research Project is a substantial piece of self directed research into an unfamiliar area of data science, or in your subject specialisation area with a focus on data science. The project can be practical, theoretical or both, and is designed to develop your research, analysis and report-writing skills.
