financial_aid.content:
The **Inspiring Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship** is available to all new international students to Durham who meet the eligibility criteria. Each scholarship is a competitive award worth up to **£10,000** in tuition fee discounts towards the original tuition fee for a postgraduate programme starting in **September 2026**.
| Field | Details |
| --- | --- |
| Amount | The scholarship is offered in two award types: **Inspiring Excellence £5K** - £5,000 in tuition fee discount; **Inspiring Excellence £10K** - £10,000 in tuition fee discount |
| Year of Entry | Scholarships are available for programmes commencing in 2026. |
| Number of awards available | Limited |
| Level of study | Postgraduate Taught |
| Eligible programmes | One-year, full-time (in-person) taught MSc, MA, LLM or MDS qualification (MBA, MSW programmes and MA in Theology and Ministry are excluded). |
| Duration | One-year |
To be eligible, applicants must:
- have applied to a one-year, full-time (in-person) taught MSc, MA, LLM or MDS qualification (MBA, MSW programmes and MA in Theology and Ministry are excluded).
- start postgraduate studies at Durham University in **September 2026**.
- be classed as an overseas student for fee-paying purposes.
- self-funded and not already in receipt of any other scholarship, funding or sponsorship.
- meet or exceed the entry requirements for the programme applied for at Durham University.
- complete the [Inspiring Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship Application Form](https://eur01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fforms.office.com%2FPages%2FResponsePage.aspx%3Fid%3Di9hQcmhLKUW-RNWaLYpvlF0WV-CJxblAsFZLqIzpDTZUQU4xSFo1WUdIVzhOT044V1hYWEJMUEFYQi4u&data=05%7C02%7Cbethea.etherington%40durham.ac.uk%7C130312b9ee024d43c26b08ddff49a6ac%7C7250d88b4b684529be44d59a2d8a6f94%7C0%7C0%7C638947413974172128%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=mV6BXieSd608vvbHSUHl8EDk%2B8MqYE%2FPZ%2BbGqickNpY%3D&reserved=0).
To apply, applicants must first apply for an eligible postgraduate programme via Durham's [Postgraduate Applicant Portal](https://studyatdurham.microsoftcrmportals.com/en-US/), then submit the scholarship application form by: 1st round selection: midnight (GMT) **16January 2026**; Additional round selection: midnight (GMT) **20 March 2026**; 2nd round selection: midnight (GMT) **29 May 2026**. If an applicant fails to receive an academic offer before the deadline for the 1st round selection, or is unsuccessful in the 1st round selection, they will be automatically considered for the next round selection and **do not need to submit the scholarship application form again**.
The Durham Inspiring Excellence Postgraduate Scholarship applies to courses commencing in September 2026. The scholarship award is not transferable, not deferrable and will be applied as a tuition fee waiver directly to the postgraduate programme tuition fees. No cash alternative is offered. The tuition fees will be adjusted at the time of enrolment at Durham University. Awardees will lose eligibility for the award if they are no longer classified as overseas students for fee purposes, or receive other scholarships, funding, or sponsorship from Durham or external institutions during their degree.

We’re able to consider, on a case-by-case basis:
- Change of year
- Change of course
- Change of mode of study.
You can request a change through your Applicant Portal homepage. We aren’t able to approve all requests, but if we are able to you will receive a new offer letter which you will be able to view in your Applicant Portal. If you request a deferral your application will be deferred and reconsidered when the next admissions cycle opens. academic_requirements.content:
**High 2:1 honours degree (or overseas equivalent).** You are expected to have a degree with a substantial proportion of social science content; as a minimum you should have completed **two degree level units** on topics from any of the following: sociology, psychology, anthropology, economics, history, human geography, political science, public health.
The following includes other skills/experience that would increase the chances of being selected:
- Evidence of applying statistical modelling to social sciences.
- Non-academic experience with the application of statistical models to social issues.
- Experience working on public policy issues or similar.
In your application, you should demonstrate aptitude, knowledge and/or interest in three areas:
- data analytics and/or statistics;
- computational subjects; and
- pathway specific requirements.
These can be demonstrated by course units taken at undergraduate level and high school level, or professional experience.
For applicants from China (Mainland): taught master's applicants with a bachelor's degree from a recognised good-quality Chinese university, with a **minimum overall average grade of 80%** or a **minimum GPA of 3.0 (out of 4.0)** will be considered for admission on to taught masters programmes; entry requirements differ between courses and applicants should refer to the entrance requirements of individual programmes for further guidance.

program_overview.content:
- **Duration:** **1 year**. **Degree awarded:** MSc. **Study mode:** Full-time, in person.
- MSc Data Science (Social Analytics) is a uniquely interdisciplinary programme that brings together expertise from across Manchester’s facilities, giving you strong foundations in data science and the opportunity to collaborate across disciplines to tackle local and global challenges. The course focuses on the data techniques and uses most relevant to social analytics.
- The course prepares you for a successful career in this high-demand field by developing abilities in data analysis, project design, computational methods, and data stewardship. It aims to train you to ask important research questions, evaluate the quality of available evidence, select appropriate methods, and use analytical skills to visualise, interpret and provide strategic advice and insight.
- The programme welcomes applicants from a range of STEM, business and humanities backgrounds, allowing it to create a diverse cohort and enrich discussions around the uses and potential of data.
- Special features include an interdisciplinary approach spanning Statistics, Demography, Social Networks, Data Science, Economics, Politics, Criminology, Health, Sociology, and other fields, and hands-on experience analysing real-world data using R, Python, SQL, Excel and other tools.
- The course is taught by an interdisciplinary team through lectures, computer based practicals, e-learning, workshops, student presentations, group work, and individual research.
- A master’s degree is formed of 180 credits. 120 credits are made up by a mix of mandatory and optional course units, and the remaining 60 credits are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of an **8500-word extended research project**. The project mirrors a real-world data science investigation, including replication code and an accompanying overview video for stakeholders, and is supported by weekly research methodology lectures.
- Graduates develop a highly valued skillset for careers in policy, business, research and more. Previous students have gone on to roles such as data scientists, civil servants, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, and in AI. Career paths include banking and financial services, charities and research organisations, the Civil Service, the IT and tech sector, business management, high performance sports analysis, large retail chains, and the pharmaceutical industry.
- The course is eligible for the fully-funded 1+3 studentship offered by the ESRC North West Social Sciences Doctoral Training Partnership (NWSSDTP), offering a route from master’s-level study into postgraduate research and PhD study. [Find out more on the 1+3 ESRC NWSSDTP webpage](https://www.humanities.manchester.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-research/funding/list-of-awards/1-3-esrc-nwssdtp/#:~:text=Open%20to%20applicants%20from%20all,structured%20pathway%20into%20postgraduate%20research.).
- The University of Manchester is one of the UK’s most targeted universities by top graduate employers, and students have access to the dedicated [Careers Service](https://www.careers.manchester.ac.uk/) during the course and for two years after graduation.

- For this pathway, applicants are expected to evidence an interest and/or experience in topics related to urban analysis. Examples include:
- working experience in urban-themed topics (e.g. data analyses for spatial phenomena, public policies or real estate market analysis);
- experience in working in spatial or GIS-based data analysis;
- evidence of training in urban-themed methods or topics (e.g. GIS).

program_overview.content:
- Duration: **1 year**. Degree: MSc. Study mode: Full-time, in person.
- This MSc Data Science (Urban Analytics) prepares students for data science careers with a focus on the data techniques and uses most relevant to urban analytics, including areas such as property, policy and town planning.
- The course is intended for graduates from a broad range of disciplines; applicants from STEM, business and humanities backgrounds are welcomed.
- Students develop skills in data analysis, project design, computational methods, and data stewardship. The course aims to train students to ask important research questions, evaluate the quality of available evidence, select appropriate methods, and use analytical skills to visualise, interpret and provide strategic advice and insight.
- The programme takes an interdisciplinary approach, covering varied aspects and applications of data science from Statistics, Demography, Social Networks, Data Science, Economics, Politics, Criminology, Health, Sociology, and other fields.
- Teaching is delivered by an interdisciplinary team through lectures, computer-based practicals, workshops, online courses and surgeries, meetings with industry partners, group work, and individual research.
- The master's degree comprises 180 credits. 120 credits are made up of a mix of mandatory and optional course units, and the remaining 60 credits are awarded through a compulsory research component in the form of a **12,000-to-15,000-word dissertation** supported by weekly research methodology lectures.
- Graduates develop a skillset aimed at careers across policy, business, research and more; previous students have gone on to roles such as data scientists, civil servants, consultants, researchers, entrepreneurs, and roles within AI. The course is described as providing data skills for careers in banking and financial services, the Civil Service, the IT and tech sector, high performance sports analysis, large retail chains, the pharmaceutical industry, and urban planning. Students also have access to the University's [Careers Service](https://www.careers.manchester.ac.uk/) during the course and for two years after graduation.
- The course is eligible for the 1+3 studentship offered by the Economic and Social Sciences Research Council (ESRC) North West Social Sciences Doctoral Training Partnership (NWSSDTP), providing a fully funded route into postgraduate research and a pathway from master's-level study to a PhD. [Find out more on our 1+3 ESRC NWSSDTP webpage.](https://www.humanities.manchester.ac.uk/study/postgraduate-research/funding/list-of-awards/1-3-esrc-nwssdtp/#:~:text=Open%20to%20applicants%20from%20all,structured%20pathway%20into%20postgraduate%20research.)

interview_requirements.content:
Admissions staff may consider a range of factors in assessing suitability for their programmes including, but not limited to, interviews, work experience, assessment of a piece of written work, etc.
For campus-based programmes, the length of time it will take to process an application and arrive at a decision will depend both on whether the academic School concerned requires additional information or uses additional selection procedures, such as an interview. Depending on the programme, an application may be considered on the basis of the information provided in the application form and supporting documentation, or the applicant may be required to attend for interview or provide additional evidence of relevant work experience or submit a piece of work or an essay for consideration by the selector.
For some programmes, decisions are made on the basis of the information provided by the applicant only; in other cases, applicants may be called for interview. In some Schools, interviews may be used only for candidates who have unusual or non-standard qualifications, in order to give them an opportunity to demonstrate that they have the skills and knowledge required for them to thrive on their chosen programme of study. Where appropriate, applicants may be interviewed via telephone, Zoom, MS Teams or Skype.
For international applicants, to ensure that the University complies with relevant United Kingdom legislation and immigration regulations, the University may choose to undertake additional checks during the admissions process and this may be post offer. program_overview.content:
Qualification type: MSc. Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months full-time or 24 months part-time.
Advance your expertise in statistics, machine learning and responsible AI for healthcare innovation. The MSc Data Science and AI for Health Innovation prepares students to tackle real-world healthcare challenges using advanced statistical methods, machine learning and artificial intelligence.
Healthcare is being transformed by data science, artificial intelligence and digital technologies. From electronic health records and wearable devices to AI-driven diagnostics and public health surveillance, healthcare systems now generate vast amounts of data with enormous potential to improve patient care and health outcomes. This programme combines advanced statistical analysis, machine learning, artificial intelligence and computational methods to explore how health data science can drive meaningful healthcare innovation.
Designed around flexibility and student choice, the programme allows students to tailor their studies around their own interests and career ambitions. Students can specialise in areas such as prediction modelling, artificial intelligence, machine learning, casual inference and healthcare evaluation while developing analytical, computational and professional skills.
The programme has strong links with the [Civic Health Innovation Labs (CHIL)](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/civic-health-innovation-labs/), an internationally recognised multidisciplinary research centre based at the University of Liverpool. CHIL brings together experts from academia, the NHS, local government, charities and industry to develop responsible approaches to data use and AI for health and society. Students have opportunities to engage with dissertation projects linked to areas such as healthcare data analytics, digital health, public health informatics and community health innovation, contributing to cutting-edge research with real-world impact.
The programme is designed for students with prior quantitative experience who wish to develop advanced expertise in health data science and artificial intelligence, and is also suitable for professionals seeking to strengthen their analytical and computational skills for careers in healthcare, research and innovation. It is also open to intercalating students on clinical programmes.
The curriculum combines core foundations in health data science with flexible specialist pathways in statistics, machine learning and artificial intelligence. Students develop expertise in using health data to better understand disease and improve healthcare; applying data science approaches to real-world healthcare challenges; statistical modelling, inference and prediction; machine learning and artificial intelligence for healthcare innovation; causal inference and healthcare intervention evaluation; managing and interpreting complex health data; computational and programming methods for health research; responsible and ethical approaches to AI and healthcare data use; communication of analytical findings; collaborative and interdisciplinary working; and designing and completing an independent health data science research project.
The programme has a blended format with a mix of face-to-face lectures, workshops and practical sessions. Full-time students complete the programme in three semesters and part-time students complete it in six semesters. Work towards the dissertation module runs across the length of the programme, with the dissertation completed in semester three.
Teaching takes place within a welcoming and collaborative academic community supported by staff with expertise across statistics, health data science, artificial intelligence and healthcare research. Teaching is enriched by guest lecturers and research collaborations connected to organisations including the NHS, industry and CHIL.
Graduates from the MSc Data Science and AI for Health Innovation are equipped with advanced statistical, computational and analytical skills sought across healthcare, industry and research. The programme prepares graduates for careers including healthcare analytics, NHS data science, pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, clinical trials and health research, public health and epidemiology, digital health innovation, AI-driven healthcare technologies, healthcare evaluation and policy, and academic and methodological research. Graduates may work within hospitals, government agencies, research organisations, pharmaceutical companies, healthcare technology companies and innovation-focused startups. The programme also provides preparation for doctoral study and research careers in health data science, statistics and artificial intelligence.

financial_aid.content:
All or part of your tuition fees can be [funded by external sponsorship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/feespayment/tuition/external-sponsorship/).
We’re showing the scholarships available to students from **United Kingdom**. We offer a range of scholarships and bursaries that could help pay your tuition and living expenses.
- [Graduate Loyalty Scholarship – UK](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/graduate-loyalty-scholarship-uk/): UK or Republic of Ireland students who completed an undergraduate degree at the University of Liverpool could receive a **£1,500 tuition fee discount**, subject to the full eligibility criteria. This scholarship will be awarded to all eligible students.
- [The Salters’ Fellowship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/fees-and-funding/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/the-salters-fellowship/): students who have graduated with an undergraduate degree in Chemistry and accepted a place on a master's course could be entitled to a **£10,000 contribution towards tuition fees**. The master's can be in a range of subject areas and is not restricted to Chemistry; available to one student per academic year who's considered to be from a widening participation background.
- [Bracken Scholarship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/bracken-scholarship/): open to two UK students in the **2026/27 academic year** and worth **£5,000**. Students must be studying a postgraduate course at the University of Liverpool; those on data science or coding courses may be given priority.
- [Health Data Research UK Master’s Degree Scholarships](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/health-data-research-masters-scholarship/): joining our Health Data Science MSc? UK students could be eligible to apply for **£10,000 of funding** and the opportunity to conduct a research project with one of HDRUK’s partner organisations. Partners include Diabetes UK and Alzheimer's Research UK.
- [John Lennon Memorial Scholarship](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/study/paying-for-your-studies/scholarships-and-bursaries/masters/john-lennon-memorial-scholarship/): UK students either born in or with strong family connections to Merseyside could be eligible to apply for a fee discount of up to **£4,500**. Applicants need to demonstrate an active interest in global, community and environmental issues.

program_overview.content:
Qualification type: MSc. Study mode: full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months full-time or 24 months part-time.
This course will enable you to develop a high level understanding of quantitative and computational geographical methods, including skills in GIS software and statistical programming languages such as R or Python. Within an applied setting, you will develop skills in the visualisation, modelling and statistical analysis of conventional and novel sources of data, ranging from censuses and social surveys through to satellite imagery and social media using both web-based and traditional techniques.
Human activity is increasingly associated with the generation of large volumes of data, including transactional data, administrative data, social media data shadows, and smart-card linked transport data. Many grand human challenges concern problems of a geographical nature, and growing volumes of big data about the form, function and dynamics of human activities are providing new opportunities to advance such debates within a framework of Geographic Data Science.
This MSc is also available with the alternative title Geographic Data Science MSc for entry September 2026, and gives students the option to graduate with either of these two MSc titles.
This course is for you if you want to understand and analyse the role of geography in everyday life through geographical and computational reasoning.
What you'll learn includes integrating the modern GIS toolkit with Data Science tools to solve practical real-world problems; applying GIS in the handling and analysis of spatial data in planning and social sciences; research methodology, philosophy, strategy and design; ethical and practical considerations associated with conducting research; social survey data analysis using descriptive and inferential statistics, data visualisation, regression modelling and model diagnostics; analytical techniques for spatial data; and major debates of society, environment, space and place.
The programme includes compulsory modules in Geographic Data Science that introduce the field where GIS and Data Science intersect, programming with Python, the importance of GDS for social science applications, GIS tools for creating digital representations of the world, qualitative research methods and research design, and social survey data analysis using R. In semester two, students learn statistical techniques for handling spatial data, current debates in the discipline, web-based map visualisation and analysis, and the importance of time and location in new forms of data. Optional modules allow study in areas such as Big Data problems, database systems and SQL, biologically inspired optimisation, population science theory, digital trace data analysis, and social and spatial inequalities. The final project includes an introductory dissertation seminar, progress sessions, and supervision sessions or pastoral tutorials with a dissertation supervisor to support development and completion of the dissertation.
You’ll learn through lectures, seminars, and hands-on workshops in the computer lab. Assessments are designed flexibly to provide student centred, research-led learning, and take the form of short (~3000 word) reports, computational essays, oral presentations, computer exercises, examinations and a 12,000 maximum word dissertation.
You will work with academic staff within the [Geographic Data Science Laboratory](http://www.geographicdatascience.com/) and the Centre for Spatial Demographic Research. You can also access the [Consumer Data Research Centre](http://cdrc.ac.uk/), created as part of a £6m investment in Big Data by the Economic and Social Research Council.
This program will give you the high-level skills you need to kickstart your career in applied geographical information science, data science with a geographic focus, or research with expertise in spatial analysis, GIS, and data science. Career options after graduation include PhD or postdoctoral research, GIS/Data Science consultant roles, employment in the commercial or public sector, IT consulting, or teaching in higher education. With the programming and web development skills you’ll gain, you’ll be in high demand in the job market for newer spatial data handling skills, which are more in demand than traditional GIS skills.

program_overview.content:
Data Science and Analytics (MSc) is offered full time over 1 year with a September start. The course equips students with a theoretical understanding and practical experience of applying methods drawn from data science and analytics. Students develop in-demand skills for extracting and handling ‘big data’ and applying modelling tools to help businesses and government organisations make better decisions. On completion, graduates are well placed to progress into roles in data-intensive industries or a related research career.
The degree falls under the umbrella of the [Data Science Academy](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/data-science-academy) (DSA), run by the School of Computer Science and Informatics in partnership with the School of Mathematics. Students benefit from the shared knowledge and skills of both Schools, although the degree is run by the School of Mathematics. Teaching takes place in the newly-built flagship building Abacws.
The programme is a two-stage programme taught over one year for a total of 180 credits: a 120-credit taught stage followed by a 60-credit research project. Students undertake 100 credits of compulsory 20-credit modules and choose a further 20 credits from optional modules. The 60-credit summer project will typically involve working with a company on a problem of real importance.
Teaching uses a mixture of lectures, seminars, computer workshops and tutorials. Programming skills and relevant software packages are taught in dedicated computer suites. Industry experts are often invited to give presentations. For the dissertation project, students are usually allocated three supervisors: two academic staff members with an interest or specialism in the research field and a sponsor supervisor from the organisation they work with during the project.
Graduates have gone on to work with companies and Government organisations including the Office for National Statistics, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, British Airways, Network Rail, UK Government, The Financial Times, Virgin Media, Welsh Water and Admiral Insurance.
An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation, which allows students to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world problem or a more theoretical problem. This may involve working with an external company or organisation; in previous years students have worked with Admiral Insurance, Lloyds Banking Group, the Office for National Statistics and the National Health Service.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Applicants may be allowed deferred entry to a programme, subject to meeting the entry requirements and places being available. The maximum period of deferral granted will be **no more than 12 months**. Applicants wishing to defer admission for a longer period will be required to reapply. In exceptional circumstances, where an applicant may wish to seek an extension to the deferral period, the School must submit a case for approval to the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Student Experience and Academic Standards). Applicants should use the [online form](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/study/ask-a-question) to request a deferral.
For postgraduate taught programmes, Cardiff University reserves the right to close programmes and/or to offer a deferred entry place where a programme has reached capacity, and may operate a waiting list as appropriate. The University also reserves the right to offer deferred entry to applicants who apply within 12 weeks of the start date of a programme if there is not sufficient time to process all the requirements for an applicant to start their programme by the last date of enrolment.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
If you have not yet met the entry requirements, you can usually still apply for a course. You may receive an offer of a place on the condition that you meet the requirements before you start the course.
A **Conditional offer** means you have been offered a place, but something is missing from your application - most likely one of your supporting documents or you are still to complete one of the qualifications required to gain admission to the university. Your offer letter will clearly state what evidence needs to be supplied. Once Cardiff University has everything, your offer will change to Unconditional.
Your offer is subject to you accepting your place and meeting the exact conditions of your offer **a minimum of 14 days before the start date of your programme**, unless otherwise agreed by the university.

application_materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together. Please do not upload academic documents to the funding section.
Your application must include:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume: include an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa, for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
- If you entered your current degree programme later than year 1, include separate details of the qualification used to gain entry into that later year, including any transcripts and certificates for that qualification.
If you have them, please include:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard, but could strengthen your application in circumstances such as explaining a gap in your education or if your education/degree subject is not directly relevant to the programme. The personal statement should be **no more than one side of A4** and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases a reference may be required to help make a decision.
Country-specific documents:
- Applicants with Chinese degrees: provide evidence of your current/final overall weighted percentage (%); GPA or arithmetic percentage is not accepted.
- Applicants with Indian degrees should include a copy of your bachelor’s degree certificate, consolidated mark sheet, semester mark sheets, University marking scheme, and official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%). If you have not completed your degree, provide the bottom three items.
- Applicants with Canadian degrees: provide details of the grading system used on your transcript, including the percentage pass mark for your degree. If your degree was taught in English, include official evidence of this.
Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal so the document links to the correct application automatically.

interview_requirements.content: We aim to make decisions within **three to five weeks** if all necessary documents have been received. You will be contacted directly if we require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview or audition.

A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons)** in a subject containing a substantial mathematical, statistical and/or computing component. Successful applicants will have **strong grades (mainly firsts with no marks below 2:2)** in mathematical modules. You must provide a list of the type and level of maths/computing modules that you have studied if this is not obvious from your transcript. We may ask for further detailed module information if these are not clear on your transcript. We do not normally accept degrees in accountancy or finance for this MSc. We accept a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications).
For applicants from China: accepted qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. If the course asks for **2.1**, applicants need **70%-85%, depending on your institution**. If the course asks for **2.2**, applicants need **70%-80%, depending on your institution**.

program_overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The Data Science and Analytics MSc addresses the increasing demand for people who can manage, control and provide insight into the way data is used. It develops understanding of computer science and mathematics, alongside familiarity with data needs and processes in areas including healthcare, business, government and the environment. The course offers the opportunity to develop skills in analysing structured and unstructured data, analysing large datasets, critically evaluating results in context, and getting insights from data.
The course combines expertise from the Schools of [Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing), [Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography) and [Mathematics](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/maths) with [Leeds University Business School](https://business.leeds.ac.uk/), allowing students to benefit from a range of data science perspectives and applications and tailor the course to their career ambitions. Students can choose modules from the School of Mathematics, the School of Computer Science, the School of Geography and Leeds University Business School. Mathematics modules are available for students who are not from a mathematics/statistics background, while computing modules are suitable for students who are not from a computer science background.
The course introduces different perspectives on data science, including the mathematical and computational underpinnings of the subject and its applications in specific contexts. Students put theory into practice through a project focused on a real-world problem, applying knowledge acquired throughout the course and demonstrating independent research skills necessary for a professional or academic career. Many recent projects have involved co-supervision with the Leeds Clinical Trials Unit, Leeds Institute for Data Analytics (LIDA) and the MET office. It is possible to involve an industrial partner in the dissertation, subject to approval of the programme manager.
Research conducted on campus feeds directly into the course, shaping learning in areas such as probability and financial mathematics, modern applied statistics and analysis. Students benefit from close links with organisations including [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/), [Leeds Institute for Fluid Dynamics](https://fluids.leeds.ac.uk/) and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the UK’s national institute for data science and artificial intelligence.
Teaching is through lectures, tutorials, seminars and supervised research projects, with extensive use of IT and a wide range of materials to enhance and extend formal teaching. The programme team includes academics from the Schools of Mathematics, Computer Science, Geography and Business. Programme leader [Dr Luisa Cutillo](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/maths/staff/5526/dr-luisa-cutillo) researches networks and network applications, including validating network structures and biomedical network applications, and is one of the Women in Machine Learning Boards of Directors. Students may also be taught by industry professionals and trained postgraduate researchers.
Assessment is by a range of methods, including formal examination, assignments, coursework, reports and practical activities.
There is increasing demand for individuals who can manage and control the way data is used. Data scientists are increasingly important in helping governments, businesses, researchers, NGOs and other organisations make sense of growing amounts of information. University of Leeds students are among the top 5 most targeted by top employers according to [The Graduate Market 2024, High Fliers Research](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/). Previous data science graduates have secured roles including Product SME at Shell UK, Senior Software Engineer at London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG), and Data Integration Lead at Stainless Games.
While studying at Leeds, students have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with their academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. The work experience is formally integrated into the degree, enabling students to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The course will equip you with the knowledge and skills you need to meet the challenges of data science in the modern world. You can choose modules from the School of Mathematics, the School of Computer Science, the School of Geography and Leeds University Business School. Mathematics modules are available for students who are not from a mathematics/statistics background, while computing modules will be suitable for students on this programme who are not from a computer science background.
Course structure: the list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time.
Compulsory modules:
- **Data Science –15 credits**: This module gives you an insight into some general principles of the work of a data scientist and teaches you some of the underpinnings of artificial intelligence and statistics in the practice of data science.
- **Project skills in Data Science –15 credits**: This module will develop your skills for your project, potential further research, and employment. This will include presentation skills and teamwork, some of which will be developed through real-life case studies.
- **Project in Data Science and Analytics – 60 credits**: The project gives you the opportunity to demonstrate independent research skills necessary for a professional or academic career. It allows you to deepen your knowledge and understanding of practical issues whilst applying skills acquired throughout the programme. The list of topics to choose for your project is wide-ranging, dealing with a real-world problem. It will typically require a literature review, project planning, data collection, analysis and interpretation. Many recent projects have involved co-supervision with the Leeds Clinical Trials Unit, Leeds Institute for Data Analytics (LIDA) and the MET office. It is possible to involve an industrial partner in your dissertation, subject to the approval of the programme manager.
Optional modules are indicative of typical options:
- Machine Learning – 15 credits
- Deep Learning – 15 credits
- Programming for Data Science – 15 credits
- Geographic Data Visualisation & Analysis – 15 credits
- Big Data and Consumer Analytics – 15 credits
- Business Analytics and Decision Science – 15 credits
- Forecasting and Advanced Business Analytics – 15 credits
- Machine Learning in Practice – 15 credits
- Statistical Theory – 15 credits
- Statistical Theory and Methods – 15 credits
- Statistical Learning – 15 credits
- Statistical Computing – 15 credits
- Transport Data Science – 15 credits
Teaching is through lectures, tutorials, seminars and supervised research projects. Assessment is by a range of methods, including formal examination, assignments, coursework, reports and practical activities.
As part of your course, you will have access to the [Professional and Academic Communication module](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Ffaculty-engineering-physical-sciences%2Fdoc%2Fguide-professional-academic-communication-module&data=05%7C02%7CS.Wilson3%40leeds.ac.uk%7C657723c6ba5e4936433308ddd107b250%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638896553169948867%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=rdKf6rUQYbTAMfHoMZQ7w1sQZJ%2FeYamQmwtgwgZIdd8%3D&reserved=0), delivered through a combination of in-person workshops and independent online study.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to complete an eight-week [virtual work experience](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Feps.leeds.ac.uk%2Fwork-experience&data=05%7C02%7CB.Cairney%40leeds.ac.uk%7Cd370f21983754013f75008dddb4ffad7%7Cbdeaeda8c81d45ce863e5232a535b7cb%7C0%7C0%7C638907858738083812%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=dvWiCk8T2J7H9dGR3nbAmyvRxD5fVNGRuJ2w7%2F0R6Oo%3D&reserved=0), working on a project aligned with your academic discipline and partnered with a relevant company. This practical experience is formally integrated into your degree, enabling you to graduate with an MSc with Work Experience.

financial_aid.content:
We have up to £9.4 million worth of scholarships available for international students commencing their studies in September 2026.
- **International Regional Scholarships**: An automatic **£6,000 fee reduction scholarship** is available for international Masters students from an eligible country/region. International Masters Regional Scholarships are automatically awarded to eligible students as a fee reduction.
- Eligibility criteria: passport holder from Egypt, India, Japan, Mexico, Peru, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, Turkey, United States of America, Vietnam; classified as an international fee-paying student; self-funded or partially-funded; hold a conditional or unconditional offer for a Masters degree (including MRes) starting in September 2026.
- You do not need to apply for the International Masters Regional Scholarship. If you meet the eligibility and award criteria, you will automatically receive the scholarship.
- This scholarship award **cannot be deferred** to the following year and is only transferable to other eligible courses at the University of Leeds. It **can be combined** with the International Excellence Scholarship or external funding as long as this does not exceed 100% of your tuition fees. You may also be able to combine this scholarship with a School or Faculty scholarship. This scholarship is paid as a fee reduction for your first year of study only and can only be used as a fee reduction; it **cannot be used** towards other costs, including but not exclusive to maintenance or accommodation costs.
- **International Excellence Scholarships**: 500 scholarships, worth either **£3,000, £6,000 or £16,000**, are available to support eligible international students. The awards recognise and reward high academic achievement for students applying to study a taught Masters course starting in September 2026. Applications for the International Excellence Scholarships are now **closed**.
- Eligibility criteria: classified as an international student for fee purposes; have a conditional or unconditional offer for an eligible taught Masters course starting in September 2026; be self-funded or partially-funded; demonstrate an excellent academic track record, and be predicted to achieve or have achieved a minimum of a Bachelor’s degree with a 2:1 (hons) or equivalent; show excellent professional and personal skills evidenced through work experience and/or extracurricular activities.
- Applications for this scholarship have now **closed**. If you applied by the 29 May deadline, you will be notified of the outcome of your application by 26 June.
- The International Excellence Scholarship **can be combined** with the International Regional Scholarship or external funding as long as this does not exceed 100% of your tuition fees. You may also be able to combine this scholarship with a School or Faculty scholarship. The scholarship award **cannot be deferred** to the following year and is non-transferable to other courses at the University of Leeds. The scholarship is paid as a fee reduction for your first year of study only and can only be used as a fee reduction; it **cannot be used** towards other costs, including but not exclusive to maintenance or accommodation costs.

program_overview.content:
Master of Science in Data Science and Analytics (62027-DFM-DPM)
Entrance Year: Sept 2026
Programme Code: 62027
Stream Code: DFM (Full-time); DPM (Part-time)
Mode of Study: Mixed Mode
Normal Duration: 1.5 years (Full-time); 3 years (Part-time)
Credits Required for Graduation: 31
Programme Leader(s): **Programme Leader** Prof. QI Houduo _BSc, MSc, PhD_; **Deputy Programme Leader** Prof. LIU Yang _BSc, PhD_
Remarks: Non-local applicants must be registered as full-time students.
**Programme Aims**
In today’s era of big data, large data sets are generated every day in various areas of society and industry, from social networking to finance. It is challenging to extract and analyse information from such an unprecedentedly large volume of data. To create value from such data, one must combine techniques from mathematics, statistics and computer science. This programme nurtures graduates with expertise across the core disciplines of mathematics, statistics and computer science. It develops students’ analytical and critical thinking as well as their problem-solving skills. This enables graduates to pursue careers as data analysts in various industries, such as finance and information technology.
**Characteristics**
Data science and analytics involve the use of mathematical, statistical and computing techniques to extract useful information from large-scale data and make decisions accordingly. Statistics, optimisation methods and computer science are widely acknowledged to form the three pillars of modern data science. This programme is designed to provide a balanced treatment of these three pillars, with the aim of cultivating future data analysts. Graduates with highly developed mathematical, statistical and computing skills are in great demand globally, in both industry and academic settings.

curriculum.content:
Study pattern: Each subject takes place once a week in the evening over a 13-week semester. Full-time students normally take four or five subjects in a semester, whereas part-time students usually take two or three subjects. Students are required to complete **31 credits**.
Students need to complete either of the following options:
- Option 1: 18 credits of Compulsory subjects; 12 credits of Elective subjects; 1 credit of Academic Integrity and Ethics (AIE) subject [free of charge]; non-credit bearing National Education (NE) requirement.
- Option 2: 18 credits of Compulsory subjects; 3 credits of Elective subjects; 9 credits of Dissertation; 1 credit of Academic Integrity and Ethics (AIE) subject [free of charge]; non-credit bearing National Education (NE) requirement.
Normally, only students who have completed 6 Compulsory subjects (18 credits) and the AIE subject (1 credit) with GPA 3.0 or above at the end of Semester 2 will be considered for Option 2.

program_overview.content:
Data Science and Analytics (MSc) is offered full time over **17 months** with a **January start**. The course equips students with a theoretical understanding and practical experience of applying methods drawn from data science and analytics, developing in-demand skills for extracting and handling “big data” and applying modelling tools to help businesses and government organisations make better decisions. On completion, students will be well placed to progress into roles in data-intensive industries or a related research career.
The degree falls under the umbrella of the [Data Science Academy](https://www.cardiff.ac.uk/data-science-academy) (DSA), run by the School of Computer Science and Informatics in partnership with the School of Mathematics, and benefits from the shared knowledge and skills of both Schools. The degree is run by the School of Mathematics.
Key features include:
- A cross-disciplinary network of experts across the School of Mathematics, the School of Computer Science and Informatics, and other University research groups.
- Professional work placements and projects with leading data science practitioners in the UK and abroad.
- Project-based learning using real-world datasets and problems.
- Teaching in the newly-built flagship building Abacws.
The programme structure includes 100 credits of compulsory modules, 20 credits from optional modules, and a 60-credit project which will typically involve working with a company on a problem of real importance. Teaching uses a mixture of lectures, seminars, computer workshops and tutorials; programming skills and relevant software packages are taught in dedicated computer suites. Industry experts are often invited to give presentations.
For the dissertation project, students are allocated three supervisors, usually two academic staff members with an interest or specialism in the student’s field of research and a sponsor supervisor from the organisation worked with during the project. Students are also allocated a personal tutor within both the School of Mathematics and the School of Computer Science and Informatics.
The programme develops programming skills, data handling and extraction skills, machine learning and informatics skills, problem solving and modelling skills, communication skills, teamwork, and logical and analytic thinking. Graduates have gone on to work with companies and Government organisations including the Office for National Statistics, Lloyds Banking Group, Nationwide, British Airways, Network Rail, UK Government, The Financial Times, Virgin Media, Welsh Water and Admiral Insurance.
An important feature of the MSc programme is the project dissertation, allowing students to apply the methods and skills acquired in the taught programme to either a real-world or more theoretical problem. This might involve working with an external company or organisation; in previous years students have worked with Admiral Insurance, Lloyds Banking Group, the Office for National Statistics and the National Health Service.

program_overview.content:
Data and Decision Analytics (MSc) is a Master of Science course starting September 2026, lasting 1 year, delivered full-time at Highfield campus. This qualification is awarded by the University of Southampton.
Develop the analytic and professional skills for success in data science on this Data & Decision Analytics MSc. You’ll learn advanced level mathematical modelling, statistical analysis, and computation. This UK master’s course will give you the skills and knowledge to make better decisions based on data. There is also a strong focus on real work experience, with opportunities for summer projects in a range of industries.
Through this degree you’ll learn:
- programming skills in R and in Python
- advanced theory and methods of applied statistics
- practical application of operational research
- modelling of deterministic and stochastic systems
- industry career skills working on a project with an external organisation
You'll take on a 3-month summer project which can be in operational research, statistics, data science or a combination of each. This is excellent preparation if you want to go onto a PhD in one of these areas. There are 2 options for this project:
- The opportunity to compete for a 3-month project with an external organisation
- An internal project linked to the latest research led by one of our academics
You'll also get the chance to meet with the CORMSIS Business Advisory Board which is represented by major companies including Tesco, Shell, British Airways and [HM Revenue & Customs](http://www.hmrc.gov.uk/). They ensure this MSc continues to be fresh and relevant to the needs of employers, so you’ll have excellent employment prospects.
Professor Alain Zemkoho is your course leader. Read [Professor Zemkoho’s profile](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xd5hn/professor-alain-zemkoho) to learn more about his work.
This course is based at [Highfield](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/student-life/campuses/highfield).
This is a full-time MSc which runs over 12-months from September to the following September. There are 2 semesters of taught material. You’ll then complete an MSc project, usually in the summer. In semesters 1 and 2 you'll study a combination of modules that everyone on the course must study, and additional modules you'll get to choose from a range of options. These will provide you with the necessary foundations in operational research and statistics.
The learning activities for this course include careers talks from external organisations, employability skills training, computer programming, collecting and analysing data, using IT for optimisation, simulation, and statistical software, coursework, and individual and group projects. Assessment includes coursework and essays, a dissertation, group essays, individual and group projects, and written exams. You'll need to submit a dissertation on your project work soon after the end of the taught period of study.
This degree will allow you to develop and evidence subject-specific and targeted employability skills, including the required skill set for a range of future careers, further study, or starting your own business. The skills you can expect to focus on and gain from this course include research, critical thinking, self-management, communication, and problem solving.
Graduates commonly work in a range of organisations or sectors including Education, Engineering, Finance, Banking, Accountancy, Government, Insurance, IT, Business consultancy, Marketing, Market research, Health, and Research. Careers directly related to this course include Data analyst, Data engineer, Data scientist, Data consultant, Operational researcher, Market researcher, Management consultant, Systems analyst, Statistician, and Quantitative analyst.
Example job titles of Southampton MSc Data and Decision Analytics graduates include Data scientist, Software engineer, Data analyst, Algorithm developer, Business consultant, Data architect, Data warehouse engineer, Head of data, Financial systems officer, and Systems analyst.
Job prospects for MSc Data and Decision Analytics graduates: £33k average professional salary; 93% in a skilled profession or further study; 98% graduate employment rate. Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics are taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about the activities and perspectives of graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

program_overview.content:
Qualification type: MSc. Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: 12 months or 24 months.
Become a data-driven marketing expert and learn how to harness the power of data analytics to drive business success.
This course has been designed to boost your digital marketing skills and meet the increasing demand marketers who can effectively utilise digital technologies and make strategic data-driven decisions. This course offers a range of exemptions for the CIM professional qualification modules, which are highly sought by employers and will give you a significant advantage in the job market. You will learn how to employ digital techniques and insights from marketing analytics to build stronger relations with consumers, improve business performance and identify new opportunities. You will also gain practical problem-solving skills through an in-depth study of real-life case studies, alongside rigorous training in research methods, data analysis techniques, critical thinking and the use of analytics toolkits.
To pass the programme, you need to successfully complete six 20-credit modules and a final 60-credit applied research project or dissertation. To achieve your MSc qualification, you need to complete 180 credits: Semester One: three 20-credit modules (60 credits in total); Semester Two: three 20-credit modules (60 credits in total); Final project: 60 credits. You must pass all the modules with a minimum grade of 50%. Subject to meeting specific criteria outlined by the University, you will graduate with a Pass, Merit or Distinction.
This course is an ideal option for aspiring digital marketers, marketing professionals, business analysts and entrepreneurs who want to gain expertise in using digital technologies and analytics tools to make data-driven decisions. This course is open to those who already hold a degree in any discipline or have substantial and demonstrable experience in the field.
What you'll learn:
- Social media marketing
- Marketing management
- Research methods in practice
- Integrated marketing technology
- Marketing strategy and analytics
- Critical perspectives and consumption.
The University of Liverpool Management School is one of an elite group of institutions worldwide to hold the gold standard ‘triple-crown’ accreditation from AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS. This programme is delivered by the triple-accredited [University of Liverpool Management School](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/management/). The School has a thriving international master’s community with a comprehensive, interdisciplinary programme of social and extra-curricular events and dedicated careers and employability support.
Our Digital Marketing and Analytics MSc is delivered via online material, lectures, tutorials, practical tasks, interactive activities, case studies and project work. Lectures will provide you the main of concepts, principles and theories around data-driven marketing. You will then apply what you have learned during the lectures in practical sessions focused on real-life case studies, involving group or individual work. Following semester two, you will complete a dissertation with the support of an academic supervisor. This final project will deepen your knowledge, understanding and capabilities by undertaking research in a distinct area of data-driven marketing. Teaching time accounts for an average of 10 hours per week. However, you should anticipate an additional 24 hours of self-directed study and group work per week.
Assessment tasks are varied, and some may be explicitly designed to meet the learning outcomes of a particular programme of study. You can expect to be assessed via coursework, essay, group work, (video) presentations, case studies, infographics, reports and examinations. The weighting of individual assessment components varies across modules.
Graduates acquire the essential skills to thrive in marketing-related careers across digital marketing, marketing strategy, marketing research, data analyst roles, and consultancy positions in both private and public sector organisations. Employment outcomes are strong, with 90% of graduates securing employment within six months of graduation. Popular job titles include:
- Management Associate (Brand Management)
- Digital Marketing Manager
- Social Media Manager.
Recent alumni have gone on to work for notable employers such as:
- Marriott International
- WatchNation
- Central Marketing Group.
These opportunities span locations including London, Liverpool, the wider UK, as well as India and Dubai.

program_overview.content:
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics is a one-year full-time programme that prepares students for the data-driven marketing landscape by combining strategic marketing expertise with digital and analytical capabilities. The programme develops proficiency in leveraging analytics tools and creating evidence-based marketing solutions that drive measurable business impact. Through applied learning including industry projects and capstone research, it equips marketing graduates with the technical and strategic competencies required to lead digital transformation initiatives and optimise marketing performance in contemporary organisations.
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics programme offers students the opportunity to engage directly with industry through the Capstone Dissertation's dual-pathway approach. Students can undertake an Applied Marketing Project working with industry partners to address real organisational challenges, benefiting from industry mentorship and collaborative problem-solving. Or they can apply for a competitive industry placement within a company, agency, or marketing department. The programme is further enriched through regular guest speakers from leading industry professionals, live case study-led assessments, and networking opportunities with industry practitioners, alumni, and peers.
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics is delivered at Queen's Business School through in-person instruction, combining traditional lectures with student-focused workshops and hands-on practical classes. The course can only be taken on a full-time basis. Students undertake 4 modules in semester 1 and a further 4 in semester 2. In semester 3, students undertake the Capstone module. Students who successfully complete eight taught modules (120 CATS) and the Capstone module (60 CATS) are awarded an MSc in Digital Marketing and Analytics degree. Other exit qualifications available: students may exit with a Postgraduate Diploma by successfully completing 120 CATS from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate by successfully completing 60 CATS from taught modules.
Semester 3 is a 60 CATS Capstone Dissertation module. The Capstone Dissertation represents an independent piece of research with the opportunity to apply knowledge and skills acquired over previous semesters to design, develop, and propose marketing solutions for real-world business or societal challenges. Students have two pathways to choose from: (i) Applied Marketing Project, working on an organisation; or (ii) Industry Placement Project, working in an organisation.
Classes will be delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops and they will be interactive and discussion-based, blending theory with practical examples. Learning and engagement approaches include case studies, software demonstrations, practical workshops, role plays, groupwork, scenario discussions and organisation visits. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through the capstone projects where students choose between different pathways. Students are assigned dedicated academic support for these projects and company mentors where relevant. There are 4 taught classes per week, 3 hours each. Additional academic and employability support classes are timetabled throughout the week.
People teaching you: [Dr Grace Carson](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/grace-carson-2), Programme Director, Queen's Business School.
The programme prepares graduates for high-demand careers in specialised roles such as Digital Marketing Manager, Customer Insights Specialist, Marketing Performance Analyst, Social Media Strategist, Marketing Analytics Consultant, and Brand Development Manager. Graduates will be equipped to drive digital transformation initiatives, optimise campaign performance through data analytics, and lead marketing innovation across diverse industries including technology, retail, financial services, healthcare, and digital agencies. Graduates from this programme have secured roles with employers such as PwC, BBC, Marriott International, Warner Brothers, ASOS, Primark, Selfridges, Yahoo, Amazon, and many others.
Course location: [Queen's Business School](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/queens-business-school/).

curriculum.content:
The MSc Digital Marketing and Analytics is a **one-year full-time programme** delivered at Queen's Business School through **in-person instruction**, combining traditional lectures with student-focused workshops and hands-on practical classes. The course can only be taken on a **full-time basis**. Students undertake **4 modules in semester 1** and **4 in semester 2**. Students who successfully complete **eight taught modules (120 CATS)** and the **Capstone module (60 CATS)** in semester 3 are awarded an MSc in Digital Marketing and Analytics degree. Other exit qualifications available: students may exit with a Postgraduate Diploma by successfully completing **120 CATS** from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate by successfully completing **60 CATS** from taught modules.
- **Semester 1:** structured through a **60 CATS** package consisting of **4 core modules**, each worth **15 CATS**: Digital Marketing Principles and Practice; Marketing Management; Digital Business Strategy; Generative AI and Business Intelligence.
- **Semester 2:** structured through a **60 CATS** package consisting of **2 core modules**, each worth **15 CATS**, and an additional **2 15 CAT modules**, selected from 4 options.
- **Semester 2 core modules:** Consumer Behaviour in the Digital Age; Marketing Analytics.
- **Semester 2 optional modules:** Strategy, Change and Analytics; Social Media and Reputation Management; AI Frontiers; Cyber Security & Digital Risk Management.
- **Semester 3:** a **60 CATS Capstone Dissertation module**. The Capstone Dissertation is an independent piece of research applying knowledge and skills acquired over previous semesters to design, develop, and propose marketing solutions for real-world business or societal challenges.
- The Capstone Dissertation has two applied pathways: **Applied Marketing Project (working on an organisation)**, where students conduct an independent research project analysing and proposing solutions to specific digital marketing challenges faced by a real organisation/s; or **Industry Placement Project (working in an organisation)**, where students undertake a placement within a company, agency, or marketing department, conducting research that directly informs their host organisation's marketing strategy and operations.
- Classes are delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops, interactive and discussion-based, blending theory with practical examples. Learning and engagement approaches include case studies, software demonstrations, practical workshops, role plays, groupwork, scenario discussions and organisation visits. program_overview.content:
The MSc in Earth and Environmental Analytics for Sustainability at CUHK prepares the next generation of environmental data scientists by combining traditional Earth system science with advanced computational methods, artificial intelligence, and data analytics. Students gain expertise in handling diverse environmental datasets, from satellite imagery to sensor networks, while developing proficiency in environmental modeling and ESG analysis.
The programme features world-class faculty, state-of-the-art computational facilities, and strong industry connections. Through project-based learning and industry collaboration, students work on actual environmental challenges. An optional research pathway allows talented students to pursue publication-quality research, preparing them for either professional careers or academic pursuits.
Programme structure includes **five required courses** and **three elective courses**. The normative study period is:
- Full-time: 1 year
- Part-time: 2 years
Graduates may pursue roles in environmental consulting, government agencies, research institutions, or corporate sustainability. Relevant areas include climate risk assessment, environmental monitoring, ESG analysis, and sustainable urban planning.

**Electives (three courses from the following):**

program_overview.content:
MSc Economic Policy and Data Analytics is offered full-time or part-time, with a duration of 12 months full-time or 24 months part-time. It is an opportunity for students who wish to pursue a career requiring state-of-the-art analytical skills to address policy issues.
Data is reshaping the way that policymakers understand, design, implement, and evaluate effective public policy. Translating this increasing amount of data into useful insight requires an understanding of cutting-edge analytical methods, strong technical skills, and a strong foundation in economics. This programme offers rigorous training in economic theory and the analytical methods needed to answer pressing policy questions facing public institutions, international organisations, consulting firms, research institutions, and think tanks.
With a strong emphasis on technical skills, the modules cover a range of economic policies, including healthcare, the social safety net, economic inequality, environmental sustainability and energy policy, and tax and fiscal policy. Modules are taught by world-class researchers who publish in world-leading academic journals on the topics they teach. The faculty teaching on this programme maintain close relationships with businesses, governments, and non-profit organisations, linking their research and teaching to real-world impact.
The course is ideal for those who want rigorous training in the analytical methods and economic theory needed to answer pressing policy questions facing public institutions, international organisations and businesses. Students learn data management and visualisation for economics, econometric and statistical methods, machine learning and big data econometrics, labour and public economics, and applying economic analysis to public policy.
The 12-month programme consists of five compulsory modules and one optional module followed by a dissertation carried out over the summer period upon completion of Semester two. Students are required to complete 180 credits to achieve a full MSc. Teaching time accounts for an average of 10 hours per week, with an additional 30 hours of self-directed study and group work expected.
Modules are taught using active learning techniques including real-world case studies, social media, lecture capture and real-time financial and business data using the Bloomberg trading floor. The principal forms of teaching are face-to-face lectures and seminars, and the course offers an enhanced programme of events and activities such as coding bootcamps and guest speakers. Following semester two, students complete a dissertation with support from an academic supervisor.
This programme is delivered by the triple-accredited [University of Liverpool Management School](https://www.liverpool.ac.uk/management/). The University of Liverpool Management School holds ‘triple-crown’ accreditation from AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS.
The School has a thriving international master’s community with a comprehensive, interdisciplinary programme of social and extra-curricular events and dedicated careers and employability support.
This programme focuses on the analysis of public policy through economic theory and state-of-the-art analytics. Students study sectors like healthcare, inequality, sustainability, taxation, and social protection while gaining a strong grounding in machine learning, big data econometrics, and applied econometric methods. Employability is central: students access one-to-one careers support, targeted workshops including coding bootcamps in R and Python, seminars, and networking events with professionals from industry and the civil service.
Skills developed include analytical fluency in R, Python, and econometric techniques; policy evaluation and data-driven decision-making; articulation of economic insights for diverse stakeholders; and strategic problem-solving in policy contexts. Graduates will be well-suited for roles in government, international organisations, think tanks, or research-intensive environments.

application_materials.content:
As part of your application, you must provide the following supporting documents:
- **Your official transcript.** Please read UCL’s guide on [getting your academic transcript](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/getting-your-academic-transcript "Getting your academic transcript").
- **A personal statement.** UCL’s [personal statement guidance](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/writing-your-personal-statement "Writing your personal statement") offers advice on writing an effective personal statement.
- If you need a visa to study at UCL, you will need to provide a copy of your current **passport**. If you do not have a valid passport, you can complete the Missing passport document and provide your passport later.
- Some courses require additional documents as part of the application. Full details can be found on UCL’s [additional course requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/degree-types/courses-additional-requirements "Courses with additional requirements") page.
- If you meet UCL’s [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/english-language-requirements "English Language requirements") using a UCL-recognised test, you should upload your official test report form or qualification. If you cannot provide this evidence when you submit your application, your application will still be considered.
The number of references needed to support your application can be found on the prospectus page for your course. You should read UCL’s guidance on [selecting your reference](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/graduate/how-apply/selecting-your-references "Selecting your references") and contact your nominated referee(s) before starting your application to check they can provide a reference for you.
Do **not** password-protect or encrypt files. Before submitting, make sure you have uploaded the correct version of each supporting document, that your official transcripts clearly show your name, institution, modules and any grades received, that you have provided accurate details of any work experience or previous employment either in the employment section or uploaded CV, that you have uploaded any compulsory supporting documents required for your course, and that any referee details use institutional or professional email addresses. You cannot replace or add additional documents once you have submitted your application.
