program_overview.content:
Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA) MSc is based in London, Bloomsbury. The programme equips students with advanced data science, artificial intelligence and energy modelling skills to address complex challenges in the energy transition and prepares them for careers in energy analytics, policy, consulting, or smart technology development.
Designed in collaboration with industry, the degree combines technical knowledge of energy systems with expertise in data science and AI. Students develop expertise to:
- Use data science, machine learning and AI to extract insights from large and diverse datasets.
- Analyse complex energy systems, including supply, demand, sector interdependencies, and infrastructure planning.
- Apply modelling tools to support decarbonisation, smart grid optimisation and low-carbon transitions.
- Evaluate and deploy methods in supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning and predictive analytics.
- Work with spatial data to understand the geographic and place-based dimensions of energy systems.
The course is suitable for those with a quantitative background who have an interest in energy and are motivated by using data science to solve sustainability problems; those with an energy background who are interested in data science; and early and mid-career energy professionals looking to expand their data skills and domain knowledge.
Study mode is full-time, part-time, or flexible. Duration is 1 calendar year full-time, 2 calendar years part-time, or 5 calendar years flexible. Students undertake modules to the value of 180 credits. Upon successful completion of 180 credits, students are awarded an MSc in Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA); 120 credits leads to a PG Dip; and 60 credits leads to a PG Cert.
Learning takes place at the [UCL Energy Institute](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/bartlett/environment-energy-resources/energy), part of [The Bartlett School of Environment, Energy and Resources](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/bartlett/environment-energy-resources), where experts shape policy, drive innovation and collaborate with industry across the energy sector. Students benefit from a learning environment grounded in real-world challenges and live research, guest lectures and practitioner input across government, industry, consultancy, and the non-profit sector, close links to London’s energy, climate and data sectors, and opportunities to collaborate on applied projects and build a professional network.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures, workshops, hands-on practical sessions, collaborative projects, and self-directed study. Assessment includes problem sets, individual assignments and coursework, group-based data analysis assignments with a report and presentation, unseen examinations and a dissertation. Full-time students study eight taught modules across Term 1 and Term 2, then complete the dissertation during Term 3 and the summer. Part-time students take the taught modules over two years and complete the dissertation in Term 3 of the final year. Flexible students have up to five years to complete eight taught modules.
100% of Energy Systems and Data Analytics MSc graduates were in employment or further study within 15 months of graduation ([HESA Graduate Outcomes Survey 2019-23](https://public.tableau.com/app/profile/katy.coyte4085/viz/WhatDoUCLGraduatesDo/WhatdoUCLgraduatesdo)). Graduates have gone on to careers in government, consultancy, energy utilities, data and AI start-ups, and global NGOs. Typical roles include energy analysts, data scientists, sustainability consultants, and climate policy advisors. Notable employers include Octopus Energy, Deloitte, Shell, China Huadian, and Atkins. Many graduates also pursue advanced research opportunities and PhD study at institutions including UCL.
The course develops technical and analytical skills sought in the Net Zero workforce, including hands-on experience in data science, machine learning, and energy systems modelling using real-world energy datasets; expertise in Python, data visualisation, and statistical analysis tailored to energy applications; the ability to interpret and communicate technical insights for energy policy and business decisions; and critical problem-solving skills through interdisciplinary, research-led teaching and group project work.
The Energy Systems and Data Analytics MSc is affiliated with the Energy Institute (EI) through its Learning Affiliate (LA) scheme, giving students free EI membership during their studies and access to professional development resources, industry networks, and sector events. The LA status supports the course’s current pursuit of full professional accreditation by the EI.
The course offers networking opportunities through events with fellow students, alumni, faculty, and industry experts, plus guest lectures and seminars with industry leaders. Its London location provides access to industry events, exhibitions, and conferences.

curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time, Part-time, Flexible. Duration: Full-time **1 calendar year**; Part-time **2 calendar years**; Flexible **5 calendar years**. Programme starts September 2026.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures, workshops, hands-on practical sessions, collaborative projects, and self-directed study. Assessment is through problem sets, individual assignments and coursework, group-based data analysis assignments with a report and presentation, unseen examinations and a dissertation. Full-time students typically engage in 8 to 15 contact hours per week in Terms 1 and 2, with Term 3 dedicated to independent dissertation research.
Modules:
- Full-time: You take eight taught modules across Term 1 and Term 2. You complete the dissertation during Term 3 and the summer, having had preparatory tutorials during the previous terms. You take seven compulsory modules and choose one optional module.
- Part-time: You take eight taught modules across Term 1 and Term 2 over two years. You complete the dissertation during Term 3 of your final year. You take seven compulsory modules and choose one optional module.
- Flexible: As a flexible student you have up to five years to complete eight taught modules. You take seven compulsory modules and also choose one optional module.
Compulsory modules:
- [Energy Systems](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-systems-BENV0090)
- [Advanced Machine Learning for Energy Systems](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/advanced-machine-learning-for-energy-systems-BENV0148)
- [Energy Data Analysis](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-data-analysis-BENV0091)
- [Statistics for Energy Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/statistics-for-energy-analytics-BENV0094)
- [Energy Data Analytics in the Built Environment](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-data-analytics-in-the-built-environment-BENV0092)
- [Energy and Transport Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-and-transport-analytics-BENV0095)
- [Dissertation: Energy Systems and Data Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/dissertation-energy-systems-and-data-analytics-BENV0096)
- [Spatial Analysis of Energy Data](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-analysis-of-energy-data-BENV0093)
Optional modules:
- UK Energy and Environment Policy and Law
- [Energy, Technology and Innovation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/energy-technology-and-innovation-BENV0016)
- [Systems Thinking and System Dynamics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/systems-thinking-and-system-dynamics-BENV0047)
- [International Commodity Trade](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/international-commodity-trade-BENV0074)
- [Econometrics of Energy Markets](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/econometrics-of-energy-markets-BENV0122)
- [Electricity Market Design for the Energy Transition](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/electricity-market-design-for-the-energy-transition-BENV0185)
- [Applied Bayesian Methods](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/applied-bayesian-methods-STAT0031)
Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of **180 credits**, you will be awarded an MSc in Energy Systems and Data Analytics (ESDA).

financial_aid.content:
- Spärck AI Scholarship: UK Government award supporting talented leaders in AI and its application across diverse disciplines.
- **Value:** Full tuition fees plus £22,780 stipend (for one year).
- **Available to:** Prospective students.
- **Selection criteria:** Academic Merit; strengths and motivations, prioritizing underrepresented groups.
- **Eligible fee status:** Home and Overseas.
- **Eligible programmes:** Selected 1-year full-time Master's programmes, including [MSc Energy Systems and Data Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/taught-degrees/energy-systems-and-data-analytics-esda-msc).

multiple_applications.content:
You may submit applications for a maximum of **two** taught graduate courses for entry to the 2026/27 academic year. The applications must be for different courses. If an application fee is charged, it will be charged per application. UCL does not accept multiple applications for the same course in the same academic year.
If you apply for more than one course the fee is payable for each application that requires an application fee.
If you would like to apply for a different course, you will need to submit a new application for the course you wish to be considered for. Please be aware that you may submit applications for a maximum of two graduate courses for entry to the 2025/26 academic year.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer. However, UCL will consider a request to defer only in exceptional circumstances outside of your control, including:
- The serious illness of the offer holder or the serious illness of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The death of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The need to take parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months.
- Where the offer holder is directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster, such as war, earthquakes or flooding.
- The offer holder has been awarded a UCL scholarship, including UCL partnership agreements and Faculty awards, or a full scholarship from a recognised funding body for study in the following academic year.
To be eligible for a deferral you must hold an unconditional offer which you have accepted. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt, if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme. If you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the permitted categories, you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, but applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.
To request a deferral, you must do so on the offer page of your application portal. If requesting a deferral due to illness or parental or adoption leave, you must provide a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. If requesting a deferral on the basis of a scholarship for study in the following academic year, you must upload a copy of your official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information before making a final decision.
An application cannot be deferred twice. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If a deferral request is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment. You will receive a new offer letter and may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
- The offer page of the applicant portal and the offer letter will clearly outline if the offer is conditional and what conditions must be met.
- Offer holders must accept their offer to upload documents to clear condition(s), and documentary evidence must be uploaded through the Document Uploads section of the [applicant portal](https://evision.ucl.ac.uk/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn); UCL cannot accept documents provided by offer holders through email.
- If a degree condition has not been met, applicants should upload evidence of their degree and final grade to the [applicant portal](https://evision.ucl.ac.uk/urd/sits.urd/run/siw_lgn) so UCL can review them.
- For standard **28 September** starters, conditional offer holders must provide documentary evidence to clear condition(s) by **11 September 2026**. Documents provided after this date will be considered on a case-by-case basis and at UCL’s discretion. For all other start dates, applicants should check the offer letter for the deadline that applies to the course.
- Applicants who need to take a UCL accepted English language test are strongly encouraged to book a test as soon as possible.
- International students holding a conditional offer will be asked to confirm that the details UCL holds are correct and supply anything incorrect or missing. Upon receipt of responses and once the offer is unconditional firm, UCL will aim to issue the CAS as soon as possible.
- Pre-enrolment invitations can only be sent once the applicant has accepted the offer and met any conditions.

program_overview.content:
The NUS Master of Technology in Enterprise Business Analytics programme (MTech EBAC) is crafted to meet the industry's need for data scientists and machine learning specialists, with a focus on advancing enterprises through data and AI. The business analytics course is a gateway to specialist, expert and leadership positions in data science.
- Duration: Full-time 1 year (2 semesters); Part-time 2 years (4 semesters).
- MTech EBAC offers holistic training in key aspects of data science and AI, from exploratory data analysis and predictive modelling to natural language processing, recommender systems and big data engineering.
- Professionals will be equipped with technical expertise to harness data, machine learning and enabling technologies to develop and deploy effective data-driven solutions that enhance decision-making, optimise operations, drive profitability and elevate user experiences within enterprises.
- Recognition: Top student is awarded the IBM Medal and Book Prize; Best Project Prize.
- This programme is suited for professionals looking to build or deepen expertise in data science, business analytics, and AI, and take on specialist or leadership roles in data-driven functions. It is also ideal for those who want to apply data and machine learning to solve business problems and improve decision-making.
Graduates of the enterprise business analytics course will be capable of undertaking tasks such as discovering insights from data; applying concepts and techniques to solve major business problems; designing and customizing marketing campaigns through efficient targeting; analysing sales channels; optimising the marketing mix of their organisations; improving decision-making to increase returns on investments; predicting future profitability; and automating production fault detection in manufacturing using predictive modelling.
Learning outcomes include helping enterprises move towards a stronger emphasis on computer tools and statistical and machine learning techniques to develop high-performance analytics capability; translating massive and complex unstructured data into insights; producing predictive models to solve problems across business functions and units; and contributing to more effective business strategies and plans for sustainable growth and competitive advantage.
MTech EBAC candidates must successfully complete the following business analytics course components to be awarded the degree:
- **Fundamental** - Complete 2 Graduate Certificates.
- **Specialist** - Complete 2 of 5 Graduate Certificates.
Fundamental analytics areas include Analytics Project Management and Business Analytics Practice. Specialist analytics areas include Customer Analytics, Big Data Analytics, Practical Language Processing, Specialised Predictive Modelling & Forecasting, and Intelligent Financial Risk Management.
A central element of the MTech programme is the project module. Student projects for MTech Enterprise in Business Analytics Course students will include intense full time engagement of 5 months with companies for full time students. For part-time students the capstone engagement will be for 7-12 months. Students are allowed to conduct their project as a team-based internship if desired. The expected commitment for the project is 30 man-days per team member. Objectives include practising new technical skills in a real industry environment and applying tools, methods and techniques learnt.
As an MTech EBAC graduate, students will be prepared for specialist, expert and leadership roles in enterprise business analytics to create business value through strategic use of data, visualisation methods, modelling techniques and frontline tools. Career prospects include Business Analytics Manager, Data Scientist and Architect, Business Analyst, Optimisation Strategy Consultant, Business Intelligence and Performance Management Consultant, Enterprise Intelligence Manager, Market Intelligence Analyst, CRM Data Analyst, Risk Analyst, Marketing Analyst, and Big Data Analyst.
MTech alumni are pursuing their careers at global organisations including Accenture, Creative Technology, DBS Bank, Defence Science & Technology Agency, Deutsche Bank AG, Fuji Xerox Asia Pacific, HP Singapore, IBM Singapore, Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore, Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, Jurong Port, Microsoft, Murex, NCS, NEC Asia Pacific, NTUC, OCBC Bank, Revolution Analytics, Singapore Telecommunications, Standard Chartered Bank, Starhub, ST Electronics, and Tata Consultancy Services.
The [NUS-ISS Career Services Office](https://www.iss.nus.edu.sg/graduate-programmes/career-services) helps students to match jobs based on their skills and experience. There will be bi-yearly Career Fairs held for students and graduates to network with employers. For fresh graduates with no work experience, the average salary starts from S$4,000 onwards. Graduates with more than 3 years of work experience can expect a starting pay of S$6,000 and above.
Teaching staff have more than 20 years of industry experience.

Choose **ONE** from **EBA5004: Practical Language Processing** - New Media and Sentiment Mining; Text Processing Using Machine Learning; Conversational UIs, **EBA5005: Specialised Predictive Modelling and Forecasting** - Complex Predictive Modelling & Forecasting; Product & Pricing Analytics; Analytics for Commercial Excellence, or **EBA5008: Intelligent Financial Risk Management** - Advanced Machine Learning for Financial Services; Explainable & Responsible AI for Finance; Credit Risk Modelling and Analytics; Alternative Data for Fintech Innovation.

- Year 2 Semester 1 (Jan - May): Choose **ONE** from **EBA5003: Customer Analytics** - Customer Analytics; Advanced Customer Analytics; Campaign Analytics, or **EBA5006: Big Data Analytics** - Big Data Engineering for Analytics; Recommender Systems; Processing Big Data for Analytics.

- Year 2 Semester 1-2 (Mar - Sep): **Team-based Internship or Off-site Project** - hands-on project with external organisation; assessment by project, presentation & report.
Students are evaluated through a combination of course work, project work and examinations. All students are required to complete a three-hour examination for each fundamental and specialist module taken.

multiple_applications.content:
Applicants are allowed to apply to multiple programmes based on interest. However, you can only enrol in one programme. For applicants who are undecided, I recommend submitting multiple applications. This would give you more choices and may increase your probability of admission. Applications for different programmes are reviewed by different admissions committees, and they have no impact on each other. As such, you may want separately prepare your application for each programme to best emphasise your fit for a programme. Also, please note that **each application would incur a separate application fee**.
If you apply for multiple programmes within the same application period, please create all applications and rank them in order of preference. Please note that they cannot be modified after submission. Your preferences will only be considered if you are applying to multiple programmes offered by the same School, Faculty or College. As your preferences cannot be changed after submission of application, please finalise your order of preference before submitting your application (i.e. when the Application Status is at “Pending online submission”). Your preference will not be a consideration if you are applying for programmes offered by different Departments or Schools.

conditional_admission_policy.content:

- Students may apply for matriculation after completing all the required GradCerts and should meet a **minimum CAP of 3.0** to apply, in addition to all other NUS/ISS requirements.

application_materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together. Please do not upload academic documents to the funding section as we cannot access these.
Your application must include the following:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, please provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume: an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa, for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
- If you entered your current degree programme later than year 1, separate details of the qualification used to gain entry into that later year of your degree, including any transcripts and certificates for that qualification.
If you have them, please include the following:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard, but could strengthen your application by explaining a gap in your education or if your education/degree subject is not directly related to the programme. The personal statement should be **no more than one side of A4** and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
Documents which are not required:
- References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases a reference may be requested to help make a decision.
Country specific information:
- Applicants with Chinese degrees: provide evidence of your current/final overall weighted percentage (%); GPA or arithmetic percentage is not accepted.
- Applicants with Indian degrees should include: a copy of your bachelor’s degree certificate; a copy of your consolidated mark sheet; a copy of your semester mark sheets; a copy of your University marking scheme; official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%). If you have not completed your degree you should provide the bottom three items.
- Applicants with Canadian degrees: provide details of the grading system used on your transcript, including the percentage pass mark for your degree. If your degree was taught in English, include official evidence of this.
Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal so the document links to the correct application automatically.

program_overview.content:
Year of entry 2026. Start date September 2026. Delivery type: on campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The Environmental Data Science and Analytics MSc is designed to give you a fuller understanding of data and what appropriate interpretation and insight generation means in various environmental contexts. Throughout, you'll develop a broad understanding of environmental issues and how data driven analysis can help address these. You’ll build the skills needed to analyse, understand, interpret and visualise complex environmental data; generating insights that address real-world environmental challenges. You’ll apply techniques from data science including environmental modelling, machine learning, visualisation and data curation to environmental data, with a focus on analysis through programming.
At Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to learn from leading researchers in the field, with input from the School of Geography and the School of Earth and Environment. By the end of the course, you’ll be equipped with the specialist knowledge and skills that are sought after across multiple industries, especially those dealing with large scale environmental data to address the needs of society.
The course is designed to give you an understanding of the end-to-end workflow of data in an environmental context, allowing the nuances of how and why data from the environment is collected, and the need for appropriate analysis for policy and management relevant insights. The course has a particular focus on the data science and analytic techniques, giving you the skills to apply them to complex environmental issues. A multitude of environmental data, and its specific context and form, is considered and worked with to give a breadth of experience necessary to derive insights and solutions creatively to real world problems.
You'll take compulsory modules that are designed to progressively include more programming and data science, moving from fundamental knowledge to application of skills in a creative manner. On completion of the course, you'll be able to demonstrate in-depth data science techniques to environmental data, with understanding of the data context allowing for sophisticated insight generation that is appropriate to inform decision making in multiple scenarios. The combination of relevant data science techniques to environmental data and understanding of environmental science context will allow you to demonstrate an ability to generate creative solutions, alongside insights.
Why study at Leeds:
- Globally-renowned research from the [School of Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research), [School of Earth and Environment](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/see-research-innovation) and the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/), the national institute for data science and artificial intelligence, feeds into the course.
- You can advance your skills and knowledge in areas such as environmental policies, programming for data science, machine learning, AI, satellite technology and interpreting large hyperdimensional data.
- You can tailor the course to suit your career aspirations with a selection of optional modules in areas like web-based GIS, GIS and environment and digital image processing for environmental remote sensing.
- You will conduct your own project work, enabling you to develop transferable skills as a researcher while investigating a real-world issue that explores and develops your interests.
- You will have access to specialist facilities including laboratories and an excellent GIS computer cluster with industry-standard software.
- Teaching is delivered by a programme team of academics actively engaged in ground-breaking research in the School of Geography and the School of Earth and Environment.
- Fieldwork opportunities allow you to develop understanding and skills in data acquisition and deployment of sensors to collect environmental data.
The project takes the place of the traditional dissertation. Your project submission is designed to reflect the types of data science outputs you might encounter in your future career in the form of a ‘notebook’-style analysis and an associated practical briefing report. This brings together skills in data science and programming, and meaningful insight generation that can be used to inform decision making in multiple contexts, including influencing policy.
The course takes a problem-based learning approach, presenting real-world problems where you must use your growing skills and knowledge to develop creative solutions. This is embodied using practical sessions, individual and group, where you’ll practice skills, reducing the number of modules that are purely lecture based. Datasets used are sourced from leading researchers in the field, or from industry, reflecting a variety of data types and contexts. A combination of face-to-face learning in practical labs, lectures, seminars, and group working is used alongside digital platforms.
You’ll be taught by an experienced team of academics and researchers who are actively engaged in cutting-edge research and part of the Centre for Spatial Analysis and Policy, River Basin Processes and Management, and Ecology and Global Change research groups within the School of Geography, School of Earth and Environment. On this course, you’ll be taught by expert academics, from lecturers through to professors. You may also be taught by industry professionals with years of experience, as well as trained postgraduate researchers.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme. As a Masters student at Leeds, you’ll have the opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with the Global Industry Programme, developing key professional skills and gaining insight into working in your chosen field by helping to solve a real business problem from a live company brief. The programme is fully online and designed to fit around your studies, includes opportunities to make professional networks, and allows you to work as part of a team across disciplines to tackle real business needs.
The specific environmental context of the course allows you to enter specialised careers that require a contextual understanding of data and context from the environmental domain, including environmental consultancies, transport, engineering, utilities such as water, energy and renewables, and government agencies. More widely, the course will equip you with data science and analytical skills that are vital to many industries across the globe, including local authorities and governments, industry such as finance and telecoms, and NGOs. University of Leeds students are among the top 5 most targeted by top employers according to [The Graduate Market 2024, High Fliers Research](https://online.flippingbook.com/view/747999993/).

curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The course is designed to give you an understanding of the end-to-end workflow of data in an environmental context, allowing the nuances of how and why data from the environment is collected, and the need for appropriate analysis for policy and management relevant insights. You'll take compulsory modules that are designed to progressively include more programming and data science, moving from fundamental knowledge to application of skills in a creative manner.
The list shown below represents typical modules/components studied and may change from time to time. [For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Environmental Data Science and Analytics MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-EDS%26A-FT).
Compulsory modules:
- **Programming for Spatial Data Science - 15 credits**
- **Skills for Environmental Data Scientists - 15 credits**
- **Data to Insights in Multiple Environments - 15 credits**
- **Data Science for Practical Applications - 15 credits**
- **Creative Coding for Real World Problems - 15 credits**
- **Machine Learning for Environmental Data - 15 credits**
- **Environmental Data Science Project - 60 credits**. This project will take the place of the traditional dissertation. Your project submission is designed to reflect the types of data science outputs you might encounter in your future career in the form of a 'notebook'-style analysis and an associated practical briefing report.
Optional modules: The modules listed below are indicative of typical options.
- **GIS and Environment - 15 credits**
- **Digital Image Processing for Environmental Remote Sensing - 15 credits**
- **Environmental Assessment - 15 credits**
- **Web-Based GIS - 15 credits**
Fieldwork provides a great opportunity to study a fascinating subject in contrasting environments away from the University. On this course, we offer the opportunity to undertake fieldwork as part of the Data to Insights in Multiple Environments module, in the UK, to develop your understanding and skills in data acquisition and deployment of sensors to collect environmental data. In addition, you can also opt to conduct fieldwork as part of your dissertation.
While studying at Leeds, you'll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme.

academic_requirements.content:
- **UK applicants:** A minimum high 2:1 undergraduate Bachelor’s (honours) degree with a final mark of **at least 65% or above**.
- If you have a lower degree classification, or a degree in an unrelated subject, your application may be considered if you can demonstrate **significant relevant work experience**, or offer a related graduate qualification such as a Masters or PGDip.
- **Programme specific requirements:** Undergraduate degree with high 2:1 honours, i.e. overall average of **at least 65% across all years of study**, required in a social or applied science such as finance, economics, management, engineering, applied mathematics, computer science or other relevant subject, or equivalent overseas qualification.
- The programme is most suitable if you have **some quantitative background in either finance and/or economics** or have a degree with some quantitative elements.
- If you are still studying, you should be achieving an average of **at least 65% or above** in the UK marking scheme.
- **China applicants:** Degree from Prestigious Institution: Award of Bachelor degree with an average score of **85%**, as evidenced by a Bachelor Degree Certificate and Final Transcripts with official English translations.
- **China applicants:** Degree from a Recognised Institution: Award of Bachelor degree with an average score of **88%**, as evidenced by a Bachelor Degree Certificate and Final Transcripts with official English translations.
- For postgraduate programmes within the King’s Business School and some programmes, offers will usually only be made to applicants from universities considered prestigious by UK ENIC at the point of assessment. A “prestigious institution” is one which is classified as by UK ENIC or within the Project 211/Double First Class list of institutions. You will be a stronger candidate for admission if you have high grades and are attending a university considered prestigious.

This is also the case for applicants who have successfully completed an undergraduate degree (of at least three years duration), a postgraduate taught degree (of at least one year), or a PhD in a majority English speaking country ([as defined by the UKVI](https://eur03.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.gov.uk%2Fstudent-visa%2Fknowledge-of-english&data=04%7C01%7Ccecily.peach%40kcl.ac.uk%7Cb4259f20b3944ff5d16d08d98e4ff7f6%7C8370cf1416f34c16b83c724071654356%7C0%7C0%7C637697296372933336%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJWIjoiMC4wLjAwMDAiLCJQIjoiV2luMzIIiwibBTiI6Ik1haWwiLCJXVCI6Mn0%3D%7C1000&sdata=ah%2F%2FNnl5VP3nelM68z6oOMxxVD7vND1hwQ7cFYQetXg%3D&reserved=0)) within five years of the course start date.

program_overview.content:
The world of finance is changing. With recent advances in technology, huge amounts of data are generated every second on a global scale. Finance professionals of the future will need to harness advanced technologies to process, analyse and ultimately extract key insights to tackle the challenges facing the industry. Students will acquire the knowledge and develop the skills and expertise needed for a broad range of careers in finance and other multinational organisations.
With a focus on big data analytics, the Finance Analytics MSc is designed to provide rigorous applied training in quantitative and empirical methods in Finance. This course is suited to individuals with strong quantitative backgrounds who desire the skills and expertise needed for a range of highly skilled technical professions in finance. Students study topics at the cutting edge of the finance industry such as data visualisation, big data, FinTech and robo-trading.
- Course type: Master's
- Delivery mode: In person
- Study mode: Full-time
- Duration: One year
- Credit value: 180
- Start date: September 2026
- Taught in: [King’s Business School](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/business "King’s Business School")
The Finance Analytics MSc course offers a combination of a rigorous academic programme that teaches the recent developments in data analytics and a unique practitioners’ view of how these developments are shaping the practical aspects of finance. The programme teaches big data methods with applications to risk management, product origination, and trading; text mining techniques with applications to forecasting; automation techniques with applications to robo-advice/trading; and FinTech developments in banking.
Graduates will gain knowledge and skills that are highly sought after by financial industry firms, including incumbent large financial institutions as well as disruptor/start-ups focusing on innovation. Given the importance of analytics in a broader context, the course also provides skills that can be used across a wide range of industries outside Finance, including e-commerce, hospitality, retail, pharmaceutical, and media.
Student employability is one of the main focuses of the Programme. The Programme has been designed in close collaboration with leading financial industry practitioners; active senior finance industry practitioners participate in the teaching of a large proportion of the modules; and the Programme offers additional ungraded modules that enhance students’ programming skills as well as their understanding of financial markets.
The course is most suitable for students with a background in finance, economics or business, or a degree with some quantitative elements. Located in the heart of London, King’s Business School has a strong reputation for research-led teaching and close links to the financial industry.
Base campuses include [Strand Campus](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/visit/strand-campus "Strand Campus") and [Waterloo Campus](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/visit/waterloo-campus "Waterloo Campus"). Locations are determined by where each module is taught and may vary depending on the modules studied.

curriculum.content:
Courses are divided into modules. You will normally take modules totalling **180 credits**.
Required modules:
- Introduction to Analytics in Finance (15 credits)
- Principles of Finance (15 credits)
- Big Data Analytics and Visualisation (15 credits)
- Business Risk Analytics (15 credits)
- Dissertation (60 credits)
Optional modules:
- You are required to take 15 credits from: Big Data and Text Business and Finance Analytics (15 credits); FinTech Analytics and Robo Trading (15 credits); Conduct Risk Management (15 credits).
- You are required to take 45 credits from a range of optional modules that may typically include: Empirical Finance (15 credits); Corporate Finance (15 credits); Financial Econometrics (15 credits); Applied Behavioural Finance (15 credits); Portfolio Management (15 credits); Financial Derivatives for Data Analytics (15 credits); Mathematical Finance (15 credits); Risk Management for Data Analytics (15 credits).
Teaching methods:
| Module | Lectures, seminars and feedback | Self-study |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per 15-credit module | Between 20 and 30 hours which typically consist of a combination of lectures, case discussion and class activities; there may be some variation in the precise format. | Approximately 120-130 hours. |
| Dissertation module | Dissertation workshops and one-to-one supervision. | Approximately 595 hours self-study and project work. |
Typically, one credit equates to 10 hours of work. Face to face teaching will be complemented and supported with innovative technology so that students also experience elements of digital learning and assessment.
Assessment may typically include written examinations, coursework, individual or group projects, presentations, case studies and multiple-choice tests. Your performance will be assessed through a combination of coursework and written/practical examinations.
Key information: Course type: Master's. Delivery mode: In person. Study mode: Full-time. Duration: One year. Start date: September 2026.

multiple_applications.content:
- Yes, you can apply for more than one course at King's. You may be required to pay multiple applications fees for each programme.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
After careful consideration, King’s has taken the decision **not to allow any deferrals for postgraduate taught courses from the 2025/26 or 2026/27 academic year to future academic years**. King’s says it will announce whether it will permit deferrals from the 2027/28 academic year nearer the time.
Standard deferral guidance includes:
- King’s is unable to defer conditional offers; **all conditions must be met before King’s can defer your place**.
- If funding or a scholarship has been awarded for a specific academic year, there is no guarantee that same funding will be available after deferral, and applicants may have to re-apply for the academic year in which they intend to join.
- If a visa is required, the CAS and visa are assigned to a specific start date and course; if the start date changes, applicants [may have to apply for a new CAS or visa in the year that they wish to study](https://www.kcl.ac.uk/campuslife/services/student-advice-support/how/international-student-support/index).
- If the programme start date is deferred, fee status could be affected, and the Admissions Office reserves the right to re-assess fee status for the deferred start date.
- English language tests are only eligible for two years; if a deferral would make the English language test out of date, King’s reserves the right to amend the offer to a conditional offer based on demonstrating current proficiency with a new test.
- If accommodation, disability or dyslexia support arrangements have been made, applicants may need to re-apply or update arrangements for the new start date.
- For military service deferrals, **a deferral of two academic years** will usually only be considered if an applicant is completing compulsory national or military service which exceeds 12 months. Applicants need to provide evidence that they will be undertaking compulsory service with their deferral request, and all requests should be made via [King’s Apply](https://apply.kcl.ac.uk/).

conditional_admission_policy.content:
- Check if you need to meet any offer conditions to confirm your place at King’s and the deadline to meet these conditions.
- If you are given an offer which requires you to meet a condition(s) before your place can be confirmed, you will need to send King’s a message on King’s Apply using the “Meeting Offer Conditions/Confirmation” message category with evidence that you have met your conditions **by the deadline stated in your offer letter**.
- If you have an academic condition, King’s will need your final transcripts/certificates. The documentation must confirm that you have been awarded your qualification and the grade you have received to be accepted. If this is not in English, you must provide an official translation with the original.
- If you have an English Language condition, King’s will not accept scores that do not meet the requirements and cannot accept a combination of scores from multiple tests. If you are undertaking a pre-sessional English language programme with King’s to meet an English language condition, you should still meet any academic condition by the deadline in your offer letter; King’s will wait for the results of the pre-sessional course.
- If you have not met your academic condition, send your final documents to King’s; they will consider your application before making a final decision on whether your place can be confirmed on the programme.
- Remember if you have conditions to meet on your offer you will need to provide evidence of meeting these and any other requirements before the enrolment process can begin. **Failure to meet the stated deadlines may result in you losing your place on the course.**

application_materials.content:
For PGT courses, you’ll provide a personal statement. It should share your motivation and enthusiasm for your chosen course and show your suitability for postgraduate study. Your statement should include examples of relevant work, voluntary or study experiences, and incorporate skills such as time management, project management, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. You should also cover successes and achievements relevant to the course, outline why you have chosen the course and Newcastle University, and explain how you will apply your current skills, knowledge and experience. You may also consider showing how the course fits into your career plans and ambitions.
You’ll need to include contact details for **two referees**. At least one referee should be able to comment on your academic ability. Newcastle will contact your referees to request references, usually at the same time as sending the conditional offer. If you already have a reference, you can attach it in the application portal; the reference must be **signed by your referee, dated and on official letterhead**.
Check the “How to Apply” tab on your course page to see what documents to include. The main documents the University requires for postgraduate programmes are:
- A transcript of your degree studies; if you are still studying, provide a current transcript of your degree studies to date.
- Certificates to confirm your degree or highest qualification, if your degree is complete.
- Evidence of your English language ability.
- A copy of your passport.
- A curriculum vitae.
- A Personal Statement.
- Any transcripts of marks or certified documents should be translated into English.
Before submitting your application, you must attach a copy of any mandatory documents including your degree transcript. When uploading documents, select “Supporting Documentation,” click “Upload Documents,” select the document type from the dropdown list, choose files, and click “Submit.” For transcripts, select whether the document is a “transcript” or a “translated transcript.”

program_overview.content:
Develop your career in the financial services, or as an analyst in investment banking and risk management fields. The financial services sector has grown worldwide, fuelling demand for suitably qualified graduates. With the Financial Analytics and Risk Management MSc, you will be ready to meet this demand. This programme strengthens your understanding of generalist finance issues and develops specialist practical skills in financial analytics and risk management. As a graduate, you'll be able to develop a career in the financial services sector. The course is also suitable for future analysts in economics and finance. This programme is delivered by the [Finance subject group](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/about/subject-groups/finance/).
The course provides the opportunity to develop relevant skills and a practical understanding of:
- the operation and behaviour of international financial markets
- the ability to analyse the strategies of financial market investors
- the role of finance in a modern economy
The course is modular. Depending on your modules, you'll be assessed through a combination of dissertation, essay, PC examination, portfolio, problem-solving exercises, report, written examination, and written exercise. Throughout your studies, you’ll have access to support from academic staff, academic advisers and research supervisors, the University Student Services Team, student representatives, and peers. You'll also be assigned an academic member of staff, who will be your academic adviser throughout your time with us.
Newcastle University Business School is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](http://www.aacsb.edu/), [European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS)](https://efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/), and [Association of MBAs (AMBA)](https://www.associationofmbas.com/about-us/). Only **1% of business schools worldwide** hold this triple crown. Newcastle University Business School is also recognised as an Academic Partner of the CQF Institute, the awarding body for the Certificate in Quantitative Finance (CQF). All students studying at the Business School are eligible to access member benefits.
You'll benefit from Newcastle University Business School’s status as a Bloomberg Experiential Learning Partner. Through self-study, you'll complete the Bloomberg Market Concepts certificate, which gives you an interactive introduction to the financial markets. You can take part in a live financial trading simulation delivered by a leading global provider of finance simulations, gaining insights into different roles in the financial industry and boosting your employability. You will get the chance to showcase your skills on the trading floor. You can also attend guest lectures that complement the study of theoretical frameworks and analyse recent trends in financial markets and banking industries.
Newcastle University Business School is an academic partner of the **CQF Institute**. You can register for free membership and access member-only benefits, including online technical talks and conferences, networking opportunities, career advice, thought leadership, and finance-focused introductory workshops.
The new Dual Award programme allows you to spend an additional academic year at Grenoble École de Management in Grenoble, France. After completing your postgraduate studies at Newcastle, you would join the last year of their Grande École programme, Masters in Management - M2 year. On successful completion, you will be awarded your Newcastle University degree and an MSc in Management from Grenoble. The Postgraduate Semester Abroad is an opportunity to study a complementary subject for one semester at a European partner university at the end of your studies, once you have submitted your dissertation/final project.

Graduates from this course will be able to undertake various roles, including financial trader, financial analyst, risk analyst, engineer on economic modelling, investor relations adviser, economist, and auditor. This course prepares you for a wide range of careers with employers such as HSBC Bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Normura, Tiburon Partners LLP, PwC, KPMG, and State Oil Company of Azerbaijan Republic.
Career development and employability are woven throughout teaching, learning and student experience. The School has dedicated employability support and career spaces to support you during your studies and for up to three years after graduation. Business School students get access to both the wider University careers service and exclusive Business School events and resources, including one-to-one career support, industry-specific career events, online career learning tools, career planning and information sessions, an annual careers week, networking opportunities, specialist careers and business start-up support, and the chance to apply for various work experience opportunities while studying.
Newcastle University Business School has over 4,000 students from over 85 countries. Its community includes regional, national and international leaders, over 37,000 alumni in 152 countries, leading professionals and academics, and businesses and partners in academia. The Business School is the gateway to [Newcastle Helix](https://newcastlehelix.com/home), a landmark 24 acre hybrid city quarter. Facilities include computer clusters, lecture theatres, seminar and teaching spaces, a dedicated Student Hub and Quiet Space, employability support and event hubs, a Bloomberg lab with over 20 terminals, and the Experimental and Behavioural Economics Lab.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
There are two types of offer: unconditional and conditional.
- **Conditional offer:** “You’ll receive a conditional offer if there are conditions that you need to meet before you can start your course.” The conditions are in the “Terms and Conditions of your Offer” section of the offer document and can also be viewed in the application portal.
- To evidence that conditions have been met, applicants must upload supporting documents to the application portal. If still studying, upload documents as soon as they are available. If supporting documents are not in English, certified English language translations must be provided.
- “When your documents demonstrate that you’ve met your offer conditions, your offer will become unconditional.” If an applicant has “just missed the conditions” of the offer, they are encouraged to upload results anyway; Newcastle will review the application and “may still be able to give you a place on your chosen course.”
- Types of condition include academic conditions, such as “a transcript of your degree studies” and “your degree certificate or a certified copy”; references; and English language conditions.
- English language conditions can be met by taking an [international language test](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/international/language/#overview) such as IELTS, TOEFL, or Pearsons, or by completing one of Newcastle’s six- or ten-week English language courses at the [International Study Centre](https://nclisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english).
- When applicants have accepted the offer and met any conditions, Newcastle sends a Confirmation of a Place (COP), which is “formal confirmation of your acceptance of the unconditional offer.”

program_overview.content:
The MSc Financial Analytics is for students with an interest in financial markets or financial technology (FinTech) who enjoy working with data. It shows how data science, analytics, statistics and programming tools are used in the real world for the analysis and modelling of financial and economic data. The programme equips students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational techniques utilised by industry leading firms, bridging the gap between complex quantitative models and financial decision making by developing dual skillsets in both finance and data analysis.
Attendance is 1 year full-time, and the course location is Queen's Business School. The degree can lead to careers in areas such as financial data science, trading, software development, portfolio management, consulting, data analytics, risk management, business analytics and academia.
Queen’s University is ranked third in the UK for Graduate Prospects in Accounting and Finance (Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2024).
Professional accreditations and partnerships:
- The programme has been accepted into the CFA Institute University Recognition Program and aligns with the Candidate Body of Knowledge (CBOK), the core knowledge, skills, and abilities generally accepted and applied by investment professionals worldwide.
- Queen’s Business School is an academic partner of the Certificate in Quantitative Finance (CQF) Institute. Through this partnership, MSc Financial Analytics students benefit from access to CQF Institute resources including industry talks and workshops, research, networking opportunities and career tools.
Facilities and student experience:
- Many classes are held in the state-of-the-art FinTrU Trading Room, which provides access to Bloomberg software used by many leading financial institutions worldwide.
- Students also have exposure to S&P Capital IQ and learn in-demand programming and data science skills such as Python, R, SQL, Hadoop, Spark, Google Cloud, and Posit Workbench, an Azure-based enterprise grade data science platform.
- Students are strongly encouraged to join the Student Managed Fund, where they have an opportunity to manage real money.
Course structure:
- This degree equips students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational techniques used by leading finance and FinTech firms and prepares them for careers in quantitative finance, trading, portfolio management, data analytics or risk management.
- Students learn how data science, business analytics, programming and statistical tools are used for the analysis and modelling of complex financial data.
- In Semester 3, students complete either an Academic Dissertation, described as a thesis-based research project motivated by contemporary quantitative academic research with supervision from an academic expert in the chosen area, or an Applied Research Project, an industry-focused module with a taught component at the start of the summer and a final report in the form of an in-depth equity analyst report of a CFA standard.
People teaching you:
- [Dr Fearghal Kearney](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/fearghal-kearney), Programme Director, Finance. Email: F.Kearney@qub.ac.uk
Learning and teaching:
- The programme equips students with cutting-edge quantitative and computational analytical skills demanded by leading firms worldwide and prepares them for future careers in quantitative finance, trading, more general finance, FinTech and business consulting environments.
- The course bridges the gap between quantitative models and financial decision-making, with many modules focusing on learning through simulation.
Career prospects:
- This programme equips students with quantitative and computational techniques and strategies used by leading finance and financial technology firms.
- Full-service finance and business consulting firms employ Financial Analytics professionals, as do boutique firms such as asset managers and hedge funds. IT software organisations are also attracted to graduates from this programme because of their specialism at the interface between computing, data analytics and finance.
- Graduate prospects from the MSc Financial Analytics are described as excellent; Queen’s was ranked first in the UK for Graduate Prospects in Accounting and Finance (Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2023).
- Graduates have secured roles with employers such as Citi, Deutsche Bank, Bank of China, Davy Group, Citco, Amazon, FD Technologies, Data Intellect and many others.
- Typical roles include data scientists, financial engineers, software developers, equity analysts, consultants, portfolio analysts, risk analysts, business analysts, and traders.

program_overview.content:
The MSc in Geographic Data Science and Spatial Analytics focuses on using data and analytics to improve cities and solve spatial problems. Students learn to utilise cutting-edge tools and methods from the data science domain to analyse spatial data and tackle challenges across spatial scales, from neighbourhoods and cities to regions and supra-national systems.
The programme is designed for students from backgrounds in Geography, Planning, Social Sciences more broadly, or numerate subjects such as Computer Science and Engineering. It welcomes students seeking to master data science and machine-learning algorithms, GeoAI tools, and data infrastructures, and apply them to core theories and concepts in social and environmental sciences. Students will employ cartographic and geographic theory and concepts to map and model big geographic data, understand engineering principles around scientific computing and GeoAI, and use them to help tackle global challenges across disciplines.
The MSc builds upon the Quantitative Spatial Science (QuSS) research group within the [School of Geographical Sciences](http://www.bristol.ac.uk/geography/) and its longstanding history and excellence in quantitative geography and spatial analysis. Students join a School ranked **first** in the UK for 'Geography and Environmental Studies' research (_Times Higher Education_ analysis of REF 2021), with weekly seminars organised by the School’s academic research groups, invited speakers, specialist workshops, reading groups, and postgraduate social events.
Key programme details:
- Programme duration: One year full-time; Two years part-time. Part-time study requires daytime weekday attendance.
- Delivery method: On-Campus.
- Location: [Clifton campus](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/study/clifton-campus/).
- Award available: MSc.
The programme structure follows the data science workflow from data collection and access to data analysis and visualisation. It teaches core skills and knowledge of AI methods, machine learning models, and geographic theories, with a focus on geospatial applications including city science, policymaking, and environmental management. It aims to train the next generation of geographic data scientists who can responsibly use and develop a wide range of methods and tools to tackle pressing societal and environmental challenges. [Visit our programme catalogue](https://www.bris.ac.uk/unit-programme-catalogue/RouteStructure.jsa?ayrCode=26%2F27&byCohort=N&programmeCode=2GEOG002T) for full details of the structure and unit content.
Career prospects: This MSc provides graduates with the skills needed for successful careers as data scientists and data consultants in the private and public sectors. Students have gone on to work in consultancy and in technology and engineering companies, as well as governmental and third sector/non-profit organisations. Many graduates continue in research institutes and think-tanks or pursue further study through a PhD.

program_overview.content:
Global Healthcare Management (Analytics) MSc is taught in London, Stratford at UCL East. Study modes are full-time, part-time, and flexible, with durations of 1 calendar year, 2 calendar years, and 5 calendar years respectively.
A course with tangible real-world value, the Global Healthcare Management (Analytics) MSc is a degree that has been co-created by academics and industry experts. It equips students with essential skills and connections to change the world in healthcare through opportunities to specialise in analytics.
Taught at the world’s first business school dedicated to health in a global top 10 university (QS World University Rankings 2026), this course offers an opportunity to learn from the sector while gaining valuable and in-demand skills. Equipping students with a critical foundation in the theories, principles and practices underpinning healthcare management, the Global Healthcare Management MSc empowers future healthcare managers and leaders with knowledge. Learning about global differences and interconnections, quality improvement, patient safety and workforce management are also fundamentals on this course. A group business project ensures that problem-solving and innovation in the healthcare context are qualities instilled in all students.
This course is taught from UCL’s state-of-the-art bespoke facilities on the [UCL East campus](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/ucl-east/), on the Queen Elizabeth Olympic Park in east London. The UCL Global Business School for Health is situated in the Marshgate building with access to hi-tech teaching areas and collaboration spaces, a library, and a refectory.
The course is ideal for individuals who strive to become excellent managers and changemakers within healthcare settings. Applicants may be new or recent graduates in a health, science or business field, or have relevant work experience in healthcare. For the analytics specialism, UCL additionally encourages an interest and aptitude in engaging with quantitative data to support healthcare management.
Graduates of the Global Healthcare Management MSc with a specialist route in analytics can expect to gain a wide-ranging understanding of healthcare management; skills in data analytics to support healthcare management; the ability to analyse statistical data, technological and information sources to support healthcare management decisions; significant research and analytical skills for data-driven healthcare management; communication skills for healthcare managers and leaders; expertise to assess value for patients, organisations and society; the ability to manage and lead a diverse workforce; and experience in teamwork, collaboration, innovation and continuous professional development.
Graduates are likely to pursue careers with private, non-profit and multinational organisations in the policy or analytics space. Recent graduate destinations include PhD study, including securing scholarship opportunities, and data analytics at AstraZeneca. Paths after the course include public, private or non-governmental organisations in health and healthcare, healthcare specialisms in professional services, and government and public bodies.
Teaching is primarily through face-to-face lectures and seminars/tutorials across Terms 1 and 2, with weekly group seminars, case-based presentations and discussions, and project development workshops. In Term 3, students undertake a business project with colleagues, drawing on interaction with an industry mentor and project supervisor, and complete an individual desk-based research project under the mentorship of a research supervisor. Assessment includes written exams, coursework essays, presentations, a business project, a research project, and health and business case written analysis.
The analytics route develops breadth and depth of understanding of global healthcare management challenges and opportunities in the digital age. Students gain an advanced understanding of the role of data applied to business and management for healthcare and focus on applying these tools within the global health landscape. All students complete two projects: a group business project developing an idea for a healthcare improvement from concept to business case report and presentation, and a research project critically examining an aspect or question related to analytics learning. Students undertake modules to the value of 180 credits; upon successful completion of 180 credits, they are awarded an MSc in Global Healthcare Management (Analytics).

curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time, Part-time, Flexible. Duration: 1 calendar year, 2 calendar years, 5 calendar years. The course is taught at UCL East in London, Stratford.
Module teaching is primarily in the form of face-to-face lectures and seminars/tutorials across Terms 1 and 2. In Term 3, students embark on the business project and finish the individual desk-based research project. Full-time students can expect 15 to 18 hours per week in Terms 1 and 2 in face-to-face teaching sessions, plus 17 to 20 hours per week in self-directed study. Part-time and flexible students study at a pro-rata rate.
Full-time: The Global Healthcare Management MSc course with an analytics route offers breadth and depth of understanding of global healthcare management challenges and opportunities in this digital age. On the analytics route, students gain an advanced understanding of the role of data applied to business and management for healthcare and focus on the application of these tools within the global health landscape, as well as further develop analytic skills.
All students complete two projects:
- A group business project involving developing an idea for a healthcare improvement from concept to business case report and presentation.
- A research project where students work on a research paper that critically examines an aspect or question related to the selected route, analytics.
Part-time: The two-year part-time structure consists of 180 credits. Students take 90 credits in Year 1 and Year 2.
Flexible: The modular/flexible structure gives students the flexibility to take 180 credits worth of modules over three-five years. Students can choose as many or as few modules as they wish each year.
Compulsory modules:

Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of **180 credits**, students will be awarded an MSc in Global Healthcare Management (Analytics).

deferral_admission_policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer, except in limited exceptional circumstances. Deferral requests will be considered only for: serious illness of the offer holder or serious illness/death of a parent, guardian, partner or child; parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months; being directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster; being awarded a UCL scholarship or a full scholarship from a recognised funding body for study in the following academic year; or holding an offer to study the UCL International Pre-Masters.
- To be eligible for a deferral, you must hold an **unconditional offer which you have accepted**. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt, if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme.
- Deferral requests must be made on the offer page of the application portal. Requests due to illness or parental/adoption leave require a letter from a relevant medical practitioner; scholarship-based requests require an official scholarship award letter. UCL may request more information before making a final decision.
- **An application cannot be deferred twice.** Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
- The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
- If a deferral request is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment. A new offer letter will be issued, and a new English test may be required if the current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.
- If the deferral request is unsuccessful, or if you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the listed categories, you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, but the application will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.

conditional_admission_policy.content:

- If you have not met your English language test condition but have received scores that meet the UCL level 1 requirement, you can still supply your test scores to UCL for review. UCL will not ordinarily accept a lower score than stipulated in the offer and cannot consider test scores that do not meet the UCL level 1 requirement.

program_overview.content:
Develop a skillset in Statistics, Machine Learning, and Artificial Intelligence to fully exploit complex health data and perform rigorous big data analyses. Analyse and integrate complex and high-dimensional blocks of health data with cutting-edge quantitative methods. Apply your knowledge to extended real-world large scale research projects supervised by leading academics and industry experts.
- Qualification: MSc
- Duration: 1 year
- Start date: September 2026
- Study mode: Full-time
- Delivered by: [School of Public Health](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/medicine/departments/school-public-health/)
- Location: Hammersmith; White City
Broaden your expertise in analysing health data in this Master's course. You will gain expertise in developing, applying and interpreting results from cutting-edge statistical, machine learning, and artificial intelligence approaches for analysing and integrating complex sets of data that are emerging in the health field.
The course is delivered by international experts. They leverage their extensive experience to design materials which better equip you to handle the complexity of real-world health data. Lectures provide rigorous and accessible theoretical background to the advanced methodology. Each lecture is paired with a hands-on session which applies the theoretic concepts to real-world data. This strong technical component will prepare you for a career in health data sciences.
You will apply the cutting-edge skills you gain to unexplored scientific questions with potential real-world impact. Through closely supervised individual and group projects, you will learn how to perform rigorous research to international publication standard. You will be integrated into a world-leading academic or industrial research team for your final project. This capstone project will give you demonstrable experience applying the comprehensive skillset from the course in a role as a data expert.
The course structure includes core modules and a research project. You’ll carry out an extensive individual research project during the third term (4 months full-time research). During this project, you’ll apply advanced techniques you have been taught to real data sets. You’ll be supervised through the process of conceiving, delivering and assessing a high standard scientific publication, with your work assessed by a paper-style report and oral examination.
Teaching and learning methods include lectures and practicals, seminars and technical tutorials, small group tutorials, group work, computing-based practicals, research projects, presentations and peer evaluations, and a virtual learning environment.
You will acquire in-demand hard skills including coding, data analysis, machine learning, and AI, as well as soft skills including problem-solving, communication, teamwork, and the ability to learn and adapt. You will gain a specific skillset relevant to fast-growing industries such as Data Science, Healthcare, Pharmaceutical, Medicine, Life Science and Biotech, and a transferrable skillset in demand in industries such as Finance, Retail, and Energy. The course highlights local employment opportunities in London, described as the leading biotech capital of Europe with over 400 companies and research institutions generating over £11B in revenue.
Course Directors: [Professor Marc Chadeau-Hyam](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/m.chadeau) and [Dr Sabrina Andrade Rodrigues](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/people/s.andrade-rodrigues).

Research project: You’ll carry out an extensive individual research project during the third term (**4 months full-time research**). financial_aid.content:
Applications for the School of Public Health scholarships close at **23:59 (BST) on Thursday 30 April 2026** for 2026 entry.
- **The School of Public Health offers a number of scholarships for our postgraduate taught programmes.** For on-campus programmes, including **MSc in Health Data Analytics and Machine Learning**, the scholarship will cover the tuition fees only equal to the cost of a home student.
- **Overseas (including EU) students can be awarded scholarships but will be required to cover the remaining balance of their tuition fees.**
- There are a total of five scholarships for 2025/26 entry, including **one** for the **MSc in Health Data Analytics and Machine Learning**.
- Applications for the School of Public Health scholarships need to be made by a [separate form](https://imperial.eu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a8BBZRchfOfLxY2), in addition to the full application for admission for the relevant programme of study. Applicants need to have been made an offer for a School of Public Health programme for 2026/27 entry in order to be considered for a scholarship for the same year of entry.
- Applications are invited from candidates from the UK, the EU, Overseas and current Imperial College London students who have the potential to become leaders in their field.
- These awards are open to all students who make an application to the School of Public Health by the deadline for admission to study for a Master's programme, starting in October 2026. These awards can only be given to students who are studying a programme run by the School of Public Health.
- Applications are accepted from talented candidates from across the world for the School of Public Health Scholarships which will cover home tuition fees only.
- The application form will ask applicants to outline why they are in 'need' of the scholarship, including: financial income and family situation; interest and motivation; achievements and awards; and benefits of scholarship.
- Candidates will need to have applied for their programme of choice and be assessed for entry, in line with entry requirements. As part of the scholarship review process, programme teams will review academic potential, personal statement, research experience and publications, and references.
- To be considered for a scholarship, candidates must apply for a place on a Masters programme run by the School of Public Health and complete the School of Public Health's Scholarships [online application form](https://imperial.eu.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_a8BBZRchfOfLxY2). Candidates who do not apply through the online scholarship form will not be considered.
- **Scholarship decisions will be communicated in June 2026.**
- Both part-time and full-time students are eligible to apply. Home/EU and Overseas/Islands applicants are eligible to apply. However, scholarship funds cover the amount of Home/EU tuition fees only for any successful awardee and applicants would be required to pay the difference towards any remaining fees.
- Imperial policy dictates that students can only hold multiple awards if one is for fees and the other is a stipend. As the School of Public Health Master's Scholarships provide an award for fees, recipients would be permitted to also hold an award for a stipend, but will not be permitted to hold more than one full scholarship.
- Applicants are welcome to apply for other types of funding from Imperial while applying for a School of Public Health Masters Scholarship. However, these scholarships cannot be combined with any other scholarship that covers fees.
