program_overview.content:
The NUS MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics is designed to equip the next generation of Human Capital Management leaders with future-ready human capital management skills and competencies. This programme is available both Full-Time and Part-Time.
This master’s degree is designed to equip recent graduates with future-ready human capital management skills and competencies. With significant developments in various human resources (HR) areas over the past 20 years, the HR function will demand talents with new and improved proficiencies, particularly in data analytics. The NUS Business School curriculum will combine functional human capital management capabilities with an analytical perspective, to help you transform data into actionable insights and develop suitable changes in the workplace.
The field of Human Capital Management is at a pivotal time in history. Organizations around the globe are navigating unprecedented challenges and opportunities: technological advancements, shifting employee expectations, the rise of data-driven decision-making, and increasing diversity. This program will help you harness analytics to drive strategic decisions, foster environments where people thrive, and ensure that organizations are equipped to meet the demands of a dynamic world.
**Emily M. David** is Academic Director, MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics.
**Industries our graduates work in**
By Industry, graduates are hired across a wide range of industries such as:
- Banking & Financial Services
- Consulting & Market Research
- Consumer Goods
- Engineering & Manufacturing
- Distribution, Logistics & Supply Chain
- Public Sector
- Information Communications & Technology
By Job Function, graduates are involved in job functions such as:
- Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP)
- Regional Talent Acquisition Analytics Specialist
- Global HR Product Manager
- Human Capital Consultant
- Organizational Development Specialist
- People Analytics Specialist

curriculum.content:
**12 Months. 44 Units.** The [MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics](https://mschcma.nus.edu.sg/) programme is delivered intensively over **12 months** that includes an experiential learning component. Students are expected to complete **44 Units** to graduate. Please [click here](https://www.nus.edu.sg/registrar/calendar) for the NUS Academic Calendar.
| First Semester | Special Terms | Second Semester |
|---|---|---|
| Jan - Apr | May - Jul | Aug - Nov |
| 6 Courses (20 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units)* | 7 Courses (20 Units) |
*Alternatively, students can also do their experiential learning **after their second semester between JAN - APR**.
Courses are structured over 12 months. Full Course = 4 units (3 hours/week, 13 weeks duration); 2 units (3 hours/week 6-7 weeks duration).
- Artificial Intelligence for HR (4 Units)
- Communication for HR Professionals (2 Units)
- HR technology (2 Units)
- People Analytics (4 Units)
- Quantitative Methods for HR (4 Units)
- Talent Management (4 Units)
- Experiential Learning (4 Units): through an individual industry internship, faculty research project or a HR consultancy project. These internships and applied projects are primarily self-sourced.
- Compensation and Performance Management (4 Units)
- Ethics in Human Resource (2 Units)
- HR as Strategic Partner for Growth and Transformation (2 Units)
- Labour and Employment Law (2 Units)
- Leading and Managing Difficult Employees (2 Units)
- Negotiation and Dispute Resolution (4 Units)
- Talent Assessment & Selection (4 Units)
*The curriculum is subject to changes. The University reserves the right to revise the curriculum.
To graduate from the NUS MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics programme, students must complete the programme requirements and achieve a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least **3.2 (out of 5.0)**.

program_overview.content:
The new concentration in Human Resource Analytics and Digital Transformation is designed to prepare students for a rapidly changing business landscape, where data-driven decision-making and technological expertise are critical. This concentration ensures that graduates possess a strong understanding of HR theories and practices in both local and global contexts, enabling them to leverage advanced analytics and AI to improve organisational effectiveness.
**Aims**
- **Data-Driven Decision Making** - Equip students with the skills to make strategic decisions using HR analytics and digital transformation tools, enhancing organizational efficiency and HR management practices.
- **HR Technological Proficiency** - Develop students’ expertise in HR technologies, including AI, machine learning, and HRIS, ensuring their ability to effectively integrate these technologies across various HR functions.
- **Analytical and Strategic Application in People Management** - Empower students to apply organisational behaviour (OB) concepts to analyze HR data, predict employee behavior, and align HR strategies with broader organizational goals
- **Ethical and Innovative Practices** - Foster the ability to evaluate and implement HR strategies that are ethical, socially responsible, and innovative, particularly in the context of digital transformation and data privacy.
- **Professional Development** - Prepare students for leadership roles in HR analytics and digital transformation by providing hands-on experience, industry-relevant skills, and opportunities for internships and placements, thereby enhancing their employability.
On completing the Programme with new HRADT concentration, students will be able to explain the evolving role of digital transformation in HR management and its implications for HR policies, planning, and practices, including the integration of AI-driven innovations and data analytics; apply data-driven decision-making skills and digital tools to manage and develop people effectively in dynamic environments; demonstrate critical and innovative thinking in solving complex HR problems using AI, big data, and digital transformation strategies; utilise organisational behaviour concepts and advanced HR analytics to identify, analyse, and resolve people management issues; evaluate ethical and legal frameworks related to data privacy, diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) in HR; and develop and communicate effective HR strategies that align with organisational goals, integrate advanced technologies, and demonstrate the strategic value of HR through data-driven insights and presentations.

program_overview.content:
**Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics (MSc)** is a **Master of Science** course at the University of Southampton, starting **September 2026**. It is a **full-time**, **1 year** course based at **Highfield** and awarded by the University of Southampton.
Gain the expertise to manage the movement of goods, people, data or money across a supply chain on this master’s degree course. You’ll develop advanced management and analytical skills, and have the chance to work on a real business project during a 3-month industry placement. You’ll be taught by academics from one of the country’s leading analytics research groups, and graduate with the skills and knowledge for a successful career in logistics.
On this MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics degree, you'll learn advanced management skills and the ability to use data to make good business decisions. You'll gain a thorough grounding in:
- integrated and international logistics supply chain management
- software and programming skills
- quantitative, qualitative and technical skills
You'll graduate from the course knowing how to:
- formulate a hypothesis and use data to test it
- use analytical techniques to support decision making
- develop computer-based decision support systems to gain insight from data
The course is taught in association with the University's cross-disciplinary [Centre of Operational Research, Management Sciences and Information Systems](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/cormsis/about/index.page) (CORMSIS), one of the largest groups of its kind in the UK. This means you'll benefit from a wider choice of optional modules which you can use to pursue your own interests or career plans. You can choose to specialise in the following aspects of logistics and supply chain management:
- Operational Research
- Risk Management
- Finance
- Sustainability
This is full-time master’s course. Your studies will last a full 12 months. For the first 8 months (semesters 1 and 2) you'll focus on the taught part of your course. Each semester is made up of a combination of modules that everyone on the course takes, and modules that we’ll ask you to choose from a list of options. For the remainder of the course, you’ll work independently on your dissertation. You’ll have one-to-one meetings with your supervisor during this time to discuss your progress.
You’ll carry out a research project resulting in a 15,000-word dissertation, on a subject of your choice (to be agreed with your supervisor). The project is a chance for you to develop your research skills and show in-depth knowledge of your chosen subject. You might have the chance to complete your project as a 3-month summer placement with an external organisation. We place more than 50 students in external projects every year.
Your course leader is [Dr Fangsheng Ge](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5zbxnh/doctor-fangsheng-ge), Lecturer in Management Science.
Accreditation: [**Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)**](https://www.aacsb.edu/).
Graduates commonly work in a range of organisations or sectors including: Airlines, Department of Transport, Education, Government Organisations, National Air Traffic Services, NHS, Royal Mail, Private companies, Third sector organisations.
Careers directly related to this course include:
- Inventory and warehouse manager
- Logistics engineer
- Logistics planner
- Supply chain analyst
- Supply chain manager
- Supplier relationship manager
- Vehicle fleet manager
- Vehicle route planner
Example job titles of Southampton MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics graduates include Researcher, Management trainee, Business analyst, Data analyst, IT consultant, Logistics manager, Supply chain coordinator, Supply manager, Purchasing manager, and Management consultant.
Job prospects for MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Analytics graduates: **£33k Average professional salary**, **81% In a skilled profession or further study**, **95% Graduate employment rate**. Source: Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about the activities and perspectives of graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

program_overview.content:
Machine Learning for Visual Data Analytics MSc is part of AI, Computer and Data Science. As recent developments in computers and sensors make the generation, storage and processing of visual data easier, methods that enable a machine to analyse and understand images and videos become increasingly relevant. This programme is designed to train engineers to work in the analysis and interpretation of images and video.
- Undertake high-level training in programming languages, tools and methods necessary for the design and implementation of practical computer vision systems.
- Be taught by world-class researchers in the fields of multimedia analysis, vision-based surveillance, structure from motion and human motion analysis.
- Work on cutting-edge research projects, gaining hands-on experience.
- Study options include full-time September 2026 | 1 year, part-time September 2026 | 2 years, and full-time September 2027 | 1 year. Location: Mile End.
This course will enable students to study cutting-edge technologies in the field of machine learning for visual analytics, and will provide them with the background and skills they need to pursue careers in research or industry. Course content covers fundamental methods and techniques in computer vision, machine learning and image processing; programming tools, languages and techniques for the application of machine learning methods to analyse visual data; and methods and techniques for systems and applications.
The programme is taught by academics from the Computer Vision and Multimedia and Vision research groups. The groups consist of a team of more than 100 researchers (academics, post-docs, research fellows and PhD students) performing world-leading research into the fields of surveillance, face and gesture recognition, multimedia indexing and retrieval and robotics. The School has collaborations, partnerships, industrial placement schemes and public engagement programmes with organisations including Vodafone, Google, IBM, BT, NASA, BBC and Microsoft.
This degree is accredited by [BCS](https://heaccreditation.bcs.org/), The Chartered Institute for IT, for the purposes of partially meeting the academic requirement for registration as a Chartered IT Professional. This degree is also accredited by [BCS](https://heaccreditation.bcs.org/) on behalf of the [Engineering Council](https://www.engc.org.uk/education-skills/course-search/recognised-course-search/), for the purposes of partially meeting the academic requirement for registration as a Chartered Engineer.
Structure:
- Eight modules divided into two streams; students choose **one** stream to follow once they start in September.
- Compulsory final project module (60 credits).
- Streams include Vision and Language, and Computer Vision and Image Processing. These streams will allow you to further develop your professional profile and graduate with industry-relevant expertise.
Assessment:
- 67% Modules
- 33% Research project
- Modules are assessed through a combination of coursework and written examinations. You will also be assessed through your final research project.
You will devise and carry out a major final project, which you may do in collaboration with an industrial partner. Examples of past project topics include automatic road segmentation, sponsored by Yamaha Motors Ltd.; 3D face reconstruction from a few images; and sentiment analysis in images.
Students of this course can expect to take part in lectures, in which the theory and algorithms are presented, and practical sessions and labs, where they can get hands-on experience with tools and algorithms. Each module provides contact time with your lecturers, supported by lab work and self-directed further study. You will be assigned an Academic Advisor who will guide you in both academic and pastoral matters throughout your time at Queen Mary. Part-time study options often mean that the number of modules taken is reduced per semester, with the full modules required to complete the programme spread over two academic years.
Faculty include [Professor Shaogang Gong](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/gongshaogang.html), Professor of Visual Computation, whose research focuses on object recognition, action and behaviour recognition, and video analysis; [Dr Miles Hansard](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/hansardmiles.html), whose research interests cover statistical scene and image models, depth-cameras and multi-view scene reconstruction, binocular vision, eye-movements and 3D displays; [Professor Ioannis Patras](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/patrasioannis.html), Professor of Computer Vision and Human Sensing, whose research focuses on analysis of human behaviour, emotions and cognitive states from images, video and their neurophysiological signals; [Professor Massimo Poesio](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/poesiomassimo.html), Professor of Computational Linguistics; [Dr Paulo Rauber](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/rauberpaulo.html), Lecturer in Artificial Intelligence; and [Dr Fabrizio Smeraldi](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/people/profiles/smeraldifabrizio.html), Senior Lecturer in Artificial Intelligence.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s main [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital. The School has bespoke facilities including the newly refurbished [Informatics Laboratory (ITL)](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/eecs/about-us/facilities/informatics-teaching-laboratory---itl--facilities/), transformed through a £20 million investment; Augmented human interaction (AHI) laboratory; Antenna measurement laboratory; qMedia and arts technology studios; Robotics laboratory (ARQspace); and Dedicated Postgraduate Teaching Facilities.
Career paths: skills and knowledge in intelligent image and video processing are valuable across industries including multimedia indexing and retrieval, motion capture, media production, medical imaging, security and defense, and robotics. Expertise in machine learning, signal processing, and programming is highly sought after in various other industries. Many faculty members collaborate on research projects with industry partners, including Disney, BBC, Technicolor, and STMicroelectronics, and also engage in consultancy work. You will be well-prepared to pursue further research or PhD studies. **100%** in highly skilled jobs 15 months after graduation.

program_overview.content:
The CEMS Master in International Management (MIM) is a strategic global alliance of [leading business schools](https://www.cems.org/academic-members/school-list), [multinational companies](https://www.cems.org/corporate-social-partners/cems-corporate-partners) and [non-governmental organisations](https://www.cems.org/corporate-social-partners/cems-social-partners) coming together to offer a unique pre-experience master’s programme. As a proud member of this alliance, NUS Business School provides our students exceptional international opportunities. This highly-ranked, global, one-year, pre-experience MIM programme emphasises and develops management and leadership competencies with an emphasis on internationalism and responsible leadership.
**Programme benefits**
- **Global Exposure:** Study across **two world-class institutions** with a mandatory international internship and exclusive global skill seminars.
- **Dual Qualification:** Specialise in Marketing Analytics & International Management.
- **Elite Network:** Join a selective community of high-achieving graduates across **33 countries** with lifelong access to the CEMS alumni network.
- **Corporate Connections:** Engage directly with **multinational corporate partners** through exclusive recruitment events, business projects and mentorship opportunities.
| Year 1 | Year 2 |
| --- | --- |
| Semester 1: Aug – Dec, 5 MSc in Marketing Courses (20 Units)* | Semester 1: Aug – Dec, CEMS Block Seminar (3 ECTS), CEMS Compulsory Course: Global Strategy (6 ECTS), 3 Courses (18 ECTS)**, Skills Seminar |
| Semester 2: Jan – May, 4 MSc in Marketing Courses (16 Units)* | Semester 2: Jan – May, CEMS Compulsory Course: Global Leadership (6 ECTS), CEMS MIM Course (6 ECTS), CEMS Business Project (15 ECTS), Skills Seminar, CEMS Global Citizenship Seminar (1 ECTS) |
| Special Term: May – Jul, Credit-bearing Internship (MAI and CEMS Requirement) (4 units) | |
| NUS | CEMS Partner University / NUS |
| **Total: NUS MSc in MAI (40 Units) + CEMS MIM (66 ECTS) + Internship** | |
* 2 [MAI courses](https://mscmarketing.nus.edu.sg/academics/) (8 units/12 ECTS) will be used to map to meet CEMS Requirement. At NUS, the workload of each course is expressed in terms of Units. The European equivalent of workload representation is ECTS credits. A typical course consists of 4 Units (or 6 ECTS), representing about 10 hours of work per week.
**What CEMS MIM Offers**
- **International Exchange Programme:** You are required to spend one term at a CEMS partner school. Destination for the term abroad will depend on availability. Location and sequence preferences will be taken into consideration, but those with better academic standing (including good GMAT scores) may stand a higher chance of getting their preferred placement.
- **Block Seminar:** You will begin the CEMS MIM term with a mandatory intensive one-week Block Seminar that is an ideal start to the programme as it facilitates discussion of management topics from different cultural and academic perspectives.
- **Unique Global Courses:** You will have to successfully complete exclusive CEMS courses such as Global Strategy, Global Leadership and Global Citizenship. The Global Citizenship Seminar is a two-day course that brings together representatives from corporate and / or social partners, professors and students to have the opportunity to engage with the UN Sustainable Development Goals through experiential learning.
- **Skills Seminars:** These shorter seminars provide training on a wide variety of essential and practical skills for an effective professional career. They are held throughout the two terms and are often in cooperation with corporate organisations.
- **CEMS Business Project:** Adopting a consultancy-like approach, you will work in small teams and apply your skills and knowledge to solve a real business problem for an international organisation. Your student team will work independently and will be supervised and evaluated by both your faculty advisor and the corporate representatives. The Business Project will amount to about half of Semester 2’s workload.
- **International Internship:** The objective of this internship is to turn academic and theoretical knowledge into a professional and multi-cultural experience. Your internship can take place at a CEMS Corporate Partner, an international company, or a non-profit organisation, as long as the company operates in an international environment, and your work responsibilities correspond to that of a new graduate hire.
- **Global Network:** As part of the CEMS network, you will have the opportunity to interact with a truly international team, benefiting from the great diversity of your peers, our professors, and our alumni.

- **Achievers**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have achievements in activities outside of the classroom, e.g. promoting or contributing to the UN SDGs; community service in social, environment, or other sectors; entrepreneurship, etc.
- **Local Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are Singaporeans or Singapore PRs.
- **ASEAN Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are nationals of an ASEAN country.
- **NUS Alumni**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are NUS Alumni.

**12 Months. 40 Units.** This applies to students enrolled in the single-degree [MSc in Marketing Analytics and Insights programme](https://mscmarketing.nus.edu.sg/). The programme is structured over 12 to 15 months, and students learn from distinguished faculty members with recognised expertise in their fields, alongside peers and colleagues from diverse cultures and backgrounds.
| Orientation Week | 1st Semester | 2nd Semester | 3rd Semester |
| :-: | :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Early August | Aug – Nov | Jan – Apr | May – Jul or Aug – Nov |
| 1 Course (0 Units): Principles of Marketing | 3 Core Courses (12 Units); 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | 2 Core Courses (8 Units); 2 Elective Courses (8 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units) |
Students need to take a total of four elective courses, totalling 16 units. The Experiential Learning component can be completed in Special Terms 1 and 2 (May to July) or Semester 1 (August to November) of each Academic Year. Students complete one out of two options: an Industry Internship or a Marketing Analytics Consultancy Project. Through the internship, students engage in experiential learning by analysing and solving problems faced by peers working in marketing and analytics functions in various industries. Through the Marketing Analytics Consultancy Project, students work in groups to analyse and solve marketing- and analytics-related problems faced by actual companies, resulting in a comprehensive, in-depth business proposal or solution.
Alumni comments describe the programme as covering key topics from programming and branding to consumer behaviour, providing in-depth practical skills, opportunities to work with real businesses on genuine problems, and preparation for a career in APAC through studying in Singapore. program_overview.content:
**Marketing Analytics (MSc)** is a **Master of Science** course starting **September 2026** for **1 year**. It is a **full-time** course based at **Highfield** and awarded by the **University of Southampton**.
With the marketing analytics MSc, students learn industry-specific skills to make strategic marketing decisions using data and evidence, using a multi-channel approach to analyse and interpret data. The course is for those curious about how data informs everyday marketing techniques and who want to become a marketing analyst. It incorporates industry-specific topics covered by only a small number of marketing analytics courses in the UK, including social media data analysis and text mining.
MSc Marketing Analytics is aimed at those who have an undergraduate degree in marketing and a good understanding of quantitative studies, or marketing work experience and want to specialise within an analytics role. Southampton states that it was the first university in the UK to offer a marketing analytics master's. The programme collaborates with leading industry practitioners who inform the curriculum using best-practice marketing techniques and the latest research.
Students learn how to integrate and use marketing channels within different markets or sectors; interpret and manage large datasets to make evidence-based decisions; use online analytics to analyse how consumer choices are influenced by social media; incorporate different marketing frameworks and behaviour models to create an analytical tool; use industry-standard data analysis software; and learn from traditional churn modelling models to offer customer incentives to enhance business profitability.
The course is a 12-month programme: students complete all taught modules in the first 9 months, and in the final 3 months work on a dissertation. Compulsory modules provide a balanced grounding in marketing analytics skills, and optional modules offer opportunities for specialism in areas including project management, data protection law and forecasting. The first semester builds knowledge of digital marketing analytics, including marketing in the 21st century, customer insight, data analytics, text mining and social network analytics.
The programme is accredited by [The Institute of Data and Marketing (IDM)](https://www.theidm.com/). Marketing students on an IDM-accredited course are eligible to sit a 2-hour online exam to achieve the IDM Certificate in Digital and Data-Driven Marketing. IDM Tutor for this programme: [Dr Monica Mihalache](mailto:monica.mihalache@soton.ac.uk).
The course leader is [Dr Carmen-Monica Mihalache](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/people/5xhy9y/doctor-monica-mihalache) MS, PhD, FHEA. Monica has over 12 years of experience in digital and offline communications, with focus on visual and video communication. She studied for a Master Degree in Marketing Research at Texas A&M University, worked as a Specialist Referent in Marketing for the Public National Romanian Television, and is a member of CIRCOM Network of trainers in television.
Students learn through lectures, group work, computer lab sessions, real-world case studies and data. They prepare a dissertation in a domain of interest in Marketing Analytics, use industry-standard tools for managing, analysing and presenting big data, and industry speakers from the marketing analytics field are invited to discuss current sector issues. Previous speakers have come from companies such as Alitex, LV=, and Firebrand Training. The relatively small intake means students get individual attention from module leaders.
Graduates commonly work in specialist marketing, advertising and PR agencies, and marketing departments in all sectors. Example job titles of Southampton MSc Marketing Analytics graduates include Data analyst, Marketing specialist, Research executive, Digital marketing planner, Insight analyst, Marketing analyst, Marketing assistant, Operations analyst, Performance strategist and Product manager.
Job prospects for MSc Marketing Analytics graduates: **£33k Average professional salary**, **81% In a skilled profession or further study**, and **95% Graduate employment rate**. Source: Example graduate job titles and job prospect statistics taken from The Graduate Outcomes Survey, which gathers information about graduates 15 months after finishing their course.

curriculum.content:
Marketing Analytics (MSc) is a **1 year**, **full-time** course based at **Highfield**. The course starts in **September 2026**.
This is a **12-month course**: you’ll complete all your taught modules in the first **9 months** and in the final **3 months** you’ll work on your dissertation. Compulsory modules provide a balanced grounding in the skills of marketing analytics. You'll then choose from optional modules that provide opportunities for specialism in areas including:
- project management
- data protection law
- forecasting
The first semester will build upon your knowledge of digital marketing analytics. You'll look at marketing in the 21st century, building customer insight, data analytics and text mining and social network analytics.
For entry in academic year **2026 to 2027**, Year 1 modules:
You **must study** the following modules:
- [**Digital Marketing Strategy**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6573)
- [**Digital and Media Analytics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6528)

You **must also choose from** the following modules:

- [**International Corporate Social Responsibility and Ethics**](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/courses/2025-26/modules/mang6535)

You’ll learn through a range of teaching methods, including lectures, group work, computer lab sessions, real-world case studies and data. You will prepare a dissertation in a domain of interest in Marketing Analytics. You’ll need to use the methods, techniques and skills you learn in the taught part of the programme to write a **15,000-word dissertation**. Researching and writing your dissertation will require around **600 hours**.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
Applicants in possession of an unconditional offer of a place may request that it be deferred to the next intake. The University does not typically permit more than a single deferral. For postgraduate taught study, applicants can make a request via their online application portal and requests for deferral will typically be accepted where there are unforeseeable life events and circumstances outside of the applicants’ control.
Reasons typically accepted for deferral include bereavement due to the loss of a close family member; serious illness and health problems; victim of a natural disaster; victim of conflict and political unrest that prohibits travel to the UK; personal accident or injury of a significant nature; child care responsibilities or caring responsibilities; relevant work experience/placements/internships; military service; change of employment circumstances; unforeseen ATAS delays; and unforeseen Visa delays.
Reasons not typically accepted for deferral include being unsuccessful in securing funding (e.g. scholarship), except in cases of the Sanctuary Scholarship, and undertaking employment or travel unrelated to the degree programme applied for.
Where a candidate with disabilities is offered a place and reasonable adjustments cannot be implemented in time for the beginning of the academic year for which the offer has been made, alternative arrangements will be discussed, and a deferral or transfer to another course may be offered where appropriate.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
If you receive an offer from us, it is stated as either conditional or unconditional.
**Conditional offer**
Your offer could be conditional for a number of reasons, such as:
- you are still awaiting results, either academic or English language
- we need to verify your qualifications
- you have to meet other non-academic entry requirements such as an Occupational Health check
- you need to pay a tuition fee deposit, if applicable to your programme
The offer letter will clearly state any academic or non-academic conditions that you need to meet along with the given deadlines. We will ask you to send us evidence confirming that you have satisfied the conditions specified in your offer letter. You should upload the evidence in your applicant portal. You will also be able to see your deadlines on your applicant portal.
If your offer was initially conditional and you have met all the academic and non-academic conditions of your offer, we will send you an unconditional offer via the applicant portal. If you are an international student, you can [apply for your visa](https://www.southampton.ac.uk/studentservices/visa-and-immigration/index.page#_ga=2.46743972.2027954709.1658132442-903936629.1657527147) when you receive an unconditional offer.

application_materials.content:
For Masters applicants, supporting documents include:
- **A transcript**: “We will need a transcript (in English or a certified translation) giving full details of subjects studied and grades/marks obtained.” Applicants should send scanned or certified copies of transcripts and **not** originals during the admissions process.
- **English language proficiency results**: applicants who are not nationals of a [majority English-speaking country](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/) need to submit evidence of English proficiency.
- **One completed reference**: applicants should check whether one or two references are required for the programme. At least one reference should normally be from an academic referee able to comment on academic work and suitability for postgraduate study; where this is not possible, references from other sources such as an employer or colleague may be accepted. References from family members, partners or spouses cannot be accepted.
- References can be uploaded via the online application system, via the Gateway after applying, posted, sent through the [enquiry form](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/enquiry/), or emailed by the referee from a university or company email address. Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company official stamp, or provided on official institution/company letterhead.
- References for Postgraduate applications must be in **pdf format, on headed paper, dated, signed/stamped and recommend you for your chosen programme**. If sent directly by the referee, they should come from the referee’s institutional or company email address and be sent to [pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk](mailto:pg-ad@exeter.ac.uk), with the student reference number, name and programme of study.
- **Personal statement**: “not all programmes require one,” but applicants may provide one. Exeter advises tailoring it to the course, explaining how the course links past and future study/career plans, showing abilities and fit with the course, giving evidence of skills, commitment and enthusiasm, explaining reasons for studying at Exeter, and describing particular interest in the subject. The personal statement should **stick to under 500 words**, use short clear sentences, may use headings, should be proofread, and should use a standard font such as Arial or Times New Roman, text size 11.
For an initial decision on taught programme applications, applicants should send as many required supporting documents as possible with the application. As a **minimum**, they must complete the Module Information section of the application form with details of outstanding modules and expected completion date, and send any interim transcripts available to support the application. International students do not need to provide original copies at the application stage and are advised not to send them during the application process.

program_overview.content:
Duration: 1 year full time. Campus: Streatham Campus.
- The MSc Marketing and Business Analytics course dives deeper into the analytical side of marketing while providing a strong foundation of core marketing skills.
- The programme develops skills at the intersection of marketing, programming, and analytics for making data-driven marketing decisions.
- Students gain expertise in marketing and analytics through marketing strategy, digital marketing planning, applied digital analytics, programming for business analytics and hands-on projects with real businesses. The course explores Statistics, AI, Data-based technologies and Consumer behaviour.
- Students learn through real-world applications, industry partnerships and digital analytics tools to tackle contemporary marketing challenges.
- Students learn from expert academics and industry guest speakers while joining a diverse, international student community and active business societies.
- Students can choose a business project or marketing project option to align the degree with career goals.
- High achieving students have the opportunity to apply for the Quantitative Techniques for Economics and Management (QTEM) programme, which includes an internship and semester abroad.
Top 10 in the UK for Business graduate prospects, Complete University Guide 2025. Triple accredited Business School: AMBA, AACSB, EQUIS. Top 10 in the UK for Business, Management and Marketing: 9th in The Times and The Sunday Times Good University Guide 2025 and [8th in the Complete University Guide 2027](https://www.thecompleteuniversityguide.co.uk/league-tables/rankings/business-and-management-studies). 1st in the UK for Marketing graduate prospects, [The Complete University Guide 2027](https://www.thecompleteuniversityguide.co.uk/league-tables/rankings/marketing?sortby=graduate-prospects).
The MSc Marketing and Business Analytics programme is accredited by the Chartered Institute of Marketing (CIM). Students who choose the marketing project pathway and achieve an overall Pass grade or higher on this programme receive exemptions towards the CIM’s Professional and Digital Marketing qualifications (Level 3 Foundation Certificate; Level 4 Certificate; or Level 6 Diploma). To achieve the full CIM qualification, graduates must enrol in CIM’s study programme, evidence their degree award, and pass the remaining CIM units within five years of graduation.
The MSc Marketing and Business Analytics offers a dynamic curriculum that blends core marketing theory with advanced analytical techniques. By developing the ability to collect, analyse and interpret data from various sources, students are empowered to make informed, data-driven marketing decisions that drive business growth and success. The course fosters transferable skills such as analysis, problem-solving and resilience, and modules introduce the latest technologies shaping the industry. In the final term, students can tailor their learning through two pathways: a consulting project working with real businesses on live marketing challenges, or a business project focused on business analytics applications. Both options allow students to apply classroom knowledge to real-world contexts, building practical experience highly valued by employers. The course ensures a balance of theory and practice, preparing students to bridge creative marketing strategy with the analytical precision demanded in today’s marketplace.
The programme is delivered through a mix of lectures, seminars, tutorials, industrial presentations, case studies, industry visits, computer simulations, project work and a dissertation. Students develop transferable skills such as management and communication skills, computational techniques, data handling and analysis, problem solving, decision making and research methodology, many addressed within an industrial and commercial context.
Students are allocated a Personal Tutor who is available for advice and support throughout their studies, along with support and mentoring from graduates who are now in industry. There is also a Postgraduate Tutor available to help with further guidance and advice.
Students are taught by experts active in research and practice, discuss the latest ideas, research discoveries and new technologies in seminars and in the field, and become actively involved in a research project. Academic staff are active in internationally-recognised scientific research across a wide range of topics, and students are also taught by leading industry practitioners.
Nataliia Pysarenko is Programme Director for the MSc Marketing and Business Analytics and Senior Lecturer in Marketing at the University of Exeter Business School. Winner of the Woman in Marketing Global Award (Science, 2024), she brings 25 years’ experience in corporate consulting, executive education, research, and mentoring. Nataliia has taught across undergraduate, postgraduate, Executive MBA, and CIM programmes, designing modules in strategy, brand management, and digital marketing. She is also a CIM Fellow and Visiting Professor at the International Institute of Business, Ukraine. [View staff profile](https://experts.exeter.ac.uk/41449-nataliia-pysarenko).
Graduates of marketing and business analytics are in high demand for roles that combine creative marketing insight with analytical and programming language expertise. The MSc in Marketing and Business Analytics gives students the ability to collect and analyse data from different sources, applying statistics, analytical tools, and programming languages to find valuable insights and recommend data-driven marketing strategy and tactics. Pathways include Marketing Analyst, Digital Marketing Analyst, Customer Insights Specialist, Marketing Data Analyst, Data-Driven Brand Manager, Content Analyst, and Data-driven Marketing Manager. As part of the Russell Group, Exeter is ranked among the UK’s top 10 most targeted universities by leading employers, ensuring strong career prospects. Supported by the award-winning careers service and global alumni network, students are equipped to thrive in today’s data-driven business landscape.
After the first year of studies at Exeter, students can progress onto the [QTEM Programme](https://business-school.exeter.ac.uk/study/studyabroad/pgstudyabroad/qtem/). QTEM aims to prepare students with excellent quantitative and analytical skills to support their future careers as decision makers leading the global business environment. If accepted onto the QTEM Programme, students spend an additional semester studying at one of the prestigious academic partners, followed by a quantitatively focussed internship and participation in the [QTEM Data Challenge](https://www.qtem.org/en/students/data-challenge/1), which includes online data science and leadership courses as well real data analysis. Students are selected and nominated to QTEM by the University of Exeter Business School following a competitive internal application process. Places are limited. The QTEM Programme is open to high achieving students enrolled in selected University of Exeter Business School programmes, including [MSc Marketing and Business Analytics](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/msc-marketing-and-business-analytics/).

conditional_admission_policy.content:
Your offer will be either **Conditional** or **Unconditional**:
- **Conditional** means that you have not yet satisfied academic, English language or any other entry requirements. Details of offer conditions and how to satisfy these requirements, including [paying your deposit](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/masters-degrees/fees/tuition-fee-deposit/), will be given in the offer letter.
- For a **full-time taught postgraduate programme**, applicants need to pay the deposit to secure their place and should pay by the deadline even if they have not yet met all the conditions of the offer.
- The deadline for meeting all conditions is normally **31 August** for September entry. Applicants must supply documentation showing that they have met outstanding academic requirements, English language and/or references, or inform the University by **31 August** what conditions remain and when they expect to meet them.
- If the University does not hear from an applicant by **31 August** and outstanding conditions remain, it reserves the right to either **withdraw or defer the application to the following year**.
- To receive a formal unconditional offer letter and, where needed, a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies, applicants must meet: academic conditions by providing degree certificates, transcripts and references as explained in the Conditional offer letter; non-academic conditions such as a [DBS](http://www.exeter.ac.uk/dbs/) check; and the required standard of English language competence by providing an English language test certificate meeting the [English language requirements](https://www.exeter.ac.uk/study/englishlanguagerequirements/).
- Offer holders who successfully complete a [Pre-Sessional English course at the University of Exeter International Study Centre](https://www.exeterisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english) and meet the requirements for progression to their chosen degree are not required to undertake an additional IELTS or TOEFL test. The University does not accept pre-sessional courses delivered by other INTO centres or organisations.

application_materials.content:
You will need to provide the following documentation as part of your application. This list of documents may vary slightly from course to course.
- **Academic qualifications:** Please provide a transcript for your degree study. If you have not yet completed your degree please provide a transcript of your results achieved to date. If you have completed more than one university qualification, please provide a transcript and certificate for both.
- If your degree was awarded by a UK university, please upload a transcript of your marks for each year or an electronic Higher Education Achievement Reports (HEAR).
- If your degree was awarded by an overseas institution, you should supply a transcript of your marks for each year of your studies and a copy of your degree certificate together with a certified translation if the document is not in English. International and EU applicants are also advised to include high school transcripts.
- We accept copies of physical transcripts and degree certificates as well as electronic transcripts and certificates. Please **do not** submit originals of certificates or transcripts by post.
- If you are submitting copies of physical documents, you should upload clear, colour photographs or scans of your original qualification documents. These documents must confirm that the qualification has been awarded, show the date of the award, and show the final awarded grade.
- **Referee details:** Please provide the contact details of one or two referees on your application as required. You should provide details of an academic referee if you are currently studying, or if you have graduated within the last five years. Professional references may be considered if you have graduated more than five years ago.
- Open references will normally only be accepted if they are written on headed paper, provided as a colour copy of the original, and provide the referee’s work contact details. If you have open references, please upload these at the time of application.
- If you do not have open reference, Queen Mary will contact your referee(s) via email to supply a reference, preferably electronically. A reference provided by email must be sent from a university or company email address; references from a personal email address such as Yahoo or Hotmail are not acceptable.
- Paper reference forms should be endorsed by an appropriate institution/company stamp or on official institution/company letterhead, and should be provided as a scanned colour copy of the original.
- **Statement of purpose:** Your statement of purpose should explain why you want to study your chosen programme and how it will help your future career aspirations. This should typically be one side of A4 paper.
- **Curriculum Vitae (CV)/Resume**
- **English language certificate (if applicable):** If English is not your first language, you should provide evidence of English language ability: IELTS, TOEFL, or other acceptable proof.
- You can still apply even if you haven't yet received your final transcript or your Certificate of English proficiency. Some postgraduate programmes may require applicants to have submitted their Reference letters before a decision has been made.
- Once you have submitted your application, you will have access to the [MySIS applicant portal](https://mysis.qmul.ac.uk/), where you can upload any further documents.

program_overview.content:
The MSc Marketing and Digital Analytics programme is designed to provide insight into marketing and its relationship with the online data economy. Students will develop critical insights into the changing nature of marketing, and learn how to drive campaigns and build consumer relationships within a digital environment. The programme is open to graduates of all disciplinary backgrounds and is also suitable for individuals who are looking to start or develop their own businesses.
- Specialise in data analytics and their use in B2B and B2C marketing, and beyond.
- Examine techniques to measure, track and code human and consumer behaviour.
- Explore the opportunities and challenges within the Big Data economy.
Study options include full-time study starting September 2026 or September 2027, each lasting 1 year. Location: Mile End.
The core modules aim to build foundational knowledge and skills in marketing and digital economy concepts and theories. Broad skills developed during the course include the ability to develop independent insights on marketing in the digital economy; critically evaluate competing approaches and viewpoints, and justify decisions on Big Data and data analytics; review the use of data and its relevance in different cultural contexts; and act ethically and with responsibility in terms of data analytics, with attention to data ethics including data privacy, anonymity and governance.
Structure:
- Seven compulsory taught modules
- One elective module
- Compulsory Dissertation for Marketing or Working with Open Data
Learning outcomes are assessed using a mix of coursework, essays, projects, presentations and, in some cases, exams. There will be variation across modules, and some are wholly examined by coursework. Compulsory dissertation with a choice between Dissertation for Marketing or Dissertation with Open Data.
The teaching team is comprised of Teaching and Research and Teaching and Scholarship staff, complemented where relevant by visiting lecturers with professional expertise in sectors such as communications, advertising and public relations. Students will benefit from this mix of expertise, gaining insights from research, scholarship and industry. Students typically have 3 contact hours per week in each module. Students could take part in a range of different teaching and learning activities, including one-to-one tutorials, guest lectures, simulation game(s), computer-lab based activities, group-work, independent studies, research projects and team learning.
Programme Directors: [Dr Swagato Chatterjee](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/chatterjees.html) and [Dr Haytham Siala](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/sbm/staff/academic/profiles/sialah.html). Dr Swagato Chatterjee is Senior Lecturer in Digital Marketing & Analytics and Joint Programme Director of MSc Marketing and Digital Analytics. He has over 9 years of experience in marketing, operations, and analytics and has worked with companies including Coca-Cola, Times of India, Technosoft, Mitsubishi, Nomura, Yes Bank, CSC, Ernst and Young, Godrej, Genpact, and Indian Oil in consultancy and training assignments related to analytics. Dr Haytham Siala is a Senior Lecturer (Associate Professor) in Marketing, specializing in Digital Marketing and Analytics, Technology Enhanced Learning, Digital Healthcare and Digital Well-Being.
Teaching is based at Queen Mary’s [Mile End campus](https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/howtofindus/mileend/), one of the largest self-contained residential campuses in the capital. Facilities include a ThinkPod interactive collaboration space, Media suite with industry-standard design and editing software (QUBE), Graduate Centre, and 24-hour library on campus.
The School of Business and Management is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business](https://www.aacsb.edu/about-us)(AACSB). Queen Mary is also part of the [Russell Group](https://russellgroup.ac.uk/).
Graduates of this course will be well-placed to pursue roles in social media management, marketing campaign management, market research, advertising, SEO, CRM communications, marketing analytics or business analytics.

program_overview.content:
MSc Operations Research and Analytics is a Graduate (Taught) programme in the Department of Mathematics. It is available full-time for 12 months for Home and Overseas students, with a start date of 28 September 2026 and location at Houghton Street, London.
This programme is designed for students wishing to deepen and broaden their mathematics knowledge, and gain skills in high demand in the marketplace. With study in practice and theory, students gain insight into analytics problems faced by businesses, governments, and nonprofits. On the practical side, students learn how to model real-world problems using optimisation, stochastic simulation, and machine learning, using specialist software taught in tutorial sessions. On the theoretical side, students learn to recognise canonical underlying mathematical problems and solve them with state-of-the-art methods. Courses are taught by faculty members with world-leading research profiles.
In the first term, students learn the fundamentals of operations research and machine learning. In the second term, they can choose from a range of courses in mathematics, statistics, finance, and management. Students undertake a final project where, working in a consultancy role and using the tools learned in the degree, they tackle a real problem faced by a partner organisation. Past and present partners include Amazon, BT, British Airways, Emirates Airlines, FICO, Ford Motor Company, Just Eat, Legal and General, the National Audit Office, and Transport for London. As an alternative to the project, more theoretically minded students can write a dissertation supervised by a faculty member.
The programme takes three compulsory courses and options within the Department and across other relevant departments, including Management and Statistics. During the summer, students are required to do either a project in Operations Research and Analytics or a Dissertation in Operations Research and Analytics. The project involves work in a host organisation in business, government, health, or a social non-profit organisation, in a consultancy role, typically turning a real problem faced by the organisation into a mathematical model whose solution provides tangible benefit. The dissertation requires study of an area of research, or an application of advanced techniques, and a report of findings.
Teaching combines traditional lectures with seminars. Several courses, including all three compulsory ones, involve using a programming language or specialised computational tools. Students develop these skills in a pre-sessional Python course and in the respective courses' seminars. Within the programme students take courses, including half unit courses and full unit courses, to a total of four units.
2024 admissions data: 290 applications, 24 intake, 12:1 ratio.
Student perspectives describe the programme as balancing theoretical foundations and industry applications, offering flexibility in course choice, and providing networking opportunities. One MSc Operations Research and Analytics student said the programme allowed study of topics such as combinatorial optimisation, advanced statistics, and algorithmic techniques for data mining.
The Department of Mathematics aims to be a leading centre for the study of mathematics in the social sciences. Its research encompasses four main overlapping areas: discrete mathematics; mathematical game theory; financial and related mathematics; and optimisation and algorithms. All aspects of its research were ranked world-leading or internationally excellent in the most recent [Research Excellence Framework (2021)](https://results2021.ref.ac.uk/profiles/institutions/10004063), submitted jointly with the Department of Statistics. The department offers three postgraduate programmes and has close ties with other departments at LSE, including Statistics, Economics, Finance, Management and the Data Science Institute.
This programme is ideal preparation for a range of careers in quantitative positions in consultancy, management, finance, government and business, anywhere in the world. Recent graduate placements include: Consultancy: Accenture, BCG, Deloitte, EY, PwC, McKinsey, Bain & Company, Decision Point Analytics, LET Consulting, and Turner & Townsend. Government: Ofgem and Ministry of Defence (Singapore). Business: Ali Baba, BMW group, BT group, Dish Network, Johnson & Johnson, Just Eat, Procter & Gamble, Renault group, Ocado, Red Bull, and Samba TV. Transportation: Airbus, British Airways, DiDi, Emirates, Laskarides Shipping, and Ryanair. Tech: Amazon, Ant Group, BT group, China Telecom Europe, Databricks, Flexciton, Huawei, Satalia, and Yahoo Japan. Banking and finance: Central Bank of the Bahamas, CiBanco, Citi, Credit Suisse, CITIC Securities, FinTru, Jane Street Capital, Guodu Securities, Point72 Asset Management, Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, and UBS. PhD study: Goethe University Frankfurt, Imperial College London, Monash University Malaysia, National University of Singapore, and University of Warwick.
Top 5 sectors students work in: Financial and Professional Services; Information, Digital Technology and Data; FMCG, Manufacturing and Retail; Insurance; Other Professional, Scientific and Technical Activities.

curriculum.content:
Study mode / programme availability: Home full-time students (**12 months**) and Overseas full-time students (**12 months**). Start date: 28 September 2026. Location: Houghton Street, London.
In the first term, students learn the fundamentals of operations research and machine learning. In the second term, students can choose from a range of courses in mathematics, statistics, finance, and management. Course topics include algorithms and computation, optimisation, game theory, and further topics in machine learning and AI.
Programme content: students take three compulsory courses and choose courses from a range of options within the Department and across other relevant departments, including Management and Statistics.
Year 1:

During the summer, students are required to do either a project in Operations Research and Analytics or a Dissertation in Operations Research and Analytics. Within the programme students take a number of courses, including half unit courses and full unit courses, to a total of **four units**. Teaching combines traditional lectures with seminars; several courses, including all three compulsory ones, involve using a programming language or specialised computational tools. Students develop these skills in a pre-sessional Python course and in the respective courses' seminars.

cost_of_attendance.content:
LSE broadly estimates that students should allow **£1,550 per month** for all living expenses, including accommodation, travel, food, laundry, study costs, and other personal expenses. This will vary depending on lifestyle and requirements.
- If you're an overseas student and require a student visa, you must ensure that you have sufficient funds for the first year of tuition fees and **up to nine months of living costs**, and provide evidence of these funds.
- Private housing costs in London can vary considerably depending on location and accommodation type, but start at approximately **£650 per month**.
- LSE estimates that students will spend **£150-£300 per month on food**, depending on whether they live in catered or self-catered halls, or in private accommodation.

financial_aid.content:
Applications for this programme are considered on a rolling basis; however, if you’d like to be considered for any funding opportunities, you must submit your application and all supporting documents by the funding deadline.
- **Fee reduction:** Students who have completed and passed an undergraduate degree at LSE and are beginning taught graduate study at the School are eligible for a 10 per cent tuition fee reduction. Students who have completed and passed two or more Summer School courses are eligible for a five per cent reduction. If eligible for both discounts, the higher 10 per cent discount rate will apply. [Find out more about the LSE alumni discount](https://info.lse.ac.uk/staff/divisions/Finance-Division/Fees-Income-and-Credit-Control/Rewards-and-Discounts).
- **Scholarships and other funding:** LSE provides scholarships to help both home and overseas students. Some needs-based awards are offered for this programme, including the [Graduate Support Scheme](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/secure/graduate-support-scheme). To apply for an award, you must have an offer of a place and submit a Graduate Financial Support application before the funding deadline. The funding deadline for needs-based awards from LSE is **23 April 2026**.
- In addition to needs-based awards, LSE offers [scholarships for students from specific regions of the world](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding) and [awards for certain subjects](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/Department-or-programme-specific-funding). You can’t apply for a Graduate Support Scheme or LSE scholarship once you’ve joined the School.
- You can also apply for [Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding/ESRC-Studentships) funding when you apply as part of a 1+3 research programme. The 1+3 scheme provides funding for a one-year research training master's linked to a three-year PhD. To be considered for ESRC funding, you need to supply your application and any [supporting documents](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/Prospective-students/Supporting-documents) before the funding deadline. Funding deadline for ESRC funding: **14 January 2026**.
- LSE expects students who register for a programme to have sufficient funds for the duration.
- Learn more about [fees and funding opportunities](https://www.lse.ac.uk/study-at-lse/Graduate/fees-and-funding).

multiple_applications.content:
You may submit an application via the online application system only ONCE within the application cycle (October 2025 to September 2026). When completing your initial online application, you may choose up to **two programmes** in order of preference. **If you are applying for two programmes, please submit a separate statement of academic purpose for each programme**. Your choices will be considered in sequence, and it is only possible to hold one offer of a place, so if you are offered a place on your first-choice programme you will not be considered for your second-choice unless you specifically request it.
If you are unsuccessful in your application to both of your initially chosen programmes and you wish to be considered for further, additional choices, you may do this by submitting the **Add/Amend programmes** form via the [Graduate Applicant Portal](https://lseportal.force.com/admissions/s/track-my-graduate-application) and paying an additional administrative fee of **£105**. You should not use this form to add choices 3 and 4 before receiving a decision on each of your original programme choices, unless you wish to withdraw your initial programme choices.
**You may only submit an application using the online application system ONCE in the same admissions cycle. If you submit a second online application within the same admissions cycle, it will not be considered.** **To apply to further programmes after you have submitted your initial online application, you must use the process above.**

deferral_admission_policy.content:
LSE has a no-deferrals policy for offers for graduate programmes. The only exception to this is in cases of unforeseen illness or bereavement.
If your deferral is agreed in exceptional circumstances, LSE asks you to submit a deferral deposit as requested in your deferral letter, using the student self-funding [payment portal](https://portal.lse.ac.uk/payments/s/fees) to pay. The deposit must be received by the **January 31st deadline** to secure your new offer for next year. The deferral deposit is offset against your tuition fees once you register.
Your deposit may be refunded in exceptional circumstances, determined at the School's discretion. Documentary evidence of your inability to travel/attend your programme will be required. Examples of valid circumstances include: outbreak of war, refusal of Visa, inability to travel due to injury or illness, bereavement, and declining your offer before or on the **31 January deadline**. Circumstances where a refund would not be made include choosing to attend a different university and failure to secure funding.
If your circumstances match those above, you may request to defer your offer using the Extenuating Circumstances form on the Graduate Applicant Portal. If your request is agreed, your offer for the current year will be declined automatically, as you do not intend to come to LSE in this cycle.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
In order to take up your place you must fulfil the conditions that have been applied to your offer. These may include satisfying academic conditions, providing English language test results and/or degree results, or attendance at introductory or LSE Summer School courses. To fulfil the condition(s) you must send official documentary proof of your final degree mark or test scores, or attend the specified summer school or pre-sessional courses.
Introductory (pre-sessional) courses in mathematics and statistics are run in September for various courses - details are on your offer letter.
If you have failed to reach the standard of your conditions you should still send the official proof of your results. It may still be possible to confirm your offer - your results will be sent with your application file to the selector and a final decision will be made. If you have failed to attain the required language score by a large margin, you may arrange to re-take the test as long as you can submit the required score before the registration period begins.
If the selector has examined your degree results and your offer has not been confirmed, this decision is final - no appeal is possible. If your offer has been non-confirmed on the basis of your language test score you may arrange to re-take the test.

application_materials.content:
- **Application essay:** An application essay is a key component of the application process and must accompany the initial application. The statement should capture your motivation to pursue the MSc in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management at University College London in a genuine and specific manner; demonstrate a clear interest in people management, organisational behaviour, social psychology, data analytics, and statistics, as well as prior experience and knowledge in these areas; specify your career aspirations after completing the degree, outlining well-researched and grounded short- and long-term professional and personal objectives; and cover why you are looking to pursue this programme, what you will bring to the UCL communities, and evidence of leadership and teamwork.
- **CV:** “We also require a copy of your CV.”
- **Required documents:** “You will need to include a degree transcript in one of the suggested disciplines, two references, and a personal statement.”
- **English evidence:** Applicants are encouraged to include evidence of their English language qualification at the time they apply. Overseas applicants should also supply evidence of their English language ability through one of UCL’s accepted [English Language Tests.](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements)
- **Current students:** If your predicted final results meet the minimum entry requirements, you can apply before receiving final degree results; include details of predicted results on the application form and an official transcript of results so far.
- **References:** References should be provided digitally by your referee unless this is not possible due to accessibility requirements, in which case contact the [UCL referees team](mailto:eferees.pgadmissions@ucl.ac.uk).

interview_requirements.content: Applicants who meet the entry requirements and provide an appropriate professional statement will be reviewed. Those considered eligible for the next stage will be invited to an online video interview, with the invitation sent by email from Kira Talent. Interview performance is a crucial component of the application process, as it provides evidence of the applicant’s genuine interest in the programme and the specific qualities sought: excellence, drive, critical thinking, integrity, and teamwork skills.

application_deadlines.content:
**Start date:** September 2026
**Application deadline:** Applications for the 2026/27 cycle will open on **20th October 2025** and close on **26th June 2026 at 5pm UK time for applicants who require a visa**; and on **28th August 2026** for those who do not.
A staged admissions process is in place for this programme.

academic_requirements.content:
- A minimum of an **upper second-class Bachelor's degree from a UK university or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard**, in relevant subjects, such as **business and management, social psychology, and social sciences**.
- Degrees and work experience in other fields are also considered if students have a strong motivation to pursue a career in people and management-related areas.
- Applicants are expected to have a **basic understanding of statistics, business, and management** through formal or informal education and work experience, and should be prepared for quantitative, managerial, and people management topics.
- China-specific equivalency: A **four-year bachelor's degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered; the required grade varies depending on the awarding university.

- China-specific equivalency for the required upper second-class (2:1): applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education need a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 90%**.

program_overview.content:
The UCL People Analytics and Human-Centric Management MSc is a full-time, one-calendar-year programme in London, Canary Wharf. Developed in partnership with industry leaders, it is designed to give students critical and latest knowledge and skills in people analytics, leadership, and the future of work, and is aimed at those aspiring to careers in management, people analytics, and human resources.
Organisations today face complex challenges related to people management and leadership, such as attracting and retaining top talent, ensuring employee engagement and well-being, and adapting to rapid technological changes. The programme combines fundamental HR and management knowledge with cutting-edge research and practice in people analytics, strategic management, work design, and employee well-being. Its curriculum goes beyond traditional HR education so students can gain the skills required to lead sustainable change and growth in various organisations, focusing on people not just as resources but as individuals with needs, values, and potential.
The programme is ideal for students aiming for high-level careers in people analytics, HR analytics, management, or HR. It covers quantitative, managerial, and people management topics and welcomes applicants from a wide variety of academic backgrounds, including business and management, social psychology, and social sciences.
This degree offers opportunities to:
- Acquire the skills and knowledge required to lead organisations, not only to drive business success, but also promote a healthier society and work environment.
- Develop analytical skills to inform strategic decisions and navigate organisational issues through a people- and human-centric approach.
- Benefit from a bespoke Careers and Employer Engagement Programme and a dedicated careers team.
- Learn from expert faculty producing research rated as ‘world-leading’ and ‘internationally excellent’ in the latest [Research Excellence Framework (REF 2021)](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/news/95-som-research-outputs-world-leading-internationally-excellent-ref). The teaching team is comprised of academic leads and practitioners, exposing students to cutting-edge research and industry knowledge.
- Study on levels 38 and 50 of Canary Wharf’s One Canada Square in state-of-the-art lecture theatres, with purpose-built student facilities, hubs, and quiet study spaces.
As graduates, students are equipped with essential HR and analytics knowledge, a multifaceted skillset, and attributes for strategic, people-focused roles across multiple industries. Developed in collaboration with employers and guided by an advisory board of industry leaders and experts in people and management, the programme prepares graduates for roles including People Analytics Consultant, Workforce Strategy Analyst, Employee Experience Designer, Organisational Development Specialist, HR Technology Analyst, Leadership Development Advisor, Diversity & Inclusion Manager, and Change Management Consultant.
The programme offers networking opportunities through careers workshops with employers, alumni events with other postgraduate students from the UCL School of Management, access to UCL societies and clubs, engagement with the global business community in Canary Wharf, one-on-one careers advice, exclusive corporate events, the alumni community, and the School of Management’s [New Technologies & Innovation Speaker Series](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/newtechnologyspeakerseries) and [Business Leader Speaker Series](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/business-leaders-speaker-series).
UCL School of Management is AACSB accredited, a global mark of excellence recognising its commitment to innovative, research-led teaching, rigorous academic standards, and preparing students for impactful global careers in business and management.
The programme is delivered through lectures, case studies, class discussions and group projects. Students typically study compulsory modules in Terms 1 and 2, while the Dissertation project takes place over Term 3. The programme also includes multiple bootcamps throughout the year, where industry leaders teach the latest knowledge and techniques in data analytics, artificial intelligence, and organisational design. Assessment is through written examinations, individual/group coursework, and a 12,000-word dissertation project, which typically involves practical topics chosen by the student and addresses people-related challenges faced by organisations. Students undertake modules to the value of 180 credits; upon successful completion of 180 credits, they are awarded an MSc in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management.

curriculum.content:
Study mode: **Full-time**. Duration: **1 calendar year**. Location: London, Canary Wharf.
The programme is delivered through a combination of lectures, case studies, class discussions and group projects. Students typically study **4 compulsory modules, each worth 15 credits in Terms 1 and 2**. The Dissertation project takes place over Term 3. In addition to the core modules, the programme includes multiple bootcamps throughout the year, where industry leaders visit to teach the latest knowledge and techniques in data analytics, artificial intelligence, and organisational design.
Assessment is through written examinations, individual/group coursework, and a **12,000-word dissertation project**. The dissertation project will typically involve practical topics chosen by the student, and address a range of people-related challenges faced by organisations.
Each taught module in Terms 1 and 2 is delivered over 10 weeks, with 3 contact hours per week comprising lecture content and interactive components. Students can expect approximately 12 contact hours per week in Terms 1 and 2, plus approximately 7-12 hours a week for each module on assessment and independent study. The total number of weekly hours will vary from 20 - 25 hours according to the module and activities. Contact hours reduce to approximately 2-5 hours per week during Term 3, when students focus on their dissertation module.
Full-time compulsory modules:
- [Data Visualisation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/data-visualisation-MSIN0167)
- [Leadership and Communication](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/leadership-and-communication-MSIN0077)
- [Organisational Behaviour B](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/organisational-behaviour-b-MSIN0142)
- [Influence and Negotiations](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/influence-and-negotiations-MSIN0148)
- [Managing Diversity](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/managing-diversity-MSIN0236)
- [Strategic Human Resources Management](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/strategic-human-resources-management-MSIN0265)
- [People Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/people-analytics-MSIN0266)
- [Sustainable Work Design](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/sustainable-work-design-MSIN0267)
- [Dissertation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/dissertation-MSIN0268)
The compulsory modules provide the basis and foundation in key HR theories and Data Analytics knowledge and bootcamps give students the opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge about more specialised areas of HR management. The compulsory dissertation module (research project) takes place in Term 3. Throughout the year the programme will expose students to opportunities to identify dissertation topics, such as inequity in organisations, adoption of flexible work policies, and leading remote teams.
Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of **180 credits**, students will be awarded an MSc in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management.
