deferral_admission_policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer. However, UCL will consider a request to defer only in the following circumstances:
- The serious illness of the offer holder or the serious illness of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The death of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The need to take parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months.
- Where the offer holder is directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster (i.e., war, earthquakes or flooding).
- The offer holder has been awarded a UCL scholarship (including UCL partnership agreements and Faculty awards); or a full scholarship (tuition fee and maintenance support) from a recognised funding body - for study in the following academic year. (A ‘scholarship’ does not include student loans. The UCL Student Funding office can confirm the standing of a funding body or partnership as required).
- The offer holder holds an offer to study the UCL International Pre-Masters.
To be eligible for a deferral you must hold an unconditional offer which you have accepted. The exception is if you hold an offer for the International Pre-Masters, in which case an accepted conditional offer is allowed. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt (if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme). program_overview.content:
Psychology and Behavioural Analytics MSc, entry year 2026, is delivered full time over 1 year.
Top reasons to study include:
- A powerful combination of psychological tools applied to data analysis
- Placement-based dissertation, graduating with demonstrable experience on your CV
- Approved as postgraduate research training by the Economic and Social Research Council
Digital data now dominates all aspects of our lives. Every action we take – from smartphone use to social media activity, public surveillance and even our online purchases – leaves a digital trace. Analysing digital data tells one story, but it isn’t enough to fully understand human behaviour. To do that, you need the insights that psychology provides. The MSc Psychology and Behavioural Analytics integrates psychological insights with an understanding of digital data. You will develop a specialised skill set highly sought after in today’s data-driven world, which will set you apart in the job market, opening new career opportunities.
**Who is this programme for?** Anyone who wants to understand digital data through human psychology. We welcome individuals from diverse backgrounds, including computer science, business, sociology, criminology and many more. You don’t need a psychology degree to apply.
Taught by world-leading academics, you will develop a rare combination of technical data analysis and psychological expertise, providing a broader perspective to tackle a wide range of professional challenges. You will also:
- Develop key critical thinking and communication skills, allowing you to evaluate data and convey your findings to a range of audiences
- Develop your skills with data analysis software such as R, Python, Nvivo and BORIS
- Enhance your skills in qualitative and quantitative research methods to analyse both individual experiences and large-scale trends
- Undertake a placement-based dissertation, allowing you to apply and develop your skills towards impactful, real-world projects
- Learn how to ethically and responsibly handle digital data
Through a dynamic mix of data science and psychology-focused modules, you will gain hands-on experience with various types of digital data, including visual data such as CCTV footage, body-cam videos and social media; natural language such as social media posts, blogs and online forums; and mobile sensor data such as movement tracking, sound and usage logs. You will build a strong foundation in key psychological concepts related to behaviour, including identity, personality and cognitive decision-making. Important topics are covered, such as data limitations, bias and the principles of responsible research.
The final term is where everything comes together with your dissertation. Gain valuable, practical experience working on a project with either a partner organisation or within the Department of Psychology. The programme provides dedicated support to guide you through the process, ensuring you gain relevant experience that will make you stand out to employers.
Students have investigated how CCTV recordings can provide insight into bystander behaviour and behavioural biometrics from digital footprint data, such as mobile phone usage. Staff are involved in the Policing Academic Centre of Excellence, providing links to digital data in policing practices.
The programme is in the Department of Psychology, Faculty of Science and Technology.
Careers: The master’s in Psychology and Behavioural Analytics opens the door to a wide range of career paths. The qualitative and quantitative insights you will be able to provide make you a valuable asset to any employer. Roles of interest may include social researcher, data analyst, behavioural analyst, data scientist, AI trainer, market research analyst, human resources specialist and customer experience analyst. You may also use this master’s as a stepping stone for further study, including a career in academia as either a lecturer or researcher.

curriculum.content:
Duration: **Full time 1 year**.
Course structure: Core modules include:
- **Advanced Modelling with Psychological Data**: Apply advanced analysis methods to psychological data, including handling large-scale, rich and sometimes messy real-life datasets, constructing models, presenting evidence-based visualisations, coding in R, and working in a team.
- **Analysing Talk and Text**: Introduction to qualitative and quantitative approaches to analysing talk and text, structured around conducting a research project. Topics include Natural language processing; Thematic Analysis and Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA); Conversation analysis and discursive approaches; Quantitative analysis through Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC); Sentiment analysis and its applications.
- **Digital Data Applications**: Interdisciplinary psychology and computer science module in a laboratory environment, using tools such as R, Python, Java MakeCode, BORIS and Netlogo. Covers digital data types such as video, sensor data and digital trace data, with methods including data cleaning, predictive modelling, behavioural coding and data visualisation.
- **Programming for Health Data Science**: Teaches fundamentals of computing and programming in R and Python, including structured programming, data structures, functions, data file input/output, selection and filtering, exploratory graphics, project management for data and code, reproducible research, source code management, NumPy and Pandas, and plotting basic graphics.
- **Psychological Perspectives and Digital Behavioural Data**: Explores meta-level issues in psychology and behavioural analytics, including psychological theories, digital data, research ethics, morality and scientific practice.
- **Psychology and Behavioural Analytics Dissertation**: A **three-month dissertation project** involving a substantial research project intended to tackle a real-world challenge. Students may undertake a project through an external placement with an industrial or research organisation working in partnership with the University, or carry out an academic project. The project includes completing a comprehensive literature review, formulating testable research hypotheses or defining parameters of an explorative analysis, conducting empirical work, and analysing and interpreting data.
- **Understanding Humans Through Data**: Applies core analytic methods across psychological research and practice settings through lectures and practical workshops, building coding capacity in R. Covers statistical tests, data analysis and processing tools, analysis approaches for testing predictions, describing findings through text and visualisations, and translating data analysis findings into psychological insights.

program_overview.content:
During a time of great global uncertainty, particularly in the areas of climate change, health and regulation, many organisations are looking for risk managers who have both traditional risk management knowledge and data analysis skills to solve the problems presented in the world today. This programme provides students with a comprehensive grounding in risk management, including risk analytics, data analytics and the application of statistics in risk management. Within second semester elective modules, students will have the opportunity to specialise in certain areas of risk management such as risk regulation, and sustainability and climate risk.
- Become highly employable in a variety of industries including finance, medicine, IT, science, technology, and regulatory bodies, where risk management professionals are in high demand.
- Learn real-world key risk management knowledge in areas affecting our world today.
- Opportunities to take elective modules in areas such as risk regulation and sustainability and climate risk.
This programme is designed for students who want a career in risk regulation across the globe. With such a large number of industries requiring risk management professionals, students who graduate from this programme will have the skills and knowledge to work in a wide range of industries including finance, medicine, IT, science, technology and regulatory bodies.

curriculum.content:
Study options for Risk Analytics MSc include **Full-time, September 2026 | 1 year**, **Part-time, September 2026 | 2 years**, and **Full-time, September 2027 | 1 year**. Location: **Mile End**.
- Semester One: students focus on compulsory modules providing foundations for a risk-related career, covering fundamental risk analytics tools, statistics, data analytics, machine learning, and key risk management theories in Enterprise Risk Management and Finance.
- Semester Two: students choose all modules and tailor the programme to interests, career plans or professional background. Elective modules allow specialisation in areas such as Enterprise risk analytics (with Actuarial Risk Management 2), Financial risk analytics (with Digital and Real Asset Analytics and Financial Data Analytics), Sustainability and Climate Risk Analytics, and Regulatory Risk Analytics.
- Semester Three: students work on a dissertation, developing hands-on skills for industries, government agencies, or academic institutions.
Structure:
- Four compulsory modules
- Four elective modules (chosen from 7)
- Final project and dissertation
Compulsory/Core modules:
- Actuarial Risk Management 1
- Foundations of Mathematics and Statistics
- Risk Analytics Dissertation: each Risk Analytics MSc student is required to complete a **60 credit project dissertation**. A student must find a potential supervisor and fill out a Risk Analytics MSc Project Approval Form by the end of Semester B. The supervisor and project must be approved by the Risk Analytics MSc Programme Director. A typical MSc project dissertation consists of about 30 pages, covering a specific research-level topic in Risk Analytics, usually requiring the student to apply risk management tools to measure, predict, or manage certain types of risks. An MSc project may also involve collaboration with a collaborator based in industry.
- Financial Instruments and Markets
- Data Analytics
Elective modules:
- Regulatory Risk Analytics
- Optimisation for Business Processes
- SAS for Business Intelligence
- Digital and Real Asset Analytics
- Computational Statistics with R
- Actuarial Risk Management 2
Assessment:
- 67% Modules
- 33%
- Students are assessed by a mixture of formal examinations and coursework in taught modules.
- Students complete a substantial Risk Analytics Project with strong industrial relevance, focusing on practical applications, professional skills, and the latest developments at the frontier of the field.
Teaching is primarily through a combination of lectures and tutorials, in addition to independent study and research.

program_overview.content:
Risk management is an important subject in both the financial and public sectors. A successful risk management system incorporates expert knowledge from mathematics, statistics, actuarial science, finance, computing and engineering. The Risk Management Science programmes offered by the Department of Statistics and Data Science at The Chinese University of Hong Kong have played leading roles in the development of the risk management discipline in Hong Kong. The highly successful Master of Science Programme in Risk Management Science was launched in 2003 and was renamed M.Sc. in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics in 2021-22 to reflect the new elements of the evolving field of data analytics. Graduates are equipped with state-of-the-art risk management expertise that will allow them to play a leading role in the industry.
- Study mode: Full-time (1 year) or Part-time (2 years).
- Lecture format: Each course consists of a three-hour lecture each week.
- Time and venue: Weekday evenings and Saturdays at CUHK in Shatin.
- Programme structure: Students are required to complete a minimum of 24 credits in order to graduate. The full-time mode normally lasts one year, with core and elective courses across two semesters. The part-time mode normally lasts two years, with core and elective courses across the first and second years.
- Academic partnership: The M.Sc. in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics programme is an Academic Partner of the Global Association of Risk Professionals (GARP). GARP describes the programme as highly rigorous and interdisciplinary, providing students with a solid grounding in mathematics, finance, statistics and related areas, positioning them to pursue the FRM designation and assume strategic roles within the global risk management profession.
- Accreditation: The M.Sc. in Risk Management Science and Data Analytics has been accredited by the Royal Statistical Society (RSS). Graduates may apply for Graduate Statistician status with the RSS, subject to a satisfactory combination of modules completed. The accreditation covers the 2023-24 intake through the 2028-29 intake.
- Experiential learning: The practicum provides a bridge between the classroom and the real business world. Students complete a project assigned by a company or organization on a part-time basis under the joint supervision of an instructor and a member of the company or organization, then give a final project presentation and submit a written report.
- Career support: The programme provides workshops on CV writing and interview skills, career talks and company visits to support students’ career development. Activities mentioned include interview skills and assessment centre workshops, CV writing and individual CV editing, career talks by the Census and Statistics Department of the HKSAR Government and on cryptocurrency, and company visits to Bloomberg L.P. Hong Kong Office, Natixis, and the Census and Statistics Department.
- Facilities and industry-related learning: The Department of Statistics provides state-of-the-art computing facilities for teaching and research, including a computer laboratory with Microsoft 365/Office 2016 Professional Plus, MATLAB, R, SAS and IBM SPSS Statistics, and Bloomberg Terminals providing real-time financial data and news. NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute workshops were organized, giving students a chance to apply GPU-accelerated machine learning algorithms and receive an electronic NVIDIA DLI certificate after passing the assessment.
- Faculty and teaching staff include Dr Wong Tat Wing, Director of the MSc RMDA programme and Lecturer at CUHK’s Department of Statistics, who holds Associate of the Society of Actuaries and Financial Risk Manager designations and is a Certified Instructor and University Ambassador at the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute; Dr Cheung King Chau, Deputy Director of the MSc RMDA programme and Lecturer, whose research interests are in network and financial data and portfolio management; Professor Wong Hoi Ying, Professor of Statistics, Outstanding Fellow of the Faculty of Science, and Associate Dean of Science (Student Affairs), whose research focuses on mathematical finance, actuarial science, FinTech, and machine learning; Professor Zhang Jiacheng, Assistant Professor in the Department of Statistics, whose research focuses on probability theory, stochastic optimization, stochastic partial differential equations, partial differential equations, mathematical finance, stochastic portfolio theory and stochastic volatility modeling; Dr John Alexander Wright, Senior Lecturer whose research interests lie in applied probability, especially financial mathematics, and who holds FRM and Professional Risk Manager designations; and Professor Yau Chun Yip, Professor in the Department of Statistics, whose research interests include financial time series, change-point analysis, and extreme value theory.
- Guest lecturers include Juan Lago, Managing Director and Chief Representative Asia-Pacific at Banco Security, with 18 years of finance experience in Madrid, New York, Chile and Hong Kong; Dr Joaquin Calvo, with more than 20 years of financial industry experience in consulting and major financial institutions across APAC, Europe and the Americas, including service as Head of Market Risk and Liquidity at a bank in Hong Kong; Franco Leung, Director, Market Outreach at S&P Global Ratings, with over 20 years of experience in credit analysis, corporate rating and research, corporate treasury, fixed income markets, risk governance and portfolio risk management; and Terrence Ho, who shares 30 years of trading experience.
- Alumni outcomes and perspectives include graduates working as a pilot at Cathay Pacific, an Operational Risk Management Specialist at an international bank, Director of Risk Consulting at KPMG Advisory (HK) Limited, Fitch Ratings, Data and Information Management at HSBC Insurance Asia Limited, PhD studies in Informatics at Nagoya University, Business Analyst at NumeriX LLC, The Bank of East Asia, and Nanyang Commercial Bank. Alumni describe the programme as balancing theoretical and practical learning, offering small-class teaching, flexible and well-structured study, practical programming skills, exposure to practitioners, project-based assignments, company visits, workshops, guest lectures, job opening referrals, and preparation for careers in risk management, banking, insurance, FinTech, consulting and further research.

curriculum.content:
Study format: Full-time (1 year) or Part-time (2 years). Each course consists of a three-hour lecture each week. Time & venue: weekday evenings & Saturdays at CUHK in Shatin.
Students are required to complete a minimum of **24 credits** in order to graduate. Students should take at least 2 elective courses at RMSC6000 level or above, or at STAT5000 level or above.
Part-time mode: the normative study period is two years. Students should satisfy the following requirements:
- 1st Year: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- 2nd Year: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- Total: **24 credits**
Suggested study plan for part-time mode:
- 1st Term of Year 1: RMSC5002, RMSC5101, RMSC6003
- 2nd Term of Year 1: RMSC5004, RMSC5102, STAT6105, STAT6104
- 1st Term of Year 2: RMSC5003, RMSC6002, STAT5103
- 2nd Term of Year 2: RMSC5001, RMSC6001, RMSC6007, STAT6209
Full-time mode: the normative study period is one year. Students should satisfy the following requirements:
- 1st Semester: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- 2nd Semester: Core courses: 6 credits; Elective courses: 6 credits
- Total: **24 credits**
Suggested study plan for full-time mode:
- 1st Term of Year 1: RMSC5002, RMSC5003, RMSC5101, RMSC6002, RMSC6003, STAT5103
- 2nd Term of Year 1: RMSC5001, RMSC5004, RMSC5102, RMSC6001, RMSC6007, RMSC6008, STAT5105, STAT6104, STAT6105, STAT6204, STAT6209
Core courses:
- RMSC 5001 Advanced Statistical Theory in Risk Management: modern applications of advanced statistical methods in finance, including Monte Carlo simulation, EWMA and GARCH model, Value at Risk, and data mining methods.
- RMSC 5002 Principles of Risk Management: fundamental concepts of risk and risk management, and risk management tools used in financial products.
- RMSC 5003 Risk Measures: methodologies of calculating Value-at-Risk (VaR), including historical simulation, parametric VaR, delta-gamma approximation and Monte-Carlo simulation.
- RMSC 5004 Cases for Risk Management in Practice / Special Topics in Risk Management: students need to present and discuss literatures assigned to them by the instructor on topics of current interest in financial risk management.
Elective courses:
- RMSC 5101 Statistical Methods in Risk Management and Finance
- RMSC 5102 Simulation Techniques in Risk Management and Finance
- RMSC 6001 Interest Rates and Fixed Incomes Risk Management
- RMSC 6002 Credit Risk Management
- RMSC 6003 Risk Management in Financial Institutions
- RMSC 6006 Portfolio Theory with Risk Management Perspective
- RMSC 6007 Risk and Financial Data Analytics with Python
- RMSC 6008 Practicum: students will be required to complete a project assigned by a company or an organization on a part-time basis, under the joint supervision of an instructor and a member of the company or organization; students will give a final project presentation and submit a written report.
- STAT 5103 High-Dimensional Data Analysis
- STAT 5105 Applied Survival Data Analysis
- STAT 6104 Financial Time Series
- STAT 6105 Basic Actuarial Principles and Their Applications
- STAT 6204 Advanced Time Series
- STAT 6209 Special Topics in Statistics
Other university requirements: students must fulfill the Term Assessment Requirement of the Graduate School, and a student must achieve a cumulative grade point average (GPA) of at least **2.0** in order to graduate.
Course exemption: students who passed FRM Part 1 Exam are eligible for exemption of core course RMSC5002 Principles of Risk Management. Only the course but not the units are exempted. Students who are exempted RMSC5002 must complete another 3-unit course to fulfil the graduation requirements.

program_overview.content:
**Programme Information**
- Award Title: **Master of Science in Risk, Insurance and Actuarial Analytics Degree** **(MSc in RIAA)**
- Intermediate Award: Postgraduate Diploma in Risk, Insurance and Actuarial Analytics (PD in RIAA)
- Study Mode: Full-Time
- Duration: Normal: 1 year; Maximum: 2 years
**Special Features**
- The degree gives a broad and in-depth coverage of the major areas in risk management, insurance and actuarial science with an emphasis on professional practice.
- The degree helps students obtain professional qualifications such as Chartered Insurance Institute (CII), Financial Risk Manager (FRM) and actuarial science related qualifications, e.g. Associate of the Society of Actuaries (ASA) / Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA).
- Combining finance, economics, computer science and quantitative skills training, the degree offers a comprehensive understanding of risk and insurance, thereby enhancing the degree's attractiveness to both students and potential employers.
- The program provides students with opportunities to gain access to an extensive network of alumni and industry professionals and benefit from dedicated career services, including job placement, resume workshops and interview preparation.
**Learning Outcomes**
- Explain the theories and practices of risk management, insurance and actuarial science;
- Devise suitable risk management and actuarial strategies for different individuals and corporations;
- Demonstrate a mastery of quantitative skills in applying risk and actuarial models and performing risk analysis;
- Apply risk and actuarial analytics and insurance products to control risk exposures; and
- Explain regulatory compliance and regulations for insurance businesses in the insurance market.
**Career Destination**
Career opportunities include positions in insurance companies, banks, and other related financial institutions. MPhil or PhD Programmes are also options.

program_overview.content:
Social Data Analytics (SDA) combines the analysis of large or complex data that arise from human and social interactions with social sciences theories and concepts. In the private, public and academic sectors, there is a strong demand for social scientists who are also trained in data science and computationally intensive methods.
MSocSc(SDA) pools computational and quantitative research expertise across the Faculty of Social Sciences to offer students the data analytical skills and prepare them for further doctoral training and to work as data sciences professionals in NGO and governmental agency, business, advertising, marketing, and other jobs across the knowledge economy that require integrating social sciences domain expertise with large datasets in computational systems.
The unique emphasis in Social Data Analytics is on the computational use of formal social sciences theories. This has two specific ends: a) simulating the behaviour of formal theories in computational contexts to generate largescale predictions, often requiring agent-based simulations to predict the behaviours and interactions among complex social systems and networks; and b) interpreting large-scale naturalistic data through the lens of these formal theories to improve generalisation, prediction, and explainability.
Programme Aims:
1. Provide students with the theory, skills and techniques they need to undertake data analytics in a social sciences context, enabling critical thinking and preparing them to work as data science professionals and for further doctoral training.
2. Engender in students an awareness of both the possibilities and limitations of a range of methodological approaches and techniques used across the social sciences in identifying and researching real-world problems.
3. Use teaching informed by research to provide a stimulating culture of learning, the development of high-level research skills, and enthusiasm for applying these within.
The HKU MSocSc(SDA) Programme is a 1-year full-time Programme that consists of a mandatory boot camp and three different categories of courses: (i) compulsory courses, (ii) elective courses, and (iii) capstone project.

curriculum.content:
Students are required to complete **5** compulsory courses, **3** elective courses and **1** capstone project throughout their studies. Before the commencement of the programme, all students must attend **a mandatory 18-hour social data analytics summer boot camp**. The boot camp will be taught over three to four days, organised around topics including R and RStudio, algebra, probability and statistics, objects and classes in R-Studio, data cleaning/reshaping/restructuring with the tidyverse, basic programming, and communicating/collaborating with RMarkdown, Rpres, Shiny and Github.
**Compulsory Courses**
- **MSDA7001 Introduction to social data analytics** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7002 Statistical foundations** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7003 Machine learning** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7004 Research design and inference in the social sciences** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
- **MSDA7005 Programming for social scientists** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.
**Elective Courses**
At least two elective courses from the following list*:
- **MSDA7101 Big data solutions to social problems** - 6 credits; Assessment: 100% coursework.

program_overview.content:
Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining MSc is based in London, Bloomsbury. It gives advanced understanding of GIScience, databases, spatial analysis, data mining, analytics and related areas, and builds specialist expertise to analyse, represent, and model large and complex spatio-temporal datasets. Study mode is full-time or part-time, with a duration of 1 calendar year full-time or 2 calendar years part-time.
This specialist MSc trains students to extract insights from large amounts of data to discover patterns and knowledge from spatio-temporal data. Teaching combines theory with extensive hands-on experience across big data, including spatio-temporal analysis and computation guided by statistical and machine learning techniques, space time data, parallel computing, system design, social media analysis, text mining, and programming. Students apply their skills to real-world scenarios, creating models for social media listening, understanding weather patterns, predicting earthquakes, and determining global warming trends. The programme also includes ethical and social angles to big data, helping students understand the wider context of their work.
The programme is ideal for students who want to elevate their expertise in big data to advance in a career or go on to further research. UCL welcomes applications from recent graduates in engineering, architecture, physical or computational sciences, mathematics, earth sciences, physics or related fields, and from those with recent professional experience.
The programme offers opportunities to study alongside expert academics and researchers in data science, cybercrime, computation, infrastructure, geospatial sciences, urban simulation, machine learning, and more. It is supported by close industry and research links, including exclusive seminars and exhibitions with industry leaders at UCL. Students gain hands-on experience with data acquisition tools, software, programming languages such as R and Python, real-case data, and open-source software. UCL’s Bloomsbury campus is in the heart of a London district known for cultural and educational institutions.
Graduates from the programme have gone on to work with employers such as UBS Investment Bank, Panasonic, Datacup, and Wegaw, while others have moved into research positions at institutions including the University of Cambridge and Universidad del Azuay ([Graduate Outcomes Survey 2017-22](https://public.tableau.com/app/profile/katy.coyte4085/viz/WhatDoUCLGraduatesDo/WhatdoUCLgraduatesdo)). The programme combines theory, practice, and innovation to provide a strong technical and contextual foundation for big data careers in industry or further research.
Students have regular opportunities to connect, collaborate, and build professional contacts through guest lectures, special seminars, collaborative group projects, field trips, site visits, case studies, workshops within the department and with industry partners, and [UCL Careers](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/careers) resources and events.
The MSc is delivered through seminars, lectures, laboratory work, projects, and practicals, often drawing on real-life industry case studies with opportunities for hands-on experience. Assessment is through examinations, presentations, essays, coursework, and a research project submitted as a dissertation. Full-time students can expect 12-16 hours of contact time per teaching week, plus around 20-25 hours per week of self-directed study and assessment work; the full-time course is approximately 35-40 hours a week.
The programme consists of compulsory modules, optional modules, and a dissertation/report. Full-time students complete the structure over the MSc, part-time students over 2 years, and modular/flexible students over the course of their studies. Upon successful completion of 180 credits, students are awarded an MSc in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining; upon successful completion of 120 credits, students are awarded a PG Dip in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining.

curriculum.content:
Study mode: Full-time or part-time. Duration: full-time **1 calendar year**; part-time **2 calendar years**. Programme starts September 2026.
Teaching and learning: This MSc programme is delivered through a mix of seminars, lectures, laboratory work, projects and practicals. Assessment is through examinations, presentations, essays, coursework, and a research project submitted as a dissertation. Full-time students can expect 12-16 hours of contact time per teaching week, plus around 20-25 hours per week of self-directed study and assessments. This is a full-time course, with an expected working schedule of approximately 35-40 hours a week.
Modules: Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of 180 credits, students are awarded an MSc in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining.
Programme structure:
- Full-time: total of **180 credits**; consists of 3 compulsory modules, 5 optional modules and a dissertation/report.
- Part-time: total of **180 credits over 2 years**; consists of 3 compulsory modules, 5 optional modules and a dissertation/report.
- Flexible: total of **180 credits** over the course of studies.
Compulsory modules:
- [Geospatial Science](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/geospatial-science-CEGE0094)
- [Machine Learning for Data Science](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/machine-learning-for-data-science-CEGE0004)

- [Geospatial Programming](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/geospatial-programming-CEGE0096)
- [Spatial Analysis and Geocomputation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-analysis-and-geocomputation-CEGE0097)
Optional modules:
- Web and Mobile GIS - Apps and Programming
- [Spatial Databases and Data Management](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/spatial-databases-and-data-management-CEGE0052)
- [Sensors and Location](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/sensors-and-location-CEGE0095)
- Introduction to Complex Infrastructure Systems
- [Urban Simulation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/urban-simulation-CASA0002)
- Mining Social and Geographic Datasets
- [Cybercrime](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/cybercrime-SECU0043)
A Postgraduate Diploma, consisting of five core modules (**75 credits**) and three optional modules (**45 credits**), taken full-time over nine months is also offered. Upon successful completion of **120 credits**, students are awarded a PG Dip in Spatio-temporal Analytics and Big Data Mining.

deferral_admission_policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer. However, if you need to defer for one of the reasons below, UCL will consider your request.
UCL will consider a request to defer only in the following circumstances:
- The serious illness of the offer holder or the serious illness of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The death of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The need to take parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months.
- Where the offer holder is directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster (i.e., war, earthquakes or flooding).
- The offer holder has been awarded a UCL scholarship (including UCL partnership agreements and Faculty awards); or a full scholarship (tuition fee and maintenance support) from a recognised funding body - for study in the following academic year. A “scholarship” does not include student loans.
- The offer holder holds an offer to study the **UCL International Pre-Masters**.
To be eligible for a deferral you must hold an unconditional offer which you have accepted. The exception is if you hold an offer for the International Pre-Masters, in which case an accepted conditional offer is allowed. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt, if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme.
If you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the above categories you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, however, applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.
To request a deferral for one of the above reasons, do so on the offer page of your application portal. If requesting a deferral due to illness or parental or adoption leave, you need to provide a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. If the request is based on a scholarship for study in the following academic year, you must upload a copy of your official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information before making a final decision.
An application cannot be deferred twice. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If your deferral request is unsuccessful, you may apply for the next academic year once applications open, however, applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that particular intake.
If your deferral request is approved, you will receive a new offer letter and may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date. If your request to defer is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
You must meet all your conditions and hold an unconditional offer before you can enrol.
- Your offer letter will contain information on any deadlines that apply to your offer. If circumstances mean that you will not be able to meet your offer conditions by these dates, contact the [Graduate Admissions Team](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/study/prospective-students/stay-touch/ask-admissions-postgraduate-and-teacher-training-enquiries).
- Academic degree documents: “We cannot accept anything other than **final official documents** to meet the conditions of your offer.”
- English Language conditions: If you need to take an English language test to meet your offer conditions, UCL recommends booking a test as early as possible. Official results must be provided; UCL will not accept screenshots of your results portal.
- [UCL Pre-sessional English courses](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses/pre-sessional-english-courses/pg): “You can take a Pre-sessional English course at UCL to settle the English language condition in your offer.”
- To clear offer conditions, upload documents to the applicant portal if you have an academic condition and have received degree documents and transcripts from your university. Proof of English language proficiency must also be uploaded to the applicant portal.
- If you have not met your academic offer condition, you should still upload your documents; the Admissions team will still consider whether your offer can be confirmed.
- If you have not met your English language test condition but have received scores that meet the **UCL level 1 requirement**, you can still supply your test scores to UCL for review. UCL “will not ordinarily accept a lower score than stipulated in the offer” and “cannot consider test scores that do not meet the **UCL level 1 requirement**.”

program_overview.content:
The MSc Supply Chain and Analytics is a **one-year full-time** programme developed to equip students with the qualitative and quantitative skills and knowledge to effectively manage supply chains using AI and business analytics. The programme focuses on business analytics, digital technologies, AI, and supply chain management, with emphasis on tools, processes, and practices that organisations can use to improve the productivity, sustainability, and resilience of operations and supply chains.
Students develop capabilities to evaluate, manage, and improve operations and supply chain processes; analyse operations and make evidence-based decisions; design effective and sustainable supply chain strategies and processes; develop and manage relationships in global supply chains; manage supply chain risks; and improve resilience. The programme provides exposure to real-world business problems, professional connections with employers and alumni, a culturally diverse learning environment, and access to world-class facilities.
Typical careers include Purchasing Manager, Supply Chain Manager, Operations Manager, Logistics Manager, Business Analysts, and Consultants.
- **Industry links:** The Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone is a final semester module that combines learning from across the degree and includes a dynamic online simulation where students work in teams to develop the global strategy of a firm in a game-based scenario. Capstone projects are applied practical projects where students work with real-world organisations to generate solutions to complex challenges.
- **Capstone pathways:** Students can choose from a Consultancy-Based Dissertation, Analytical Problem-Solving Dissertation, or Internship-Based Dissertation.
- **Career development:** A module on Developing Careers and Employability Skills is dedicated to enhancing students’ employability. Employer insights, networking circles, LinkedIn workshops, and job talks are embedded throughout the programme.
- **Student experience:** The programme focuses on how global managers and organisations navigate grand challenges and megatrends, including artificial intelligence, data analytics, sustainability, geopolitical instability, innovation, ethics, and doing business in emerging markets.
MSc Supply Chain and Analytics is structured across **3 semesters**. Students who successfully complete eight taught modules (120 CATS) and a Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone module in semester 3 are awarded an MSc in Supply Chain and Analytics. Exit qualifications are also available: a Postgraduate Diploma after 120 CATS from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate after 60 CATS from taught modules.
Students take seven core modules and choose one optional module, then complete a final capstone dissertation. The modules cover key knowledge and skills in operations and supply chain management, business analytics, and AI. Semester 1 provides knowledge of Business Analytics and AI; Semester 2 focuses on more specialised areas of supply chain management, including digitalisation, sustainability, and advanced analytics skills; Semester 3 is centred on the Capstone Dissertation, where students integrate supply chain management with AI and business analytics techniques and apply skills to real-world business scenarios.
People teaching the programme include [Dr Byron Graham](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/byron-graham), Reader in Business Analytics; [Dr Rohit Nishant](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/rohit-nishant), Professor of Information Systems; and [Prof. Min Zhang](https://pure.qub.ac.uk/en/persons/min-zhang), Professor in Operations Management and Business Analytics.
For semesters 1 and 2, students have 4 classes per week, all 3 hours long. Classes are delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops, using case studies, software demonstrations, practical workshops, role plays, groupwork, scenario discussions and organisation visits. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through capstone projects; students are assigned dedicated academic support and company mentors where relevant.
Assessments are applied and practical in focus, encouraging students to produce actionable recommendations for real-world scenarios and problems. Assessment types include presentations, reports, podcasts, game-based simulations, analytics practicals, teamwork and business plans.
Course location: [Queen's Business School](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/queens-business-school/). Queen’s Business School includes a 6,000 square metre building with digital infrastructure for media lecture capture, TED Talk provision and collaborative breakout sessions, a 250-seat tiered educational space, 120-seat Harvard style lecture theatre, 150-seat computer laboratory, breakout study spaces, FinTrU Trading Room, café, and Business Engagement and Employability Hub.

curriculum.content:
Attendance: **1 year (Full-time)**. Course location: [Queen's Business School](https://www.qub.ac.uk/schools/queens-business-school/).
MSc Supply Chain and Analytics is a one-year programme structured across **3 semesters**. Students who successfully complete **eight taught modules (120 CATS)** and a **Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone module** in semester 3 are awarded an MSc in Supply Chain and Analytics. Exit qualifications are also available: students may exit with a Postgraduate Diploma by successfully completing **120 CATS** from taught modules or a Postgraduate Certificate by successfully completing **60 CATS** from taught modules.
Students on the programme will take **seven core modules** and will get to choose **one optional module** (eight modules in total at **15 CATS**). They will also complete a final capstone dissertation.
- **Semester 1:** Statistics for Business; Operations Analytics; Gen AI and Business Intelligence; Design Thinking with AI.
- **Semester 2:** Data Driven Decision Making; Digital Supply Chain Management; Supply Chain Sustainability; and one optional module from **Cybersecurity and Digital Risk Management** or **Emerging Technologies for Business**.
- **Semester 3:** The Capstone Dissertation module is the culmination of the MSc Supply Chain Analytics programme, allowing students to apply skills and knowledge from the taught modules to real-world business scenarios and propose viable and realistic solutions to an organisational or societal challenge.
The Supply Chain and Analytics Capstone is a final semester module that fosters capstone thinking and combines learnings from across the degree. It involves a dynamic online simulation where students work in teams to develop the global strategy of a firm in a game-based scenario. Capstone Projects are applied practical projects where students work with real-world organisations to generate solutions to complex challenges. There are **3 pathways** to choose from:
- **Consultancy-Based Dissertation:** engaging directly with an organisation to identify opportunities where supply chain analytics can be strategically implemented.
- **Analytical Problem-Solving Dissertation:** addressing a clearly defined organisational or societal problem through supply chain analytics techniques.
- **Internship-Based Dissertation:** designed for students undertaking an internship, where they critically analyse the ways in which the host organisation deploys supply chain analytics solutions to enhance its competitive position or resolve challenges.
For semesters 1 and 2, students will have **4 classes per week**, all **3 hours long**. Classes will be delivered as a mix of seminars, lectures and workshops. Semester 3 is structured around independent and applied learning through the capstone projects where students choose between different pathways.

program_overview.content:
**Unleashing the Power of Data Analytics in Sustainable World: Introducing the Master of Science in Sustainability and Environmental Analytics**
The Master of Science in Sustainability and Environmental Analytics (SEA) programme offered by Lingnan University's Science Unit (SU) is a response to the growing demand for sustainable development and environmental management in the 21st century. The programme is designed to equip students with the necessary skills and knowledge to address the challenges of sustainable development and environmental management and prepare them for the complex challenges they will encounter in their careers.
What sets SEA apart is its focus on data analytics to assist sustainable transformation and achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The programme is centred around the SDGs, addressing a majority of them, including affordable and clean energy (SDG7), sustainable cities and communities (SDG11), and climate action (SDG13), and among others. Students will learn about strategies for analysing environmental data and designing effective sustainability plans, gaining a deep understanding of the social, economic, and environmental factors that influence sustainable development.
Data analytics is also a key tool for implementing Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Planning, which is a core component of the programme. SEA students will learn how to use data analytics to evaluate and improve the ESG performance of organisations and projects, as well as to communicate their ESG impacts to stakeholders and tackle the ESG challenges.
SEA is developed in collaboration with renowned industry partners, ensuring that the programme meets future industry needs while prioritizing sustainable growth. SEA students will gain hands-on experience in applying their knowledge to real-world environmental and sustainability problems through field trips led by NGOs and/or experts in the field, as well as through research training and internship opportunities. These experiential learning deepens students' understanding of the concepts and theories taught in the programme, improve their experiences and skills in tackling global and local real-world problems, and more importantly enhance their up-to-date understanding of the job market.

program_overview.content:
The Urban Analytics MSc provides knowledge and skills to design and conduct appropriate analyses, with experience working with cutting-edge datasets and exposure to emerging tools, including those driven by artificial intelligence (AI). It is taught at the [Glasgow: Gilmorehill campus](https://www.gla.ac.uk/explore/campuses/gilmorehill/) and is available as **12 months full-time** or **24 months part-time**. Academic contacts include [Dr Michael Sinclair](https://www.gla.ac.uk/schools/socialpolitical/staff/michaelsinclair/) and [socpol-student-recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk](mailto:socpol-student-recruitment@glasgow.ac.uk).
The programme provides a critical appreciation of the potential for big data and urban analytics, including AI-driven methods, to inform urban planning and policy making, as well as an understanding of practical and ethical limitations. It offers hands-on experience with statistical and GIS software and programming tools used to capture, process and analyse data. Students are exposed to cutting-edge datasets typically encountered by urban analysts and learn to apply analytical methods, from traditional statistical approaches to emerging AI techniques, to extract insights and address real-world urban challenges. The programme also develops students’ ability to convey results of complex data analyses in ways that have impact on policy makers and public debates.
Students benefit from the programme’s strong connection with the [Urban Big Data Centre](https://www.ubdc.ac.uk/) (UBDC), Glasgow’s world-leading urban analytics centre of expertise, and from close work with [the Data Lab](https://www.thedatalab.com/), an internationally leading research and innovation centre in data science. Students may have opportunities to visit [Aalto University](https://www.aalto.fi/en) in Helsinki, Finland under a funded academic exchange programme through the UK Turing Scheme, dependent on yearly funding success.
The programme structure includes five core and two to four optional courses, plus a research-based dissertation. Knowledge-focused courses introduce the context for urban planning and policy making, while skills-focused courses on statistical methods, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and programming provide opportunities to use a variety of real-world datasets. Courses are delivered via a mix of lectures, tutorials, supervised computing lab sessions and small group work. A wide range of optional courses allows students to pursue personal interests and enhance particular skills or domain-specific knowledge such as transport studies or urban design.
Career opportunities for graduates include positions in government agencies, urban planning organisations, city governments, public health boards, retail businesses, real estate companies, transport, and other private consulting firms. Alumni have also gone on to work in non-profit organisations and to be accepted into highly competitive PhD programmes in the UK, Europe, USA, and China, ranging from government, universities and technology companies.
The programme offers frequent connection with industry. It has strong links with the Urban Big Data Centre (UBDC), a research centre and national data service based at the University of Glasgow, and a vast majority of academic staff teaching on the MSc programme are involved with the centre. Students are regularly invited to join the CUSP London Data Dives, applying their learning in a fast-paced environment to improve understanding of real-world data science and develop skills in formulating questions, analysing data and presenting results. All students are eligible for the Data Lab Academy and have access to paid internships through the Data Lab.

If you are made a conditional offer, then you should upload your final results (transcript and degree certificate) when you recieve them.
You can normally apply for a programme if you have not yet met the English language requirements. If you receive an offer, it will be conditional on you meeting the English language requirements by the date stated on your offer letter. Please note a few exceptions to the rule where an English test is required at time of application exist. Please check the programme page for details.
If you cannot provide all the required documents when you apply, it is still possible to apply, but you must include in your application:

The university may then be able to make you a conditional offer. You can then upload the remaining documents at a later date. Please note: some programmes require all the listed documents before a decision can be made.

program_overview.content:
The Master of Science in Urban Analytics (MSc(Urban Analytics)) is offered as a one-year full-time programme. The evolving technological basis of cities is reshaping our urban life and allowing us to understand, plan, manage and optimise cities in completely new ways. The MSc(Urban Analytics) programme is designed to train and upskill students and professionals able to apply novel urban science and analytics in planning and managing the development of cities. Aiming to bridge the disciplines of social science, urban planning and design and data science, the programme provides a balance between analytical and practical skills on the one hand, and on the other, domain knowledge and urban theory from social, economic, behavioural, environmental and management sciences.
**Programme aims**
- Equip students and urban professionals with cutting-edge analytics and modelling skills
- Enable good understanding of urban sciences underlying smart city development techniques
- Support urban policy makers and urban planning/design/surveying practitioners with urban analytics
**Professional Accreditation**
MUA has received “specialist” accreditation from the Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI). Graduates could become members of RTPI under the [Associate Route](https://www.rtpi.org.uk/membership/about-rtpi-membership/apply/associate/). They can become RTPI Associate Members after 2 years of planning experience and then become RTPI [Chartered Member](https://www.rtpi.org.uk/membership/about-rtpi-membership/apply/chartered-town-planner/) after another 2 years of planning experience via [A-APC](https://www.rtpi.org.uk/membership/assessment-of-professional-competence/associate-apc/).
**Careers of Graduates**
The majority of MUA graduates are working in planning and design institute/company/organizations in HK and Mainland China. Another group of students find urban analytics/data scientist jobs in world leading finance and internet companies.
**Main Teaching Staff**
Yeh, Anthony G.O.; Ma, Jun; Yang, Tianren; Zhang, Xiaohu; Zhao, Zhan; Zhou, Yulun.

curriculum.content:
MSc(Urban Analytics) requires **69 credits within the 1-year full-time study**. The curriculum of the programme consists of seven urban analytics courses (6 credits each), two urban theory courses (6 credits each; two from an approved list of courses), and a dissertation/capstone project (15 credits).
**Urban analytics courses (Compulsory)**
- Programming and Foundations in Urban Data Analysis
- Geographic Information System (GIS) for Urban and Regional Planning Development
- Urban Big Data Analytics
- Artificial Intelligence for Future Cities
- Spatial Mobilities Analytics
- Spatial Planning Analytics
- Science of Cities
**Urban theory courses (Choose Two)**
- Urban Development Theories
- Planning Practice, Law and Ethics in Hong Kong
- Public Transport Systems
- Transport Policy and Planning
- Transport Economics
- Transport Network Analysis and Modelling
- Housing, Planning and Sustainability
- Globalization and Urban and Regional Development in China
- Planning Future Cities and Regions
- International Planning Policy and Practice
- Housing Economics
- Transitional Cities: Urban and Housing Development
- Design, Survey and Modelling for Urban Health
- Principles of Healthy Cities
- Values of Urban Design: Urban, Social, Environmental Economics
- Morphologies and Urban Design Theories
\* The course list may vary at the time of selection.
**Dissertation/ capstone project**
- Dissertation OR
- Smart Planning and Design Studio

cost_of_attendance.content:

- Books and supplies (excluding personal computers & accessories): around **HK$11,440-HK$55,600 p.a.**

- Hall miscellaneous charges: **HK$2,000-HK$3,000 p.a.**; these include students' association membership fees, compulsory high table fees, room and/or smartcard deposits, etc., excluding air-conditioning charge which varies with individual lifestyle and seasons (approximately **HK$200 per month in summer**).
- Compulsory hall meal charges: **HK$9,000-HK$12,000 p.a.** (not all meals are covered).

conditional_admission_policy.content:
If you have not completed your undergraduate study at the time of application, you are required to provide your latest official transcript of your current study and other available documents to the Faculty for admission panel’s consideration. If you receive a **conditional offer of admission** subsequently, you are required to resubmit the finalized official transcript in due course for vetting purpose.
Applicants who receive a **Conditional Offer letter** should forward visa application documents to the Hong Kong Immigration Department via CEDARS (for overseas students) or China Affairs Office (for mainland students), and are advised to apply as soon as possible because visa completion takes around **8-10 weeks**.
If an applicant receives a Conditional Offer and pays the deposit for securing the place, then receives the Firm Offer later, the applicant must settle the balance of the first installment of the composition fee and the caution money (**HKD 350**) by the deadline stated in the Firm Offer letter.

application_materials.content:
As part of your online application you will need to upload scanned documents. All academic documentation should be scans of the originals, not photographs. The scans should be complete and of a good quality, showing the 4 corners of all pages of the original document. Please do not merge separate qualifications together.
Your application must include the following:
- A copy of your degree certificate and complete transcript. If you are still studying, please provide your latest transcript plus a list of modules yet to be studied.
- Evidence of your final or current overall % or GPA.
- A copy of your grading scale/scheme if this is not on your degree transcript.
- CV/Resume. Please include an up-to-date CV showing your relevant work experience and education.
- CAS, BRP and Visa - for international students that have previously studied in the UK on a student visa.
If you have them, please include the following:
- Your approved English Language test, if applicable.
- A personal statement. A personal statement is not required as standard however it could strengthen your application in circumstances such as explaining a gap in your education or if your education/degree subject is not directly related to the programme. The personal statement should be no more than one side of A4 and should include details on how your prior studies are linked to your future plans and why you want to study the programme you have applied for.
Documents which are not required:
- References are not usually required, but in specific borderline cases we may request a reference to help us make a decision.
Applicants with Indian degrees should include:
- A copy of your bachelor's degree certificate.
- A copy of your consolidated mark sheet.
- A copy of your semester mark sheets.
- A copy of your University marking scheme.
- Official evidence of your current/final overall award as a percentage (%).
Supporting documents should always be sent via an enquiry or condition response in the applicant portal as this will link the document to the correct application automatically.

interview_requirements.content: We aim to make decisions within **three to five weeks** if all necessary documents have been received. You will be contacted directly if we require any further information or wish to invite you for an interview or audition. You will receive an email asking you to check your applicant portal for more details.

academic_requirements.content:
A bachelor degree with a **2:1 (hons)** in a subject including, but not limited to, geography, urban planning, engineering, land resource, statistics, data science, information management, transport or computer science, where quantitative and/or computing skills can be evidenced. Alternative subjects which may be considered include, but are not limited to, architecture, finance, mathematics or psychology. All applicants should possess an interest in using data science to tackle real-life urban challenges.
Applicants with a **2:2 (hons)** will be considered on a case-by-case basis where they can demonstrate relevant work experience or competence in a relevant specialist field. Professional qualifications and relevant experience can also be considered.
International applicants: The University accepts a range of [international equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/admissions-qualifications).
Applicants from China: accepted postgraduate qualifications include **4 year Bachelor degrees**. The University of Leeds uses institutional lists when assessing applications from accepted Chinese institutions, and requirements may vary by school. Applicants should check that their institution is accepted and that they meet the entry requirements before making an application. If the programme asks for **2.1**, applicants from China need **70%-85%, depending on institution**. If the programme asks for **2.2**, applicants from China need **70%-80%, depending on institution**.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
IELTS **6.5 overall**, with **no less than 6.0 in any component**. For other English qualifications, read [English language equivalent qualifications](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/international-admissions/doc/entry-requirements "English language equivalent qualifications").
International students who do not meet the English language requirements for this programme may be able to study a postgraduate pre-sessional English course, designed with a progression route to the degree programme. Options include [Language for Science (6 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i204/language-for-science), [Language for Science: General Science (10 weeks)](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/i203/language-for-science-general-science), the [six week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j615/online-academic-english-presessional-6-weeks-), the [10 week online pre-sessional](https://courses.leeds.ac.uk/j614/online-academic-english-presessional-10-weeks-), and longer [postgraduate pre-sessional English courses](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre-courses/doc/masters-pre-sessional-english).

program_overview.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: on campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
Urban data science and analytics are critical to helping cities evolve, providing insight into urban processes, dynamics within cities, and local and global issues. The Urban Data Science and Analytics MSc offers the opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge of the methods and approaches of data science and learn how to apply them in understanding cities and setting urban policy. The course combines technical training in the latest data science techniques, from data wrangling to machine learning, visualisation, and beyond, with the critical thinking needed to interrogate and understand complex urban and mobility challenges.
At the heart of this course is a commitment to tackling real-world challenges facing cities. Researchers at the University of Leeds are finding novel data-driven solutions to challenges such as traffic congestion, social and economic equality, healthy cities, and competition for resources. Graduates are intended to be equipped with the experience, technical skills, and knowledge needed to pursue careers in areas such as data science, software development, or urban planning.
Why study at Leeds:
- Learn the latest innovations in critical areas of urban analytics with exposure to impactful research across the [School of Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research), the [Institute for Transport Studies](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/transport-research), the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/), the national institute for data science and artificial intelligence which feeds directly into the course.
- Advance skills and knowledge in key topics sought after in industry, including programming for data science, creative coding for urban problems and analytics for urban policy.
- Tailor the course to career aspirations with optional study in areas like geographic data visualisation, geodemographics and transport data science.
- Conduct project work to develop transferable research skills, investigating a real-world issue that explores and develops individual interests.
- Access specialist facilities including research-grade laboratories in the [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and a GIS computer cluster with industry-standard software.
- Experience theoretical and practical teaching delivered by academics actively engaged in research and part of the [Institute for Spatial Data Science](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research-centre-spatial-analysis-policy), [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/) and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/collaborate-turing/current-partnerships-and-collaborations/university-leeds).
- Build industry connections through working with external organisations and stakeholders, co-developing creative solutions to urban problems.
- Put theory into practice with fieldwork opportunities in an urban context, observing how data science can be used to create and shape urban policy and how policies impact urban systems and processes.
The course combines technical training in data science with a rich exploration of urban systems and policy, enabling students to create novel data analyses informed by a contextual understanding of cities. The first term introduces the theory and application of urban data science through complementary study of data science applications, urban analysis, and programming. The second term builds and expands this knowledge through urban policy analytics, field trips, creative problem-solving, group work with industry experts, and optional deeper training in spatial analysis or transport.
Over the summer months students complete a 60-credit dissertation-style research project, bringing together learning from each module and producing a documented code workbook with a supporting 5000-word practical briefing. The project focuses on how data science methods can inform policy interventions and decision-making, allows students to apply learning to a real-world problem, and may include the opportunity to work with industry partners. Example dissertation themes include urban economics, cities and crime, urban inequalities, transport and mobility, housing and real estate, health and wellbeing, smart cities, pollution, vulnerable populations, geodemographics, and fieldwork.
Field courses provide opportunities to explore urban analytics on the ground in urban environments. Students consider cities from different perspectives, observe urban systems across policy areas, collect data, make observations and assessments, and explore cities in new ways.
The course incorporates innovative modes of delivery with a focus on practical, problem-based learning. Face-to-face learning in workshops, small groups, drop-ins, laboratories, lectures, and seminars is combined with teaching and learning delivered using interactive digital platforms. Students are taught by an experienced team of academics and researchers actively engaged in cutting-edge research and part of the [Institute for Spatial Data Science](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography-research-centre-spatial-analysis-policy), [Leeds Institute for Data Analytics](https://lida.leeds.ac.uk/), and the [Alan Turing Institute](https://www.turing.ac.uk/). Teaching may also be delivered by industry professionals and trained postgraduate researchers.
Assessment is primarily through the production of code and critical analysis for the exploration of urban phenomena and problems. Some modules focus more on qualitative analysis of urban systems, while others incorporate team-based assessment. Code and analyses through a personal protected GitHub repository are documented and act as a portfolio of work for future employers.
This course is taught by the [School of Geography](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/geography), [School of Computer Science](https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing), and [Institute for Transport Studies](https://environment.leeds.ac.uk/transport).
Career opportunities: the course teaches in-depth technical knowledge and skills in data science along with training in workflow practice, teamwork, and “hacking” sought by employers. Students also build an online portfolio of work developed throughout the course to demonstrate skills to prospective employers. On completion, graduates have the technical knowledge to secure employment in local government, companies handling spatial data, start-ups, transportation authorities and operators, urban planners and consultancies such as Arup and Mott MacDonald, in roles such as data scientist, data analyst or software developer. Previous students on this course have secured positions including Data Analytics at Amey, Graduate Scheme at Ernst & Young, and Data Science Internships at LIDA.
Work placements and industry experience: Masters students at Leeds have the opportunity to gain real-world industry experience with the Global Industry Programme, developing professional skills and gaining insight into working in their chosen field by solving a real business problem from a live company brief. The programme is fully online and designed to fit around studies, offers professional networking opportunities, builds consultancy experience with a UK or international organisation, involves team work across disciplines, and helps students put course teaching into practice.

curriculum.content:
Start date: September 2026. Delivery type: On campus. Duration: 12 Months (Full time).
The course combines technical training in data science with a rich exploration of urban systems and policy, enabling you to create novel data analyses that are informed by a contextual understanding of cities.
- Semester 1: Data Science for Practical Applications; Analysing Cities; Programming for Spatial Data Science.
- Semester 2: Analytics for Urban Policy; Creative Coding for Real-World Problems; optional modules incorporating deeper training in spatial analysis or transport training.
[For more information and a full list of typical modules available on this course, please read Urban Data Science and Analytics MSc in the course catalogue](https://catalogue.leeds.ac.uk/Programme/202627?code=MSC-UDS%26A-FT).
Compulsory modules:
- **Programming for Spatial Data Science – 15 credits**
- **Data Science for Practical Applications – 15 credits**
- **Creative Coding for Real-World Problems – 15 credits**
- **Analysing Cities – 15 credits**
- **Analytics for Urban Policy – 30 credits**
- **Urban Data Science Project – 60 credits**: over the summer months you'll work on a 60-credit dissertation-style research project, producing a documented code workbook with a supporting 5000-word practical briefing. You'll also have the opportunity to work with industry partners on this project.
Example dissertation themes for Urban Data Science and Analytics MSc include:
- Urban economics
- Cities and crime
- Urban inequalities
- Transport and mobility
- Housing and real estate
- Health and wellbeing
- Smart cities
- Pollution
- Vulnerable populations
- Geodemographics
- Fieldwork
Optional modules are indicative of typical options:
- **Geographic Data Visualisation & Analysis – 15 credits**
- **Geodemographics and Neighbourhood Analysis – 15 credits**
- **Transport Data Collection and Analysis – 15 credits**
- **Transport Data Science – 15 credits**
Field courses provide students an opportunity to explore urban analytics ‘on the ground’ in inspiring urban environments, with a chance to collect data, make observations and assessments, and explore cities.
The course incorporates workshops, small groups, drop-ins, laboratories, lectures, and seminars, combined with teaching and learning delivered using interactive digital platforms. The ‘Creative Coding’ module focuses on problem-based learning, where you'll work with other students in teams to tackle problems and datasets provided by external stakeholders.
While studying at Leeds, you’ll have the chance to work with clients and gain consultancy experience as part of a 2-week online Global Industry Programme.
