deferral_admission_policy.content: Please note that we do not permit deferrals.

conditional_admission_policy.content:
A conditional offer from the University of Leeds means you need to achieve the grades or points outlined in your offer letter. The offer letter will also explain any English language requirements, if applicable.
- If you have an academic offer condition, the University may need to see your degree certificate and transcripts as evidence.
- If you have an English language condition, you may be able to meet the requirements by taking a [pre-sessional course at the Language Centre](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english).
- You can upload evidence that you have met your conditions and accept your offer in the [application portal](https://myleedsportal.leeds.ac.uk/signin-landing/).
- You may have to accept your offer again if it becomes unconditional.
- If your offer has an academic condition, you will need to include official translations alongside your final academic documents if they were not originally produced in English.
- If you take a [pre-sessional English course](https://www.leeds.ac.uk/language-centre/doc/postgraduate-pre-sessional-english) with the Language Centre to meet your language condition, you may be eligible for a combined offer. This means that when you pass your pre-sessional, and have met any conditions in your offer letter, you are automatically enrolled on your degree course.

application_materials.content:
All supporting documents including GMAT/ TOEFL/ IELTS scores must reach SMU by the stipulated application phase deadlines. Applicants should get ready contact details of two referrals for uploading and read the Applicant's Guide to Admission before submitting the application online.
How to Submit Your Application: complete the online application form and attach copies of the required documents as instructed. Keep a copy of your submission for your records. Your application will only be processed when all required documents have been received.
**Documents to submit**
1. Updated Resume
2. Undergraduate Degree Scroll
3. Undergraduate Degree Transcript
4. Any other supporting documents
5. SMU Admissions Test/GMAT/GRE
6. IELTS/TOEFL if undergraduate degree was not taught in English
7. Passport
8. Two References: please provide the name, email and contact number of two referees (they can be from your colleagues, superiors or friends). Referees will be notified to complete their referral forms online.
Applicants must also provide a personal statement explaining why they want to take the programme and how it fits with their career aspiration. Applicants are also required to provide contacts and details of two referees; an automated email upon submission of application will be sent to them to fill up the referral form.

interview_requirements.content:
Eligible candidates will be shortlisted for an interview with the Admissions Panel. Interviews will be conducted between October to June for shortlisted applicants, and successful applicants will be informed within 1-2 weeks after the interview.
The application criteria state: “Shortlisted applicants will be invited for an online interview by members of the MSA Admissions Panel.”
FAQ: “Only shortlisted applicants are invited for a personal interview. This will allow us to assess the applicants holistically, taking into account his/her achievements in all areas and to select candidates who have the commitment, experience, motivation and potential to benefit from, and contribute to, the programme.” For international students, telephone interviews will be conducted if they are not in Singapore.

application_deadlines.content:
The online application for the **August 2026 intake** starts **1 August 2025** with the following admissions phases:
- Phase 1 - **1 Aug to 31 Aug 2025** (Early Admission)
- Phase 2 - **1 Sep to 31 Dec 2025**
- Phase 3 - **1 Jan to 31 March 2026**
- Phase 4 - **1 Apr to 31 May 2026**
All supporting documents including GMAT/ TOEFL/ IELTS scores must reach us by the stipulated deadlines above.

academic_requirements.content:
- Applicants must demonstrate **good prior academic performance in an undergraduate degree from a recognised institution of higher learning** / a **Good Bachelor's Degree**.
- Applicants must have sufficient background in **Accounting/Finance/Statistics/Business**; the application criteria also state applicants must have sufficient background in **Mathematics/Calculus**.
- Relevant working experience is not compulsory, but applicants with relevant/post-undergraduate working experience “will have an added advantage” and work experience “will be considered favourably by the MSA Admission Panel.”
- To assess sufficient background in Statistics/Accounting/Finance/Business, criteria include satisfactory completion of some mathematical courses at university level, completion of at least two mathematical courses at polytechnic level with **minimum B grade**, or an acceptable foundation in mathematics at GCE A-level or O-level or its equivalent.
- Applicants without a bachelor's degree are not eligible: “Our accreditation from the professional bodies specifically states that our applicants must have a bachelor's degree. Applicants without a bachelor's degree will not be eligible for the programme.”
- For SMU Admissions Test/GMAT/GRE exemption only: SMU Bachelor’s degree graduates with a **minimum cGPA of 3.0/4.0** within 5 years of graduation, and SUTD/NUS/NTU/SUSS/SIT Bachelor’s degree graduates with a **minimum cGPA of 3.5/5.0** within 5 years of graduation, are exempted; however, meeting the cGPA academic input does not guarantee acceptance.

gre_gmat_requirements.content:
- Applicants have the option to take [SMU Admissions Test (SMUAT)](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/sites/masters.smu.edu.sg/files/PDF%20docs/SMU%20candidate%20guide_refreshed.pdf) or GMAT or GRE as an admission test for application to the MSA programme.
- You are required to take an Admission Test for admission to the MSA programme, regardless of your academic background or prior qualifications. You may choose to take the GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) / GRE (Graduate Record Examinations General Test), or the [SMUAT (Singapore Management University Admissions Test)](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/sites/masters.smu.edu.sg/files/PDF%20docs/SMU%20Admission%20Test%20Factsheet.pdf).
- If you have previously taken the GMAT or GRE, it must have been taken within **five years** of the date of your application submission.
- The following groups of candidates are exempted from GMAT/GRE/SMU Admissions Test: SMU Bachelor’s degree graduates with a minimum **cGPA of 3.0/4.0** (within **5 years** of graduation); SUTD/NUS/NTU/SUSS/SIT Bachelor’s degree graduates with a minimum **cGPA of 3.5/5.0** (within **5 years** of graduation). However, meeting the cGPA academic input does not guarantee acceptance and candidates may still be asked to take the GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test.
- Official score reports can be sent via the following Institution Codes: GMAT: **F8D-3B-44**; GRE: **2861** (Department Code: **4001 - Accounting**).
- To enhance the competitiveness of your application, you should attain a **GMAT score of 600 or higher**, OR a **GMAT Focus edition score of 595 or higher**.
- To make your application more competitive, you should achieve a minimum **GRE combined score of verbal and quantitative components of 312**.
- GMAT score with a minimum score of at least **60 percentile for quantitative component** may be used in evaluating the applicant's background in statistics/accounting/finance/business.
- Candidates without GMAT/GRE or with low scores have the option to sit for the [SMU Admissions Test (SMUAT)](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/sites/masters.smu.edu.sg/files/PDF%20docs/SMU%20candidate%20guide_refreshed.pdf). However, if you don't sit for SMUAT, then we will need your GMAT/GRE score to assess your application. SMU's GMAT institution code for MSA is **F8D-3B-44**.
- GMAT/GRE scores are valid for **5 years** after the test date. If your GMAT/GRE results are older than **5 years**, you will need to re-sit your GMAT/GRE.

english_proficiency_requirements.content:
Applicants must show proficiency in the English language. A **TOEFL (Min score: 90 or Band 4.5)** or **IELTS (min. score of 6.5)** test is required if the applicant's undergraduate degree was not conducted in English.
If your undergraduate studies were not taught in English, you must take the IELTS (International English Language Testing System) or TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language). An **IELTS (min. score of 6.5)** or **TOEFL (Min. score: 90 or Band: 4.5)** report is required. Either test must be taken within the last **two years** of your application submission. You will need to email the unofficial results of your test to the SMU Admissions Office and make a request at the relevant test centre to send your official score report to SMU.
All supporting documents including GMAT/ TOEFL/ IELTS scores must reach SMU by the stipulated application deadlines. Documents to submit include: IELTS/TOEFL if undergraduate degree was not taught in English.
SMU's institution code for TOEFL is **9014**; official score reports can be sent with TOEFL institution code **9014** (Department Name: Accounting).
TOEFL or IELTS test is required if the medium of instruction in your undergraduate or graduate education was not English. More information can be obtained from the [TOEFL](https://www.ets.org/toefl/) website and the [IELTS](https://www.ielts.org/) website. TOEFL/IELTS scores are valid for **2 years** after the test date.

program_overview.content:
The MSA is designed for professionals who are interested in developing expertise in applying data technology into their domain knowledge to solve business problems, especially in the finance and accounting sectors. The availability of massive amounts of data has created a high demand for skilled data analytics professionals who can analyse such data and obtain the insight needed for informed decision-making. This is extremely vital to accounting and financial services firms as they have been dealing with large amount of information produced by their clients.
Duration: 18 months

curriculum.content:
- Duration: **12-18 months full-time** (with flexibility to complete in 12 months) or **24 months part-time**.
- The MSA programme consists of **15 course units (CU)**, including **8 CUs Programme Core, 4 CUs Track Electives, 2 CUs Open Electives and 1 CU Professional Development Courses**, taught over 24 months on a part-time basis or over 12-18 months on a full-time basis, commencing in August of each calendar year.
- Full-time students may continue from August to January after Term 3 for an internship and/or global immersion programmes. Part-time students will be enrolled in the evening classes.
- Classes are conducted on weekday evenings from **7:00pm to 10:15pm** and on some Saturdays **8:45am to 12:00pm** and **1:00pm to 4:15pm**.
Programme Core - **8 CUs**:
- ACCT651 Managing Sustainable Value Creation
- ACCT686 Financial Reporting and Analysis in the IFRS World
- ACCT648 Applied Statistics for Data Analysis
- ACCT649 Programming with Data
- ACCT652 Data Management
- ACCT653 Forecasting and Forensic Analytics
- ACCT679 Visual Analytics for Accounting
- ACCT685 Accounting Processes and Analysis
Data and Analytics Track Electives - choose **4 CUs**:
- ACCT655 Analytics for Financial Instrument
- ACCT656 Analytics for Value Investing
- ACCT673 Data Governance and Quality
- ACCT684 Automation for Finance Transformation
- ACCT687 Sustainability Accounting and Analysis
- ACCT691 Corporate Financial Planning with Agentic AI
- ACCT680/681 Innovation and Technology Capstone (SMU-X) (0.5 CU + 0.5 CU)
Open Electives - choose **2 CUs**:
- Courses from MSA Programme curriculum
- Courses from other SMU Master Programmes (up to 2 CUs)
- Overseas immersion, exchange programme
Students are required to complete a minimum of **4 Track Electives** to complete Track requirements; the remaining **2 open electives** can be track elective, internship, overseas immersion or exchange programme, or courses from other programmes. Eligible students may complete the internship anytime during their course of study, provided the minimum of **10 weeks** is fulfilled.
Internship: students can choose a part-time internship assignment or full-time internship assignment by clocking at least **400 hours** to qualify for **1 course unit**. Part-time students and students with three-year relevant working experience and above will be exempted from the internship graduation requirement.
Full-time programme calendar:
- Aug-Nov: 5 Core Modules
- Nov-Dec: 1 Track/Open Elective
- Jan-Apr: 3 Core Modules and 1-2 Track/Open Elective
- Apr-Aug: 3-4 Track/Open Electives
- Jul-Nov: 1 Internship Elective and Professional Development Courses
Part-time programme calendar:
- Aug-Nov: 3 Core Modules
- Nov-Dec: 1 Track/Open Elective
- Jan-Apr: 1 Core Module and 1 Elective
- Apr-Jul: 1 Core Module and 1-2 Track/Open Elective
- Aug-Nov: 2 Core Modules
- Nov-Dec: 1 Track/Open Elective
- Jan-Apr: 2 Core Modules and 1 Track/Open Elective
- Apr-Aug: 2-3 Track/Open Elective and Professional Development Courses

Application is not required; it is awarded to students in the MSA Programme after due consideration by the Programme Directors/faculty, during admissions interview. However additional scholarship interview may be required.
Sustainability Scholarship (**$5,000**): Eligibility criteria include Interest in Sustainability; Academic Achievement, generally with a minimum GPA of **3.5 out of 5.0** or equivalent in undergraduate studies; Project Proposal; and Personal Statement. Application is not required; it is awarded to students in the MSA Programme after due consideration by the Programme Directors/faculty, during admissions interview. However additional scholarship interview may be required.
Entrepreneurship Scholarship (**$10,000**): Eligibility criteria include Entrepreneurial Experience; Academic Achievement, generally with a minimum GPA of **3.5 out of 5.0** or equivalent in undergraduate studies; Business Proposal; and Personal Statement. Application is not required; it is awarded to students in the MSA Programme after due consideration by the Programme Directors/faculty, during admissions interview. However additional scholarship interview may be required.
Leadership Scholarship (**$10,000**): Eligibility criteria include Leadership Experience; Academic Achievement, generally with a minimum GPA of **3.5 out of 5.0** or equivalent in undergraduate studies; Proven Leadership; Extracurricular Activities; and Personal Statement. program_overview.content:
18-month duration (full-time); 24-month duration (part-time). Fresh graduates are welcome to apply.
The industry-relevant curriculum of the Master of Science In Applied Finance (MAF) is designed to provide you with a strong foundation in the principles, practices and operations of international and domestic financial markets. Learn how to apply updated and relevant knowledge in real-world situations through internship opportunities in SMU's network of more than 3,000 companies worldwide.
As a collaborative partner with Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) Institute and Chartered Alternative Investment Analyst (CAIA) Association, the curriculum aligns with the CAIA and full CFA curriculum and is an ideal form of preparation if you wish to pursue your CAIA or CFA designation. Students will cover curriculum spanning CFA Levels 1 to 3 upon graduation.
Benefit from the experience and expertise of eminent faculty members with PhDs from top-ranked universities around the world. Gain valuable career insights from thought leaders with deep industry experience and network and share their passion for learning.
Students have the opportunity to specialise in Fintech, Fund Management, Real Estate or Sustainable Finance. Designed for flexibility, the MAF programme is available in both full-time (12 months + internship) and part-time (24 months) modes of study. Students are required to complete 15 Credit Units which include 9CU Core Modules, 4CU Elective Modules, 1CU Open Module (Internship or Capstone Project or MAF elective or other modules offered by other schools), 1CU Postgraduate Professional Development Course in order to be awarded the Master of Science in Applied Finance degree.
Class Profile: Gender 1:1; Average Age 25; International Students 81%; Nationalities 13; Average Years of Work Experience 1.8. Student profiles taken from Classes of 2018-2021 (Full-time & Part-time).
Industries that MAF Graduates Work In: Audit / Accounting 9%; Consulting 7%; Business / Financial Services 58%; Real Estate 3%; Technology 11%. Industry diversity data collated from graduating students from 2020 and 2021.
The MAF Part-Time track is an 20-month part-time course spanning over six terms at SMU. This track admits Singaporeans, Singapore permanent residents and foreigners holding a valid employment or a dependant's pass. The MAF Full-Time track is an 18-month full-time course, with the option to complete in 12-months. The programme spans over four terms at SMU, including internship option. This track admits Singaporeans, Singapore permanent residents and international students. All candidates will receive the same degree i.e. the Master of Science in Applied Finance degree, fully conferred by SMU.
The MAF programme was launched in 2002, offering only the MAF Part-Time track. The MAF Full-Time track was launched in July 2011.
To date, MAF graduates have been well sought-after locally and internationally. The programme provides a stepping-stone for those who want to enter the finance and banking industries. Most graduates venture into the fund management, banking and consultancy sectors.
All lessons and examinations are conducted in English for all the tracks under the MAF programme. A typical class size is about 50 to 60 students. The programme will be taught by well-qualified and experienced SMU and industry professionals. The syllabus is customised for the local and regional financial environment with international perspectives.
Duration: 18 months

financial_aid.content:
Students may apply for SMU MAF Programme Scholarships upon admission. These scholarships entail award amounts up to **30% of the tuition fee**, with no bonds attached.
- **Academic Excellence Award**: offered to high-quality candidates with exceptional academic performance. Awards are based on academic merit, final grades and GMAT score. Tier One awardees must have achieved a GMAT of **720 or above** and demonstrated outstanding academic achievement. Tier Two awardees must have achieved a GMAT of **700 or above** and demonstrated outstanding academic achievement.
- **Global Awareness Award**: given to individuals who will contribute to classroom diversity and enrich the learning experience of students by way of cultural, personal or professional backgrounds.
- **Leadership Award**: recognises individuals who have exhibited outstanding leadership potential during their studies, or in their community or organisation. Applicants must demonstrate strong leadership potential in personal and professional instances; assessment includes interview performance, a 500-word essay, and leadership quality recognition.
- **Community Impact Award**: recognises candidates who have contributed to society through outstanding community work and impacted members of the community/society in a positive manner; assessment includes interview performance, an essay, and impact of community work.
- **Impact on Asia Award**: for students who can demonstrate achievements in professional, social and personal life that have created an impact on Asia; assessment includes interview performance, a 500-word essay, and impact.
- **Women in Business Award**: recognises exceptional women who have demonstrated outstanding leadership capabilities or potential in their professional or personal endeavours. Applicants must have successfully received an admissions offer.
- **AGL Irudayaraj Scholarship**: motivates outstanding postgraduates of Indian ethnicity at the University to greater heights of academic excellence; assessment includes interview performance and an essay on leadership experience, community involvement and financial need, if any.
- **Mapletree Postgraduate Scholarship**: funded by Mapletree for education and enhancing the Mapletree Real Estate Programme at the Lee Kong Chian School of Business. Scholarship awardees must be enrolled as a full-time or part-time student in the MAF programme and commit to complete the Real Estate specialization track within the MAF programme.
- **SkillsFuture**: SkillsFuture Funding is available for Singapore Citizens. The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme provides Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above the opportunity to receive the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top up of **$4,000**, intended to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after **1 May 2024**.
- **SMU Alumni**: graduates from SMU undergraduate or postgraduate programmes are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of **S$8,000** when applying to the MAF programme.
- **Singapore Local Autonomous University**: graduates from NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, or SIT are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of **S$4,000** when applying to the MAF programme. Eligible candidates may receive exemptions for up to four credit units, with a discount of **$3,000** awarded for each credit unit exempted.
- **SG/PR**: Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$5,000**.
- **ASEAN Citizens**: ASEAN citizens are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$3,000**.
- **Corporate Partner**: eligible company-sponsored candidates are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$6,000**.
The above discounts are applicable to students joining the programme from the **January 2025 intake onwards**. Each student is only eligible for one discount; should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount will be applicable. The tuition fee discount is deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST).

program_overview.content:
The SMU Master of Business Administration (MBA) is designed to shape students into versatile and dynamic leaders through an interactive and rigorous curriculum that captures the forefront of management research and proven approaches in management practice.
Designed for flexibility, the MBA programme is available in both full-time and part-time modes of study:
- Full-time: 15 months, with the flexibility to complete within 10 months. The full-time programme spreads over 12-15 months with an option to complete an internship; students engage in pre-term self-study before commencement. Core classes take place Monday to Thursday in the morning or afternoon, and elective classes take place Monday to Thursday, 7pm to 10.45pm, and Saturday. Fridays are catered for make-up classes, career opportunities and leadership development. Students can opt to do an internship, go for overseas exchange, or take an SMU-XO elective.
- Part-time: 20 months, with the flexibility to complete within 15 months. The part-time programme is designed for working professionals over a span of 18-20 months; students engage in pre-term self-study before commencement. Core classes take place on Monday and Tuesday evenings, and elective classes take place Monday to Thursday, 7pm to 10.45pm, and Saturday. Part-time and full-time students attend elective classes together.
The programme structure includes pre-study modules, 8 core modules, 10 elective modules with choice of tracks, and career development. Full-time students may complete an internship or New Venture Creation project; part-time students may take the Management Study Module or Overseas Exchange. Successful completion of 5 pre-study assessments covering 3 modules is mandatory for programme enrolment. The duration of each class is 3 hours and 45 minutes.
The SMU MBA offers optional specialisations in Communications, Entrepreneurship, Finance, or Human Capital. It also equips students with knowledge of Data Science, including Basic R and Python Programming, and includes core learning in “Leading Digital Transformation” and “Business Analytics.” ESG content is woven into all MBA core courses, and all MBA students are required to attend a compulsory 1-day Sustainability workshop.
The programme offers real-world experience through internship opportunities for full-time students via SMU’s network of 3,000 companies worldwide. Exchange partners include Keio University in Japan, Seoul National University in South Korea, Peking University in China, IE in Spain, and University of British Columbia in Canada. Full-time students also have the opportunity to take part in the Overseas Immersion Programme, where students learn about operating and leading organisations in the Asian context.
The SMU MBA was ranked 10th among universities in Asia and 51st worldwide in the Financial Times Global MBA Ranking 2022. 80% of graduates are employed within 6 months, often in positions of leadership, and the programme provides networking and career opportunities supported by dedicated career counsellors.
Class profile data from the Classes of 2018-2021 (Full-time & Part-time): gender ratio 3:2, average age 30, international students 63%, 26 nationalities, and average years of working experience 5.9.
Industries MBA graduates work in, based on Classes of 2018-2020 (Full-time & Part-time): Business / Financial Services 22%, Technology 20%, Consulting 16%, Healthcare 12%, Manufacturing 6%, Real Estate 4%, Transportation / Logistics 3%, and Others 17%.
The programme is taught by internationally renowned and experienced SMU faculty and industry professionals. The part-time and full-time MBA both require physical attendance, though some modules use web and online updates to supplement time in class.
SMU’s dedicated career services team actively helps students prepare for internships. The career services also provide self-assessment guides and career coaching to improve participants’ overall job performance and long-term career goals. Companies that have hired MBA graduates include Julius Baer, Yahoo, Unilever, Givaudan, Keppel, HSBC, PriceWaterhouseCoopers, ExxonMobil and Bain.
Duration: 15 months

curriculum.content:
Designed for flexibility, the MBA programme is available in both full-time (**15 months, with the flexibility to complete within 10 months**) and part-time (**20 months, with the flexibility to complete within 15 months**) modes of study.
- **Full-time Programme:** spreads over **12-15 months** with an option to complete an internship. Students are engaged in pre-term self-study before commencement. Students have the option to complete the full-time SMU MBA in **10 months** when all the credit requirements have been fulfilled.
- Core classes (Terms 1 and 2) take place from Monday to Thursday, either in the morning or afternoon.
- Elective classes (Terms 3 to 5) take place from Monday to Thursday (**7pm to 10.45 pm**) and Saturday. Part-time and Full-time Programme students attend these classes together.
- Fridays are catered for make-up classes, career opportunities and leadership development.
- The duration of each class is **3 hours 45 minutes**.
- Students can opt to do an internship, go for overseas exchange, or take an SMU-XO elective (TBC).
- **Part-time Programme:** designed for working professionals over a span of **18-20 months**. Students are engaged in pre-term self-study before commencement. Students have the option to complete the full-time SMU MBA in **15 months** when all the credit requirements have been fulfilled.
- Core classes (Terms 1 to 4) take place on Monday and Tuesday evenings.
- Elective classes (Terms 5 to 7) take place from Monday to Thursday (**7pm to 10.45pm**) and Saturday. Part-time and Full-time Programme students attend these classes together.
- The duration of each class is **3 hours and 45 minutes**.
The programme calendar includes **Pre-Study Modules**, **8 Core Modules** plus Career Development, and **10 Elective Modules** with choice of tracks. For Full-time students, it is optional to complete either the Internship or New Venture Creation project. For Part-time students, it is optional to take the Management Study Module or Overseas Exchange. Successful completion of **5 pre-study assessments covering 3 modules** is mandatory for programme enrolment.
**8 Core Modules**
- Corporate Finance
- Financial Accounting
- Leading Digital Transformation
- Business Analytics
- Marketing
- Operations Management
- Organisational Behaviour and Leadership
- Strategic Management
ESG content is woven into all MBA core courses. In addition, all MBA students are required to attend a compulsory **1-day Sustainability workshop**.
**Up to 14 Elective Modules**
| Track-specific Elective Modules | Modules offered |
| --- | --- |
| Finance Track | Entrepreneurial Finance; Financial Analytics and Innovation; Hedge Funds; Merge and Acquisitions; Risk Management; Sustainable and Impact Investing |
| Leadership / Operation Track | Business Value of Digital Disruptions - CXO Perspectives; Service and Operations Analytics; Negotiating in Business; Supply Chain Strategy and Management; Risk Management in Global Supply Chains; Innovation in Digital Operations |
| Management / Strategy Track | Critical Thinking; Entrepreneurship and Business Planning; Global Economy - Issues and Challenges; Managing Innovation and Growth; Business Analytics for Decision Making; Design Thinking; Managing Teams; Online Business and Marketplaces |
| Marketing and Communications Track | Advance Marketing Strategy; Applied Marketing Research and Analytics; Consumer Behaviour; Digital Marketing Strategy; Pricing; Storytelling for Brands and Leaders |
The SMU MBA comes with optional specialisations in Communications, Entrepreneurship, Finance, or Human Capital. **10 electives are required** to complement **8 core modules**. With a wide range of electives available, including those on offer by partner universities, participants are encouraged to choose from a number of electives based on their interests and knowledge gaps.
The Part-Time programme is designed for working professionals over a span of **20 months**. Core classes (Terms 1 to 4) take place on either Saturday morning and afternoon (January Intake), or Monday and Tuesday evenings (August Intake). Elective classes (Terms 5 to 7) take place from Monday to Thursday (**7pm to 10.45pm**) and Saturday.
The Full-Time programme spreads over **15 months** with a **compulsory internship**. Core classes (Terms 1 and 2) take place from Monday to Thursday, either in the morning or afternoon. Elective classes (Terms 3 to 5) take place from Monday to Thursday (**7pm to 10.45 pm**) and Saturday. The duration of each class is **3 hours 45 minutes**. The Full-Time schedule includes a **minimum 10-week, compulsory paid internship**.
The programme is not taught via e-learning: both Part-time and Full-time MBA require physical attendance. Some modules use web and online updates to supplement time in class.

financial_aid.content:
- Partial scholarships for the Master of Business Administration (MBA) programme entail award amounts up to S$21,000 of the tuition fee, with no bonds attached. The prevailing GST will still apply for the full tuition fee before the scholarship award.
- All candidates are automatically submitted for consideration for the SMU-ASEAN, Academic Excellence and Global Awareness Scholarships upon meeting scholarship criteria.
- Scholarships listed: Academic Excellence, Global Awareness, Leadership Potential, Community Impact, Impact on Asia, Women in Business, SMU-ASEAN. Leadership, Community Impact, Impact on Asia, and Women in Business are scholarships that students can apply for upon admissions into the MBA programme.
- Academic Excellence Award: based on academic merit, final grades and GMAT score (700 and above).
- SMU-ASEAN Scholarship: no application required; award amount is S$10,000 with no bonds attached. Eligibility: successful admission into the SMU Full-time or Part-time MBA Programme; open to nationals of ASEAN member countries except Singaporeans.
- Lee Kuan Yew Scholarships: in addition to the one-off sum of S$10,000, private sector awardees receive an annual allowance of S$50,000, while public sector awardees receive S$10,000 if concurrently sponsored by their organisations. Eligibility includes Singapore citizenship, at least a Second Upper Honours Degree or equivalent, and excellent leadership/service record.
- APEC Scholarship: bond-free scholarship awarded annually to deserving Full-time SMU MBA candidates from APEC member economies excluding Singaporeans. Package includes monthly stipend of S$1,350, book allowance of S$500, tuition fee, health insurance, examination fee and other approved fees/allowances/expenses, one overseas Business Study Mission, travel from home country to Singapore, and travel from Singapore to home country upon successful completion. Eligibility includes citizen of an APEC member economy, good academic results, at least two years of management or professional experience, English proficiency, good GMAT score, and no prior study abroad.
- SkillsFuture: SkillsFuture Funding for Singapore Citizens. The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme provides Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above the opportunity to receive the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top up of $4,000 to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after 1 May 2024.
- Tuition discounts: SMU alumni are automatically eligible for an alumni discount when applying to the MBA programme. Graduates from NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, or SIT are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of S$4,000. Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of S$5,000. ASEAN citizens are eligible for a one-time discount of S$3,000. Eligible company-sponsored candidates are eligible for a one-time Corporate Partner Award discount of S$7,500. These discounts apply to students joining from the January 2025 intake onwards; each student is only eligible for one discount, and only the higher discount applies if more than one is available.
- FAQ: The SMU MBA Programme offers a number of scholarships for both Full-time and Part-time students. Students can apply for scholarships upon admission to the Programme. Award amounts up to 30% of tuition fees. There are no bonds attached to the scholarships. There are no financial aid schemes available for the MBA programme.

academic_requirements.content:
- The Master of Science in Business AI programme is open to applicants from **all academic backgrounds** who aspire to lead in an AI-enabled business environment.
- Candidates must hold a **recognised bachelor’s degree with a strong academic record**.
- Prior technical or quantitative experience is **beneficial, but not required**; the programme is designed for those seeking to apply AI strategically rather than develop technical AI systems.
- **1 to 5 years of work experience** is preferred; candidates with **no experience** can apply if they possess strong motivation and demonstrate a keen interest in business AI in their application and interview.
- Quantitative or technical experience is preferred.
- No business or technical background is required: the programme accepts applicants from **any discipline** and does not require prior technical training, though quantitative awareness is helpful.
- Coding or programming skills are **not required**.
- SMU graduates with cumulative GPAs of **3.0/4.0 or better**, and graduates from local Autonomous Universities (NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, SIT) with cumulative GPAs of **3.5/5.0 or better**, will not require a GMAT/GRE/SMU Admissions Test Score for admissions. An undergraduate GPA is valid for **5 years after graduation**. Meeting the above GPA academic criteria does not guarantee admission.

gre_gmat_requirements.content:
Applicants must meet the programme’s AIQ requirement, which can be fulfilled through **GMAT (≥600), GMAT Focus (≥595), GRE (≥312), or the SMU Admissions Test (≥55)**.

An undergraduate GPA is valid for **5 years after graduation**. Speak with your [**Admissions Manager**](mailto:mbai.admissions@smu.edu.sg) to find out more.

program_overview.content:
The SMU Master of Science in Business AI (MBAI) programme develops AI-savvy business leaders who can bridge the gap between technical teams and senior management. Graduates will gain strategic vision, analytical excellence, and the technical literacy needed to lead AI-driven transformation.
The Master of Science in Business AI programme is a **12-month** programme offered on a full-time basis, with a maximum course duration of 1.5 years. It comprises **15 course units** designed to build both AI literacy and strategic business capability. Students engage in **three dedicated AI capacity-building modules** and **six core modules**, both distributed across the programme year. To tailor their learning, students choose **two programme electives** along with **three open electives** that may include courses from other SMU master’s programmes, a **10-week internship**, or an **SMU-X/capstone project**. In addition, students complete **postgraduate professional development workshops** that enhance leadership and career readiness. The programme blends classroom learning with real-world application, ensuring graduates are prepared to lead AI-driven transformation across industries.
Who will benefit from the programme:
- Professionals who want to use AI strategically.
- Managers and aspiring leaders seeking AI literacy to drive business transformation.
- Career switchers aiming to enter the AI-enabled business landscape.
- Practitioners in marketing, finance, HR, operations, or strategy who want to apply AI in their functions.
- Consultants and analysts who need to translate AI insights into clear business recommendations.
- Future-ready leaders looking to manage change, influence stakeholders, and guide responsible AI adoption.
The programme builds strong foundations in business intelligence, responsible AI, and data-driven decision-making with no technical background required. Students learn to apply AI tools and insights across business functions through hands-on modules, real cases, storytelling with data, and a capstone project that bridges classroom learning with real-world execution. Graduates are prepared for roles in consulting, digital transformation, product management, analytics, and more. Students are guided by faculty and industry experts who teach the frontiers of AI-enabled business, equipping them with insight, confidence, and strategic capability to drive change.
Master of Science in Business AI graduates can work in:
- Professional Services and Consulting
- Banking and Financial Services
- Data Analytics
- E-commerce
- Logistics
- Manufacturing
- FMCG
- Government
The programme is a one-year full-time programme that develops business leaders who understand AI technologies and can translate them into strategic, organisational, and operational impact—without training students to become engineers or data scientists. It focuses on business-first, AI-literate leadership. Students learn how to use AI to make decisions, drive transformation, and manage change, not how to build models or code systems.
Graduates will be able to interpret AI-driven insights, lead AI initiatives, manage responsible AI adoption, design data-informed strategies, and influence stakeholders through data storytelling. The programme delivers a balanced mix of managerial and technical content, emphasising strategic understanding of AI applications rather than deep programming or algorithm development. The curriculum structure is highly practical: beyond AI foundational and core modules, students have terms for open electives, an internship, and/or a capstone project designed to solve real-world industry problems. The capstone practicum includes direct engagement with industry experts, and internships provide real-world exposure to AI-enabled business environments.
Typical roles include AI Strategy Manager, Business Intelligence Manager, Product Manager (AI/Data), Digital Transformation Lead, HR Analytics Manager, and Financial/Marketing Intelligence Analyst. SMU's dedicated career services team will actively help students prepare for internships and career opportunities in Singapore and beyond. Career counselling and workshops will be provided to MBAI students, and MBAI students will have access to a career counsellor who will assist with post-graduation placement through guidance and advice. The internship component is also expected to improve employability by providing opportunities for early exposure to the work environment of Singapore. Industries that typically hire Master of Science in Business AI graduates include consulting, finance, technology, e-commerce, public sector, logistics, and analytics-driven industries seeking business professionals fluent in AI.
Duration: 12 months

- **Impact on Asia:** The committee assesses interview performance, a 500-word essay on Asian-focused professional development, entrepreneurial or personal projects, and impact such as reach, entrepreneurial projects, awards and helping increased awareness of Asia.
- **Women in Business:** Applicants must have successfully received an admissions offer. The committee assesses interview performance, a 500-word essay, and leadership quality recognition.
- **Community Impact:** The "Community Impact Award" recognises candidates who have contributed to society through outstanding community work and positively impacted members of the community/society. The committee assesses interview performance, an essay, and impact of community work.

Eligibility criteria include: full-time student matriculated in the MBAI programme; Singapore Citizen; must demonstrate academic excellence; must not be a recipient of other Scholarship or sponsorship. program_overview.content:
**AUGUST / JANUARY INTAKE**
18 Months Full-Time (with flexibility to complete in 12 months)
30 Months Part-Time (with flexibility to complete in 24 months)
Economic data are generated at high volume, velocity, and variety. As companies collect ever-increasing amounts of data, those who can effectively extract value from it will come out on top. Discover the power of data with a Master of Data Science in Economics (MDSE) from the School of Economics at Singapore Management University.
The Master of Data Science in Economics (MDSE) is a multi-disciplinary programme with a unique curriculum that equips you to analyze economic issues more effectively by combining the strengths of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and econometric methods. The MDSE stands out for its strong industry relevance and hands-on learning approach.
- Learn industry-relevant programming languages: Gain proficiency in Python, SQL, and R — three of the most in-demand languages for data science.
- Turn data into insights: Master the skills needed to query, analyze, and model large-scale economic data using distributed computing techniques on both on-premises and cloud clusters. Apply statistical models and machine learning algorithms to generate explainable predictions, accurate classifications, and actionable recommendations.
- Sharpen your competitive edge: Equip yourself with the skills needed for the future of work, including expertise in big data technologies such as Apache Hadoop, Apache Spark, and Apache Cassandra. Stay ahead with current knowledge and practical skills necessary to tackle data-driven challenges, through talks and workshops delivered by industry practitioners.
- Apply your skills in real-world projects: Develop the ability to effectively communicate your results to project stakeholders by documenting and explaining your analysis to both technical and non-technical audiences. Showcase your work on GitHub and GitHub Pages, and build a portfolio of projects to demonstrate your skills to prospective employers.
Industries MDSE graduates will work in include Financial Services, Government, Technology, Healthcare, Consulting, and Telecommunications.
August, January and April are regular 10-week terms. November and July are optional 5-week terms. Students may graduate as soon as they have met all requirements, even if this is earlier than the expected completion dates indicated above. The maximum candidature is 2.5 years for full-time students and 4 years for part-time students. Part-time students typically take 1–3 CUs per regular term (Aug, Jan, Apr), whereas full-time students take 2–5 CUs.
The MDSE programme features a 15-CU curriculum with internship opportunities that equip students with advanced, up-to-date knowledge and skills in data science for economics. The curriculum structure comprises Foundation (2CUs), Core (6CUs), Elective (3CUs), Open (3CUs), and PGPD (1CU). Each course unit (CU) comprises ten 3-hour sessions.
The Foundation component is designed to equip students from non-technical backgrounds with essential training in probability theory, statistics, and programming. Students with strong technical knowledge may be exempted from this component. The Core component equips students with rigorous training in programming, statistics, data analytics, data management, AI, ML, and econometrics. Students with strong technical knowledge may be exempted from up to 2 CUs in this component. MDSE students have the flexibility to select 3 electives, allowing them to expand their expertise in specialized areas.
To enhance their academic experience and holistic development, MDSE students can choose to complete a 10-20 week internship (1-2 CUs), undertake a Capstone project (1 CU), and take up to 3 pre-approved electives from other SMU Master’s programmes, such as the MSE and MSFE. Students are required to complete a series of full-day, skills-based, developmental workshops or experiential components facilitated by SMU faculty and experienced trainers from various industries. These activities enhance students’ professional standing, help them acquire new skill sets beyond the curriculum, and expand their network with fellow students across SMU’s Master’s programmes.
Full-time students are required to complete a minimum 10-week internship during the April Term. If you are unable to take a credit-bearing internship, you may seek approval from your Academic Director to arrange an equivalent replacement (e.g., a Capstone Project or electives). Students who have accumulated, or will have accumulated, two years of relevant work experience by their graduation date may be exempted from the internship requirement, subject to approval.
Classes are scheduled on weekday evenings (from 7pm onwards), Saturday mornings, or Saturday afternoons. These timings have been chosen to accommodate the working schedules of part-time students who are concurrently working and full-time students who are engaged with industry attachments. However, full-time students may have some weekday morning or afternoon classes (8.15am, 12pm or 3.30pm onwards) in their first term.
All students will have a dedicated career coach who will be assigned to them throughout the Master’s programme. Career support includes Career Planning and Coaching, Internship and Job Search, Resume and Cover Letter Critique, Interview Preparation, Administration of Personality Inventories, Recruitment and Networking Events, and Career Development Workshops. Students can use SMU’s internal online job portal to search and apply for internships and jobs. In addition, career coaches maintain close connections with industry partners to source opportunities on an ongoing basis.
Duration: 18 months

The offer is conditional on matriculation into the MDSE, i.e., the scholarship awardee must matriculate into the programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
MDSE Diversity Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility Criteria:** SOE Applicants with good academic backgrounds and who are citizens of countries that are underrepresented in the programme are eligible for the SOE MDSE Diversity Scholarship. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
MDSE Industry Distinction Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility Criteria:** The Industry Distinction Scholarship is intended for experienced professionals who bring valuable industry insights to the MDSE classroom. Applicants should have at least three years of work experience in areas such as economics, finance, or related fields.
MDSE Women in Leadership Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility Criteria:** The Women in Leadership Scholarship is open to women applying to the MDSE programme who have demonstrated strong leadership potential and a commitment to advancing women in economics, finance, or related fields. Applicants should have a record of academic achievement and professional or community involvement that reflects leadership and initiative.
MDSE DSA Distinguished Alumni Scholarship
- **Benefits:** Merit 1 is valued at **S$10,000 (inclusive of GST)**. Merit 2 is valued at **S$6,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility Criteria:** This DSA Distinguished Alumni Scholarship is awarded to SMU Data Science & Analytics (DSA) Second Major alumni who have demonstrated both academic excellence and outstanding leadership.

academic_requirements.content:
- **Good Bachelor's degree**.
- Effective August 2026 intake: the August intake will be open to students from diverse academic backgrounds. **Foundation courses will be provided to bridge any knowledge gaps**. Students with strong quantitative backgrounds may be exempted from these courses and complete the programme in 12 months.
- The MSE includes an entry pathway for students without prior training in economics; the programme has a pathway for non-Econ majors.
- Foundations are intended for students from non-Economics backgrounds who do not have the necessary training in economic theory and advanced quantitative techniques required by the MSE. Students with strong economics knowledge and advanced quantitative techniques are exempted from this component.
- MSE Programme Foundations: Principles of Economics 1, Principles of Economics 2, Mathematics for Economics, Further Mathematics for Economics. Effective August 2026: Principles of Economics, Math for Economics, Probability and Statistics.
- UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for: **SMU alumni with CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above, within five years of graduation**; **NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above, within five years of graduation**. Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission.
- Work experience is not mandatory.

gre_gmat_requirements.content:
- Application documents include **GMAT / GRE / SMU Admission Test Score Report**.
- Admission Requirements include: **Good score in GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test**. _EQ: A very good score in the quantitative section will be expected_.
- UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for the following applicants:
- SMU alumni with **CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above**, within five years of graduation.
- NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with **CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above**, within five years of graduation.
- _Note: Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission, and you may be advised to submit your GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test score to improve your chances of admission._
- The GMAT/GRE is recommended. However, if you have not taken the GMAT or GRE test, you may consider taking the online SMU Admission Test, which comprises three components: verbal, numerical, and inductive reasoning. Please click [Fact Sheet](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/MAE/SMU%20Admission%20Test%20Fact%20Sheet%20%28MSE%29.pdf) for information on SMU Admission Test registration and test details.
- If you intend to take the SMU Admission Test, please proceed to complete the MSE application first and make a payment of **S$125** in addition to the MSE application fee of **S$100**. Once you have completed payment for the test, send an email with your full name, application number and payment receipt to [mse@smu.edu.sg](mailto:mse@smu.edu.sg).
- For GMAT, we are looking for scores **600 or above**. For GRE, the verbal plus quantitative average should be **156 or above**. For SMU Admissions Test, the Verbal/Numerical/Integrated Reasoning average should be **55 or above**. For CAT, your score should put you into the **80th percentile or above**. Note that these are not hard cut-offs. We look at your overall application to see if you are a suitable candidate for us. We can accept students who fall below one or more of these minimums if there are positives in the application that compensate. Finally, we only need one of GRE/GMAT/SMUAT/CAT.
- Must I take the GRE/GMAT? For most applicants, yes. UG CGPA may be used in place of GRE/GMAT/SMU Admission Test scores for the following applicants: SMU alumni with **CGPA 3.0/4.0 or above**, within **5 years of graduation**; NUS/NTU/SUTD/SUSS/SIT alumni with **CGPA 3.5/5.0 or above**, within **5 years of graduation**. Note: Meeting the CGPA academic criteria listed above does not guarantee admission, and candidates may be recommended to submit GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test scores if it is felt this would improve chances of admission.
- Can I apply for the programme before taking GMAT/GRE? Yes, you can submit your application prior to taking the GMAT/GRE. Once you have completed your online application, an officer from our admissions team will get in touch with you within a month to advise you on the next steps, including the submission deadline for your GMAT/GRE exam scores.

program_overview.content:
- The Master of Science in Economics (MSE), with tracks in Applied Economics (AE), Econometrics and Quantitative Economics (EQ), offers in-depth study of economics and economic data analysis. It includes an entry pathway for students without prior training in economics.
- The MSE is available for part-time or full-time study. Full-time study is 18 months, with flexibility to complete in 12 months; part-time study is 30 months, with flexibility to complete in 24 months. Maximum candidature is 2.5 years for full-time students and 4 years for part-time students.
- Effective August 2026 intake, the August intake will be open to students from diverse academic backgrounds, with foundation courses provided to bridge knowledge gaps. Students with strong quantitative backgrounds may be exempted from these courses and complete the programme in 12 months through the accelerated pathway, available in both August and January intakes.
- Students follow a strong core programme and a track system that allows a more practice-oriented focus or a more data-analytic and theoretical focus, along with an open category that allows courses outside the chosen track or from other programmes.
- The Applied Economics track is for working professionals who make or will make critical and strategic decisions in companies or public sector agencies and who can benefit from a good understanding of the market and the economy. It gives a comprehensive understanding of global economic issues for strategic decision making in the public sector and corporate world.
- The Econometrics and Quantitative Economics track is for students who wish to learn more about data analysis with a special focus on economic, financial and social data, pursue careers involving technical economics research, or pursue further graduate study in Economics. It focuses on modern and rigorous data analysis methods and covers economic theory, practice and research.
- The MSE programme features a strong yet flexible core, tracks that sharpen students’ focus, and a wide range of electives in the chosen track. Students may also take courses outside their track or programme for a personalised programme.
- The MSE is a 15 course unit (CU) programme with internship opportunities. Its structure comprises Foundations, Core, Electives, Open, and PGPD components; effective August 2026, the structure will be Foundation (3CUs), Core (3CUs), Elective (5CUs), Open (3CUs), and PGPD (1CU).
- The Foundations component is intended for students from non-Economics backgrounds who do not have the necessary training in economic theory and advanced quantitative techniques required by the MSE. Students with strong economics knowledge and advanced quantitative techniques are exempted from this component.
- The MSE Core equips students with rigorous knowledge in microeconomics, macroeconomics, and econometrics, providing the analytical framework on which sub-areas of economics are built.
- The Open component gives students flexibility to take courses from any MSE track/MSFE electives. Up to 1CU may be taken from pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes. Students may choose to do a 10-week internship or a capstone project that satisfies a 1CU requirement.
- From the AY2021/22 intake onwards, internship will be a graduation requirement. Full-time students are required to complete a minimum 10-week internship in the April Term; students unable to take up a credit-bearing internship may seek approval to arrange an equivalent replacement such as a Capstone Project or electives.
- Average age in the class profile is 22 - 31 yrs, with gender profile 45.8(M) : 54.2(F), based on Classes of 2018-2021 (Full-time & Part-time).
- Industries MSE graduates work in include Business / Financial Services (19%), Consulting (13%), Investment / Securities (10%), Education (10%), Public Sector (8%), Healthcare (8%), Fintech (6%), Telecommunications (4%), Manufacturing (4%), and Others (18%), based on Classes of 2018-2020 (Full-time).
- Students will learn from frontline researchers, teaching specialists, industry practitioners and professionals.
- SMU has an internal online job portal for students to search and apply for internships and jobs. Students are assigned a dedicated career coach to provide career advisory and prepare them for internship and job placement.
- Careers after the MSc Econ include banks, investment banks, consultancies, insurance companies, government and regulatory agencies, education, research, business and HR, marketing, and related fields. Students on the Econometrics & Quantitative Economics track can also pursue careers as data scientists/analysts.
Duration: 18 months

curriculum.content:
- **Duration / study mode:** August / January intake. **18 Months Full-Time** with flexibility to complete in **12 months**; **30 Months Part-Time** with flexibility to complete in **24 months**. The MSc in Economics is available for part-time or full-time study. Maximum candidature is **2.5 years for full-time students**, and **4 years for part-time students**.
- August, January and April are regular **12-week terms**. November and July are optional **5-week terms**. Part-time students take **1-3 CU per regular term**; full-time students take **2-5 CU per regular term**.
- **Programme calendar:** **AY2026-2027** [download](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/PG_Doc/PG%20Academic%20Calendars%20(BRC%20Programmes)%20AY2026-27.pdf); **AY2025-2026** [download](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/PG_Doc/PG%20Academic%20Calendars%20(BRC%20Programmes)%20AY2025-26.pdf); **AY2024-2025** [download](https://economics.smu.edu.sg/sites/economics.smu.edu.sg/files/economics/PG_Doc/PG%20Academic%20Calendars%20(BRC%20Programmes)%20AY2024-25.pdf).
- The Master of Science in Economics (MSE) programme features a strong yet flexible core, tracks that sharpen your focus and a wide range of electives in your chosen track. Students may take courses outside of their track or programme for a personalised programme.
- Tracks: **Applied Economics Track** is available full-time or part-time. **Econometrics and Quantitative Economics Track** is full-time, with part-time option if able to take weekday daytime classes. Part-time study is available only to Singapore-based students: citizens, permanent residents, and those holding valid employment passes.
- **Programme Curriculum:** The MSE is a **15 course unit (CU)** programme with internship opportunities. Current structure: **Foundations (4CU), Core (3CU), Electives (5CU), Open (2CU), PGPD (1CU)**. Each course unit comprises ten 3-hour sessions. The academic requirement for graduation is a **Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of at least 2.50 out of 4.00**.
- Effective August 2026, the curriculum structure will be updated to: **Foundation (3CUs), Core (3CUs), Elective (5CUs), Open (3CUs), PGPD (1CU)**. The foundation component will be reduced by **1 CU**, and the open component increased by **1**, allowing for more flexibility and personalization.
- **Foundations:** Intended for students from non-Economics backgrounds who do not have the necessary training in economic theory and advanced quantitative techniques required by the MSE. Students with strong economics knowledge and advanced quantitative techniques are exempted from this component. Foundation courses listed: Principles of Economics 1, Principles of Economics 2, Mathematics for Economics, Further Mathematics for Economics. Effective August 2026 foundation courses listed: Principles of Economics, Math for Economics, Probability and Statistics.
- **Core (3CU):** Microeconomic Analysis, Macroeconomic Analysis, Econometric Analysis. EQ track students may apply to take PhD-level equivalent courses.
- **Track Electives (5CU):** Choose **5CU from the single track** to attain track status. Not all courses are available every year; course titles and content are subject to change and new courses are added from time to time.
- **Applied Economics Track courses:** Health Economics; Money, Banking, and International Finance; Macroeconomic Accounts and Public Finance; Economics of Growth, Poverty and Inequality; Politics, Institutions, and Economics; International Trade: Theory and Policy; Behavioural Economics; Infrastructure Economics and Policy; Environmental Economics; Economics of Competition Law; Spatial Econometrics and Data Analysis.
- **Econometrics and Quantitative Economics Track courses:** Spatial Econometrics and Data Analysis; Time Series Econometrics; Data Sampling; Panel Econometrics and Data Analysis; Machine Learning in Economics and Finance; Financial Econometrics; Continuous Time Financial Economics and Econometrics; Mathematical Methods for Economic Dynamics; Advanced Microeconomic Analysis; Empirical Industrial Economics; Macroeconomics 1 PhD; Selection of PhD Advanced Research Topics (ARTs).
- **Open (2CU):** Students may take courses from any MSE track/MSFE electives. Up to **1CU** may be taken from pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes. Students may choose to do a **10-week internship** or a **capstone project** that satisfies a **1CU** requirement. The Open component will expand to **3CU effective August 2026**.
- Full-time students are encouraged to complete a minimum **10-week internship**. If unable to take up a credit-bearing internship, students may arrange an equivalent replacement such as a **Capstone Project or electives**. Full-time students may choose to complete a minimum of 10 weeks internship to satisfy **1CU** requirement under the open course category; students who do not wish to take up a credit-bearing internship may choose courses from any MSE track/MSFE electives, a capstone project, or up to **1CU** from pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes.

financial_aid.content:
SOE MSE Academic Merit Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The Merit 1 Scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**. The Merit 2 Scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$4,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** Outstanding applicants to the MSE are eligible for the Merit Scholarships. The scholarship offer is conditional on matriculation into the MSE, i.e., the scholarship awardee must matriculate into the programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
SOE MSE Diversity Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$8,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** SOE Applicants with good academic backgrounds and who are citizens of countries that are underrepresented in the programme are eligible for the SOE MSE Diversity Scholarship. The scholarship awardee must matriculate into the MSE programme in order for the scholarship to be disbursed. Deferment of studies beyond the financial year would render the scholarship award null and void.
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All eligible applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
SMU ASEAN PG Scholarship
- **Benefits:** The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$10,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Eligibility criteria:** The scholarship is open to citizens of ASEAN member countries or observer nations (PNG and Timor-Leste). The recipient must matriculate into the MSE programme to receive the award (no deferment of studies beyond the financial year of the award).
- **Exclusions:** You must not be a concurrent recipient of any other SMU-funded scholarship.
- **Application Process:** All eligible applicants are automatically considered for the scholarship; no additional application is required.
Roberto S. Mariano Best MSE Student Award
- **Benefits:** The award comprises a monetary award of **S$1,000 (inclusive of GST)**.
- **Exclusions:** All graduating students are eligible.
Financing Options
- Scholarships and Outstanding Student Awards are available for deserving students.
- SkillsFuture Funding for Singapore Citizens. Click [here](https://www.skillsfuture.gov.sg/credit) for more details.
- Singapore Citizens with eligible Post Secondary Education Account (PSEA) may utilize balance funds for tuition fees. Click [here](https://www.moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/psea) for more details.
Discounts
- **Alumni Discount:** SMU and SUTD alumni are eligible for a discount of **$5,000** when applying to the MSE programme.
FAQ: “I see from your website you have scholarships ranging from $4,000 to $10,000. How do I apply?” You don’t have to. All eligible applicants will be considered for the appropriate scholarship, and informed when the offer is made. If you have an external scholarship and do not require a scholarship from us, please let us know.

multiple_applications.content:
Must I indicate a track when I apply? Yes, and if admitted, your admission will be to a specific track of the program. Switching tracks is possible, but only with the School’s permission, and only if done early enough (before the main programme starts). Occasionally, the admission committee may feel that you are more suited to another track than to the one you applied to. In that case, they may suggest to you to consider the other track instead.
Can I apply for multiple tracks? Yes and no. The application system will ask you to choose a track. You may, however, indicate in your personal statement that you are willing to consider another track, or want to be considered for both tracks. We will channel your application to the appropriate track should you not get your first choice track.
Can I apply for multiple programmes? E.g., both MSE and MSFE? Yes.

program_overview.content:
The SMU Master of Science in Entrepreneurship and Innovation (MEI) offers a cross-disciplinary, practice-driven education through world-class faculty, close engagement with thought-leading practitioners, global exposure at a leading business school, and hands-on innovation projects. Designed to engage, challenge, and grow Asia’s next generation of innovation and entrepreneurial leaders, MEI prepares graduates to create, scale, and lead in dynamic innovation ecosystems.
The full-time MEI is a 12-month programme. It is designed to equip aspiring leaders with the capabilities to lead innovation in both large organisations or breakthrough start-ups, and to ensure students acquire knowledge and competencies to successfully tackle today’s and tomorrow’s innovation challenges in various sectors. Candidates who are passionate about new value creation in business and society are identified as a target audience.
Students are required to complete **15 Credit Units** to be awarded the MEI degree: 7.0CU Core Modules, 2.0CU Electives, 4CU Venture Building Experiences, 1CU Postgraduate Professional Development Course and 1CU Overseas Immersion Programme. The programme includes a Venture Building Experience co-led by faculty, industry partners and leading venture capitalists, plus an Overseas Immersion Programme. The current partner for the international residency segment is University College London; part of the MEI curriculum involves a one-week residency at University College London.
MEI highlights include learning from eminent faculty with Ph.D. from Cornell, Harvard, INSEAD, Oxford, Stanford, Yale and other universities, industry partners and leading venture capitalists; entrepreneurial learning and exposure in partnership with University College London; and engagement with startups, founders, and innovation leaders in London.
Class profile: gender ratio 11:9, average age 36, and average years of work experience 11. Student profiles are taken from Classes of 2018-2021 (Full-time & Part-time).
Industries MEI graduates work in include Commodities 3%, Education 8%, Business / Financial Services 18%, Government Agencies 7%, Hospitality 6%, Pharmaceutical & Healthcare 3%, Manufacturing 8%, Media & Advertising 4%, Technology 18%, Transportation & Logistics 9%, Research 3%, and Others 13%. Industry diversity data was collated from graduating students from 2020 and 2021.
Alumni examples include Khairulnizam Zulkifle, Senior Manager, Transformation Office, Wildlife Reserves Singapore, Class of 2020; Tom Lee, Associate Aerosol Engineer, Philip Morris International, Class of 2021; and Giovanna Claro, Founder and CEO, eHeadset English Online, Class of 2021.
Duration: 12 months

Academic Excellence | Global Awareness | SMU-ASEAN | Leadership* | Impact on Asia* | Women in Business* | Community Impact*
\* Denotes Scholarships that students can apply for upon admissions into the programme
These scholarships entail award amounts up to 30% of the tuition fee, with no bonds attached. **The Admissions Scholarship Committee will assess the following:**
- Professional, personal, and academic achievements
- Evidence of making an entrepreneurial impact to business/society
- Interview Performance
- Recommendation from the Academic Director
Academic Excellence: The SMU MEI will offer the Academic Excellence Award to high-quality candidates with exceptional academic performance. Awards are based on academic merit, final grades and admissions test score.
Global Awareness: The SMU MEI is committed to crafting a diverse and global academic environment that will contribute to the student’s personal and professional journey. The Global Awareness Award is awarded to individuals who will contribute to the class room diversity and enrich the learning experience of students by way of cultural, personal or professional backgrounds.
SMU-ASEAN: The SMU-ASEAN Scholarships do not require any applications. Applicants who meet the criteria below will be considered. The award amounts range from S$5,000 to S$10,000 (inclusive of GST) with no bonds attached to the scholarships. **Eligibility criteria:**
1. Successful admission into the SMU MEI Programme
2. Open to nationals of ASEAN member countries
Leadership: The SMU MEI recognises individuals with strong leadership capabilities who have exhibited outstanding leadership potential in their profession, organisation or community with the Leadership Scholarship. Applicants must demonstrate strong leadership capabilities or potential in personal and professional instances. **The Admissions Scholarship Committee will assess the following:**
1. Interview Performance
2. Essay: “Please explain in 500 words why you consider yourself a leader"
3. Leadership quality recognition such as workplace career progression, line management progression, professional recognition, project success and team leadership; leadership qualities during student days; attainment of any non-academic awards and scholarships.
Impact on Asia: The SMU MEI is creating a significant impact in Singapore, extending now to Asia. We look forward to welcoming students who can demonstrate achievements in their professional, social and personal life that have created an impact on Asia. **The Admissions Scholarship Committee will assess the following:**
1. Interview Performance
