program_overview.content:
- The Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE) programme combines two central strengths of SMU – econometrics and finance – in a programme that meets the industry demand for professionals with the skills for deep analysis of increasingly complex financial problems in a new era of dynamic policy and regulation. Students learn how modelling, forecasting and surveillance methods developed in financial theory and econometrics address industry challenges. The programme is for students who seek to pursue a career in the finance industry or research.
- The MSFE is a rigorous multi-disciplinary programme that gives students in-depth understanding of financial markets and their interaction with the macroeconomy, backed by strong econometrics training for analysing economic and financial data. It offers two intakes annually, January and August, and caters to both full-time and part-time students.
- Duration: 18 months full-time, with flexibility to complete in 12 months; 30 months part-time, with flexibility to complete in 24 months. The maximum candidature is 2.5 years for full-time students and 4 years for part-time students.
- The programme welcomes applicants from all disciplines, including those who may not have prior exposure to economic theory or quantitative techniques. Students who demonstrate substantial knowledge in economics and quantitative techniques may be granted exemptions from foundational courses. Effective August 2026, foundation courses will be provided to bridge knowledge gaps, while students with strong quantitative backgrounds may be exempted and complete the programme in 12 months through the accelerated pathway, available in both August and January intakes.
- The MSFE is a 15 course unit (CU) programme, available for full-time study with internship opportunities. Its structure comprises Foundation, Core, Elective, Open, and Postgraduate Professional Development components. Effective August 2026, the Foundation component will be reduced from 4 CUs to 3 CUs and the Open component increased from 1 CU to 2 CUs, allowing more flexibility and personalization while maintaining a strong academic foundation.
- Full-time students are required to complete a minimum 10-week internship during the April Term. If unable to take a credit-bearing internship, students may seek approval to arrange an equivalent replacement, such as a Capstone Project or electives. Students with two years of relevant work experience by graduation may be exempted from the internship requirement, subject to approval.
- The programme is multidisciplinary, delivering economics, econometrics and financial theory; it teaches advanced tools of economic theory, financial econometrics and statistical computation; and it aims to equip students with fundamentals to anticipate and handle future financial crises. Students learn from econometricians, qualified and experienced faculty members and industry practitioners.
- Class profile: typical age range 25 years; gender profile 49(M) : 51(F), based on Classes of 2018-2021 full-time student profiles.
- Industries MSFE graduates work in: Financial Services 50%, Government 14%, Technology 9%, Education 9%, Consulting 5%, Real Estate 5%, Audit / Accounting 4%, Manufacturing 4%, based on Classes of 2018-2020 full-time student data.
- MSFE is a Masters Degree programme at SMU by coursework, also called a Professional Masters Program. There are no thesis requirements.
- All lessons and examinations are conducted in English for both pathways under the MSFE programme.
- SMU has an internal online job portal for students to search and apply for internships and jobs. Students are assigned a dedicated career coach to provide career advisory and prepare them for internship and job placement.
Duration: 18 months

curriculum.content:
#### Programme Structure
The Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE) programme offers two intakes annually (January and August), catering to both full-time and part-time students. August, January and April are regular 10-week terms. November and July are optional 5-week terms.
- **18 Months Full-Time** with flexibility to complete in **12 months**.
- **30 Months Part-Time** with flexibility to complete in **24 months**.
- The maximum candidature is **2.5 years for full-time students** and **4 years for part-time students**.
- Part-time students typically take **1-3 CUs per regular term** (Aug, Jan, Apr), whereas full-time students take **2-5 CUs**.
- The MSFE is a **15 course unit (CU)** programme, available for full-time study with internship opportunities.
- Each course unit (CU) comprises **ten 3-hour sessions**.
- Graduation requires a Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of at least **2.50 on a 4.00 scale**.
Current curriculum structure:
| Component | Course Units |
| --- | --- |
| Foundation | 4CUs |
| Core | 6CUs |
| Elective | 3CUs |
| Open | 1CU |
| PGPD | 1CU |
The curriculum structure will be updated effective August 2026:
| Component | Course Units |
| --- | --- |
| Foundation | 3CUs |
| Core | 6CUs |
| Elective | 3CUs |
| Open | 2CUs |
| PGPD | 1CU |
**Foundation (4CUs)**: The Foundation component provides essential training in economic theory and advanced quantitative methods. Choose four: Principles of Economics 1, Principles of Economics 2, Mathematics for Economics, Further Mathematics for Economics. The Foundation component will be streamlined to **3CU effective August 2026**, comprising: Principles of Economics, Statistical Inference, Mathematics for Economics.
**Core (6CUs)**: Corporate Finance; Econometric Analysis; Empirical Finance; Financial Econometrics; Macroeconomic Analysis; Microeconomic Analysis.
**Elective (3CUs)**: Students have the flexibility to choose 3 elective courses to enhance their knowledge in the preferred economics/finance domains. Electives include Alternative Investments and Distribution; Blockchain & Digital Economy; Continuous Time Financial Economics and Econometrics; High Frequency Trading; Machine Learning in Economics and Finance; Mathematics for Fixed Income and Derivative Securities; Portfolio Risk and Performance Analysis. Not all courses are offered every year. Course titles and content are subject to change, and new courses may be added from time to time.
**Open (1CU)**: Students may take one course from MSFE/MSE electives; or pre-approved electives from other SMU Masters programmes; or a minimum 10-week internship/capstone project. The Open component will expand to **2CU effective August 2026**.
**Postgraduate Professional Development course (1CU)**: Students are required to complete a series of full-day skills-based, developmental workshops or experiential components facilitated by SMU faculty and experienced trainers from various industries.
Full-time students are required to complete a **minimum 10-week internship during the April Term**. If unable to take a credit-bearing internship, students may seek approval from the Academic Director to arrange an equivalent replacement, such as a Capstone Project or electives. Students who have accumulated, or will have accumulated, two years of relevant work experience by their graduation date may be exempted from the internship requirement, subject to approval.
The FAQ states that the MSFE is a Masters Degree program at SMU by coursework / Professional Masters Program, and there are **no thesis requirements**. Students of the MSFE programme are required to complete **4 foundations, 6 core modules, 3 electives, 1 open and 1 Postgraduate Professional Development course**. There are two admission pathways: Accelerated Pathway and Regular Pathway. The Accelerated Pathway is for students with strong economics/finance knowledge and quantitative techniques who are exempted from foundation courses. The Regular Pathway is for students from other disciplines who do not have the necessary training in economics theory, finance and quantitative techniques. In order to graduate, students must complete **all 15 modules** and maintain an overall GPA of **2.5 and above**. All lessons and examinations are conducted in English for both pathways under the MSFE programme.

program_overview.content:
The Master of IT in Business (MITB) programme draws from thought leadership in data analytics, technological platforms and business strategies, and delves into five specialisation tracks: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Science & Analytics, Digital Transformation and Financial Technology & Analytics. The Analytics (AT) track has been rebranded to Data Science & Analytics (DSA) track as of April 2025.
MITB has a 12 to 24 months duration with August and January intake. Modes of study are Full-time & Part-Time. The Master of IT in Business is an intensive programme with 2 options for completion: full-time candidature from a minimum of 1 year to a maximum of 3 years, and part-time candidature from a minimum of 2 years to a maximum of 5 years. Students can switch between these 2 modes of candidature at any time, but the change can only be made once.
MITB class sessions are 3 hours long, and are conducted in a highly interactive, seminar-styled manner. Class sessions combine lectures with discussions, hands-on lab sessions, problem-solving practice classes, and group work. Through the pedagogy, students have the opportunity to interact closely with faculty, full-time professional hires (instructors) and student teaching assistants. Students also meet with industry experts who share their experiences and perspectives through regular seminars organised by the MITB programme. All classes are held either on weekday evenings from 7pm onwards, Saturday mornings from 8.15am onwards, or Saturday afternoons from 12pm onwards, with some weekday morning or afternoon classes for full-time students in their first term.
Why pursue MITB:
- High graduate employability: graduates are sought after by corporations from industries such as Apple, Google, PayPal, Grab, etc. 9 out of 10 graduates are employed within six months upon graduation. Download the [employment report](https://scispg.smu.edu.sg/acton/fs/blocks/showLandingPage/a/44865/p/p-002a/t/page/fm/0) to read more.
- Constantly evolving and relevant curriculum: stay up to date on the current IT market trends and technologies.
- World-class faculty and industry practitioners: learn from faculty who are experts in their fields, with opportunities to learn from real-world scenarios.
- Internships and capstone projects: choose between an internship to gain real-world working experience, or a capstone project to research independently on a specific topic.
Class profile data from Class of 2025 (Full-time & Part-time): Typical Age Range 22 - 32; International Student 47%; Total Nationalities 18; Average Years of Work Experience 4.1. Academic background data collated from graduating students from 2023 and 2024: Business / Financial Services 36%; Engineering 33%; Computing 13%; Science 13%; Art & Social Sciences 5%.
The MITB Internship is an experiential learning experience for students to apply knowledge acquired in the MITB program within the professional setting. The internships are aligned with the aims of the MITB program and students’ respective tracks, providing career-related work experience, industry exposure, professional networks, guidance and professional support.
The MITB capstone project is an extensive, applied practice research project undertaken by students, supervised by SMU faculty members who have specific expertise and interest in the topic, and sometimes sponsored by external companies. It provides an individualized learning experience to integrate and synthesize the skills, theories, and frameworks learned in the MITB programme, and to apply them in a real-world setting.
Duration: 1.5 years

curriculum.content:
The Master of IT in Business (MITB) programme delves into five specialisation tracks: Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity, Data Science & Analytics, Digital Transformation and Financial Technology & Analytics. The Analytics (AT) track has been rebranded to Data Science & Analytics (DSA) track as of April 2025.
The MITB curriculum has its courses classified into the following series:
- Core Courses: Computational Thinking with Python; Spreadsheet Modelling for Decision Making; Statistical Thinking for Data Science.
- Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) content is woven into all MITB core courses.
- Practicum: Internship (2 CUs) or Capstone Project (2 CUs).
- Students may choose to cross-enrol up to two (02) pre-approved [SCIS PhD courses](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/master_of_it_in_business/cross-enrolment-of-scis-phd-courses-for-mitb-students) and count towards MITB graduation requirements as track electives or open electives.
Modes of Study: Full-time & Part-Time. The Master of IT in Business is an intensive programme with 2 options for completion:
- Full-time candidature: a minimum of 1 year to a maximum of 3 years. Period of Candidature (Year): Minimum 1, Normal 1.5.
- Part-time candidature: a minimum of 2 years to a maximum of 5 years. Period of Candidature (Year): Minimum 2, Normal 2.5.
- Students can switch between these 2 modes of candidature at any time, but the change can only be made once. Students are allowed to apply for a conversion of their candidature (Full/Part-Time) only once in their entire duration of the programme.
Course Delivery and Timetable: MITB class sessions are 3 hours long, and are conducted in a highly interactive, seminar-styled manner. Class sessions combine lectures with discussions, hands-on lab sessions, problem-solving practice classes, and group work. All classes are held either on weekday evenings from 7pm onwards, Saturday mornings from 8.15am onwards, or Saturday afternoons from 12pm onwards. These timings have been chosen to accommodate the schedules of part-time students who are working, and full-time students who might be engaged with industry attachments. However, full-time students may have some weekday morning or afternoon classes (8.15am, 12pm or 3.30pm onwards) in their first term.
Artificial Intelligence Electives:
- Algorithm Design & Implementation; Applied Machine Learning*; Natural Language Processing for Smart Assistants*; Recommender Systems*; Agentic AI for Intelligent Autonomy; Human-AI Interaction Design; Artificial Intelligence and Uncertainty Reasoning*; Deep Learning for Visual Recognition#; Query Processing and Optimisation; Generative AI with LLMs*; Prompt Engineering for LLMs (0.5 CU); Machine Learning Engineering*; AI System Evaluation*; Introduction to Reinforcement Learning*; AI Adoption & Industry Analysis% (Without Credit); AI in Financial Markets Forecasting (0.5 CU).
- %The AI Adoption & Industry Analysis is a graduation requirement (without credit) for AI track students.
Graduation Requirements for Artificial Intelligence Track: Students must complete and pass a total of 15 Course Units (CUs) with a minimum cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.5 to graduate with the MITB degree.
- Postgraduate professional development course: 1 CU.
- Programme core: 3 CUs: Spreadsheet Modeling for Decision Making; Statistical Thinking for Data Science; Computational Thinking with Python.
- Track Core: 4 CUs: Algorithm Design & Implementation; Artificial Intelligence and Uncertainty Reasoning*; Applied Machine Learning*; Query Processing & Optimisation.
- Track electives: 3 CUs: Choose any 3 Artificial Intelligence Electives.
- Open electives: 4 CUs: Choose any 4 CUs from Internship or Capstone Project (2 CUs), courses from any series in the MITB curriculum, or courses from other SMU Masters programmes (up to 2 CUs).
Cybersecurity Electives:
- Cybersecurity Technology & Applications; AI-Driven Security Analysis; Threat Intelligence & Incident Response; Enterprise Cryptography; Strategic Cybersecurity Management; AI System Evaluation*#; Cloud Security; Agile & DevSecOps.
Graduation Requirements for Cybersecurity Track: Students must complete and pass a total of 15 Course Units (CUs) with a minimum cumulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.5 to graduate with the MITB degree.
- Postgraduate professional development course: 1 CU.
- Programme core: 3 CUs: Spreadsheet Modeling for Decision Making; Statistical Thinking for Data Science; Computational Thinking with Python.
- Track Core: 4 CUs: Cybersecurity Technology & Applications; Strategic Cybersecurity Management; Threat Intelligence & Incident Response; AI-Driven Security Analysis.
- Track electives: 3 CUs: Choose any 3 Cybersecurity Electives.
- Open electives: 4 CUs: Choose any 4 CUs from Internship or Capstone Project (2 CUs), courses from any series in the MITB curriculum, or courses from other SMU Masters programmes (up to 2 CUs).
Data Science & Analytics Electives:
- Data Management; Big Data: Tools & Techniques; Applied Data Science in Social Networks; Query Processing and Optimisation; Generative AI with LLMs*; Data Analytics Lab; Applied Data Science for Customer Insights (SMU-X); Visual Analytics & Applications; Geospatial Analytics & Applications; Applied Data Science in Healthcare (0.5 CU); Data Science for Business*; Applied Data Science in Operations; Text Analytics & Applications; Applied Machine Learning*; Prompt Engineering for LLMs (0.5 CU).
Graduation Requirements for Data Science & Analytics Track: Students must complete and pass a total of 15 Course Units (CUs) with a minimum cummulative Grade Point Average (GPA) of 2.5 to graduate with the MITB degree.
- Postgraduate professional development course: 1 CU.
- Programme core: 3 CUs: Spreadsheet Modeling for Decision Making; Statistical Thinking for Data Science; Computational Thinking with Python.
- Track Core: 4 CUs: Data Analytics Lab; Data Science for Business*; Applied Machine Learning*; Query Processing & Optimisation.
- Track electives: 3 CUs: Choose any 3 Data Science & Analytics Electives.
- Open Electives: 4 CUs: Choose any 4 CUs from Internship or Capstone Project (2 CUs), courses from any series in the MITB curriculum, or courses from other SMU Masters programmes (up to 2 CUs).
Postgraduate Professional Development Course:
- MITB Full-time Students: Compulsory to take 3 CDS workshops (0.25CU); select 3 remaining workshops from the other 3 buckets (0.75CU).
- MITB Part-time Students: CDS workshops are optional; select 4 workshops from any of the non-Career buckets to attain 1 CU.
The MITB Internship is an experiential learning experience for students to apply knowledge acquired in the MITB program within the professional setting. The internships are aligned with the aims of the MITB program and students’ respective tracks.
The MITB capstone project is an extensive, applied practice research project that is undertaken by students, supervised by SMU faculty members who have specific expertise and interest in the topic, and sometimes sponsored by external companies. Students shall identify a problem, develop the approach and methods needed to address the problem, and conduct the research and present the findings in both oral and written formats.
The Global Exposure Project (GEP) is a joint initiative between MITB and Sogang University, offered as a 1 CU practicum module, over a 5-week period during the July Term of the academic calendar.

program_overview.content:
The J.D. programme is a **full-time** 3-year programme, comprising 22 courses totaling 25 course units. The curriculum was formulated by legal academics and practitioners after extensive discussions, and endorsed by Singapore Institute of Legal Education and Ministry of Law. The academic year begins in mid-August and follows the same academic calendar/grading scheme as the LL.B programme. **The programme may be accelerated** in some cases for completion within 2 to 2.5 years subject to the approval of the J.D. Committee, which will take into consideration their first term's exam grades.
The J.D. programme bears SMU's distinctives of holistic learning, active seminar-style pedagogy and international and practical exposure. Students engage in a substantial amount of pre-class preparatory reading and thinking, and participate actively in class discussion. Classes are deliberately kept small and a multi-faceted approach to course assessment is adopted, including class participation, term assignments and oral and written presentations. A distinctive feature of the J.D. programme is that lawyers from practice, government and the judiciary will be invited to participate in classroom teaching, providing students with the opportunity to integrate practical expertise with theory and doctrine.
The J.D. programme is a meritorious honours programme. On successful completion, students will be awarded the degree accordingly, depending on their overall performance: J.D. (merit), J.D. (high merit), J.D. cum laude (with distinction), J.D. magna cum laude (with high distinction) or J.D. summa cum laude (with highest distinction). **Students will qualify for legal practice in Singapore (admitted as Advocate and Solicitor of the Supreme Court of Singapore) if they attain a GPA of at least 3.00 in the courses leading to the J.D. degree, and complete the Preparatory Course leading to Part B of the Singapore Bar Examinations conducted by the Singapore Legal Institute of Education, subject to the "Qualified Person" requirements imposed by the Legal Profession (Qualified Persons) Rules.**
Duration: 3 years

financial_aid.content:
The Singapore Management University (SMU) reserves the right to amend the discount schemes for new incoming cohorts when required. Discounts will not be awarded in conjunction with other ongoing discount schemes; discount and scholarship are not stackable. Should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount amount will be applicable.
- SMU Alumni: S$8,000 discount off total tuition fees (from 2025 intake onwards). SMU exchange and non-graduating students are not eligible for the alumni discount.
- Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents Discount: S$5,000 discount off total tuition fees (from 2025 intake onwards).
- ASEAN Nationals Discount: From 2025 intake onwards, a S$3,000 discount off total tuition fees is granted to students from ASEAN nations.
- SkillsFuture: SkillsFuture funding for Singapore Citizens is available; Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above can claim SkillsFuture Credit (Base Tier) and $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-career Tier). This credit is intended to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after 1 May 2024. SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy (up to 90% of course fees) is not applied to the SMU JD programme.
- SUTD Alumni Discount (PDPP): With effect from the 2019 admission intake, SUTD alumni who are offered a place in the J.D. programme will be granted a 10% discount under the Pre Experience Postgraduate Degree Experience Programme Agreement (PPDP), spread equally over the 4 payment instalments. The discount is only applicable when they apply within 5 years from graduation from SUTD.
- J.D. Scholarship (For Offered Candidates): Limited scholarships are available for outstanding applicants to the programme. With effect from the 2020 admission intake: First Tier: $10,000; Second Tier: $5,000. The scholarship amount shall be used to offset the programme fees across the four academic terms. Eligibility includes: offered a place in the J.D. Programme; a minimum of second class upper honors/Cum Laude degree qualification or a GPA equivalent; excellent application interview and essay scores; good letters of reference; preference will be given to students who demonstrate financial need. A complete description of the applicant’s financial status, including current savings, stocks, last monthly income as well as any outstanding debts, will be required together with the completed [scholarship application form](https://law.smu.edu.sg/sites/law.smu.edu.sg/files/2023-05/JDscholarshipapplication.pdf), emailed to the Programme Manager.
- J.D. Financial Aid (For J.D. Students): The J.D. Financial Aid is given to J.D. students who face a sudden change in financial circumstances while studying in the programme. Up to $10,000 payable in 4 equal instalments will be used to offset the student’s term course fee across the academic terms. Eligibility: matriculated in the J.D. Programme; minimum CGPA of 3.4 in the J.D. programme; evidence of financial need. Relevant documents together with the completed [scholarship application form](https://law.smu.edu.sg/sites/law.smu.edu.sg/files/2023-05/JDscholarshipapplication.pdf) need to be submitted to the J.D. programme manager.
- Kwa Geok Choo Scholarship (Postgraduate): For J.D. students who have completed at least one year of SMU J.D. studies. Up to 4 postgraduate scholarships will be awarded each year. Each scholarship is tenable for one year, subject to outstanding academic performance and continued observance of the eligibility criteria. Eligibility includes: present full-time SMU Juris Doctor student of any nationality who has completed at least one year of full-time SMU J.D. studies; outstanding academic results (minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7); outstanding leadership qualities; active involvement in co-curricular activities; and demonstrates a spirit of volunteerism. The scholarship has a value of $30,000 and will offer financial support towards tuition fees, living allowances and the purchase of textbooks. No bond is required. Students who meet the CGPA criteria will be sent the application form.
- Course Awards (For J.D. Students): Course awards can be found [here](https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/financial-matters/financial-aid). Students should key in "Juris Doctor" in the search bar to see the awards that JD students are eligible for.
- Wee Chong Jin Top J.D. Graduate Award: Given to the top graduate of the Doctor of Jurisprudence Programme at the Yong Pung How School of Law each year. Each Award has a value of S$6,000.
- Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship: Applicants must be Singapore citizens and will be assessed holistically, including track record of leadership and achievement and potential to excel in their fields/professions. More details and application process can be found [here](https://www.psc.gov.sg/scholarships/postgraduate-scholarships/lee-kuan-yew-scholarship).

program_overview.content:
Singapore, one of the world’s most cosmopolitan cities, has emerged as Asia’s legal and financial hub. As an integral part of the central business district where leading law firms and banks are located, Singapore Management University (SMU) is at the forefront of legal education.
The SMU LLM programme is carefully designed to expand your legal knowledge in classic and novel areas of the law, while simultaneously equipping you with the skills-sets essential to render on-point advice on cross-border transactions or deliver high-quality adjudication and judicial administration results.
Our professors who have gained insight from diverse work experiences will engage you with their interdisciplinary knowledge. Small class sizes allow for highly interactive seminars that also provide a challenging yet collegial learning environment.
The School of Law’s active engagement with the legal community, as well as our strong alumni network and the Career Services team, immensely benefit students’ future careers. The SMU LLM will offer you an unparalleled opportunity for advanced legal education in Singapore and Asia.
Duration: 1 year

An international student in Singapore spends, on average, about S$1,000 to S$3,000 a month on living expenses. This amount will vary depending on lifestyle and course of study.

| Utilities (including water and electricity) | $40 - $100 | |

financial_aid.content:
The Singapore Management University (SMU) reserves the right to amend the discount schemes for new incoming cohorts when required. Discounts will not be awarded in conjunction with other ongoing discount schemes; discount and scholarship are not stackable. Should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount amount will be applicable.
- **SMU Alumni:** S$8,000 discount off total tuition fees from 2025 intake onwards.
- **Singapore Citizens/ Permanent Residents Discount:** S$5,000 discount off total tuition fees from 2025 intake onwards.
- **SMU LLM Scholarship:** Up to four bond-free scholarships per academic year. Each scholarship has an annual value of S$10,000, disbursed in 2 equal installments of $5,000 to offset tuition fees in Term 1 and Term 2. Open to all LLM applicants, full-time and part-time, who are offered a place in the programme; applicants must not be recipients of other scholarship or sponsorship. Application via an application form is required once applicants accept the offer.
- **ASEAN Nationals Discount:** From 2025 intake onward, a S$3,000 discount off total tuition fees is granted to students from ASEAN nations.
- **SMU PG ASEAN Scholarship:** The scholarship co-funds outstanding individuals in pursuit of the SMU LLM / Dual LLM programme. It has a value of $10,000 and offers financial support towards tuition fees, living allowances and the purchase of textbooks. No bond is required. Open to citizens of ASEAN member and observer nations; at least "Very Good" admissions interview and essay scores; must not be a recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship; special consideration may be given to students with financial needs. No application is required; eligible ASEAN candidates will automatically be considered.
- **SkillsFuture:** SkillsFuture funding for Singapore Citizens is available; Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above can claim SkillsFuture Credit (Base Tier) and $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-career Tier). This credit is intended to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after 1 May 2024. SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy up to 90% of course fees is not applied to the SMU LLM programme.
- **Post Secondary Education Account (PSEA):** Singapore Citizens with eligible Post Secondary Education Account may utilize balance funds for tuition fees.
- **Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship:** Applicants must be Singapore citizens and will be assessed holistically, including track record of leadership and achievement and potential to contribute to and benefit Singapore and society.
- **Jones Day Master of Laws in Judicial Studies Scholarship:** Up to four scholarships for outstanding candidates enrolled in LLM (Judicial Studies). Candidates must have been accepted into the LLM (Judicial Studies), not be a Singapore citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident, hold an LLB or JD from a reputable law school, demonstrate strong leadership aspirations and abilities, and have strong professional references. Two Jones Day (Judicial Studies) Scholarships for international candidates of $40,000 each; bond-free. Candidates cannot simultaneously hold any other scholarships.
- **Jones Day Master of Laws Annual Top Scholar Award (for Judicial Studies):** The best performing graduate of the LLM in Judicial Studies will receive the Jones Day Top Scholar Award. One award per annum, with a monetary value of S$10,000.
- **Lee Kong Chian Master of Laws in Judicial Studies Scholarship:** Up to six annual scholarships for outstanding candidates enrolled in LLM (Judicial Studies), intended to offset tuition fees and cannot be used to defray living expenses. Up to 4 Singapore citizens or permanent residents and up to 2 international candidates. Candidates must have been accepted into the LLM (Judicial Studies), hold an LLB or JD from a reputable law school, demonstrate strong leadership aspirations and abilities, and have strong professional references; special consideration may be given to candidates who demonstrate financial need, in particular those from non-OECD countries. Four scholarships for Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents of $20,000 each; two scholarships for international candidates of $40,000 each; bond-free. Candidates cannot simultaneously hold any other scholarships.

interview_requirements.content:
At Singapore Management University (SMU), the interview is more than just an evaluation exercise. It is an opportunity for the admissions committee to understand your motivations, experiences, communication style, and how you may contribute to the classroom experience and broader SMU community. Whether you are applying for programmes in Management, Finance, Business Analytics, Economics, Accounting, or other postgraduate disciplines, preparation and authenticity go a long way.
- The admissions panel is often looking at qualities such as clarity of career goals and motivations, communication and articulation skills, self-awareness and maturity, curiosity and willingness to learn, ability to contribute to peer learning discussions, business awareness and critical thinking, and alignment between your aspirations and the programme.
- One of the most common interview questions is: “Why are you interested in this programme?” Strong candidates should explain what specific skills or exposure they hope to gain, why this programme fits their career trajectory, and why this is the right stage in their career to pursue postgraduate studies.
- Interviewers may ask broader or unexpected questions such as: “Tell us about a challenge you faced and how you handled it,” “What are some trends currently impacting your industry?”, “What is a recent business issue or news topic that caught your attention?”, “What do you think you can contribute to the classroom?”, “How do you handle disagreements within a team?”, and “What would success look like for you after graduation?”
- For candidates applying to more technical programmes, there may also be questions related to quantitative readiness, coding exposure, analytical thinking, and problem-solving approaches.
- The best interviews often feel less like an interrogation and more like a meaningful conversation. It is fine to pause briefly to gather your thoughts, ask clarifying questions, admit areas where you are still learning, and reflect honestly on your experiences.
- The interview process helps ensure that students not only benefit from the experience but also contribute meaningfully to the learning journey of others. The interview is also an opportunity to evaluate whether the programme aligns with your own goals and aspirations.

program_overview.content:
The SMU Master of Science in Management (MIM) programme is designed for individuals with no prior business experience to transit successfully to the world of business. With a comprehensive curriculum that covers the latest business trends, this programme offers a broad but rigorous education in business management.
The programme is a full-time, 18-month programme with two intakes per year, one in January and one in August. It is intended to appeal to students with limited or no previous business experience who are seeking a well-rounded orientation to business management. Students will develop business and management skills, enhance employment versatility in the workplace and possess the knowledge needed to be successful in today’s global environment. The programme is also suitable for those who intend to start their own businesses in the future as it covers all aspects of managing a business enterprise.
Programme highlights include practical experience through internships, immersive case studies, SMU-X Overseas and exchange programs with partner universities including London Business School in the UK and IE Business School in Spain. The syllabus integrates areas such as AI, digital transformation, sustainability, strategic problem-solving, leadership, business acumen, guest lectures from industry leaders, professional development workshops and career coaching.
Master of Science in Management (MiM) Class Profile:
- Average Age: 25
- Students: 147
- International Students: 92%
- Nationalities: 18
The programme structure includes 8 Core Modules, elective modules, an SMU-XO course, internship, and Postgraduate Professional Development Workshop. Programme highlights include:
- Internship: The internship lasts a minimum of 10 weeks and provides students with opportunities across a wide range of companies, varying in size and industry, with a monthly stipend ranging from S$1,200 to S$2,000.
- SMU-XO: SMU-X Overseas (SMU-XO) project focuses on business challenges outside Singapore. Learn more [here](https://x.smu.edu.sg/about/what-is-smu-x-overseas).
- SMU-X: SMU-X elective courses emphasize experiential and holistic learning through hands-on projects aimed at applying concepts from the classroom to solve real business issues and problems.
There are optional concentration tracks for the elective portion of the MIM programme: Marketing, Finance, Operations Management and Sustainability. Students are required to choose tracks by the end of Term 2 if they pursue a concentration. Each student may elect one concentration area; it will not reflect on the degree scroll but will be noted on the transcript.
SMU has earned accreditation from AACSB International (AACSB) for both its business and accounting undergraduate and postgraduate programmes. SMU is also one of the few Asian universities to receive a five-year EQUIS accreditation.
Career counselling and workshops will be provided to MIM students and attendance is compulsory. MIM students have access to a career counsellor who will assist on post-graduation placement through guidance and advice. The internship component is expected to improve employability by providing opportunities for early exposure to the work environment of Singapore.
SMU MIM graduates are able to explore options in different business functions such as logistics, shipping, marketing, sales and finance. Graduates can also continue to work in specialised fields such as law, architecture and engineering and complement their professions with a better understanding of how a business operates.
Our MiM graduates are hired across a wide range of industries, including Technology (23%), Audit/Accounting (14%), Financial Services (13%), Retail/Wholesale (7%), Manufacturing (7%), Consumer/Luxury Goods (5%), Transportation/Logistics (5%) and Others (26%). Over 60% of MiM graduates are involved in job functions such as Finance/Accounting, Marketing/Sales and General Management: Finance/Accounting (28%), Marketing/Sales (25%), General Management (14%), Operations (9%), Consulting (9%) and Others (15%).
Duration: 18 months

curriculum.content:
The MiM programme has two intakes every year, in January and Aug. Their respective structures are as below:
| Intake | Period 1 | Period 2 | Period 3 | Period 4 | Period 5 | Period 6 | Period 7 | Period 8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **JAN INTAKE** | Jan - Mar: 4 Core Modules | Apr - Jun: 4 Core Modules; Open Modules | Jul: PGPD* workshop | Aug - Nov: 4 Electives | Nov - Dec: PGPD* workshop / Business Study Mission | Jan - Apr: Immersion** | Jun: Graduation | |
| **AUG INTAKE** | Aug - Nov: 4 Core Modules | Nov - Dec: PGPD* workshop; Open Modules | Jan - Mar: 4 Core Modules | Apr - Jun: Immersion** | Jul: PGPD* workshop | Aug - Nov: 4 Electives | Nov - Dec: Business Study Mission | Jan: Graduation |
*PGPD = Postgraduate Professional Development. **Immersion = Internship and Consulting Project.**
The programme curriculum consists of **16 Credit Units (CU)**: Postgraduate Professional Development course (1 CU) + Programme Core (8 CU) + Track Electives (4 CU) + Immersion (1 CU) + Open Modules (2 CU).
Programme highlights include:
- **Internship:** Meld academic concepts with actual business situations and put knowledge into practice with a **minimum 10-week internship** depending on employer requirements.
- **Consulting Project:** Apply academic theories to tackle business challenges with a real business client. Designed based on SMU-X pedagogy, the Project is a project-based learning experience.
- **Global Exposure:** Experience ASEAN countries through company visits and the Business Study Mission, or pursue electives in partner schools in the global MiM network comprising London Business School or Imperial College Business School in the United Kingdom, ESMT Berlin in Germany, and Smith School of Business at Queen’s University in Canada.
8 Core Modules:

- ECON672 Global Economics
- OBHR624 Managing People & Organizations
- ACCT647 Accounting
- OPIM617 Operations & Supply Chain Management
- OPIM628 Business Analytics
- MGMT672 Strategy
- FNCE680 Corporate Finance
Elective Modules: Students choose **4 from 22** elective modules, from Common Elective Modules and Track-Specific Elective Modules. Track-Specific Elective Modules are for students who would like to do a concentration in Finance, Operations Management, Marketing, or Sustainability by taking 4 elective courses to specialise in a single track.
Common Elective Modules:
- COMM662 Management Communication
- MGMT696 Design Thinking & Creativity
- OBHR617 Negotiating in Business
- MGMT6027 Communicating Across Cultures
- MGMT687 Business Study Mission
Finance Track Elective Modules, choose any 4 courses being offered:

- FNCE6045 Sustainable Finance
Operations Management Track Elective Modules, choose any 4 courses being offered:
- OPIM618 Decision Analytics
- OPIM630 Risk Management: Building Resilient Supply Chains
- OPIM633 Online Business and Marketplaces
- OPIM632 Sustainable Operations
- OPIM629 Successful Project Management
Marketing Track Elective Modules, choose any 4 courses being offered:
- MKTG625 Consumer Behaviour
- MKTG640 Behavioural Science in Marketing
- MKTG624 Marketing Analytics (SMU-X)
- MKTG628 Digital Marketing (SMU-X)
- MKTG637 Marketing Research

Sustainability Track Elective modules, choose any 4 courses being offered:
- MGMT6026 Entrepreneurship and Intrapreneurship
- FNCE6045 Sustainable Finance
- OPIM632 Sustainable Operations
- MGMT6017 Sustainable Impact
- MKTG641 Marketing in a Sustainable World

financial_aid.content:
Students may apply for our SMU MiM Programme Scholarships upon admission. These Scholarships entail award amounts up to 30% of the tuition fee, with no bonds attached.
Scholarships include: AGL Irudayaraj Scholarship, Academic Excellence, Global Awareness, Leadership Potential, Community Impact, Impact on Asia, and Women in Business. Scholarships denoted with * are scholarships that students can apply for upon admissions into the programme.
- **AGL Irudayaraj Scholarship**: motivates outstanding postgraduates of Indian ethnicity at the University to greater heights of academic excellence. The Admissions Scholarship Committee will assess interview performance and an essay: “Please describe in 500 words why you should receive the AGL Irudayaraj Scholarship. You should elaborate on your leadership experience, community involvement and financial need, if any."
- **Ayala Postgraduate Scholarship**: valued at S$25 000, for outstanding candidates from the Philippines pursuing postgraduate education. The Admissions Scholarship Committee will assess outstanding and deserving candidates from the Philippines; full-time/part-time students matriculated to the MBA or MiM Programme; and special consideration will be given to those who demonstrate financial need.
- **Academic Excellence**: offered to high-quality candidates with exceptional academic performance. Awards are based on academic merit, final grades and GMAT score. Tier One awardees must have achieved a GMAT of 700 or above; Tier Two awardees must have achieved a GMAT of 680 or above.
- **Global Awareness**: given to individuals who will contribute to the classroom diversity and enrich the learning experience of students by way of cultural, personal or professional backgrounds.
- **Leadership Potential**: recognises individuals with strong leadership potential who have exhibited outstanding leadership potential during their studies, community or organization. Applicants must demonstrate strong leadership potential in personal and professional instances.
- **Community Impact Award**: recognises candidates who have contributed to society through outstanding community work and have impacted members of the community/society in a positive manner.
- **Impact on Asia**: for students who can demonstrate achievements in their professional, social and personal life that have created an impact on Asia.
- **Women in Business Award**: recognises exceptional women who have demonstrated outstanding leadership capabilities or potential in their professional or personal endeavours. Applicants must have successfully received an admissions offer.
**Alumni Discount**: Graduates from SMU undergraduate or postgraduate programmes are automatically eligible for an alumni discount when applying to the MiM programme.

You are required to take an Admission Test for admission to the MPA programme, regardless of your academic background or prior qualifications.

However, meeting the cGPA academic input does not guarantee acceptance and candidates may still be asked to take the GMAT/GRE/SMU Admission Test.
- To enhance the competitiveness of your application, you should attain a **GMAT score of 600 or higher**, OR a **GMAT Focus edition score of 595 or higher**. To make your application more competitive, you should achieve a minimum **GRE combined score of verbal and quantitative components of 312**.
- SMU's GMAT institution code for MPA is **F8D-3B-56**. Official score reports can be sent via the following Institution Codes: GMAT: **F8D-3B-56**; GRE: **2861** (Department Code: **4001 - Accounting**).
- Candidates without GMAT/GRE or with low scores have the option to sit for the [SMU Admissions Test (SMUAT)](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/sites/masters.smu.edu.sg/files/PDF%20docs/SMU%20candidate%20guide_refreshed.pdf). The SMUAT is an online test that can be done from home. If you dont sit for SMUAT, then SMU will need your GMAT/GRE score to assess your application.

- SMU's institution code for TOEFL is **9014**; official score reports can be sent using TOEFL institution code **9014** (Department Name: Accounting).
- Documents to submit include IELTS/TOEFL if undergraduate degree was not taught in English.

program_overview.content:
The SMU Master of Professional Accounting (MPA) is offered full-time over 18 months, with flexibility to complete in 12 months, or part-time over 24 months. The programme is designed to provide a structured pathway into the accountancy profession for graduates from non-accounting disciplines, as well as professionals seeking to strengthen their accounting expertise. It prepares graduates for careers in professional services, finance, and corporate accounting roles across a wide range of industries.
The MPA programme consists of 14 course units (CU), including 8CU programme core, 4CU programme electives, 1CU general elective including internship, and 1CU postgraduate professional development course. Students may opt to undertake an internship in lieu of one general elective course to satisfy the graduation requirement; eligible students may complete the internship at any point during their course of study, provided that the minimum duration of 10 weeks is fulfilled. Full-time students continue from August to January after Term 3 for internship and/or exchange/overseas immersion programme. Part-time students are enrolled in evening classes.
The SMU MPA offers an accelerated route towards qualification for CPA or CA status and is recognised by **nine leading global and local professional accountancy bodies**. These recognitions offer eligible graduates multiple accelerated pathways towards professional qualifications and memberships across different accounting specialisations and jurisdictions.
The programme incorporates emerging skill sets in data technologies, sustainability reporting, and analytics, equipping students with up-to-date knowledge and practical capabilities. It also offers industrial internships and overseas study immersion programmes or exchanges as part of the MPA.
More than 88% of SMU MPA graduates are employed within six months of graduation, based on a survey conducted for students who graduated in 2024. program_overview.content:
The Master of Science in Quantitative Finance (MQF) curriculum is tailored to meet the needs of the financial industry in three key areas: pricing and hedging, risk analytics and management, and quantitative trading and investment.
The programme is available in full-time and part-time modes. The programme duration for both the SMU MQF Local track and International track is 12 months + internship. The Local track is also available in a part-time mode of study at 24 months. The same core modules apply for both tracks.
- **Local track**: Students take all courses at SMU in Singapore and obtain an SMU MQF Degree. This is the preferred path for those already working in Singapore or who are unable to spend four months in London on the international track.
- **International track**: Students take Term 1 and Term 3 courses at SMU in Singapore, and Term 2 courses at Bayes Business School in London, UK, and graduate with a Joint MQF degree from both institutions.
On top of being Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB) and European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS) accredited, the Lee Kong Chian School of Business is highly ranked for its research productivity, teaching effectiveness, graduate employability and international reputation.
The SMU MSc in Quantitative Finance is designed to equip students with both an in-depth knowledge of quantitative finance and a business-oriented, entrepreneurial mindset. The curriculum bridges theory and practice, helping students build expertise and skillsets that can be immediately applied to solving real-world problems. The curriculum consists of nine core modules and four elective modules. Students may choose to specialise in one of the following elective tracks: Financial Data Science, Algorithmic Trading and Risk Analytics. The Open Module refers to an Internship OR MQF elective OR other modules offered by other Schools.
Students learn to trade real-time with live data and master trading algorithms and microstructure under the guidance of knowledgeable faculty with current and extensive quant trading experience. Students may specialise in Algorithmic Trading, Financial Data Science, Quantitative Trading or Risk Analytics.
Class profile, from Classes of 2018-2021 (Full-time & Part-time): gender ratio 13 : 7; average age 26; international students 73%; nationalities 8; average years of work experience 2.3.
Alumni outcomes and testimonials include Anirudh Somani, Head of Actuarial & Research at 360F, Class of 2020, and Tricia Goh, International Private Bank Graduate Analyst at Deutsche Bank, Class of 2021. Tricia Goh described the MQF programme as “a balanced marriage of mathematics, finance and programming” and noted opportunities to network with industry professionals through professors' networks and career talks organised by SMU Postgraduate Career Services.
Industries that MQF graduates work in, based on graduating students from 2020 and 2021: Audit / Accounting 4%; Commodities 5%; Consulting 8%; Financial Services 55%; Technology 19%.
The MQF programme equips finance and banking industry professionals and fresh graduates with current knowledge, skills, and industry best practices in risk management, algorithmic trading, portfolio optimisation, model validation, pricing and hedging across multiple asset classes and markets. Both MAF and MQF programmes are applicable to candidates planning to switch career from non-finance to the finance and banking industries.
The programme provides graduates a bridge to enter the finance and banking industries, especially those that require a high degree of computing and mathematical skills.
Students of the MQF programme are required to complete nine cores, four electives, a Postgraduate Professional Development course and one open module. The MQF is an 18-month programme, which can also be completed in 12 months, comprising two options: the local and international option. The local option is also available in a part-time mode of study at 24 months.
The programme is taught by well-qualified and experienced SMU and Bayes Business School professors as well as industry professionals.
Duration: 18 months

- **International track:** You will take your Term 1 and Term 3 Courses at SMU (Singapore), and Term 2 Courses at Bayes Business School (London, UK), and graduate with a Joint MQF degree from both institutions.

Students of the MQF programme are required to complete **nine cores, four electives, a Postgraduate Professional Development course and one open* module**. The local option is also availiable in a part-time mode of study at **24 months**.
Both tracks offer the same curriculum and list of modules, both core and elective. The key difference lies in the exposure, where students of the International track will spend **3 months in Bayes Business School in London completing 4 core modules**, and students of the Singapore track will complete their entire programme in SMU.

*Denotes scholarships that students can apply for upon admission into the programme.*
These Scholarships entail award amounts up to **30% of the tuition fee**, with no bonds attached.
- **Academic Excellence:** The SMU MQF will offer the Academic Excellence Award to high-quality candidates with exceptional academic performance. Awards are based on academic merit, final grades and GMAT score. Tier One: Awardees must have achieved a GMAT of 720 or above. Tier Two: Awardees must have achieved a GMAT of 700 or above.
- **Global Awareness:** SMU MQF Programme is committed to crafting a very diverse and global academic environment. The Global Awareness Award is given to individuals who will contribute to the class room diversity and enrich the learning experience of students by way of cultural, personal or professional backgrounds.
- **Leadership:** With a Leadership Award, the SMU MQF Programme recognises individuals with strong leadership potential who have exhibited outstanding leadership potential during their studies, community or organisation. Applicants must demonstrate strong leadership potential in personal and professional instances.
- **Community Impact:** The SMU MQF nurtures keen minds profoundly committed to leaving a positive impact on the community. The "Community Impact Award" recognises candidates who have contributed to society through outstanding community work and through their actions, have impacted members of the community/society in a positive manner.
- **Impact on Asia:** The SMU MQF is creating a significant impact in Singapore, extending now to Asia. Candidates should demonstrate achievements in their professional, social and personal life that have created an impact on Asia.
- **Women in Business:** With the Women in Business Award, the SMU MQF aims to recognise exceptional women who have demonstrated outstanding leadership capabilities or potential in their professional or personal endeavours. Applicants must have successfully received an admissions offer.
Lee Kuan Yew Scholarships: Established in honour of Singapore's former Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew, this scholarship recognises outstanding individuals with strong academic aptitude and the inclination to serve and contribute to the Singapore society at large. Eligibility criteria: 1. A Singapore citizen with at least a Second Upper Honours Degree or equivalent Degree 2. Excellent track record of leadership and service within or beyond applicant's profession. In addition to the one-off sum of S$10,000, private sector awardees will receive an annual allowance of S$50,000, while public sector awardees will receive S$10,000 if they are concurrently sponsored by their organisations.

program_overview.content:
18 months full-time (with flexibility to complete in 11 months); 30 months part-time (with flexibility to complete in 23 months).
The SMU Master of Sustainability (MST) programme delivers an inter-disciplinary curriculum, drawing on the breadth of domains across SMU schools to prepare students for current and future jobs in the green economy. Through the MST, students will engage in learning about the sustainable use of organisational and natural resources in service of socially equitable outcomes through an emphasis on essential core skills in sustainability reasoning, communication, coordination, and management. They would also gain familiarity with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the fundamentals of Singapore's Green Plan 2030. Recognising the dynamic nature of sustainability roles across various sectors, the programme is led by the School of Social Sciences and College of Integrative Studies to prepare students for thriving careers in the green economy.
The programme is a first-of-its-kind programme at SMU that merges the strengths of the School of Social Sciences and College of Integrative Studies, offering an inter-disciplinary, industry-aligned curriculum. It is designed to align with major international regulatory frameworks, such as the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs), and the Singapore Green Plan 2030. Students deepen their knowledge by selecting one of three thematic tracks in the areas of **Sustainable Resource Management**, **Urban Systems Management**, or **Environment and Sustainable Development**, or develop a broad sustainable lens without a specialisation.
Designed for flexibility, the MST programme is available in both full-time and part-time formats. It operates on 3 regular terms comprising 10 study weeks, 1 term break recess week and 1 week to administer examinations each term. All classes are held either on weekday evenings from 7pm onwards, Saturday mornings from 8.15am onwards, or Saturday afternoons from 12pm onwards. MST class sessions are 3 hours long, and are conducted in a highly interactive, seminar-styled manner. Class sessions combine lectures with discussions and group work. Through the pedagogy, students have the opportunity to interact closely with faculty, full-time professional instructors, and student teaching assistants. Students also meet with industry experts who share their experiences and perspectives through regular seminars organised by the MST programme.
The MST programme is designed to empower students as global citizens of tomorrow by providing a transformative educational experience and fostering meaningful engagement with the world around them. Students are required to complete 7 core modules, 3 courses from one of three thematic tracks, 2 MST electives, an open elective, participate in an internship or SMU-X and complete the postgraduate professional development requirement. Internship is optional for full-time students and exemptions will be made for part-time students who are currently employed. Students may also take an SMU-X course to fulfil the immersion requirement.
Industries MST graduates will work in include development finance, sustainability reporting and assurance, ESG and sustainability solution marketing, corporate strategy and development, strategic sustainability consulting, and sustainability policy professional. MST graduates will be equipped to embark on sustainability and ESG related roles including but not limited to corporate strategy and development, strategic sustainability consulting, public policy, sustainability reporting and assurance, development finance, ESG and sustainability solution marketing. All students will have a dedicated career coach assigned throughout the Masters Programme, with support including career planning and coaching, internship and job search, resume and cover letter critique, interview preparation, personality inventories, recruitment and networking events, and career development workshops. The MST programme director and manager works closely with industry partners and SMU Career Services Office to offer internship opportunities for students.
Duration: 18 months

curriculum.content:
- The Master of Sustainability (MST) is available in both full-time and part-time formats: **18 months full-time** with flexibility to complete in **11 months**, and **30 months part-time** with flexibility to complete in **23 months**. Full-time candidature is a minimum of one year and up to **5 terms**; part-time candidature is a minimum of two years to a maximum of **8 terms**.
- The programme operates on **3 regular terms** comprising **10 study weeks**, **1 term break recess week** and **1 week** to administer examinations each term. During a regular term, full-time students may take up to **5 Course Units (CUs)**, while part-time students may take up to **3 CUs**. Students may also enrol in special terms within their normal candidature period; special terms are held from July to August and November to December, with **10 sessions delivered through twice-weekly classes**.
- All classes are held either on weekday evenings from **7pm onwards**, Saturday mornings from **8.15am onwards**, or Saturday afternoons from **12pm onwards**. Full-time students may have some weekday morning or afternoon classes (**8.15am, 12pm or 3.30pm onwards**) in their first term. MST class sessions are **3 hours long** and conducted in a highly interactive, seminar-styled manner.
- Students are required to complete **7 core modules**, **3 courses from one of three thematic tracks**, **2 MST electives**, **an open elective**, participate in **an internship or SMU-X**, and complete the **postgraduate professional development requirement**.
- **Programme Core (7 CUs):** Principles of Climate Change; Collaborative Governance; UN SDG and Sustainability Policy; Inequalities in Sustainability; Systems Thinking; Sustainability Reporting; Foundations in Sustainable Finance. The seven programme core courses are compulsory and non-exemptible.
- **Thematic Track Core (3 CUs):** Sustainable Resource Management (SRM), Urban Systems Management (USM), or Environment and Sustainable Development (ESD).
- **Sustainable Resource Management (SRM):** Sustainable Agriculture & Food Systems; Energy Transitions for Sustainability; Politics of Water / Sustainable Infrastructure & Water. Politics of Water and Sustainable Infrastructure & Water are interchangeable under the Sustainable Resource Management track.
- **Urban Systems Management (USM):** Business and Climate Change; Principles of the Circular Economy; Urban Sustainability.
- **Environment and Sustainable Development (ESD):** Social Entrepreneurship & Financial Inclusion; Development, Poverty and Sustainability or Sustainability Law; Environmental Economics.
- Students may select one specialised thematic track **or** develop a broad sustainable lens without a specialisation and choose any combination of **5 electives** from the tracks or the common electives basket.
- **Common Electives (2 CUs):** Psychology of Sustainability; Behavioural Insights for Sustainability; Digital Technologies for Sustainability; Sustainability Innovation; AI and Sustainable Development; Sustainable Infrastructure & Water; Independent Study Module. The list of common electives is not exhaustive and varies termly.
- **Internship or SMU-X Course (1 CU):** Internship is optional for full-time students and exemptions will be made for part-time students who are currently employed. Students may also take an SMU-X course to fulfil the immersion requirement. Typically, the internship period is **10 weeks**; students do their internship during the one year full-time study candidature and may do their internship during term time while taking evening classes.
- **Open Elective (1 CU):** Select one course from any of the thematic tracks and common electives, or from selected Master courses offered by other SMU schools.
- **Postgraduate Professional Development (1 CU):** Select **4 workshop topics** during the candidature period. Visit [https://smu.sg/pgpd](https://smu.sg/pgpd) for more details.
- Students may read up to **2 additional CUs** beyond the graduation requirement.
- Students may switch between full-time and part-time modes of candidature at any time, but the change can only be made once and is subject to approval from the MST programme director. Students may also switch to another track after declaration, but the change can only be made once and is subject to approval from the MST programme director.

financial_aid.content:
All candidates are automatically submitted for consideration for MST Academic Excellence Scholarship, MST Scholarship and SMU Masters ASEAN Scholarships upon meeting the respective scholarship criteria.
- **Master of Sustainability (MST) Academic Excellence Scholarship**: Each scholarship, valued at **S$10,000**, is tenable for the duration of the scholar's studies, subject to good academic results. The Scholarship will offer partial financial support towards tuition fees. No bond is required. No application is required; it is awarded to students enrolled in the MST programme after due consideration by the faculty. Eligibility criteria include outstanding academic results; leadership potential, resourcefulness, and innovative thinking; qualities to be a good ambassador of the MST; and must not be a concurrent recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship. The recipient must maintain a cumulative minimum GPA of **3.0**.
- **Master of Sustainability (MST) Scholarship**: Each scholarship, valued at **S$5,000**, is tenable for the duration of the scholar's studies, subject to good academic results. The Scholarship will offer partial financial support towards tuition fees. No bond is required. No application is required; it is awarded to students in the MST Programme after due consideration by the faculty. Eligibility criteria include good academic results; leadership potential, resourcefulness, and innovative thinking; qualities to be a good ambassador of the MST; must not be a concurrent recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship; and special consideration may be given to students with financial needs. The recipient must maintain a cumulative minimum GPA of **3.0**.
- **SMU Masters ASEAN Scholarship**: The scholarship comprises a monetary award of **S$10,000** (inclusive of GST) that co-funds outstanding individuals in his/her pursuit of the MST. No bond is required. All eligible applicants are automatically considered; no additional application is required. Eligibility criteria include citizenship of ASEAN member countries or observer nations (Papua New Guinea and Timor-Leste); recipient must matriculate into the MST programme; candidate’s academic entry criteria is “very good” or “excellent” (**Minimum GMAT score 650 or equivalent**); leadership potential; qualities of MST ambassador; must not be a recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship; special consideration may be given to students with financial needs.
- **SMU Warriors Scholarship (SWS)**: For more details, visit [SMU Warriors Scholarship | SMU PG Admissions](https://masters.smu.edu.sg/smu-warriors-scholarship). Only MINDEF personnel who are Singapore citizens with not less than 10 years of full-time military service shall be eligible to apply. The applicant must be due to retire from MINDEF within no more than 3 years after the start of the relevant programme, or have retired from MINDEF for not more than 1 year prior to the start of the relevant programme, and in any event must be in-service at the point of application to SMU; satisfy all admission requirements imposed by the relevant postgraduate degree; and be recommended by SAF Personnel Management Centre (PMC) and Career Transition Resource Centre (CTRC).
- **Jollibee Group Foundation Postgraduate Scholarship**: Each scholarship award is valued at **S$20,000**. Each scholarship is tenable for the duration of the scholar's studies (up to two years), subject to good academic results. The Scholarship will offer financial support towards MST tuition fees. No bond is required. A separate application for the Jollibee Group Postgraduate Scholarship is required, after application to the MST programme has been completed. Valid for **2024-2026 intakes**. Successful MST applicants will be required to submit a separate application form for the scholarship [here](https://forms.office.com/r/FwS13sCwds). Eligibility criteria include full-time students successfully admitted to the MST programme; citizens of the Philippines; good academic achievements, as determined by SMU; those with demonstrated greater financial needs will be prioritised; and must not be a concurrent recipient of other scholarship or sponsorship. The recipient must maintain a cumulative minimum GPA of **3.0**.
- **Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship**: Scholarship recipients will receive full tuition fees coverage and an annual allowance of **S$50,000** for up to 2 years if they are pursuing a Master’s degree. Public sector awardees who are already sponsored by their agencies for their postgraduate studies will receive a one-off sum of **S$10,000**. Eligibility criteria: Singapore citizen with at least a Second Upper Honours Degree or equivalent Degree; excellent track record of leadership and service within or beyond applicant's profession. More information and application form/procedures are available [here](https://www.psc.gov.sg/home).
- **Sustainability Stewardship Award for the Top Master of Sustainability Student**: Prize value of **S$3,000**. One Award will be awarded in each academic year. Candidates must be matriculated Master of Sustainability students in their final year of study. The Award will be awarded to the top student who has achieved exceptional academic results and demonstrated commitment in the sustainability industry. Eligible candidates would be invited to respond to questions pertaining to their area of study and future endeavours in sustainability, which will be vetted by the review committee.

curriculum.content:
- The Master of Science in Wealth Management (MWM) has a **12-month duration (Modular)** and is completed within 12 months.
- The programme comprises five study blocks where classes will be conducted on **Wednesday evenings, Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays**.
- Students are required to attend an overseas segment at **University of St. Gallen (HSG)** and **Cambridge Judge Business School** for two consecutive weeks during the fourth study block.
- The graduation requirement is **15 Credit Units (CUs)** and a minimum CGPA of **2.5**. The core curriculum consists of **15 CUs**.
- Students undergo a preparatory module before the first study block, and the programme culminates in the completion of an **individual project on a research topic of your choosing**.
- Classroom learning is complemented by case studies, team activities, pre-course assignments, computer-aided learning, simulations, industry talks, site visits and field trips. The programme’s modular structure allows students to meet professional and personal obligations while pursuing an academic degree.
- Internship is optional and can be done any time during the period of study. Students have the opportunity upon application to intern in various financial institutes during a one-year period.
**Preparatory Modules**
- Jul Prep & Induction: Online Matriculation; Boot Camp; Orientation and Team Building.
**Core Modules**
- Aug Study Block I: Financial Statement Analysis; Macroeconomics and Global Financial Markets; Quant Methods for Investment Analysis; Corporate Finance.
- Oct Study Block II: Analysis of Equities and ETF; Analysis of Fixed Income; Analysis & Applications of Derivatives.
- Jan Study Block III: Portfolio Management; Wealth Planning; Advanced Topics in Wealth Management; Financial Advisers Law & Compliance.
- Mar-Apr Study Block IV: Advanced Wealth Planning; Private Equity & Venture Capital; Fintech in Wealth Management; Alternative Investing; European Family Offices.
- May-Jun Study Block V: Structured Products; Client Relationship Management; Client Book Reading; Investment Management in Family Office; Seminar in Wealth Management.
If you do not have a background in wealth management, you will be encouraged to take up internships. A number of corporations are offering to host potential candidates as interns for different durations, ranging from three months to the entire length of the 12-month programme. Internships may incorporate exposure to different aspects of wealth management, briefings and tours of departments, brief assignments during rotations through departments, and attachment to a senior officer as mentor.

financial_aid.content:
Scholarships are available based on merit for selected participants.
Academic Excellence | Global Awareness | Leadership* | Impact on Asia* | Women in Business* | Community Impact* | Keeve Tan Wealth Management Scholarship*
_* Denotes scholarships that students can apply for upon admissions into the programme._ These scholarships entail award amounts up to **S$18,000**, with no bonds attached.
- Keeve Tan Wealth Management Scholarship: supports talented Southeast Asian students with demonstrated academic excellence, and relevant work experience in asset or wealth management. Benefits: **$20,000**, tenable for one academic year.
- MWM Talent Development Scholarship: awarded to eligible individuals of any nationality who are currently working in a private bank or related financial institution, with at least five years of experience in financial or wealth management, and who are either company-sponsored or SMU alumni. MWMTD Scholarship quantum: **S$18,000 (inclusive of GST)**. Candidates are automatically submitted for consideration for MWMTD scholarship upon meeting the scholarship and application criteria. Scholarship is awarded on a highly selective and competitive basis. Terms include: bond free; all application documents must be submitted by the application deadline; successful candidates must matriculate and start the MWM in the same applied intake; no deferment, withdrawal, leave of absence during the one-year study is allowed.
- IBF-STS funding will range from **S$17,000 to S$19,000** for Singapore Citizens and Singapore PRs who have successfully completed the SMU MWM programme. Eligible students will receive the funding as a reduction to their second billing of tuition fees.
- Academic Excellence Award: offered to high-quality candidates with exceptional academic performance. Awards are based on academic merit, final grades and admissions test score. Awardees must have achieved an excellent admissions test score (equivalent to GMAT score of **700 and above**) and have demonstrated outstanding academic achievement.
- Global Awareness Award: given to individuals who will contribute to classroom diversity and enrich the learning experience of students by way of their cultural, personal or professional backgrounds.
- Leadership Award: recognises individuals with strong leadership capabilities who have exhibited outstanding leadership capabilities and potential during their studies, community or organisation. Applicants must demonstrate strong leadership potential in personal and professional instances.
- Impact on Asia Award: for students who can demonstrate achievements in their professional, social and personal life that have created an impact on Asia.
- Women in Business Award: recognises exceptional women who have demonstrated outstanding leadership capabilities or potential in their professional or personal endeavours. Applicants must have successfully received an admissions offer.
- Community Impact Award: recognises candidates who have contributed to society through outstanding community work and through their actions have impacted members of the community/society in a positive manner.
- SkillsFuture: SkillsFuture Funding for Singapore Citizens. The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme provides Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above the opportunity to receive the SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top up of **$4,000** to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after **1 May 2024**.
- CIMB ASEAN Scholarship: Learn more and apply for the CIMB ASEAN Scholarship [here.](https://www.cimb.com/en/careers/students/cimb-asean-scholarship.html)
- SMU Alumni: graduates from SMU undergraduate or postgraduate programmes are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of **S$8,000** when applying to the MWM programme.
- Singapore Local Autonomous University: graduates from NUS, NTU, SUSS, SUTD, or SIT are automatically eligible for an alumni discount of **S$4,000** when applying to the MWM programme. Eligible candidates may receive exemptions for up to four credit units, with a discount of **$3,000** awarded for each credit unit exempted.
- SG/PR: Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$5,000**.
- ASEAN Citizens: ASEAN citizens are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$3,000**.
- Corporate Partner: eligible company-sponsored candidates are eligible for a one-time discount of **S$6,000**. If 2 or more company-sponsored candidates from the same organisation are enrolling in the same intake, each will enjoy a **S$12,000** discount. If a company which has previously sponsored an employee is sponsoring another employee into the programme at a subsequent intake, that employee will enjoy a **S$9,000** discount off the total tuition fee.
The discounts are applicable to students joining the programme from the January 2025 intake onwards. Each student is only eligible for one discount; should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount will be applicable. The tuition fee discount is deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST).
